author: Khushi Arora, Local Journalism Initiative Reporter
title: Williams Lake First Nation memorializes history and justice with opening of Sḱulé7ten Park
content:
Williams Lake First Nation Willie Sellars speaks about the significance of Sḱulé7ten park during its official opening.

Photo by Khushi Arora


This story was originally printed in the

Williams Lake Tribune

 and appears here with minor style edits.


The Williams Lake First Nation (WLFN) celebrated the grand opening of a new memorial park in downtown Williams Lake, unveiling its name as Sḱulé7ten Park.


WLFN, also known as T’exelc, welcomed the community to the park on Oct. 13. The space memorializes WLFN’s journey towards reaching a historic specific claim settlement with “Canada.” The colonial government illegally displaced the First Nation from their traditional village site 165 years ago, in what’s now the City of Williams Lake.


After guiding attendees through the pronunciation of the park’s name “skoo LET nn,” WLFN member William Lulua explained that the surrounding area included spaces where people did vision quests. Although there was a disconnection from the practice as Williams Lake developed into a city, he said the names of the people received through those places could not be taken away.


William Lulua shares the history and meaning behind Sḱulé7ten park’s name during the official opening on Tuesday, Oct.13. Photo by Khushi Arora


According to the Facebook post by WLFN, the name Sḱulé7ten is the traditional Secwepemcstin word for the area that makes up downtown Williams Lake, and the name translates to “where you find yourself.”


Before the main opening drum song, Elder Virginia Gilbert was called upon to do a prayer. She spoke about attending both day and residential “schools,” expressing gratitude that her five children had not attended those institutions. She gave thanks for her ancestors, family, food, water and medicines, and asked that the park provide a place for rest for people struggling with addictions.


“Great spirit, let this place bless them and look after them,” added Gilbert.


Students from Little Chiefs Primary School performed drumming and songs during the ceremony. 


Little Chiefs Primary School students drum and sing during the official opening of Sḱulé7ten park on Tuesday, Oct.13. Photo by Khushi Arora


WLFN Chief Willie Sellars thanked the students, recognizing the strength it takes to perform and carry forward songs significant to the First Nation and their ancestors.


Sellars also thanked the contractors who helped design and build the park and said, “we couldn’t have done it without all those contractors stepping up and contributing to this project, city representatives, community members and WLFN staff who attended the opening.”


WLFN councillor and director of self-government Chris Wycotte recalled the First Nation’s persistence through decades of pursuing its specific claim.


“We just said, no, we’re going to take it as far as we can,” said Wycotte.


Community members gather to celebrate the official opening of Sḱulé7ten memorial park in downtown Williams Lake on Oct. 13. Photo by Khushi Arora


He described finding documents in the provincial archives that revealed an injustice against the First Nation. After repeated rejections, WLFN continued pursuing the claim through legal proceedings, eventually taking its fight to the Supreme Court of Canada.


“And this is what we end up with today. And this park here is just a memorial to that journey,” he added.


Chief Sellars acknowledged relationships with municipal, provincial and federal governments, saying collaboration had helped bring community to where it is today.


“And that relationship has been tough at times, but where we’re at right now, we’re in a good place,” Sellars added.


“Under the settlement, Canada provided the Williams Lake First Nation with $135 million in total compensation,” the federal government stated in a September 2023 news release about the Village Site Specific Claim.


Sellars said the First Nation’s approach to the settlement honours its ancestors while providing for future generations. He described the opening as an opportunity for the wider community to participate in reconciliation.


“That’s taking care of our generations, four, five, six, seven generations from now, and that is what we are very proud of as Williams Lake First Nation,” he continued.


WLFN manager of culture and language Cecil Sheena introduced a grass dance with Reggie Sandy and Sellars and invited drummers to take part.


Afterward, Sellars thanked Sheena and the drummers and invited another round of applause …

author: Nehaa Bimal
title: Gjoa Haven journalism student wants more Inuit telling their own stories
content:
Gjoa Haven resident Emerald Hatkaittuq is pursuing a career she has thought about since high school.


The 23-year-old is one of the first two Inuit students enrolled in Carleton University’s Certificate in Journalism in Indigenous Communities. The nine-month program, designed to train Indigenous journalists to tell stories from their own communities, is in its second year.


“Representation is so important. When applications opened for this year, I shared it with people I know because I want to see more Inuit pursuing journalism,” said Hatkaittuq. 


Hatkaittuq had considered studying journalism after high school but instead enrolled in science and technology foundations at Algonquin College, hoping to enter the medical field. 


She eventually realized science was not for her, she said, and joined Tigulavut’s media-training program in Ottawa this year. The hands-on program, launched by the Inuit Broadcasting Corporation, helps Inuit aged 18 to 30 develop skills in film, television and digital media.


During the program, Hatkaittuq met Duncan McCue, director of Carleton’s journalism certificate program, who visited as a guest speaker. He encouraged her to apply.


“

The goal of this program is for them to imagine being a media maker in their own community, and imagine our own narrative sovereignty that doesn’t necessarily include legacy media and could instead be Indigenous media,” said McCue in an interview.


Hatkaittuq was accepted into the program alongside 18-year-old Alanna Dean, whose family is from Iqaluit, and 18 others.


Alanna Dean, left, interviews fellow student Emerald Hatkaittuq while testing audio recording equipment. The two are in Carleton University’s Certificate in Journalism in Indigenous Communities on Manitoulin Island, Ont., in September. (Photo by Cedar Grace Photography)


The curriculum is delivered primarily online, allowing students to study from their home communities, with three in-person intensives for hands-on training and cultural learning.


The first intensive took place during the week of Sept. 13 at Kenjgewin Teg, an Indigenous learning institution on Manitoulin Island, Ont.


For Hatkaittuq, getting there meant flying from Gjoa Haven to Yellowknife and then to Ottawa, before driving about seven hours to Manitoulin Island.


Due to weather, she also got stranded in Yellowknife for a week on her way home.


“She travelled further than any of our learners just to get there. That’s not cheap, but we’re happy to support our northern learners in that way,” said McCue.


Travel, accommodation and meals for students attending the intensives, as well as travel for a two-week internship, are covered through a three-year, $3.2-million partnership between Carleton University and the Mastercard Foundation’s EleV program.


During the intensive, Hatkaittuq said classmates who introduced themselves in their Indigenous languages inspired her to do the same in Inuktitut.


“I was happy that we were able to share Anishinaabe culture and other First Nations cultures with Emerald and Alanna because I think that cross-cultural sharing between First Nations and Inuit can be very productive,” McCue said.


Back in Gjoa Haven, Hatkaittuq has returned to studying remotely.


“T

he only issue I’ve had so far is that we’ve been having power outages in Gjoa Haven quite often and it happened in one of my classes,” she said.   


After completing the certificate, Hatkaittuq hopes to pursue further education in journalism. 


“I remember Duncan saying to non-Indigenous people, ‘Don’t be story takers, be story tellers.’ I feel like having Inuit tell their own stories in our communities can create much bigger and better change,” she said.

author: William Gillis
title: လက်ဝဲဆိုတဲ့ ဝေါဟာရရဲ့ အနှစ်မဲ့မှု
content:
William Gillis

. Original:

The Emptiness of “The Left”

, February 21, 2017. Translated into Burmese by Hein Htet Kyaw.


ပုဂ္ဂလိကအရ ပြောရရင် “လက်ဝဲ” ဆိုတာဟာ နောက်ဆုံးမှာ တညီတညွတ်တည်းရှိတဲ့ သဘောတရား ရပ်တည်ချက်တစ်ခုအဖြစ် ခိုင်ခိုင်မာမာ ကိုယ်စားပြုနိုင်တယ်လို့ မထင်ပါဘူး။ သမိုင်းကြောင်းအရ ခဏတာ ပေါင်းစည်းထားကြတဲ့ သဘောတရားရေးရာ မဟာမိတ်အုပ်စု သက်သက်ပဲလို့ မြင်ပါတယ်။ Bastiat နဲ့ တခြား လွတ်လပ်သောဈေးကွက်သမားတွေဟာ ပြင်သစ် အမျိုးသားလွှတ်တော်ရဲ့ လက်ဝဲဘက်မှာ ထိုင်ခဲ့ကြဖူးတာပဲ။ ဒါကို စနစ်တကျရှိတဲ့ လက်ဝဲဈေးကွက် အစဉ်အလာရဲ့ အစိတ်အပိုင်းတစ်ခုအနေနဲ့ ကျနော်တို့ အခိုင်အမာ ပြောဖို့ ကြိုးစားနိုင်ပေမဲ့၊ အဲဒီတော်လှန်ရေး (ဒါမှမဟုတ် တော်လှန်ရေးအများစု) မှာ ဘယ်ဘက်မှာ ထိုင်ခဲ့သလဲ ဆိုတာဟာ ဘာကိုမှ သိပ်ပြီး ညွှန်ပြနေတာမဟုတ်ဘူးဆိုတာကိုတော့ ရိုးရိုးသားသား ဝန်ခံရပါမယ်။ ကျနော်တို့လက်ရှိစနစ်ထက် အများကြီး ပိုဆိုးရွားတဲ့ စနစ်တွေကို လိုချင်ကြတဲ့ တော်လှန်ရေးသမားတွေ အမြဲတမ်းရှိခဲ့သလို၊ လူထုလွတ်မြောက်ရေးနဲ့ လုံးဝ ဆန့်ကျင်ဘက်ဖြစ်တဲ့ ဆန္ဒတွေရှိကြပေမဲ့ “လက်ဝဲဝါဒီ” လို့ အများက သတ်မှတ်ထားကြသူတွေလည်း အများကြီး ရှိခဲ့တာပါပဲ။


ဒီနေ့ခေတ်မှာ လက်ဝဲနဲ့ လက်ယာကို အုပ်စုခွဲခြားမှုမရှိဘေးတူညီမျှဝါဒီ (egalitarian) နဲ့ အဆင့်အတန်းခွဲခြားမှုဝါဒီ (hierarchical) ဆိုပြီး ပုံဖော်ကြတာ ရေပန်းစားပါတယ်။ ဒါပေမဲ့ ဒါဟာ ရှုပ်ထွေးလှတဲ့ သမိုင်းနဲ့ လူမှုဗေဒ အရှိတရားပေါ်မှာ အတင်းအဓမ္မ စိစစ်ပုံဖော်ထားတာ ဖြစ်ရုံတင်မကဘဲ တကယ်တော့ တတ်သိနားလည်ဖွယ်ရာ အနှစ်သာရလည်း လုံးဝမရှိပါဘူး။ ဘယ်သူမှလည်း egalitarianism ဆိုတာ ဘာလဲ၊ ဒါမှမဟုတ် hierarchy ဆိုတာ ဘာလဲဆိုတာကို ရှင်းရှင်းလင်းလင်း မသိကြသလို၊ အဓိပ္ပာယ်ဖွင့်ဆိုချက် အတော်များများဟာလည်း တစ်ခုနဲ့တစ်ခု ဆန့်ကျင်နေရုံမက တူညီပါတယ်ဆိုတဲ့ အချက်တွေကိုပင် လွန်စွာဆန့်ကျင်နေကြောင်း ဖော်ပြနေပါတယ်။ egalitarianism ဆိုတာ လူတိုင်း ဓနဥစ္စာ အတိအကျ အမျှတူ ရရှိတာကို ပြောတာလား (ဒါကိုရော ဘယ်လိုတိုင်းတာမှာလဲ)။ ဒါမှမဟုတ် ပြည်သူ သို့မဟုတ် နိုင်ငံတော်ရဲ့ ဥပဒေစနစ်ရှေ့မှာ တရားဝင် သို့မဟုတ် လူမှုရေးအရ တန်းတူညီမျှမှု ဆိုတဲ့ နာမ်တရားသဘောတရားကို ပြောတာလား။ စီးပွားရေးအရ ကြိုးစားအားထုတ်ခွင့် တန်းတူရတာကို ပြောတာလား၊ ဒါမှမဟုတ် ပြည်သူ့ဆန်ဂိုဒေါင်တွေကို တန်းတူဝင်ရောက် အသုံးပြုခွင့်ရတာကို ပြောတာလား။ တန်းတူညီမျှမှုဟာ လွတ်လပ်မှုလို တခြား အကျင့်သီလအားလုံးထက် ပိုအရေးကြီးသလား။ အချို့က ပိုမိုကြီးမားတဲ့ လွတ်လပ်မှုကို ရရှိကြတာထက် လူတိုင်း တန်းတူဖိနှိပ်ခံရတာက ပိုကောင်းသလား။ ကျနော် သရော်နေတာ မဟုတ်ပါဘူး။ ကျနော်တို့ဟာ ဒီလိုနက်နက်နဲနဲ မေးခွန်းတွေကို “အင်းလေ၊ ဒါကတော့ အသိစိတ် (common sense) ပေါ့” ဆိုပြီးတော့လည်းကောင်း၊ ကျနော်တို့ရဲ့ ရဲဘော်တွေဟာ ကိစ္စသေးသေးလေးတွေမှာ ကျနော်တို့ စဉ်းစားသလိုပဲ စဉ်းစားလိမ့်မယ်၊ ပေးဆပ်ရမှုနဲ့ အကျိုးအမြတ်တွေအပေါ် ကျနော်တို့ရဲ့ မသိစိတ်ခံစားချက်တွေကို မျှဝေခံစားကြလိမ့်မယ် ဆိုတဲ့ မျှော်လင့်ချက်ဆန္ဒနဲ့ ဖုံးဖိထားကြပေမဲ့ လက်တွေ့မှာတော့ အဲဒီလို မဟုတ်ပါဘူး။ ကျနော်တို့ဟာ အမြဲတမ်း သဘောထားကွဲလွဲနေကြတာပါ။


လူတွေက “စုပေါင်းတိုက်ရိုက်ဒီမိုကရေစီ” (collective direct democracy) အကြောင်း ပြောကြတဲ့အခါ လူမှုအဖွဲ့အစည်းတစ်ခုရဲ့ တခဲနက်ဆန္ဒဟာ တန်းတူညီမျှတဲ့ အခြေအနေတစ်ခုကို ဖန်တီးပေးသလိုလို ပြောကြပါတယ်။ ဟုတ်ပါတယ်၊ အချို့သော အဓိပ္ပာယ်ဖွင့်ဆိုချက်တွေအရတော့ ဟုတ်တာပေါ့။ ဒါပေမဲ့ တစ်ခုခုသော စုပေါင်းအဖွဲ့အစည်းက ကျနော့်ဘဝအပေါ် မဲပေးဆုံးဖြတ်ဖို့ ကြိုးစားနေတာကို မြင်လိုက်ရတာနဲ့ ကျနော် “ပါဝင်” မနေချင်တော့ဘဲ့ အဲဒီအဖွဲ့အစည်းထဲ ဗုံးခွဲပစ်ချင်စိတ်ပဲ ပေါ်လာတော့တာပါ။ လက်ဝဲဝါဒီတွေဟာ “ပြည်သူ့ထံ အာဏာအပ်စက်” ဆိုတဲ့ ကြွေးကြော်သံနဲ့ “အာဏာကို ဖျက်ဆီး” ဆိုတဲ့ ကြွေးကြော်သံ နှစ်ခုလုံးကို သုံးကြပါတယ်။ ဒါဟာ လုံးဝခြားနားတဲ့ သဘောတရားစနစ်တွေနဲ့ တန်ဖိုးထားမှုတွေ ပါဝင်ပတ်သက်နေတယ်ဆိုတာကို လူတိုင်းအတွက် ကြီးမားတဲ့ သတိပေးချက် ဖြစ်သင့်ပါတယ်။ ကျနော်တို့ အားလုံး ထိုင်ဆွေးနွေးလိုက်ရင် တစ်မျက်နှာတည်းမှာပဲ လာဆုံကြလိမ့်မယ်လို့ တွေးတာဟာ လွန်စွာမှ စိတ်ကူးယဉ်ဆန်လွန်းပါတယ်။ လက်ဝဲဝါဒီအားလုံး တညီတညွတ်တည်း ရှိကြတယ် သို့မဟုတ် ဘုံဦးတည်ချက်တစ်ခု ပူးတွဲရှိကြတယ်ဆိုတဲ့ အယူအဆဟာ နှစ်သိမ့်မှုပေးတဲ့ လိမ်ညာမှုတစ်ခု သက်သက်ပါ။


လက်ဝဲဆိုတာ ကျနော်တို့အားလုံး သဘောတူနိုင်တဲ့ ကျင့်ဝတ်ဆိုင်ရာ တာဝန်ယူမှု မူဝါဒအချို့နဲ့ သတ်မှတ်ထားတာ မဟုတ်သလို အဲဒီကနေ နည်းဗျူဟာ ဒါမှမဟုတ် အကောင်အထည်ဖော်မှုတွေကို ဆွေးနွေးငြင်းခုံလို့ရတဲ့ အရာလည်း မဟုတ်ပါဘူး။ လက်ဝဲဆိုတာ တိုက်ဆိုင်မှုတွေကြောင့် ဖြစ်တည်လာရတဲ့ သမိုင်းဝင် မဟာမိတ်အဖွဲ့တစ်ခုပါ။ တော်လှန်ရေးမှာလိုပဲ ကျနော်တို့ဟာ မိမိတို့ကိုယ်ကို အားနည်းသူ တွေအဖြစ် သတ်မှတ်လေ့ရှိကြပြီး၊ အစိုးရသော လူတန်းစားတွေကို ဆန့်ကျင်ဖို့ ကျနော်တို့ သတ်မှတ်ထားတဲ့ အားနည်းသူ လူတန်းစားတွေဆာ ပေါင်းစည်းကြပါတယ်။ ဒါပေမဲ့ ဒါဟာ အမျိုးမျိုးသော ပုံစံပျက်ယွင်းမှုတွေကို ဦးတည်စေပါတယ်။ အမျိုးသမီးတွေဟာ မဟာဖိုဝါဒကြီးစိုးတဲ့စနစ် မှာ ဖိနှိပ်ခံရသူတွေဖြစ်လို့ ကျနော်တို့ဟာ ကိုယ်ဝန်ဖျက်ချခွင့်ကို ထောက်ခံကြတယ်။ ဒါပေမဲ့ တစ်ချိန်တည်းမှာပဲ တိရစ္ဆာန်တွေဟာ လူတွေရဲ့ ဖိနှိပ်မှုမှာ (အမှန်တကယ်) အားနည်းသူတွေဖြစ်လို့ ကျနော်တို့ဟာ သက်သတ်လွတ်ဝါဒ (vegan) ကို ထောက်ခံကြပြန်တယ်။ ခဏလေး၊ ကျနော်တို့က သက်ရှိအားလုံးကို တန်ဖိုးထားတာလား။ ဘာကို သီးခြားသက်ရှိလို့ သတ်မှတ်မှာလဲ။ ကျနော်တို့က အဲဒါတွေကို တန်းတူတန်ဖိုးထားတာလား …

author: Valerie Anne
title: ‘Grey’s Anatomy’ Kicked Off Season 23 With a Sapphic Smooch
content:
Grey’s Anatomy came back with a bang. (Well, a smooch. But we’ll get there.) Amelia spent the entire episode getting the cold shoulder from Toni because, as I’m sure you remember, we left them last season with Toni showing up at Amelia’s door to profess her love for her, only to realize a naked Cass was already in Amelia’s apartment.

When we return for season 23(!), Toni is giving Amelia the cold shoulder all day. Amelia desperately wants to talk to her, but Toni isn’t hearing her out. They clash over work decisions, and Amelia starts to get frustrated. And at this point I was afraid the show was ending their storyline. I thought it was going to be a dramatic fight and then back to no wlw relationships on the show. I was thankfully wrong!

Eventually, the day leads Amelia to Toni’s front door, where she apologizes again for sleeping with Cass, and explains it was an emotional reaction to being so sure Toni was about get back together with her ex. She regrets it if it means she would lose Toni. She says she’s truly, madly, deeply in love with Toni and that if Toni is done, she’ll move on, but if not, she really doesn’t want to let what they have died. Toni considers her for a moment but then breaks; she’s still in love with Amelia, and she’s not done. The two kiss about it, and while I doubt their road ahead will be paved with roses and rainbows (especially because Toni’s ex is still in the picture, and goodness knows if/when Cass will return to drop bombs) but I’m glad we at least aren’t done with their story yet. I look forward to seeing what Season 23 will bring for our resident gays; here’s hoping none of them disappear into the parking lot of no return.

+ Olivia Rodrigo dropped a remix of her song “Expectations” with a verse by Chappell Roan in it, plus a music video go to alongside it (my TikTok FYP has been enjoying Chappell in the background singing, “not kissin’ no boy, NO BOY”)

+ Speaking of, Chappell Roan got to DJ and play Pink Pony Club at The Abbey, which inspired the song in the first place

+ Inde Navarrette, Janelle Monáe, Cole Escola, Amandla Stenberg, and more showed up in style at the Academy Museum gala

+ Future seasons of Ted Lasso are up in the air now that it has pivoted to a women’s team

+ Miley Cyrus can feel her godmother Dolly Parton supporting her from the great beyond

+ Ellen Degeneres is threatening to come back to TV

+ Trans singer Violet Bennington, daughter of Linkin Park frontman, released her first single “Follow Your Heart” as Dead Name Draven

+ Gillian Anderson stars in Ben Affleck’s Netflix thriller, Animals, available now

+ Hunter Schafer wants to make a trans girl rom-com now that she has tackled action in her film Blade Runner 2099

+ Kendall Jenner isn’t a lesbian, but when Cara Delevingne asked her who she would sleep with if she DID sleep with a woman, Kendall picked Cara

+ The end of October is fast approaching, so don’t forget to check out Horror is So Gay, Part 5 and all the fun stuff that comes along with that

author: Saima Desai
title: Beating burnout in social movements requires strategy
content:
This article

Beating burnout in social movements requires strategy

 was originally published by

Waging Nonviolence

.


I recently showed up to a protest for the first time in months, looked around, and thought: “Who the hell

are

 all these people?” 


Friends I could once rely on running into at protests when I was younger were missing. 


The fact that I hadn’t been to a protest in months was unusual. I’d had a hard season of exhaustion and cynicism, and I felt I was falling out of the loop. In the last few years, I turned 30 and moved back to my hometown, and the once-intense focus on social movements that I had in my 20s was now jostling for attention with work and family. 


The absence of my comrades at that protest seemed to signal that others, too, had burned or faded out of organizing.


It’s a trend that Chris Dixon describes in his new book, which is about sticking around for the long haul in the fight for a better world: “In radical activist scenes especially,” he writes, “people tend to age out by their 30s, if not before.” 


When the manuscript of Dixon’s book came my way, it spoke to my fear of burning or fading out of the movements that have given my life meaning and momentum. (I sit on the editorial collective of Between The Lines Books, and helped select the book for publication; it was released in September 2026.) 


After a few recent boom-and-bust cycles of uprisings — 2020’s Black liberation uprising, the Palestine solidarity protests that kicked off in 2023 — it’s a timely and thoughtful book about building movements with care and commitment.


Dixon (who unfortunately shares a name with a far more famous American crypto bro) is an anti-authoritarian activist and a scholar of social movements. “For the Long Haul: How to Stay in the Fight for a Better World”

is the latest effort in his lifelong project to understand how social movements are built and sustained.


Dixon grew up in Alaska, and the book opens by describing his decades-long friendship with Ruth Sheridan, an anarchist who was in her 70s when she first came to talk to his eighth grade labor history class. That early curiosity — about how left-wing social movements are built and sustained and the unsung activists who make it happen — showed up in his 2014 book “Another Politics: Talking Across Today’s Transformative Movements,” in which he shared lessons from almost a decade spent interviewing organizers across the U.S. and Canada. 


Now, Dixon has reached back into this same conversational archive to write “For the Long Haul.” 


We meet Bill Stivers, an elder communist Dixon befriended as a teen; Rachel Herzing, the co-founder of prison abolitionist group Critical Resistance; the political prisoner David Gilbert with whom he exchanged letters from jail, and many more. 


These lifelong leftists share their observations about what leads to burnout, the many-headed monster that has long stalked social movements. During this time of totalizing neoliberalism and weakened movement infrastructure, it’s grown especially powerful. These movement veterans counsel us to be patient, open-minded and to “practice being nobody special.” 


Dixon tells the story of Stivers who, at the age of 76, travelled from Anchorage, Alaska to the state of Chiapas in southern Mexico to attend the Zapatistas’ Intercontinental Encounter for Humanity and Against Neoliberalism. It was just a couple years after the militant group’s armed uprising and a young Dixon, more swayed by a European left tradition at that time, looked on with skepticism. But Stivers ended up having the more clear-eyed assessment of this new approach to anti-capitalist struggle. Stivers had cultivated the long view, which helped him avoid cynicism and dogmatism, and encouraged him to keep learning and stay open to new developments.  


Sign Up for our Newsletter


We’ll send you a weekly email with the latest articles.


What I found most helpful about the book was Dixon’s formulation of burnout: he sees it not just as a type of overwork or exhaustion, but as a feeling of defeat that becomes more common because of a lack of strategy. Dixon introduces this idea by sharing a conversation he had with Kim Marks, a direct-action environmentalist and Indigenous solidarity organizer in Oregon: “So much of burnout is about not being effective,” she said, “and so much ineffectiveness comes from not having a plan.” 


Dixon traces the ways that people often burn out of activist groups back to …

author: By L. Cam Anderson, Contributor
title: How The Proud Boys Lost Their Name
content:
West Palm Beach, FL – On Sept. 26, the film “American Martyrs” premiered at the Kravis Center’s Cohen Pavilion in West Palm Beach, Florida. 


The subject of the film, presented by the far-right media outlet Gateway Pundit, was the Proud Boys – specifically the “seditious five,” whom a federal jury found guilty of seditious conspiracy to stop the presidential transfer of power for their role in the Jan. 6, 2021 storming of the U.S. Capitol.


The official poster for the film, promoted by Enrique Tarrio and Gateway Pundit on X ahead of its premiere. Note that Zachary Rehl, first on the left in the lineup, is AI-generated.


The five Proud Boys presenting the film were chairman Henry “Enrique” Tarrio, Ethan Nordean, Joe Biggs, Zachary Rehl and Dominic Pezzola. In reality, the actual fifth member of the “seditious five” is Jeremy Bertino, not Pezzola, who pleaded guilty and testified against the others during their trial. 


In August 2025, Bertino appeared on an episode of Tarrio’s Substack podcast titled “Kiss of Judas,” where the “government star witness” allowed the permanently sunglasses-clad chairman to humiliate him for the twelve people who liked the post. Despite this entreaty to re-enter the flock, Bertino did not make the cut as an “American martyr.”


Besides Tarrio, who received a full pardon, the others had the sentences commuted by executive order during President Donald Trump’s first day back in office on Jan. 20, 2025. 


The film premiere, held less than four miles from Trump’s Mar-a-Lago Club, was graced by numerous right-wing characters, including leading “Stop the Steal” figure and former New York City Mayor Rudy Giuliani,

QAnon digital warrior

 and former U.S. Army general Michael Flynn and convicted fraudster George Santos.


Led by right-wing media figure Lara Logan, the event opened at 7 p.m. with an open bar that overlapped with a 10-minute window set aside for “prayer, national anthem and pledge.”


After the 80-minute film concluded, the Gateway Pundit presented Tarrio with a Gateway Pundit-branded award created specifically for the occasion recognizing him “as an American Martyr and Hero.”


“It’s not an Emmy,” Tarrio wrote on X two days later. “But it’s so much better.”


[Source: Enrique Tarrio on X]


Despite the obvious connections to the Proud Boys organization, the premiere lacked any of the recognizable branding belonging to what it depicted as a persecuted “drinking fraternity.”


Even on Tarrio’s person, the golden cock and abbreviated name have given way to the branding for his streaming outfit, “War Boys,” which has gained a whopping 700 followers on Rumble since the channel was created in April last year.


And on Tarrio’s merch website – where the Afro-Cuban now in his 40s markets just about any idea as apparel, including a t-shirt reading “Enrique Tarrio Eats Cream Pies” with an AI illustration of Tarrio licking an over-sized cream pie – reveals a distinct absence of Proud Boys related merchandise.


[Source: Enrique Tarrio on X]


Tarrio’s ability to capitalize on Proud Boys merchandising, which once characterized his merch store, hit a setback last year when a D.C. Superior Court judge awarded the brand to a historically-Black church following a years-long legal battle set in the wake of the 2020 Presidential election.


At the beginning of 2025, the Metropolitan African Methodist Episcopal (MAME) church was the only place one could purchase official Proud Boys merchandise, re-branded to signify Black pride, with proceeds going toward the church’s community justice fund.


In April 2025, the church’s hold on the brand was tested on the Hudson Valley Proud Boys, who were sued in the Southern District Court of New York for their continued usage of the Proud Boys branding and merchandising.


The court reached a default judgment against the Hudson Valley Proud Boys, a chapter associated with Tarrio, earlier this year on April 8, awarding MAME $75,000 for trademark infringement and nearly $200,000 in attorney’s fees.


The judgment against the Hudson Valley Proud Boys is only a small part of the church’s pursuit to be fully compensated in the amount awarded by the court, which continues to be a major struggle to this day and sees all related parties continue to be wrapped up in the ongoing court battle.


On the night of Dec. 12, 2020, the streets of Washington were thronged with black shirts and red caps.


Beneath the hazy yellow glow of street lights, the death rattle of …

author: Halie Moses
title: The Z Factor: Young Voters and the 2026 Midterms
content:
Generation Z voters (aged 18-29) are predicted to make a significant impact on the upcoming 2026 Midterm elections. This has not always been the case, as student and youth voter turnout has historically remained low. Only 47% of Americans aged 18-29 voted in the 2024 election. This year, 50 million Gen Z Americans are eligible to vote.

In October, a report by UCLA’s William Institute examined the political priorities and voting intentions of Gen Z adults ahead of the 2026 midterms. The study found that nearly 74 percent of respondents said they were likely or certain to vote. These numbers come as no surprise to those who work with students, spend time organizing on college campuses, or identify as Gen Z during the Trump Administration. Rising living costs, ICE raids, attacks on reproductive rights access, sexual assault cases, climate change, and unwanted wars have directly impacted their lives and are driving them to the polls with a passion for change.

Leela Strong, Director of CIRCLE, who works to empower the youth vote, reflected: “Young people are sending us clear signals, not only of dissatisfaction with our politics and deep economic concerns, but also of a strong desire to take action and drive change.” Organizations such as When We All Vote are working to engage young people by connecting their priorities with the issues and candidates on their ballots. Opportunities to participate alongside friends and classmates can also encourage young people to become more involved in politics.

Campus organizing is another part of these efforts. The Feminist Majority Foundation’s Feminist Campus program is actively working to get the student vote out. Students can help their peers register to vote, understand their ballot, and march to the polls in solidarity. These efforts are particularly important for first-time voters, who may need guidance.

Not only are young people planning to vote, but they are also planning to vote overwhelmingly Democratic. In the September Economist/YouthGov Poll, when asked who they will cast their ballot for, 54% of 18-29-year-olds said the Democratic candidate, compared with 22% who said the Republican candidate. The same survey found a sentiment among youth that reflects that the Republican Party is too extreme. When asked, “Do you think the Republican Party is too extreme?” 65% of 18- 29-year-olds replied yes. In contrast, only 29% believe the Democratic Party is too extreme. These results reflect the views of respondents at the time of the survey and do not necessarily predict how young people will vote in November.

These numbers are significant and show promising signs that young people are empowered to change the course of our political and social reality. Voter registration, accessible election information, and campus organizing can help young people navigate the voting process and participate in decisions that affect their futures. To learn more, head to vote411.org/feminist.

author: Admin101
title: Sanctuary as a Verb: Experiences and Directions from Transversal Organizing for Immigrant Defense
content:
Black Rose/Rosa Negra Anarchist Federation (BRRN) is excited to announce the publication of

Sanctuary as a Verb: Experiences and Directions from Transversal Organizing for Immigrant Defense

.


Drawing on organizing experiences of Black Rose/Rosa Negra members across the United States, this pamphlet explores how workers, neighbors, and communities are building collective resistance to ICE and defending their immigrant coworkers, classmates, and loved ones. By connecting struggles across workplaces, schools, and neighborhoods, the

transversal organizing

 approach we prioritize builds solidarity across different sectors of society to confront the interconnected structures of domination that shape our lives.


You can find a downloadable PDF version of the pamphlet at the end of this text.


Two Years of Trump II: Immigrants in the Crosshairs, Resistance Under Attack


Upon returning to office, Donald Trump wasted little time fulfilling his white supremacist campaign pledge of “Mass Deportations Now.” Via a flurry of executive orders and congressional acts his administration reinstated the reviled “family separation” policy; directed virtually unlimited resources to stop a fictitious “invasion” of the country’s borders; and sought to end birthright citizenship. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents blitzed Los Angeles in June 2025 with spectacular raids, followed shortly by similar operations in dozens of cities across the country including New York City; Chicago, IL; New Orleans, LA; and Durham, NC. This “shock and awe” strategy culminated in Operation Metro Surge, a months-long invasion of the Minnesota Twin Cities that deported over 2,000 residents. 


Meanwhile, support for the deportation machine plummeted as collective action against it swelled. Everyday people covered their cars, lawns, and lips with the slogan “Abolish ICE;” as of July 2026, nearly 50% of US adults support such a measure. Both May Days since Trump’s second inauguration centered immigrant defense in their celebrations. Rapid-response networks that keep watch for ICE, document kidnappings, and sometimes disrupt them spread wildly. Know-your-rights training flourished at worksites and community centers. Millions of Red Cards–wallet-sized cards outlining the holder’s constitutional protections around interactions with ICE and other police–were distributed at schools, churches, restaurants, and municipal buildings. Children and their parents caged in concentration camps went on hunger strike as constituents bombarded politicians’ hotlines and town halls demanding humanitarian treatment and release outside their walls.


Popular responses in St. Paul and Minneapolis demonstrate the possibilities of mass resistance. Like the Los Angeles Tenant Union’s community defense centers that countered ICE’s Southern California invasion, organizers reactivated dormant neighborhood networks from the 2020 uprising and began building new ones when word spread that Commander-at-Large Greg Bovino was bringing his paramilitary forces to town. Once Operation Metro Surge launched, everyday Minnesotans refined sophisticated systems to track, delay, and disrupt arrests. ICE agents retaliated by killing rapid-responder Renée Good and shooting Julio C. Sosa-Celis, a Venezuelan immigrant targeted for deportation. Instead of cowering from the naked clampdown, neighborhood networks coordinated with unions, churches, and other civil societal organizations to shut down their cities on January 23rd. In its wake, Trump ousted Bovino and immigration enforcement plummeted.


But July 2026 saw record high immigrant detentions since Trump’s return to office with little public opposition. What explains it? ICE’s tactical shifts undoubtedly played a role. Bovino replacement and “Border Czar” Tom Homan traded provocative street operations with quiet detainers at jails and prisons and “targeted operations” at sites protected from activist impediment like airports. Escalating repression has also raised the costs of resistance. ICE’s bevy of brutality has included intimidation, beatings, and shootings, culminating in murdering Good and rapid-responder Alex Pretti. Federal grand juries fish from the shadows for information about our movements, stoking fears of informants that slow our organizing. From the Prairieland defendants to the Minnesota 15 and more, indictments and convictions on flimsy charges could make prosecuting dissidents even easier. Evidentiary discovery in the …

author: Unknown
title: The Encampment Movement against Evictions and Gentrification : A Report from Madrid and Barcelona
content:
On September 23, 2026, Spanish authorities violently evicted Maricarmen Abascal, a disabled 87-year-old woman, from her home in Madrid following her long judicial struggle with a real estate company named Urbagestión. She had lived there for 70 years, but could not afford the latest rent increases. In response, 10,000 people took the streets in protest that day. Three days later, a much larger demonstration established an encampment in the Puerta del Sol square, which had been the site of the

15-M movement

 in 2011, itself the trigger for the

Occupy

 movement in the United States.


Maricarmen Abascal passed away on October 7 as a consequence of the stress resulting from the eviction. Protesters have continued to occupy the squares in many cities across the Iberian Peninsula. A general strike has been called for November 11.


Here, our correspondents in Madrid and Barcelona offer a view from within the movement against evictions and gentrification that has spread across Spain and Catalunya.


Anti-fascists gather to defend the housing encampment in Madrid’s Plaza del Sol, 2026.


The housing movement in Spain has a long and complex history. For any period that we might choose as a point of departure, there always exists a prior precedent that could serve just as well—so where we begin depends on how we wish to make sense of what is happening today, how we wish to narrate this story that is still being written in the streets. What follows, then, is an attempt, however insufficient and incomplete, to tell this story, in hopes that you can learn or be inspired by something from it and, in this way, become part of this story and build upon it wherever you live.


We could perhaps begin with the

15-M movement

, which erupted a decade and a half ago as part of the sequence of uprisings that unfolded across the globe in 2011. Encampments spread across Spain much as they have today, full of people clamoring for “

real democracy

.”


Whereas elsewhere, repression often put these movements to an unresolved end, in Spain, this movement culminated with the formation of several far-left political parties, including Podemos, as well as strong municipalist movements in Madrid, Barcelona, and other cities. Today, these parties lie in ruins, while the municipalists have largely lost whatever power they once held. Ultimately, much like

Occupy Wall Street

 and the Arab Spring, the true legacy of this sequence remains ambiguous, contested, and open to interpretation. Perhaps the 15-M movement is not the beginning of the story we’re telling, but simply the ruins from which the current one is being told.


Riot police are covered in eggs and paint while attempting to evict a building in Barcelona, 2021.


The movement that is now swelling across Spain emerged as a result of strong and stable union-style organizations that operate apart from the official institutional structures that are otherwise so present and influential in political life here. These organizations were built to tackle the housing crisis using horizontal and grassroots power, while simultaneously driving widespread and popular mobilizations like those we are witnessing today. These unions are novel in that they don’t involve questions of work directly, but rather address the conditions in which we live. The movement’s most significant antecedents lie in the creation of organizations such as the PAH (Platform for People Affected by Mortgages), the first chapter of which was founded in Barcelona in 2009. Like the more recently created housing organizations, the PAH groups practice what we call “social unionism.”


The premise is simple: an individual problem like a person facing the threat of losing their home is transformed into a collective issue addressed through shared political action. A variety of union-style tactics soon began to emerge, leading to the halting of many imminent evictions.


A group of thirty or so people assembles in front of an apartment in the historic city center as the sun is rising. People cling to one another tightly, locked arm in arm, crowding in front of the door of the building’s entrance while several vans of riot police pull up and park nearby as scheduled. There’s an announcement from a police loudspeaker to the effect that people must disperse, but no one does. Eventually, the cops move in, struggling to pull each person away one by one, until finally everyone has been cleared. In the end, the eviction is successful, but it …

author: Elizabeth Weill-Greenberg
title: Tablets Make Communication Easier Behind Bars – But Deaf People Are Left Behind
content:
This story was co-published with


Truthout

.


Tablet computers have revolutionized communication inside prisons for hearing prisoners. Prison systems from across the country — including in

New York

,

California

, and

Illinois

 — have

distributed tens of thousands

 of tablets to incarcerated people, which they can use to call home, watch movies, message loved ones, or attend virtual classes (although they are often

charged predatory fees

 for accessing these benefits). As of 2022,

25 state prison systems

 had tablet distribution programs, according to the Electronic Privacy Information Center. 


But as the rollout of such tablets continues, many deaf incarcerated people have been left behind. 


Disability justice organization HEARD points out that

it’s

unknown

 how many deaf people are incarcerated in U.S. prisons, but a

2015 report

 by the Bureau of Labor Statistics estimated that 6.2 percent of incarcerated people in

state

 and

federal

 prisons have a hearing disability, which would equal about 71,000 people.


Daniel Valenzuela, who is deaf, is incarcerated at Danville Correctional Center in Illinois. Last year, the Illinois Department of Corrections (IDOC)

distributed tablets

 to all incarcerated people. But IDOC blocks videophone capabilities, preventing Valenzuela from communicating in his primary language, American Sign Language (ASL).  


In September, Valenzuela sued the IDOC director for violating the Americans with Disabilities Act.


“I have six kids, four grandkids, and one of my sons is in the military. I cherish and love my family so much,” said Valenzuela in a

press release

 announcing the lawsuit. “I just want to tell them happy birthday and I am so grieved when I can’t call because I don’t want them to think I forgot.”


There are at least three other deaf individuals at Danville who primarily use ASL to communicate, according to the

complaint

 filed by Disability Rights Advocates, Equip for Equality, and the law firm Much Shelist. 


“Across the Illinois Department of Corrections, people can use tablets to communicate with their loved ones, which has been a game changer in removing restrictions on communication,” Valenzuela’s attorney, Rachel Weisberg, the directing attorney at Disability Rights Advocates, told

Truthout

. “But for Mr. Valenzuela and other deaf people who use American Sign Language, that same access simply isn’t available.” 


IDOC did not respond to a request for comment by the time of publication.


Last year, in addition to distributing tablets to incarcerated people, IDOC

announced

 it would provide every incarcerated person with 775 free domestic phone call minutes per month. In a press release,

IDOC said

 that these initiatives, working in tandem, “enhance family connections and increase access to technology that supports rehabilitation.” 


But deaf prisoners are excluded from accessing these critical programs. 


Unlike hearing prisoners who can use their tablets to make calls from their cells, Valenzuela must get a guard’s permission to walk to another building to use the one videophone that’s available to him. In at least one instance, Valenzuela had to go out in the pouring rain to use the videophone, according to the complaint. 


“When prison officials don’t communicate with deaf/disabled people in ways they can understand, they may be written up for being ‘non-compliant.'”


The videophone is often unavailable because the unit itself breaks down, the prison is on lockdown, or a guard denies his request, according to the complaint. Last year, Valenzuela was unable to speak with his family during the holidays because the phone was not working for 54 straight days, from November 2025 to January 2026. However, if the tablets malfunction, there are several backup phones that incarcerated hearing people can use, the complaint says.


“We’re asking for equal access, as that’s what the law requires,” said Weisberg. “Equal access is not static — it must reflect the benefits currently offered to others and account for the needs of people with disabilities as technology and communication systems evolve.”


These issues are not limited to Illinois. Advocates say incarcerated deaf people have to contend with discriminatory communication practices in prisons throughout the country.


“In prisons where we’ve seen scores of deaf/disabled people, there may only be 2 videophones,” Kah Mendoza, the communications coordinator for

HEARD

, told …

author: Brenda Medina
title: Departamento de imigração dos EUA diz que Ramagem é imigrante ilegal e violou leis
content:
A detenção-relâmpago de Alexandre Ramagem nos EUA no começo deste ano parece ter criado uma guerra de narrativas dentro do próprio governo americano. 


Enquanto o Departamento de Estado afirma que a Polícia Federal “manipulou” o sistema legal americano,

o Departamento de Segurança Interna (DHS, na sigla em inglês) diz que Ramagem é um “imigrante ilegal” e está sujeito a detenção e deportação.

 Segundo o DHS, o fato de Ramagem ter feito um pedido de asilo político não lhe dá proteção. 


Ex-diretor da Abin e ex-deputado federal pelo PL, Ramagem foi condenado a 16 anos de prisão pela tentativa de golpe de Estado durante o governo do ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro. Ele está nos EUA desde que foi condenado pelo Supremo Tribunal Federal, em setembro do ano passado, quando fugiu do Brasil através da Guiana


com auxílio de um criminoso

 condenado por garimpo ilegal na terra Yanomami.  


Em abril, o ICE, a polícia imigratória dos EUA que responde ao Departamento de Segurança Interna, prendeu Ramagem em Orlando por permanecer além do prazo do seu visto de turista, mas ele foi libertado dois dias depois.

 Ele não pagou fiança, segundo Paulo Figueiredo, que afirmou diversas vezes que sua 

empresa

 de consultoria de imigração, a Immigrex, está auxiliando Ramagem. Procurado pelo ICIJ, Figueiredo afirmou que não sabia como localizar Ramagem e não podia falar em nome da Immigrex.


“Obrigado, Presidente Trump e todos na administração”, escreveu Figueiredo no X.

Eduardo Bolsonaro agradeceu a Trump e ao Secretário de Estado Marco Rubio. Sóstenes Cavalcante, líder do PL, disse que Rubio ajudou a acelerar a libertação

, ou ela teria levado pelo menos duas semanas.


Diferentemente de outros casos, nenhum juiz precisou ordenar sua libertação. Imigrantes detidos geralmente precisam comparecer diante de um juiz de imigração para solicitar libertação sob fiança. No caso de Ramagem, a reportagem não encontrou nenhuma petição judicial. 


O próprio Ramagem já havia sugerido antes que tinha costas quentes.

Em um

vídeo

 publicado em novembro de 2025, após o Supremo Tribunal Federal do Brasil ordenar sua prisão, ele disse que estava nos Estados Unidos com o conhecimento do governo americano. “Nas palavras até do governo americano para mim: ‘que bom que temos um amigo que está em segurança a salvo aqui nos Estados Unidos’.

 Então a gente tem esse apoio dos norte-americanos”. 


Em 20 de abril, cinco dias após a libertação de Ramagem da custódia de imigração,

o Departamento de Estado dos EUA suspendeu o credenciamento do policial federal Marcelo Ivo de Carvalho, que era o oficial de ligação da PF lotado em Miami para trabalhar com o ICE e que ajudou na localização e detenção de Ramagem. 


“Nenhum estrangeiro pode manipular nosso sistema de imigração para contornar pedidos formais de extradição e estender perseguições políticas ao território dos Estados Unidos”, escreveu o assessor do Bureau de Assuntos do Hemisfério Ocidental do departamento no X. “Hoje, pedimos que o funcionário brasileiro envolvido deixe o nosso país por tentar fazer isso”. A embaixada dos EUA no Brasil

compartilhou

 o texto. Em resposta, Paulo Figueiredo tuitou: “tchau, querido”.


No entanto, o Brasil havia protocolado um pedido formal de extradição no Departamento de Estado em 30 de dezembro de 2025, mais de três meses antes da prisão, segundo o Ministério da Justiça.


Em resposta, o governo Lula suspendeu a permissão de um agente de imigração americano lotado em Brasília, que deixou o país em 22 de abril.

Em um comunicado, o Ministério das Relações Exteriores disse que os EUA falharam em consultar o Brasil primeiro, como exige o acordo entre os dois países sobre adidos policiais

, e ignoraram a “boa prática diplomática de diálogo entre nações amigas, como Brasil e Estados Unidos, ao longo de mais de 200 anos de relações”.


Agora, o porta-voz do Departamenrto de Segurança Interna confirma que Ramagem está ilegal no país. Em resposta para a ICIJ (Consórcio Internacional de Jornalistas Investigativos), parceiros da

Agência Pública

 nesta investigação, o porta-voz afirmou: “Em 13 de abril, o ICE prendeu Alexandre Ramagem Rodrigues, um estrangeiro ilegal do Brasil. Ele entrou legalmente no país em 11 de setembro de 2025, em caráter temporário, com permissão para permanecer no país por seis meses, mas optou por permanecer ilegalmente além do prazo autorizado, em violação às leis da nossa nação. Ele foi liberado da custódia do ICE em 15 de abril, enquanto …

author: Darío Aranda
title: Elecciones en Brasil: deforestación, frontera agrícola y ultraderecha
content:
Por Raúl Zibechi


“La frontera agrícola avanza expropiando, y la expropiación necesita de apoyo político”, escribe el abogado en derechos humanos Diogo Cabral en un trabajo que cruza datos para intentar comprender dónde y cómo se produce el avance de la ultraderecha bolsonarista, concentrado en la selva amazónica. Las conclusiones de su trabajo son tremendas y pueden ser resumidas en el editorial de Eliane Brum, directora del sitio periodístico Sumaúma: si Flávio Bolsonaro vence en la segunda vuelta, describe Brum, “existe una gran posibilidad de que la selva deje de existir como tal, lo que implica que dejará de actuar como reguladora del clima y sumidero de carbono, uno de los gases responsables del calentamiento global”.


El bolsonarismo gobernará siete de los nueve estados de la Amazonia, en tanto más de la mitad de los parlamentarios electos ya han votado en contra de la selva y de los pueblos originarios, según

la investigación de Sumaúma

.


Esta realidad impone colocar la lupa sobre lo que sucede en la Amazonia Legal brasileña, (Mato Grosso, Pará, Rondônia, Tocantins, Maranhão, Acre, Amapá, Amazonas y Roraima), que ocupa el 60 por ciento del total de la selva amazónica. En las últimas cuatro décadas la territorialidad del conflicto por la tierra se ha movido desde el sureste, donde nació el

Movimiento de Trabajadores Rurales Sin Tierra (MST)

, migró primero hacia el norte y nordeste, y ahora hacia la Amazonia, siguiendo los pasos de la expansión del agronegocio.


La expansión ha sido geométrica:

en 1990 había


once


millones de hectáreas cultivadas de soja, llegando a casi 50 millones en la actualidad

; la producción del grano creció 738 por ciento en los últimos 40 años, en tanto el área sembrada se expandió en un

322


por ciento


en el mismo período

. Hacia finales de la década de 1970, más del 80 por ciento de la soja provenía de los estados del sur; en la década siguiente comenzó a extenderse por la región central (Mato Grosso, Goiás y el distrito de Brasilia). Esta región que hace 40 años representaba el dos por ciento de la producción nacional de soja, ahora alcanza el 40 por ciento.


Este cambio notable puede observarse en el mapa

(ver mapa)

, donde se combinan cuatro variables analíticas: la deforestación, los conflictos agrarios de 2025 registrados por la

Comisión Pastoral de la Tierra (CPT)

, el monitoreo de la pulverización con agrotóxicos de la Red de Agroecología de Maranhão y los resultados electorales de la primera vuelta.


En color azul los lugares donde ganó Bolsonario. En rojo donde triunfó Lula


A medida que la frontera agrícola se expande, el mapa se va coloreando de azul.

José de Souza Martino, citado por Cabral

, entiende la frontera agrícola no sólo como la línea de avance de la producción agropecuaria sobre la vegetación nativa, sino como “espacio social de conflictos”. Se trata de una expansión autoritaria, “acumulación por despojo” como la definiera David Harvey, que busca convertir la tierra en mercancía para lo que debe no sólo apropiársela sino expulsar a las comunidades indígenas, quilombolas (negras) y pueblos tradicionales.


Datos crudos e impunidad


Los datos indican que entre 2019 y 2025 Brasil perdió once millones de hectáreas de vegetación nativa, siendo la actividad agropecuaria la responsable del 97 por ciento de esa deforestación. En paralelo, se registra un promedio de 1.500 conflictos en el campo; con 26 asesinatos en 2025, el doble que en el año anterior, y los hacendados fueron responsables de 14 de las 16 muertes en la Amazonia Legal. En los 34 años en los cuales la CPT viene sistematizando datos de conflictos rurales, hubo casi

2.000


asesinatos, pero sólo 120 habían sido juzgados hasta 2018

, según la CPT.

author: anred
title: «Temo por mi vida»: denunció venta de drogas en la Unidad 58 de Lomas de Zamora y fue trasladado a Ezeiza
content:
«Temo por mi vida». La frase, pronunciada por Roberto Cristian Pérez C. en el marco de un hábeas corpus, resume la situación que su entorno familiar denuncia tras su traslado desde la Unidad Penal N° 58 de Lomas de Zamora al Penal de Ezeiza. El detenido había denunciado que personal penitenciario de la unidad penal de Lomas de Zamora había intentado incorporarlo a una red de comercialización de drogas dentro del establecimiento. Según su familia, el tribunal hizo lugar al hábeas corpus y rechazó el pedido de autorización para trasladarlo, por considerar que la medida podía comprometer su seguridad e integridad física. Sin embargo, denuncia que fue trasladado al Penal de Ezeiza, donde permanecería aislado en un sector conocido como «buzón», donde ya lleva varios días de huelga de hambre y aún no recibió atención médica.

 Por ANRed.


Roberto Cristian Pérez C.

, detenido desde 2021,

 denunció ante la Justicia que integrantes del Servicio Penitenciario Bonaerense (SPB) intentaron obligarlo a participar en la comercialización de estupefacientes dentro de la Unidad Penal Nº 58 de Lomas de Zamora

. Tras realizar la presentación judicial,

el denunciante fue denunciado penalmente por supuestas amenazas contra un agente penitenciario

. Ante esta situación,

presentó un hábeas corpus en el que manifestó que temía por su vida y cuestionó las condiciones de su detención

.


La denuncia por los hechos de narcotráfico fue radicada el 8 de agosto de 2026 bajo la

IPP 07-00-33350-26

, ante la

Fiscalía N.º 8 y el Juzgado de Garantías Nº 3 de Lomas de Zamora

. Según la información aportada por su entorno familiar, Pérez C. señaló a integrantes de la conducción de la Unidad 58, entre ellos el director del establecimiento,

el subdirector Daniel Gauto y el jefe Rubén Pacheco,

 acusaciones que se encuentran en etapa investigativa.


Tras esa denuncia inicial, el 19 de agosto,

Pérez C. fue denunciado por supuestas amenazas contra un agente penitenciario

, en una segunda causa identificada como

IPP 07-00-034350-26

, pero

él niega haber cometido las amenazas que se le atribuyen y sostiene que la denuncia en su contra se produjo después de que denunciara la comercialización de drogas dentro del penal

.


Ante el temor por su integridad física,

Pérez C. presentó un hábeas corpus para denunciar un agravamiento de sus condiciones de detención

. En esa presentación manifestó que

él y otros detenidos estaban bajo amenazas de muerte y expresó su preocupación ante la posibilidad de ser trasladado sin autorización del tribunal

. La Defensoría Oficial N° 4 informó a la Justicia que, durante una audiencia, el detenido manifestó que corría riesgo su vida y expuso nuevamente la denuncia sobre la venta de estupefacientes dentro de la Unidad 58.


La resolución judicial hizo lugar al hábeas corpus y rechazó el pedido de autorización para trasladar a Pérez C

, dado que el tribunal consideró que el movimiento podía comprometer su seguridad y su integridad física, en el contexto de las amenazas denunciadas.

El expediente también consigna que otros detenidos habían informado situaciones relacionadas: uno habría sido trasladado el 20 de agosto y otro habría salido golpeado,

 según los antecedentes aportados por el entorno del denunciante.


Pese a esa decisión,

sus familiares denuncian que el traslado se concretó igualmente

. Según la información aportada por su familia a ANRed,

Pérez C. fue llevado al Penal de Ezeiza

,

donde permanece encerrado en un sector de aislamiento conocido como «buzón», supuestamente bajo la justificación de resguardar su integridad.

 Su entorno informa, sin embargo, que, al cierre de esta nota,

lleva cuatro días de huelga de hambre y que no fue trasladado al área de sanidad para que se evaluara su estado de salud

.


A comienzos de octubre, un medio publicó reclamos de personas detenidas en la Unidad 58 sobre maniobras vinculadas con la comercialización de drogas y el control de pabellones. Asimismo, el medio Karne de Máquina publicó un video donde

Pérez C. manifiesta temor por su vida y relata las situaciones que están ocurriendo dentro del establecimiento penitenciario.


 


Ver esta publicación en Instagram


 


Una publicación compartida por Karne de Máquina (@karne_de_maquina)


Su caso vuelve a poner el foco sobre las denuncias de irregularidades dentro del sistema penitenciario bonaerense. En este marco,

su familia reclama que se garantice su integridad física, se respete la resolución …

author: CMI Argentina
title: Albigasta en lucha: el agua no se negocia frente al avance de la megaminería
content:
Vecinos de Santiago del Estero y Catamarca resisten el proyecto de litio El Alto y denuncian los riesgos para las cuencas hídricas. Cerca de 50 impugnaciones cuestionaron la consulta pública. La disputa expone las contradicciones de los gobiernos provinciales y de un modelo extractivista que el Gobierno de Milei busca profundizar con el RIGI y el Súper RIGI.


Por Adrián Flores para Red Eco


Frías, Santiago Del Estero / Sierras De Ancasti, Catamarca


El agua que da vida a las comunidades de la Región Albigasta está en el centro de una creciente disputa. Mientras los gobiernos de Santiago del Estero y Catamarca anuncian obras para mejorar el abastecimiento de agua potable mediante el Acueducto Albigasta, el proyecto minero El Alto genera preocupación por sus posibles efectos sobre las cuencas hídricas de las Sierras de Ancasti.


Las asambleas socioambientales y los vecinos autoconvocados cuestionan el avance de la exploración de litio a cargo de Litios del Norte S.A. y reclaman información pública, controles independientes y garantías para proteger el agua, los bosques nativos y el patrimonio cultural de la región.


Además,  los pobladores de la Región de Albigasta advierten que la empresa Litios del Norte S.A  amenaza con ingresar con sus vehículos a la zona de exploración, acompañada de la policía y la gendarmería.


La contradicción es evidente: se anuncian inversiones públicas para garantizar el acceso al agua mientras se impulsa una actividad privada cuyos posibles impactos sobre ese mismo recurso deben ser rigurosamente evaluados.


La Respuesta de los Pueblos: Organización y Resistencia


Según informó El Ancasti el 28 de septiembre de 2026, la Asamblea de Ancasti por la Vida, la Asamblea Friense y vecinos autoconvocados presentaron cerca de 50 impugnaciones ante la Dirección Provincial de Gestión Ambiental Minera, cuestionando las condiciones de la consulta pública del proyecto. La charla informativa prevista para el 30 de septiembre fue suspendida.


Posteriormente, el 18 de octubre, el mismo medio informó que el senador departamental Rodolfo Santillán y el intendente de Ancasti, Randolfo Piñero, solicitaron suspender preventivamente las tareas de exploración hasta contar con una Declaración de Impacto Ambiental aprobada y garantías de participación ciudadana.


Las comunidades advierten sobre un proyecto que, según la información difundida por los sectores movilizados, abarcaría más de 34.000 hectáreas, con perforaciones de hasta 300 metros de profundidad, a unos nueve kilómetros del dique El Bolsón. También cuestionan un consumo de agua atribuido a la documentación ambiental que alcanzaría los 2.100.000 litros durante una etapa de exploración. Estas cifras deben cotejarse con los expedientes y estudios técnicos completos.


Las preguntas siguen abiertas: ¿de dónde se extraerá el agua?, ¿qué riesgos existen para las reservas subterráneas?, ¿qué controles se realizarán y quién responderá ante eventuales daños?


La preocupación también alcanza al bosque nativo y al patrimonio arqueológico, incluido el Parque Arqueológico La Tunita. Las autoridades deben publicar los estudios y permisos correspondientes, responder las objeciones y garantizar que la participación comunitaria no sea un mero trámite administrativo.


Milei, el Rigi y el Súper Rigi: Más Privilegios para el gran capital


El conflicto de Albigasta no puede separarse del modelo económico nacional. El Gobierno de Javier Milei impulsa políticas destinadas a atraer grandes inversiones extractivas y exportadoras. El Régimen de Incentivo para Grandes Inversiones (RIGI), establecido por la Ley 27.742, concede beneficios fiscales, aduaneros y cambiarios a proyectos que cumplan determinados requisitos.


En mayo de 2026, el Gobierno anunció el denominado Súper RIGI, una propuesta de ampliación de incentivos para nuevas inversiones industriales. Su alcance debe distinguirse de las disposiciones vigentes, pero vuelve a poner sobre la mesa una discusión central: ¿quién se beneficia con la explotación de los bienes naturales y quién carga con sus consecuencias?


Desde una perspectiva socioambiental crítica, estos regímenes profundizan un modelo que privilegia la rentabilidad empresarial y las exportaciones, mientras las comunidades reclaman agua segura, trabajo digno y protección territorial.


El capitalismo, en su lógica de acumulación ilimitada y subordinación de la naturaleza a la ganancia, es incompatible con la defensa de la vida cuando convierte …

author: Anikibawal
title: Comunicado de los PPM del Módulo comuneros de la Cárcel de Temuco tras el llamado a Marcha por la Resistencia, el 12 de octubre pasado.
content:
Comunicado de los presos políticos Mapuche del Módulo Comuneros de la Cárcel de Temuco tras el llamado a movilización Marcha por la resistencia, del pasado lunes 12 de octubre.


«Nosotros los prisioneros políticos mapuche recluidos en la cárcel de temuko saludamos a nuestras autoridades tradicionales y a todos quienes fueron participe de la gran movilización llevada adelante, el lunes 12 de octubre en la ciudad de temuko.


Mediante este escrito, venimos a agradecer la gran convocatoria realizada este 12 de octubre en apoyo concreto a los PPM de la cárcel de Temuco y a sus demandas, por parte del movimiento social en toda su amplitud.


Agradecemos a todos aquellos y aquellas que pusieron sus ganas y newen para que todo resultara de la mejor manera: a nuestros familiares, pu afkadi, autoridades tradicionales, comunidades en resistencia de diversos puntos del wallmapu, wenuy y simpatizantes de nuestra causa.


Hoy, a días de la gran movilización, creemos que esta logró los objetivos esperados con creces. Por tanto, agradecemos a nuestro pueblo por demostrar su fuerza cuando se lo propone.


La unidad en el weichan la entendemos como aquella en la que todo nuestro pueblo tiene su espacio, en sus distintas formas, con sus aciertos y errores. Aquí tienen cabida todos quienes busquen ser partícipes de la unidad que, como pueblo mapuche, merecemos darnos. Desde el pichiche hasta los kuifiche, todo nuestro pueblo tiene su espacio cuando se trata de levantar un movimiento social mapuche sólido, capaz de reunir la fuerza necesaria para luchar por lo que nos pertenece.


Eso sí, esta unidad debe construirse siempre desde la transparencia y la honestidad, sin dar cabida a los personalismos ni a las supuestas cualidades morales particulares.


Reconocemos también a cada uno de los peñi, ka pu lamngen y wenny de la causa mapuche que destinaron un día que podrían haber utilizado para descansar o compartir con sus familias en casa, y que, en cambio, se dieron el ánimo de asistir para expresar su solidaridad consciente con los familiares y los PPM.


Extendemos, finalmente, nuestros agradecimientos a todo el movimiento social mapuche que, cuando se lo propone, demuestra que es posible confluir en ideas y aspiraciones que aglutinan y suman. Esto cobra especial relevancia en los tiempos que corren, en los que la atomización y el individualismo prevalecen por sobre la justa intención de juntarse y organizarse, con el propósito de ser partícipes concretos del movimiento social mapuche autónomo.


Fei taiñ feipiaiñ may. Chaltu may kom eimun!¡¡KIÑEWKULEAIÑ WEICHAN MEW!!


Fin a las altas condenas


Fin a la dispersión de los PPM.


Fin al estado de excepción en Wall Mapu.


No a la aplicación de la ley Antiterrorista.


A más de 500 años de resistencia no pudieron ni podrán borrar la memoria del mapuzungun. «


*Enviado a la radio.


Esta información se publicó en

Radio Kurruf

.

author: La Zarzamora
title: DESPEDIR A JUAN…
content:
Esta mañana nuestro compañero Juan Aliste Vega ha partido de su cuerpo, cuerpo que el poder mantuvo en encierro los últimos 16 años, cuerpo que practicó el conflicto y lo materializó en acciones armadas, que acompañó su vida en el álgido recorrido de ser él. Fue en el hospital penitenciario de Santiago, donde en compañia y calma, se fugó definitivamente.

Aún no podemos confirmar donde ni como será su despedida, ló que sí sabemos es que serán muchas, en muchos territorios, en las calles, en los puentes, en las jaulas, en avenidas y carreteras.

Juan Aliste es y será reivindicado, pese a los esfuerzos incansables de la prensa del enemigo y de sus múltiples intentos de desprestigiarlo, nosotrxs sus compañerxs sabemos que en este momento estamos despidiendo a un guerrero de gran envergadura. Pese a sus miserables conjunciones de palabras, el mundo sabe quien es Juan y en todos los territorios se levantará fuego en su memoria.

Que desesperanza deben sentir los poderosos, al saber que amamos pese a estar en guerra, que nuestra historia es escrita por nosotrxs, pese a sus asquerosos relatos oficiales, tan indignos como ellos mismos.

Hoy es un día de nuestra propia historia, hoy parte el guerrero combatiente que se alzó en armas contra la dictadura y la pestilente democracia de burgueses y traidores, el que no se dejó abatir, el que atacó y acertó, el que siguió compartiendo conocimientos y enseñanzas pese al encierro, el que enviaba notas y saludos, el que hacía llegar sus palabras a actividades y espacios.

Cada vez es más difícil despedir, esto no es una noticia, ni tampoco un comunicado, es nuestro adiós a un hermano…

A nosotrxs ahora nos quedará volver a mirarnos, tensionar el encierro de nuestrxs compañerxs, cuestionarnos y autocriticarnos, dejar de hacernos tolerantes al encarcelamiento, dejar de normalizar la sociedad carcelaria y hacer. Arduo camino nos dejas.

Juan que tu fuga sea eterna querido compañero.

Ternura y ataque frontal por ti y por todxs nuestrxs muertxs.

title: Revista Crítica Anticapitalista 6 – La Comuna, la clase y la lucha de clases
content:
PRESENTACION


¿Qué relación existe entre la Comuna como forma política de la emancipación social y la clase, entendida ésta no como categoría positivizada y sociológica, sino en su carácter dual y contradictorio? ¿Es la Comuna una manera de entender la clase y la lucha de clases en clave no identitaria, no positivizada? ¿La oposición entre Comuna y clase es algo derivado de una concepción anti-dialéctica de la lucha de clases? En ese campo ¿a qué dialéctica nos referimos? ¿A la dialéctica hegeliana orientada a la síntesis estatal como forma política de la identidad? ¿A la dialéctica negativa que la cuestiona? ¿La lucha de clases, entendida en clave dialéctica no-identitaria, permite entender la Comuna como proceso contradictorio de disolución de la clase? ¿Implica esto un desafío a nuestro concepto de proletariado y a la idea de revolución calcada en el canon leninista?

author: Duda Sousa
title: Flávio Bolsonaro & família: as perguntas que a Pública já respondeu e você precisa saber
content:
Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) chegou à disputa pela Presidência da República carregando um sobrenome que dispensa apresentações, e uma série de controvérsias que vão muito além dos seus discursos de campanha.

O filho 01 de Jair Bolsonaro tenta transformar a herança política do pai em votos, enquanto episódios que marcaram a trajetória política de sua família voltam ao centro do debate eleitoral na disputa do segundo turno das eleições de 2026.


Mas você sabe o que realmente aconteceu? Qual é a relação de Flávio com o banqueiro Daniel Vorcaro? O senador defendeu um policial acusado de matar uma menina de cinco anos? Seu pai, Jair Bolsonaro, sabia do plano para assassinar Lula? Reunimos o que você precisa saber sobre o candidato, o que é fato e o que é mentira, para te ajudar a esclarecer dúvidas antes de ir às urnas no domingo, 25 de outubro.


1. Jair Bolsonaro mandou matar Lula? O que era o plano Punhal Verde Amarelo?


O plano Punhal Verde e Amarelo previa o assassinato das três autoridades antes da posse de Lula, em janeiro de 2023. Sua execução envolveria militares das Forças Especiais do Exército, conhecidos como

kid pretos

, treinados para operações de alto risco.


O plano foi descoberto durante as investigações sobre a tentativa de golpe de Estado após as eleições de 2022, e detalhado em

reportagem da

Pública

 de abril de 2025. Segundo a Procuradoria-Geral da República (PGR), o documento foi elaborado pelo general da reserva Mário Fernandes, ex-integrante do governo Bolsonaro.


De acordo com a denúncia da PGR, Fernandes apresentou o plano a Jair Bolsonaro. As investigações da Polícia Federal também identificaram reuniões clandestinas, compra de celulares para comunicação entre os envolvidos e operações de monitoramento a Alexandre de Moraes.


2. Flávio Bolsonaro mentiu sobre sua relação com Daniel Vorcaro? O banqueiro financiou o filme sobre Jair Bolsonaro?


Sim, quando o assunto é o Caso Master, Flávio Bolsonaro

mentiu uma sequência de vezes

.

O financiamento de

Dark Horse

, cinebiografia de Jair Bolsonaro orçada em R$ 134 milhões, foi apontado como foco de desgaste para a candidatura presidencial de Flávio Bolsonaro. Áudios e mensagens revelados pelo

The Intercept Brasil

 contradizem declarações do senador, que havia negado manter contato com Daniel Vorcaro, ex-dono do Banco Master.


Em uma das mensagens, Flávio cobrou pagamentos atrasados para a produção. Após a divulgação das conversas, confirmou a negociação, mas mudou de versão e afirmou que se tratava de

financiamento privado para uma obra privada

, sem oferecimento de vantagens em troca.


Em áudio enviado a Vorcaro, Flávio demonstrou preocupação com os pagamentos e com a repercussão da produção: “Todo efeito positivo que a gente tem certeza que vai vir com esse filme pode ter o efeito elevado a menos um aí, cara”. Segundo informações apresentadas na

coluna de Marina Amaral

, a produtora Karina Ferreira Gomes afirmou que Vorcaro teria financiado mais de 90% da obra.


O texto também aponta que organizações ligadas à produtora receberam R$ 4,6 milhões em emendas parlamentares de deputados do PL e discute os questionamentos apresentados ao Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) sobre possível abuso de poder econômico e financiamento político irregular. Essas suspeitas dependem de apuração e decisão das autoridades competentes.


3. A família Bolsonaro é antivacina? O que aconteceu durante a pandemia?


O país terminou o governo Bolsonaro, em 31 de dezembro de 2022, com 693.853 mortes registradas pela doença. Mas as consequências da atuação do governo durante a crise sanitária foram além das declarações públicas do presidente, que incluíram o não interesse em compra antecipada dos imunizantes e o desestímulo à população de tomá-los sob risco de “virar jacaré”, como foi popularizado um de seus deboches sobre o assunto.


Reportagem da

Agência Pública

 acompanhou as investigações sobre a condução da pandemia e os resultados da Comissão Parlamentar de Inquérito (CPI) da Covid, instalada no Senado em 2021. O relatório final da comissão apontou possíveis crimes atribuídos a Bolsonaro e a outros integrantes de sua administração, entre eles epidemia com resultado morte, charlatanismo, incitação ao crime e prevaricação.


A CPI pediu o indiciamento de 78 pessoas, incluindo o ex-presidente, e apontou possíveis crimes contra a humanidade.


Uma investigação de pesquisadores da Universidade de São Paulo (USP) também identificou uma atuação …

content:
The release of Sermin Demirdağ, who is being held at Kayseri Women’s Closed Prison, has been postponed for six months for the eighth time by the Prison Administration and Observation Board.


Sermin Demirdağ, who has been imprisoned since 13 April 1993, had previously had her release postponed seven times through board decisions at Sincan Women’s Closed Prison, where she was formerly held.


With this latest decision, the total time added to Sermin Demirdağ’s imprisonment has reached four years and three months, as her release has been blocked since 7 March 2023.

author: Kodao Productions
title: Sara rants daily but totes only a toothpick
content:
Sara Zimmerman Duterte Carpio needs more than a battalion of bodyguards. But more than that, she has to deploy a division of propagandists, call them trolls and crones, operating out of Davao City and under the command of image makers who pander to Sara’s need to look charming despite her aversion to crowds and her failure to stitch together decent sentences that fourth graders could understand.


Yes, it is damn true. Sara is a bad public speaker, perhaps as worse as her record as a public official, and yet she argues that she was groomed to be the country’s president, meaning she has a franchise to occupy Malacanang. Her obsession with political power, coupled with her delusion that the Filipino people await her presidency like the coming of messiah, only confirms what his own father said many years ago—that she is pig-headed and brooks no opposition, criticism or counsel, not even from her friend and image-builder Malou Tiquia. Sara is damaged goods, and no amount of daily pablum, the endless stream of photos of tree-planting, false charity and activities designed to show that she is working would destroy her status as a non-performing official.


Yet, the Sara camp has the effrontery to engage in the industrial production of daily gibberish to massage her decaying ego, putting out praise releases in Filipino and English in a vain attempt to support her delusion that she is the choice of Filipino people. If you read the daily tongue bath they give Sara, the impeachment case is part of a conspiracy to prevent her from ascending to the pinnacle of political power. In their reckoning, all the articles of impeachment filed against were manufactured, based on fabricated evidence to subvert the will of the 32-million digitalized voters who chose her.


Sara’s case is that of a one-track mind marinated in solipsism created in a frozen cerebrum. Who the hell does she think she is? It is time for all journalists, commentators and broadcasters to put her in her proper place. She is only as good as the last press release churned out by her PR operators who also control survey firms, just like a senator who does little legislative work and disingenuously criticized his own legislative proposal. Her kilometric press statements do not cut the mustard and instead get the vapors to those who try to understand her, which is a difficult task. Her yarn about lauding the Laotian authorities for busting the shipment of 521 kilos of shabu to Manila was a dead giveaway as the parties linked to that cargo are Duterte zealots.

Ang unang tumilaok ang may kasalanan.

This episode brings back to the public consciousness the earlier allegations that the ₱6.4-billion shipment of shabu some years ago that Rodrigo Duterte dismissed as bogus was simply one of the many smuggling operations laid at the doorstep of the country alleged principal crime family.


Sara is also caterwauling about “fabrications” about her wealth, with assets listed in annual Statements of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth (SALNs) being denied as her own. These SALNs did not even bother to list the 22 firearms that she owned and the 29 guns registered in the name of her hubby Atty. Manases “Mans” Carpio. She has not explained why for several years, she had no cash in hand while hundreds of millions in bank transactions betray the utter falsehood. Sara also maintained equity in 18 companies, including several that had Jollibee and Chowking franchises. She even tried to freeload on the Senate by asking that her lawyers and staff at the impeachment trial be fed by their caterer, with the bill to be paid by the chamber. *

Muy grueso

! Like the attempt to use manager’s checks to hide ₱96-million.


The icing on the ill-gotten wealth cake was Atty. Alexander Cabrera’s forensic analysis of Sara’s bank records, credit memos, manager’s checks and corporate documents that showed she amassed ₱817,874,867 from 2022 to 2025, when she also moonlighted as vice president. Cabrera’s conservative methodology showed Sara had ₱190.63 million in undeclared assets and income in 2022, ₱167.34 million the following year and ₱264.22 million for 2024. Last year, ₱195.69 million was amassed. Cabrera explained that when other amounts are added, the alleged ill-gotten wealth would zoom to ₱1.5-billion.
