title: Fransa’da kitlesel eylemlerin ardından gözaltılar 2 bini aştı
content:
Fransa’da lise öğrencilerinin eğitimde eşitlik talebiyle başlattığı protestoların yüz binlerce kişinin katıldığı bir toplumsal harekete dönüşmesinin ardından, bugün hükümetin güvenlik politikaları, polis müdahaleleri ve sendikaların talepleri ülkenin gündemindeki yerini korudu.


17 Ekim’de ülke genelinde düzenlenen 110 gösteriye katılım, sendikalara göre 800 bine, İçişleri Bakanlığı’na göre 550 bine ulaştı. Yürüyüşlerin büyük bölümü barışçıl geçerken Paris, Marsilya, Lyon, Toulouse ve Limoges başta olmak üzere çeşitli kentlerde çatışmalar, yağma ve kundaklama olayları yaşandı.


İçişleri Bakanı Laurent Nuñez’in bugün yaptığı açıklamaya göre, gözaltı sayısı 2 bini, yaralanan polis, jandarma ve itfaiye personelinin sayısı ise 600’ü aştı.


Fransa: Öğrenci isyanı toplumsallaşıyor, 800 bin insan Cumartesi sokaktaydı


Bugün  00:34


Gözaltı bilançosu büyüyor


17 Ekim akşamı yaklaşık 400 olarak açıklanan gözaltı sayısı, gece boyunca süren polis operasyonlarının ardından hızla yükseldi.


Paris Emniyet Müdürlüğü’ne göre yalnızca başkentte 855 kişi gözaltına alındı. Yetkililer bu sayının tek bir gösteri günü için olağanüstü yüksek olduğunu belirtti.


Nuñez, kamu binalarına yönelik saldırılarla mağaza yağmalarından “aşırı sol” olarak nitelendirdiği grupları sorumlu tuttu.


Hükümet cezaları ağırlaştırmak istiyor


Başbakan Sébastien Lecornu, gösterilerin ardından yaptığı açıklamalarda şiddet olaylarına karışanların daha ağır yaptırımlarla karşılaşacağını söyledi.


Hükümet, gösteriler sırasında ortaya çıkan maddi zararın sorumlularından tahsil edilmesini amaçlayan ve kamuoyunda “zarar veren öder” (casseurs-payeurs) adıyla bilinen yasa tasarısının görüşmelerini hızlandırıyor.


Senatonun resmî takvimine göre tasarı 27 ve 28 Ekim’de Genel Kurul gündemine gelecek. Düzenleme, kamusal alandaki şiddet ve tahribat nedeniyle ortaya çıkan zararların sorumlularından karşılanmasına ilişkin yeni hükümler öngörüyor.


Lecornu, Adalet Bakanı Didier Migaud’un yarın (19 Ekim) başsavcılarla bir araya gelerek gözaltılar ve soruşturmalar kapsamında uygulanacak adli politikaları değerlendireceğini de açıkladı.


Cumhurbaşkanı Emmanuel Macron ise bu akşam Fransa saatiyle 20.00’da (TSİ 21.00) halka seslenecek. Élysée Sarayı, Macron’un konuşmasından önce hükümet üyeleriyle bir güvenlik toplantısı yapacağını duyurdu.


CGT: “Hükümet toplumsal taleplere yanıt vermeli”


Hükümetin güvenlik ve cezalandırma odaklı açıklamalarına karşı Genel Emek Konfederasyonu (CGT), 17 Ekim gösterilerinin geniş katılımını hatırlatarak toplumsal taleplerin gündeme alınmasını istedi.


CGT, yaklaşık 800 bin kişinin katıldığını belirttiği eylemlerde öğrencilerin eğitim koşullarının yanı sıra alım gücündeki düşüş, hayat pahalılığı, emekli aylıkları ve kamu hizmetlerine ayrılan kaynakların yetersizliğinin de protesto edildiğini vurguladı.


Halkın kitlesel ve barışçıl biçimde dile getirdiği taleplere ısrarla kulak tıkayan hükümet, bugün şiddetin tırmanmasından siyasi olarak sorumludur.

–CGT, 17 Ekim 2026


CGT, hükümete öğrenci ve çalışan sendikalarıyla müzakere çağrısı yaparken, gösterilere katılımı engelleyen polis müdahalelerine de karşı çıktı.


5 Kasım’da ülke çapında grev


Fransa’da sendikalar, hükümetin sertleşen güvenlik politikalarına karşın toplumsal taleplerini gündemde tutmayı sürdürüyor.


CGT’nin yanı sıra Fransız Demokratik Emek Konfederasyonu (CFDT), İşçi Gücü (FO), Birleşik Sendikalar Federasyonu (FSU), Ulusal Özerk Sendikalar Birliği (UNSA) ve Dayanışma Sendikaları Birliği (Solidaires), 5 Kasım'da kamu ve özel sektör çalışanlarının katılımıyla yeni grev ve gösteriler düzenlemeyi planlıyor.


Sendikalar, ücretlerin ve emekli aylıklarının artırılmasını, kamu hizmetlerine daha fazla kaynak ayrılmasını ve hükümetin 2027 bütçesindeki kemer sıkma politikalarından vazgeçmesini talep ediyor.


Lise öğrencileri açısından ise öğretmen açığının giderilmesi, kalabalık sınıfların azaltılması, okulların fiziki koşullarının iyileştirilmesi ve yükseköğretime erişimde eşitlik talepleri gündemdeki yerini koruyor.


Kaynaklar: AFP, Associated Press, CGT, Le Monde, Reuters

title: “No Kings” Shifts Focus to Midterms With Early Voting Day of Action
content:
Over 5 million ballots have been cast, according to an estimate, as Trump faces a historic low in approval ratings.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

Organizers launched more than 2,500 No Kings events across all 50 states and the District of Columbia Saturday, this time focusing their efforts on the midterm elections.

From roadside rallies to letter-writing campaigns and protest songs, this round of demonstrations aimed to get people to the polls early.

In the bustling and diverse neighborhood of Jackson Heights, Queens, where Bangladeshi street vendors whip up fuska — crispy, potato-filled shells — and Mexican taquerías serve up al pastor and carne asada, volunteers gathered at a popular local restaurant called The Queensboro. The organizers are part of the Jackson Heights chapter of Indivisible, one of the many grassroots organizations that have made No Kings demonstrations happen.

Arianne Mayer, 49, cofounded the chapter about two years ago after President Donald Trump was elected to his second term. On this “No Kings: Vote Early Day of Action”, she hands out pens and paper to volunteers to write letters to voters in battleground states, encouraging them to get out and cast their ballots as early as possible.

“The practice of mobilization of bodies is really helpful, especially in New York City, where you’re trying to mobilize many thousands of people,” Mayer said. “When you see those thousands of marches, you understand people everywhere are not OK with this, but it’s nice to have a different approach for this event. ”

Mayer, like many people here, said she was deeply frustrated and “disgusted” by the presence of federal immigration agents targeting her neighbors. Many people also said the federal government is implementing increasingly authoritarian policies.

Since summer 2025, the No Kings movement has held multiple massive demonstrations across thousands of sites around the country, attracting millions of people to protest against what they consider to be an overreach of government under the Trump Administration.

This time around organizers shifted their focus, understanding that the midterm elections will determine which political party controls Congress. If it’s the Democrats, they could put up roadblocks to Trump’s agenda. Organizers are hoping the day of early voting could not only increase the pool of voters, but also ease the burden on poll workers on Nov. 3, Election Day.

Voting is in full swing across dozens of states, with over 5 million ballots cast, according to the University of Florida’s Election Lab. Trump faces a historic low in approval ratings.

In Minnesota folk musician Emmett Doyle took to a stage in downtown Minneapolis to perform Lluís Llach’s “L’Estaca,” written in the 1960s in protest of Francisco Franco’s dictatorship in Spain.

Doyle is one of 15 defendants facing federal felony conspiracy charges stemming from protests against U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement’s crackdown in Minnesota.

“When I was getting pulled out of my truck by federal agents a couple months ago, one of the first things I asked them was, ‘Hey, is this about the songs?’ And they told me, ‘No, it’s about resisting ICE,’” Doyle said to the crowd of about 1,000. “I told them, ‘Well, you’re going to have to arrest all of Minneapolis if you want to hit me for that.’”

Diane Komsky, 67, drove an hour to the No Kings protest in Sioux Falls, South Dakota, because of the “madness in the White House,” she said.

“I want to give peace a real chance for families in the United States,” she said.

Mark Lyons of Centennial, Colorado, said he hadn’t been involved in much political activism or organizing before last year. Saturday’s protest was his fourth No Kings event.

With the midterms approaching, Lyons is hopeful that Democrats will take control of Congress and “put all kinds of checks and balances” on the Trump administration.

“They’ve been stealing the country blind for the last two years,” he said. “There has to be accountability, and it can’t be business as usual.”

At an event in the nation’s capital, 25-year-old Octavia Clapp said using her right to vote especially matters as Trump attempts to wield authority over voting. The Trump administration has spent more than a year in court battles with dozens of states and voting rights groups seeking to force states to provide sensitive voter data and curb voting by mail.

title: Democratisation is not about imposing conditions
content:
Mehmet Uçum (Chief Adviser to the President and Deputy Chair of the Presidential Legal Policies Board) wrote an article about the process on 17 October. Judging by his remarks, Uçum appears to be acting as the spokesperson for a group seeking to undermine the process. He claims to advocate dialogue, yet he is trying to dictate terms to the Kurdish Freedom Movement. He seems to think he is intelligent and everyone else is a fool. The article Uçum wrote is precisely the kind of article that opponents of the process, those seeking to sabotage it, would write. If it reflects the views of Tayyip Erdoğan, whom he advises, the situation is even more serious and troubling. If that is the case, the government is attempting to lay the ideological groundwork for undermining the process. Tayyip Erdoğan has repeatedly said that the process is progressing well. If Mehmet Uçum wrote his article based on information received from the presidential palace, it means the process is not going well.


Even before the law approved on 18 August was enacted, government officials had said that the status of Kurdish People's Leader Abdullah Öcalan would change, that he would meet with various groups and that even those who would work alongside him would be able to visit Imrali. These commitments were made before the law was passed. Following its enactment, the deputy chair of the Justice and Development Party (AKP) parliamentary group publicly stated, in front of television cameras, that journalists and many others would be able to visit Imrali. However, more than two months have passed since the law was enacted, and there has been no change in the Kurdish People's Leader's status.


Mehmet Uçum believes that the Kurdish People's Leader can play a role in achieving negative peace, but not genuine peace, or what is known as positive peace. He also argues that freedom for Abdullah Öcalan cannot be demanded. Who could possibly believe that genuine peace can be achieved while the central figure in the peace process remains imprisoned? Did Devlet Bahçeli not say from the very beginning that, if Öcalan called on the organisation, he could address the DEM Party parliamentary group and fully exercise his right to hope? The right to hope envisages the possibility of release from prison. Does declaring that freedom for the Kurdish People's Leader cannot be demanded, contemplated or achieved not amount to announcing the end of this process?


The Kurdish People's Leader is the principal interlocutor in this process. However, the Kurdish Freedom Movement is also a key actor in putting the process into practice. This movement has consistently insisted that Öcalan must be able to work freely. It maintains that enabling him to work freely is the first step towards securing his freedom and that nothing can be achieved without it. Yet Mehmet Uçum tells those making this demand that what they are asking for will not happen. In doing so, he blocks every possibility of practical progress. One thing is clear: the way a people's or movement's leadership is treated reflects the way that people and their organisation are treated. The Kurdish People's Leader understands this very well. In this respect, Uçum's approach represents a new version of the policy pursued towards the Kurdish people for the past century.


Democratic participation is not possible under the existing laws and legal framework. The current laws allow people to be imprisoned for even the slightest expression of opposition. Those demanding the fundamental democratic rights of the Kurdish people are immediately imprisoned. This is also how the current government operates. Opportunities for democratic participation can only emerge through new legislation. After all, it was the existing laws that created this problem in the first place. What kind of reasoning suggests that people should enter the democratic political sphere without changing these laws? Such reasoning fails to understand the essence of the process. Or perhaps it views the process as a means of achieving an entirely different objective.


Mehmet Uçum has also used the concept of “ethnic politics”, a term Turkish state officials have employed for decades, indeed for a century, to deny Kurdish existence and fundamental rights. Demanding the fundamental rights that arise from the Kurdish people's very existence is not engaging in ethnic politics. It is the state and those who share Uçum's mentality who have been practising ethnic politics …

Author

: Nolan Peltz

Title

: Prison, Persecution, and Resistance

Subtitle

: The Case of Miguel Peralta

Date

Notes

:

Translated from Peltz, Nolan, “Prisión, persecución y resistencia. El caso de Miguel Peralta Betanzos”,

 Avispa Midia

, 29 January

Source

: Retrieved 10/19/2026 from https://www.patreon.com/bloodfruit/posts/prison-and-case-165958672


 Miguel Peralta, a community defender and anarchist, exited the Cuicatlán, Oaxaca prison more than six years ago. His original arrest happened on April 2015, and on October 2018 he was sentenced to 50 years in prison for two charges, one of homicide and another of attempted homicide.


 After an intense legal battle and political pressure, he managed to appeal the sentence. A year later, on October 14, 2019, after almost a month-long hunger strike, Peralta was finally absolved of all the charges and released from prison. In all, he spend a little under 4 years and six months behind bars due to fabricated charges brought against him.


 Miguel’s arrest came following a sociopolitical conflict that erupted into violence on December 14, 2014 in the Eloxochitlán de Flores Magón municipality in Oaxaca when the Community Assembly was attacked by a violent armed group headed by the petty warlord Manuel Zepeda Cortés. In the conflict that followed, two people lost their life and many were left injured. This attack, although headed and orchestrated by Manuel Zepeda, was used as a pretext to persecute members of the Community Assembly. Thirty five community members were initially charged in the case number 10/2015, and other charges were brought against other members later. Many community members, Miguel Peralta among them, ended up spending time behind bars and, although they are all free now, the persecution against the community members continues on, for more than ten years now.


 Miguel’s father, Pedro Peralta, had previously been detained on August 10, 2012 when he was taking part in communal work in Eloxochitlán de Flores Magón, Oaxaca. When he was apprehended, he was beaten and tortured. Pedro Peralta spent nearly three years in the Cuicatlán, Oaxaca prison, even spending some weeks alongside his son behind bars before being released on July 30, 2015.


 Behind the repression and criminalization in Eloxochitlán, there are direct ties between the local petty warlords and State power, including the weaponizing of the legal system against the community defenders. Local petty warlord, Manuel Zepeda, municipal president from 2011 and 2013, used municipal funds to enrich himself, and also extracted stone, sand, and gravel from the community river, materials that furnished his stores and which he in turn sold to carry out municipal projects. When community members raised their voice against his authoritarianism, the theft of community funds, and the ecological destruction of the community, he resorted to flagrant violence.


 His daughter, Elisa Zepeda Lagunas, used the 2014 conflict as a political springboard, climbing up the hierarchy of public authority using the vocabulary of victimhood. She placed herself as municipal president in the 2017–2019 term before abandoning the position to run as local deputy for the MORENA political party. Since then, she’s been a local deputy, president of the Oaxaca Congress during the LXIV Congress Session, Secretary of Women under the Salomón Jara government, and presently, serves a second term as a local deputy for the MORENA political party. Thanks to her political contacts and power, she has mobilized the repressive State apparatus against members of the community.


 Indomitable Resistance


 Miguel Peralta’s criminalization, incarceration, and persecution is the aftermath of his struggle for the autonomy and land defense of his community, Eloxochitlán de Flores Magón. Miguel has been an important voice in the condemnation against natural resource extraction and the petty warlord-ism of the Zepeda Lagunas family. He has also been an important voice in the struggle for the community’s autonomy and self-determination against the power grab of petty warlords and political parties alike. The criminalization against him is a direct outcome of his resistance and, despite this, it has not …

author: Shireen Akram-Boshar
title: Mississippi Attorney General Declares Police Shooting of 1-Year-Old “Justified”
content:
The shooting is part of a pattern of racist police violence against Black residents of Senatobia, Mississippi.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

Mississippi’s attorney general announced Monday that the police shooting of 1-year-old Kohen Wiley in June “was justified.”

“Today, the Office of the Attorney General announced it has completed the review of a June 14, 2026, incident in Senatobia involving one officer with the Senatobia Police Department,” the statement from the office of Mississippi’s attorney general, Lynn Fitch, said. “In this incident, the Attorney General’s Office found the use of force was justified.” The review was undertaken by Mississippi’s Bureau of Investigation.

In mid-June, police in Senatobia — a town in northwest Mississippi, 40 miles south of Memphis, Tennessee — shot and killed 1-year-old Kohen in a car outside of the local Walmart. Police claim they were responding to a shoplifting call, and pursued Kohen’s mother and the friend she was with before shooting at their car. Kohen’s mother, Vallesiya Wiley, has said that no shoplifting took place. Neither she nor her friend have been charged with shoplifting.

Vallesiya also stated as recently as this month that she has never been interviewed by investigators.

Ben Crump, a prominent civil rights attorney representing Kohen’s family, stated that police have still not released video footage of the shooting.

“How can anyone accept that conclusion when Kohen’s family and the public still have not been allowed to see the body-camera footage?” Crump said in a statement on Monday.

“If the footage supports the state’s decision, release it. We will not stop fighting until this family gets the truth.”

Crump has also said that autopsy evidence indicates that the 1-year-old was shot from the side of the car, contradicting claims by the police that the car was heading towards, and aiming to hit, the police.

The Mississippi Legislative Black Caucus (MLBC) also condemned the attorney general’s announcement that the officer’s use of force was justified, and demanded the release of evidence supporting the decision, as well as a public explanation and an independent review of the police department and its practices.

“Kohen Wiley was a baby. He posed no threat. He deserved protection, and he deserved a future. His family is owed more than a conclusion. They are owed the evidence, the explanation and the truth,” said MLBC Chairman Rep. Kabir Karriem. “Attorney General Fitch cannot reasonably expect public confidence in a decision the public has not been given the evidence to evaluate. Announcing that a review is complete does not fulfill the responsibility to explain how a police encounter ended with a baby dead.”

Throughout June, Senatobia residents protested Kohen’s killing — and have said that his shooting is part of a pattern of police violence against Black residents in Senatobia, which is about 40 percent Black. Senatobia also has a high poverty rate of 26.4 percent.

Last year, a Senatobia officer violently arrested a Black woman and threatened her with a Taser in the same Walmart parking lot where Kohen was shot, claiming that she had unjustifiably parked in a handicap parking spot. In 2023, a Senatobia police officer arrested a 10-year-old Black boy for urinating outside.

In September, Senatobia fired its police chief after reporting by Mississippi Today and The New York Times revealed that he regularly used racist slurs and expletives against Black residents. He has been replaced by Angelica Maze, an interim police chief who is Black — but the replacement is unlikely to rectify issues of police violence and racism in Senatobia.

Ben Crump decried the police department in his comments Monday. “This is a department whose chief was fired after reports of racial slurs in his text messages, and whose officer faced a complaint alleging a racially offensive remark two days before he shot Kohen,” he said in his statement.

Two days after Kohen’s killing in June, protests broke out across Senatobia at the City Hall and at the Walmart where he had been shot. Police deployed teargas against the protesters. A later march at the end of June demanded the police department release the footage. The police department has yet to do so.

author: Γιάννης Βολιάτης
title: Περιστατικό ακραίας αστυνομικής βίας απέναντι σε μέλος της El Chef και ακόμη δυο άτομα
content:
Περιστατικό ακραίας αστυνομικής βίας απέναντι σε μέλος της El Chef και ακόμη δυο άτομα


Δημοσιεύουμε την καταγγελία που μας απέστειλαν από την συλλογική κουζίνα El Chef σχετικά με περιστατικό ακραίας αστυνομικής βίας απέναντι σε μέλος της δομής καθώς και σε ακόμη δυο φιλικά του πρόσωπα. Την καταγγελία συνυπογράφουν επίσης το Δίκτυο για τα Κοινωνικά και Πολιτικά Δικαιώματα και το Στέκι μεταναστών Αθήνας.


“Την Κυριακή 18 Οκτώβρη το μέλος της Συλλογικής κουζίνας El chef J. R, καθώς και δύο φίλες του, γαλλικής καταγωγής και οι τρεις, έπεσαν θύματα ακραίας αστυνομικής βίας από την διμοιρία που στρατοπεδεύει στα Εξάρχεια στην συμβολή των οδών Θεμιστοκλέους και Σολωμού.


Ο λόγος του άγριου ξυλοδαρμού ήταν προφανώς το πανό που είχαν μαζί τους, καθώς νωρίτερα είχαν συμμετάσχει σε κινητοποίηση αλληλεγγύης στην νεολαιίστικη – λαϊκή εξέγερση στην Γαλλία.


Σύμφωνα με αυτόπτες μάρτυρες οι ένστολοι δολοφόνοι πάταγαν τον σύντροφο μας στο στήθος και στον λαιμό παρα τις διαμαρτυρίες του ότι δεν μπορούσε να ανασάνει, ενώ την μία από τις δύο γυναίκες τη χτύπαγαν ακόμη και στο υπηρεσιακό όχημα που έκανε την μεταφορά τους.


Και τα τρία άτομα συνελήφθησαν και αντιμετωπίζουν βαριές κατηγορίες, ενώ κρατούνται μέχρι την δίκη που έχει οριστεί για την Τετάρτη 21 Οκτώβρη.


Δεν είναι η πρώτη φορά που αντιμετωπίζουμε ακραία αστυνομική βία στην γειτονιά μας. Ειδικά η συγκεκριμένη διμοιρία επιδίδεται συστηματικά σε παρενοχλήσεις και αναίτιους ξυλοδαρμούς πολιτών.


Στην περίπτωση του συντρόφου μας και των δύο γυναικών ο βασικός λόγος ήταν προφανώς το πανό που είχαν μαζί τους. Τα ένστολα σκυλιά της εξουσίας μισούν ότι θυμίζει εξέγερση είτε αυτή γίνεται στην Γαλλία, είτε στην Αλβανία, είτε σε οποιαδήποτε γωνιά αυτού του κόσμου.


Ως Συλλογική κουζίνα El chef καλούμε όσους ήταν παρόντες στο περιστατικό και το έχουν καταγράψει σε βίντεο να επικοινωνήσουν στην σελίδα της κουζίνας. Ήδη πολλοί αυτόπτες μάρτυρες έχουν δηλώσει την διαθεσιμότητα τους να καταθέσουν ως μάρτυρες στο δικαστήριο.


Να μπει ένα τέλος στην αστυνομική βία στα Εξάρχεια.


Κάτω τα χέρια από τους αγωνιστές.


Στους δρόμους της Γαλλίας γράφεται Ιστορία, νίκη στους λαούς και την ελευθερία.

author: ACG
title: REBELLION IN ALBANIA
content:
On October 15, the third day of the uprising and after 138 days of peaceful daily demonstrations, the streets of Tirana were under the control of students. A small student demonstration joined the protest, demanding better educational conditions. The brutal police violence against this group turned out to be the last straw – it prompted first the students, then the rest of the population, and now high school students to speak out against police brutality and demand the resignation of the Prime Minister, the government, and the complete dismantling of their entire system.


Protesters demanding the fall of the government engaged in fierce clashes with the police. Thousands of students boycotted classes and took to the streets alongside thousands of citizens from the “Flamingo Revolution” movement to protest against a corrupt system and its primary representative, the country’s Prime Minister, Edi Rama, and demanding the latter’s resignation. He has given protected natural areas to Trump’s daughter and son-in-law, Ivanka Trump and Jared Kushner, for the construction of a luxury hotel complex.


During the clashes, which lasted late into the night, the buildings housing the Ministry of Education, the Ministry of Economy and Finance, the Ministry of Justice, and the Constitutional Court—as well as a police station and several bank branches—were attacked and set on fire.


The parliament, heavily guarded by police forces, was also targeted. As a result, parliament was suspended. The Socialist Party headquarters was also attacked.


The unrest spread to a number of other cities. In Shkodër, confrontations with the police occurred during an attempt to storm the municipal building. In Korçë, clashes erupted when police tried to clear an occupation at a high school; subsequently, students targeted the Regional Directorate of Education building, smashing its windows. Clashes with the police and arrests also took place in Elbasan.


Rama claimed on Friday, October 16

th

, that foreign powers were behind the unrest. The following day, he refused to resign. Frightened by the mass unrest, he has made some concessions: 2,000 interest-free loans for young people, students and certain groups of employees, another 2,000 loans with an interest rate of three percent and a subsidy of half the rent for 3,000 apartments.


There have been 167 arrests, with 388 others facing criminal proceedings. The protests are continuing.

Les écrans, explique-t-il, feraient des élèves des « zombies », que leur téléphone, « stupéfiant-image », arracherait au monde. Leur confiscation aurait ainsi fait l'effet d'un électrochoc. Privés d'écran, les porcelets auraient enfin levé les yeux au ciel pour y découvrir leur misérable existence, et avec elle, ce que les adultes font de leur monde.


L'hypothèse est sans doute bienveillante. Le professeur précise qu'il écrit « sans aucune agressivité ni mépris envers mes élèves, que j'aime et apprécie ». On le croit, et c'est bien le problème. Le berger peut parfaitement aimer son troupeau : il n'en reste pas moins un berger. Or en matière de pouvoir pastoral, la sollicitude est parfois pire que le mépris.


Il faut en effet comprendre ce que cette hypothèse suppose : qu'avant la confiscation de leur téléphone, les lycéen

Car de porcherie, il est bien question, mais pas de celle du groin dans les réseaux. Ce sont les rats, les chiottes bouchés, les canicules dans les préfabriqués. author: Fundi Skweyiya-Gushu
title: Africa’s Cybersecurity Gap Is Not a Treaty Problem. It Is a Readiness Problem
content:
Africa’s digital economy is expanding faster than its ability to protect it.

INTERPOL’s African Cyberthreat Assessment Report 2026

, drawing on information from 36 countries, found that artificial intelligence was involved in 55 per cent of reported cybercrimes across the continent. Reported losses rose from $192 million in 2024 to $484 million, while 72 per cent of surveyed countries reported scam centres operating within their borders.


The figures expose a growing vulnerability. Africa’s digital transformation is creating economic opportunities but also expanding the terrain on which criminals operate. The question is whether African institutions can respond collectively when attacks cross borders, exploit financial systems and use AI to target victims at scale.


Morocco Cybersecurity Week

, held in Rabat from 12 to 14 October 2026, placed regional cooperation firmly on the agenda. The emphasis was appropriate. Yet Africa’s challenge extends beyond convening officials and announcing strategies. It is making institutions cooperate effectively under pressure.


Africa does not lack legal frameworks.

The African Union Convention on Cyber Security and Personal Data Protection

, known as the

Malabo Convention,

 entered into force in June 2023 after years of delays. Morocco, meanwhile acceded to the

Council of Europe’s Budapest Convention on Cybercrime

 in 2018 and signed its

Second Additional Protocol on electronic evidence

 in 2022.


These instruments provide important foundations for criminal investigations, data protection and cross-border cooperation. But legal commitments cannot, on their own, ensure that investigators obtain evidence quickly, financial institutions exchange actionable intelligence or police services coordinate an effective response.


Cybercrime crosses institutional boundaries. A fraudulent transaction may involve a mobile-money provider, a bank, a telecommunications company, a cryptocurrency exchange and digital infrastructure spread across several jurisdictions. Each holds part of the evidence. When requests are delayed or responsibilities are unclear, investigators lose valuable time while criminals move money and erase their tracks. African institutions must therefore measure cooperation by what they can accomplish together, not by the number of agreements they endorse.


There is evidence that coordinated action works.

INTERPOL’s Operation Serengeti 2.0

, conducted between June and August 2025, brought together law-enforcement authorities from 18 African countries and the United Kingdom. It resulted in 1,209 arrests, the dismantling of 11,432 malicious infrastructures and the recovery of $97.4 million. Private-sector partners contributed intelligence and technical expertise.


The lesson is not that treaties are unnecessary. Investigations still require lawful powers, admissible evidence and safeguards. Rather, Serengeti demonstrates the value of shared objectives, established channels and institutions equipped to act on intelligence together.


This is where Africa should look beyond calls by some of its leaders for a continental equivalent of

NATO’s Article 5

. On 19 May 2025, Rwandan President Paul Kagame made these remarks in his keynote address at the inaugural

International Security Conference on Africa (ISCA)

, held at the Kigali Convention Centre. Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni has also raised related questions at the

African Defence Chiefs Conference on Military Operations

. While these calls reflect growing interest in collective African security, NATO’s experience offers a more specific lesson for cybersecurity governance.

NATO recognises cyberspace as an operational domain

, and significant cyberattacks may, in certain circumstances, constitute an armed attack. However, invoking collective defence is not automatic: each case is assessed individually by the North Atlantic Council.


For African governments confronting cyber-enabled fraud, ransomware and attacks on public services, the more immediate lesson is not collective retaliation. It is collective preparedness.


Consider

NATO’s annual Locked Shields exercise

, organised by its

Cooperative Cyber Defence Centre of Excellence

. The 2026 exercise brought together approximately 4,000 participants from 41 countries to defend simulated digital systems against complex attacks. Participants tested technical responses while confronting the coordination challenges that emerge during a crisis. The …

author: Andy Mannix
title: Election Officials Fear Trump Has Compromised Cybersecurity Agency
content:
Critics say the administration has undermined an agency key to protecting election infrastructure ahead of the midterms.

Critics say the administration has undermined an agency key to protecting election infrastructure ahead of the midterms.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

A few months into President Donald Trump’s second term, political appointees at the Department of Homeland Security made an unusual request of its agency focused on cybersecurity: Secretly acquire a voting machine and hack it.

The appointees wanted the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency to procure the machine, examine it and report back the findings so they could be given to the White House, according to two former administration officials with knowledge of the request.

The proposition was shocking to CISA’s career staffers, according to one of the former officials. CISA typically worked to thwart hackers. Moreover, the agency had been directed not to alert the voting machine company if it uncovered flaws, contrary to its standard practices. The request made the CISA employees fear they were being asked to take part in political interference.

“My thought was they could keep it in their back pocket to invalidate any [election] results they don’t like,” one of the former officials said. “This goes against everything CISA represents.”

The CISA employees repeatedly told the political appointees that their request was impossible, in part because the agents capable of pulling off such an operation had just been laid off by Elon Musk’s Department of Government Efficiency initiative. The appointees eventually stopped pressing CISA.

Though not acted on, the request shows how the Trump administration has tried to use the agency for its own ends while draining it of resources for one of its critical missions: protecting the nation’s voting systems.

In Trump’s second term, his administration has laid off or pushed out more than 1,000 CISA employees, shrinking the agency by about one-third. The president’s 2027 budget proposal would reduce funding for the agency by another $700 million, which could necessitate 900 additional layoffs.

In response, Democratic lawmakers have called for an investigation into CISA’s ability to do its job and demanded answers as to why federal funds are not being used to support election security as directed by Congress.

Since Trump signed the CISA Act in 2018, the agency has worked with state authorities and voting machine vendors to help protect election infrastructure from cyberattacks. During Trump’s second term, though, CISA has abandoned much of this work. Several state election authorities said the agency provided them no assistance — and no explanation for its absence — during the most critical planning stages for the upcoming midterms.

“There is a difference between deprioritizing and being nonexistent,” said Ryan Macias, an election technology and cybersecurity expert who has worked as a consultant for CISA. In 2025 and through mid-September 2026 — when the bulk of preparations for the election typically would have been completed — “they were nonexistent. Literally nonexistent.”

While Trump has repeatedly warned that America’s elections are vulnerable to hacking, in some cases repeating disproven claims, experts said his administration is undermining the federal government’s role in helping secure them.

Though CISA re-emerged in September with a last-minute security plan for the election, some state officials told ProPublica they fear that what is left of the agency has been compromised by a conspiracy-obsessed presidential administration. In recent months, in reviving debunked theories about the 2020 election, the Trump administration has declassified troves of records, including sensitive material that state officials provided to CISA. Some state authorities said they no longer trusted the administration enough to share information with CISA, a key to the agency’s success in past elections.

“They’ve violated the entire premise of that information-sharing relationship,” said one former high-ranking federal cybersecurity official who now advises state governments on national security. “There’s no fucking way they’re ever going to give any information to CISA. And it’s unclear if they ever will in the future.”

author: Chiara Miraglia
title: CPDP 20th international conference
content:
CPDP (“Computers, Privacy and Data Protection”) is a non-profit platform founded in 2007 by research groups at the Vrije Universiteit Brussel, the Université de Namur, and Tilburg University, later joined by INRIA and the Fraunhofer Institute for Systems and Innovation Research. Today, CPDP is carried by 20 academic centres of excellence from the EU, the US, and beyond. Based in Brussels, CPDP has become a world-leading multidisciplinary conference, convening a global community across research, policy, practice, civil society, and technology to engage with cutting-edge developments in privacy and data protection.

Organiser: 20 academic centres of excellence from the EU, the US, and beyond

The governance of the digital world is fragmented and faces difficult challenges. Technologies that shape our lives develop faster than the means – or even the will – to regulate them for the protection of privacy and other fundamental rights.

What We Owe the Future invites reflection on this contribution. Building on this, it looks ahead to what the future demands of us. What will the next twenty or more years need, and how should we help to build it? What do we owe to those who will inherit the world we shape today? Which principles must endure, which protections cannot be bargained away even when the pressure to relax them is strong, and what responsibilities do the custodians of the present bear towards the future?

The year 2027 marks the twentieth anniversary of CPDP. For twenty years, the conferences have stood at the forefront of efforts to understand and contribute to improving the prospect for governance in this fast-moving digital age. As a community of academics, regulators and policymakers, civil society, industry and legal practitioners, CPDP has cast a bright light on issues, practices and rules, and has offered a forum for debate and the exchange of knowledge across a global landscape. What is worth celebrating is not the annual conference itself, but twenty years of bringing this community together and sustaining it through a period of momentous change.

The people whose lives will extend far into that future should help to design the way forward. CPDP 2027 therefore launches CPDP 20: The Next Generation, which include a team of early-career researchers from across disciplineswho will co-curate the programme and help identify its most pressing questions. This team will identify connections across fields and help to explore issues on the horizon, bringing knowledge and fresh perspectives to bear on developments and their likely consequences that will need to be addressed by policy, governance and other action.

author: Dulce Amor Rodriguez
title: Social media ban may exclude children instead of protecting them, advocates warn
content:
Child rights advocates have warned that a proposed social media ban could restrict children’s access to information, education, expression, and participation without addressing the perpetrators and platforms responsible for online abuse.


The warning followed the Senate’s approval of Senate Bill No. 2424, or the proposed Safe Media Access and Responsible Technology for Kids in Digital Spaces (SMART KIDS) Act, on third and final reading on October 8.


The Senate approved the measure by a vote of 16-1, with no abstentions, advancing a proposal sponsored by Sen. Robinhood Padilla that would restrict minors’ access to digital services classified as high-risk.


Salinlahi Alliance for Children’s Concerns argued that the government must protect children from online exploitation, grooming, bullying, and other forms of digital harm without treating their access to digital spaces as the problem.


“Banning children from social media does not make the internet safe. It impedes children’s right to participation while the perpetrators remain,” said Teacher Elle Buntag, Salinlahi secretary general.


The group warned that restricting children’s access would not, by itself, establish whether platforms would respond more effectively to abuse or whether authorities would investigate and prosecute offenders more consistently.


Instead, Salinlahi called on the government to strengthen investigations into online sexual abuse and exploitation, require platforms to detect and remove abusive content, improve reporting and rescue mechanisms, and provide survivors with psychosocial and legal support.


“If the government’s answer to online abuse is simply to remove children from the platform, then we are asking children to bear the burden of a problem created by perpetrators and enabled by weak systems,” Buntag said.


The group maintained that children have rights to information, expression, education, participation, and connection in digital spaces, and urged the government to protect these rights while making online environments safer.


“The state must not confuse restricting children’s access with protecting children. Protection means making the digital spaces they inhabit safe and holding those who exploit them accountable,” Salinlahi said.


Different approaches


The debate over the Senate measure centers partly on whether an under-18 restriction offers a proportionate response to online harm or whether lawmakers should adopt age-specific safeguards.


Sen. Risa Hontiveros, the sole senator who voted against the measure, argued for a more targeted approach that would allow older adolescents to use social media with adequate safety measures.


Hontiveros had proposed restricting access for children under 13 while allowing those aged 13 to 18 to use social media if platforms provided adequate safeguards.


The Child Rights Network Philippines’ explainer questioned the basis for setting the minimum age at 18, and urged lawmakers to examine the evidence behind a blanket restriction before limiting children’s digital rights.


Sen. Win Gatchalian, a co-author and co-sponsor of the Senate measure, argued that aligning the age threshold with the legal definition of a child under existing laws would make enforcement more consistent and easier for authorities, according to the network’s explainer.


Padilla, meanwhile, said lawmakers could amend the measure after assessing its effects, and cited other countries’ experiences with restrictions and subsequent policy reviews, the explainer said.


The Child Rights Network challenged the idea that ease of enforcement should determine the age threshold, arguing that lawmakers must also consider the measure’s effects on children’s rights and daily lives.


The debate therefore goes beyond whether authorities can enforce an age restriction and asks whether the restriction would protect children effectively without imposing unnecessary limits on their participation.


Beyond entertainment


Child rights advocates said children use social media for more than entertainment, including research, learning, creative work, communication, and maintaining relationships.


The Child Rights Network noted that children also use digital platforms to connect with friends and peers and to communicate with parents working overseas.


Salinlahi argued that the government must account for these uses when designing online safety policies, rather than assuming that removing children from platforms would resolve the …

author: April Holcombe
title: Chinese youth in a very shit time of their lives
content:
Certain quarters of the internet are filling with content lauding contemporary China as an advanced, anti-imperialist, even socialist society. Its unrivalled high-speed rail network and its continued use of Communist jargon have encouraged some disillusioned Western youth to declare themselves in “a very Chinese time of my life”.

State-of-the-art infrastructure and Communist iconography have obvious appeal to a section of people living in decaying, imperialist and increasingly far-right-controlled Western capitalism. But there is a big difference between Instagram China, a Potemkin country showcased by influencers at the invitation of the tourism bureau and marketed to disillusioned Western youth, and the real China, a nuclear superpower ruled by bureaucrat-businessmen.  

Young Chinese people on social media—students, workers and the unemployed—use a very different kind of language than influencers do. Theirs is the language of alienation, exploitation and oppression in a society every bit as capitalist as our own.

“Involution”: an obscure word for a common problem

Ever heard of “involution”? Me neither. This obscure academic term, translated into Chinese (内卷

neijuan

), has entered common parlance among young people trapped in the country’s hypercompetitive economy. Literally meaning “inwardly curling”, anthropologists repurposed the term to describe activities that increase in complexity but lead nowhere. Chinese youth decided it captured their social predicament: instructed to work ever harder to stay ahead of their peers, they end up doing much more without being any better off.

Neijuan

describes many things: the gruelling hours at Big Tech companies; the notoriously competitive university entrance examinations; the apps pushing food delivery workers to ride ever faster; and the impossible social media-influenced beauty standards. The second character is now used as a standalone verb, meaning “to work or try too hard”.

Many young people who reject the

neijuan

 rat race opt instead to “lie flat” (躺平

tang ping

), a vibe somewhere between “quiet quitting” and “bedrotting”. The Ministry of State Security finds it deeply disturbing that anyone would want to lie flat, claiming in a Douyin (like TikTok) video that “an unnamed overseas organisation heavily funds ‘lying flat’ influencers, mass producing short videos promoting ‘anti-involution equals anti-exploitation’”.

Successive surveys show scepticism and pessimism rising sharply. In 2014, 62 percent of 10,000 respondents agreed that “effort is always rewarded in our country”; only 28 percent agreed a decade later. One-fifth blamed “the unfair economic system” for poverty in 2014; more than one-third did a decade later. Two-thirds agreed their families’ lives would improve from 2014-19, but less than half thought so for 2023-28.

“Graduation means unemployment”

University degrees once guaranteed well-paid government or tech jobs, providing the Communist Party’s dictatorship with a large, stable base of middle-class support. But now, often, “graduation means unemployment” (毕业即失业

biye ji shiye

). The gradual slowdown in economic growth has intensified competition for entry-level positions (more than 600 people, for example, applied for one basic Beijing office job in November 2025). Stable employment has given way to job flux. “I have family members who, since the early 2000s, never lost their jobs”, labour researcher Kevin Lin told

Red Flag

. “Last year, my cousin was laid off for the first time. Then he struggled to find another job, got laid off again, and is on to his third job.”

Unemployment is roughly twice the official figure of 5.2 percent, according to estimates by economist Li Daokui. “There are roughly 24 million long-term discouraged unemployed people, which is highly unfavourable for social stability”, the Tsinghua University academic told the China Macroeconomic Forum in July. The youth unemployment rate, officially hitting 17.9 percent that same month, has not included students since it soared past 25 percent in 2024, and hides a vast pool of underemployed youth working as little as one hour per week.

For the first time, the Communist Party’s most recent five-year plan includes no job-creation target. On the other hand, the government has a very clear target of 70 percent AI adoption across key industries by next year, inciting fears of layoffs among many IT workers. “I still can’t shake the feeling that I’m getting closer to being …

title: Hatimoğulları'ndan Halk TV'ye dayanışma ziyareti: "Basını sansürlemekten vazgeçin"
content:
DEM Parti Eş Genel Başkanı Tülay Hatimoğulları, Parti Sözcüsü Ayşegül Doğan ve beraberindeki heyet, kayyum atanan Halk TV’nin Ankara temsilciliğine destek ziyaretinde bulundu.

Ziyaret sonrası açıklama yapan Hatimoğulları, kayyum atamasını kınadığını vurgulayarak şöyle konuştu:

"Heyetimizle birlikte sabahleyin aldığımız haber üzerine hızla buraya geldik. İstanbul'daki gelişmeleri takip ediyoruz. Halk TV'ye bir şafak operasyonuyla yüzlerce polisin baskın yapması asla kabul edilebilir bir şey değil. Kayyum rejimi bu ülkede parça parça tesis edildi. Belediyeler üzerinden başladı ve artık Türkiye'de kayyum atanmayan hiçbir şey kalmadı. Ticari kurumlardan tutalım da üniversitelere kadar ve bundan şu anda en çok muzdarip olan, gerçekten Türkiye'deki basın yayın kuruluşlarıdır, organlarıdır. Bunu kabul etmek mümkün değil. Halk TV'ye yapılan bu saldırıyı bir kez daha burada sizlerin huzurunda kınıyoruz.

Bir televizyonu yüzlerce polisle basmak demek, Türkiye'yi çok karanlık bir dehlize doğru hızla sürüklemek demektir ve biz buna defaatle tanıklık ettik. Bundan önce TELE1'de oldu ve son zamanlarda birçok kanalda gerçekleşti. Bugün şayet televizyonun sahibiyle ilgili başlatılmak istenen bir soruşturma varsa bu soruşturma televizyon kanalı kapatılarak yapılmaz. Burada televizyon kanalının kendi yayın akışına devam etmesine hiçbir şekilde müdahale etmeksizin bir soruşturma açılacaksa o soruşturma açılır. Ortada bir suç varsa onun gereklilikleri yerine getirilir. Ama ne yazık ki Türkiye'de artık bir şeye bahane üretmek için, basını sansürlemek, ekranları karartmak, kalemleri ve tuşları susturmak için önceden hazırlanmış olan hikâyeleri ortaya atıp, gerekçeler oluşturup toplumu böyle ikna edeceğini sanıyor bu iktidar. Ama yanılıyor. Bugün Halk TV'nin Türkiye'de milyonlarca izleyicisi var. Dolayısıyla milyonlarca izleyiciyi bu anlamıyla bu iktidarın yanıltamayacağını, bu şekilde bir karartmanın üstünün örtülemeyeceğini bilmesi gerekiyor. Bugün Türkiye'de tepkiler çok büyük. Bugün insanların duygusal olarak da siyasi olarak da toplumsal olarak da tepkileri son derece büyük."

Hatimoğulları, günlerdir Türkiye'nin gündemini meşgul eden fon kriziyle ilgili TBMM'de komisyon görüşmelerinin başladığına işaret ederek, şöyle devam etti:

"Böylesi bir zamanda televizyon ekranlarının karartılması aynı zamanda bu yolsuzlukların, yüzyılın fon vurgununun üzerini örtmek anlamına da geliyor. Çünkü bu anlamıyla muhalif olan bütün basını susturmak, mevcut olan iktidarla ilgili tek bir negatif yorum yapılmasına izin vermemek demek, bu dünyada görülmemiş bir basın sansürüdür. Kendi işlenen suçların üzerini örtmek için yargı yoluna başvurarak Türkiye'deki çeşitli kurumların, iktidarın elindeki kurumların devreye sokulmasıyla bu operasyonların gerçekleşmesi asla kabul edilebilir değildir. Buradan bir kez daha diyoruz ki Halk TV ekranlarını karartamazsınız. Yurttaşın haber alma hakkına müdahale edemezsiniz. Basının özgürce haber yapma hakkını elinden alamazsınız. Burada yapılan bu operasyon, şafak operasyonu ve yayın akışına doğrudan müdahale asla kabul edilemez. Bu müdahale Türkiye'deki milyonlarca yurttaşın haber alma hakkına yapılmış bir müdahaledir. Biz Halk TV'yle ve bütün Halk TV ailesiyle dayanışma içindeyiz. Sonuna kadar basın özgürlüğü için mücadele edeceğiz.

İnsanların ya da kurumların sosyal medya erişim hesaplarının engellenmesi, bu susturmaya eklenen yeni halkalar. Neredeyse her gün yüzlerce X hesabının engellendiğine, sosyal medya erişim engelinin olduğuna tanıklık ediyoruz. Bunları biz asla kabul etmiyoruz. Türkiye böyle manzaraları askerî darbe dönemlerinde görmüştür. Bu kadar ekranın karartıldığını, Kenan Evren'le bütünleşmiş olan 'gazeteler makas makas' dediği, böyle formüle edilen anlayışa biz şimdi ne yazık ki en ağır şekliyle bir kez daha tanıklık ediyoruz. Halk TV ailesine bir kez daha geçmiş olsun dileklerimizi iletiyoruz. Dayanışma içinde olduğumuzu bir kez daha ifade ediyoruz ve iktidara buradan net olarak sesleniyoruz. Basını sansürlemekten artık vazgeçin. Türkiye'yi karanlık bir tabloya sürüklemekten artık vazgeçin. Basını özgür olmayan bir ülkede özgürlükten ve demokrasiden asla bahsedilemez. Dayanışma içinde olmaya devam edeceğiz.

Şimdi biz burada bu konuşmamızı gerçekleştirirken arkadaşlarım aktardı. Polis şimdi Halk TV'nin Ankara ofisinin kapısına gelmiş durumda. Kuvvetle muhtemel İstanbul'da yaptıkları aramanın, taramanın, hukuki olmayan, yeri olmayan aramanın, taramanın birini daha galiba burada gerçekleştirecekler …

author: Unknown
title: Tom Nomad - Toward an Army of Ghosts
content:
Author

: Tom Nomad

Title

: Toward an Army of Ghosts

Subtitle

: Immanence, Conflict and Crisis

Date

: 2017

Source

: PDF provided by publisher


 


 To Emma, the love of my life,

 you’re amazing and you always will be.


Introduction


 Almost four years ago, when

Master’s Tools

 was released, I had embarked on a distinct philosophical and political project, one that had grown out of the lessons from past experiences, and that did not have a determinate destination. This project was born as much out of frustration and failure as it was out of a certain conceptual interest and political desire. What was clear at the beginning of this project were the fundamental flaws in the categories we were using to make sense of action, and in our relationship to the space where action occurs. Paradoxical structures, fanciful notions, illusions, and utopian portrayals of our social and political milieu formed the basis of a political practice that was as much separated from the terrain of activity as were the liberals that we decried. Clearly we needed to at least throw out the latencies of the activist era, which we were discussing. But, for all the pages written about this—the problem of activism, the problems of conceptually-driven conflictual practice—all too often we seemed to be replicating the same categories in our attempts at transcendence. This current book is not some attempt to determine the way out of the morass of activism and ideology; it merely points out where some sparks may reside.

Master’s Tools

 is largely a discussion of immediate questions surrounding tactics; on some level this is a companion text. Some of the ideas will seem familiar to those who have read other writings of mine, but what my earlier writing has not focused on is the larger conceptual context at the base of my previously published works. This has led to misunderstanding by some, and problematic readings by others—some going as far as to retreat into liberal concepts of the rejection of militarism as a form of superficial rejection. I hope that this text clears some of the air, and illuminates a different point of perspective on these earlier works. Though there will be some things in common (the structure of the state, the relationship of logistics to the collection of actions that we term the police) the structure of the discourse here functions in a different mode and exists for a different purpose.


 These texts exist in relation to fundamentally different, yet intertwined, forms of life and tempos of existence. Previous texts were responses to an immediate question, one that was relevant when they were written. Specifically, they tried to articulate and address the failure of the tactics and methods that we were deploying. This mode of being was at a frenzied pace, with hectic risks, rewards, and activity. It was full of late night meetings, large distances traveled, and complicities formed: a life of immediacy. This formed a project to produce and distribute materials related to specific questions, first to a small group of people within direct proximity, which then leaked out into a wider, but still self-contained readership, and finally was compiled into

Master’s Tools

 and became one of the foundations for the journal,

Insurgencies

. It was to cut a line between the current approaches of the time, which were firmly rooted in activism, and address questions relevant to that space, while at the same time critiqueing that paradigm and pointing out some possibilities of escape.


 The text that you hold, on the other hand, reflects the time in between, a mode of life constructed around study, quiet music, and intimately engaged conversations, stepping back, looking beyond reactionary polemics on some immediate question, and forming foundations to think about the questions themselves. The second project, begun concurrently to the first and proceeding in parallel, was to articulate the grounding for

Master’s Tools

. Often relevant questions have emerged from those previously published writings, such as the rejection of utopianism, the rejection of activism, the rejection of political absolutism, morality, and the structure of absolute meaning. These questions are left open by much of the post-left literature written within the Western context. This book attempts to address a specific question—what are the implications of a distinctly materialist approach to the foundations of politics—without falling into the trap of …

title: Senate Democrats Demand Trump Administration Reveal Full Costs of Iran War
content:
“Americans deserve to know how much of their money is being burned on Trump’s war,” Sen. Elizabeth Warren said.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

Democratic members of the Senate Armed Services Committee are demanding that the Trump administration release official figures about the true economic costs of the war in Iran.

Lawmakers on that congressional committee were recently briefed about the war’s costs, but the administration has not made those figures public. Noting that the Congressional Budget Office estimated the war’s cost at $38 billion in September, Democrats are saying the White House should be forthright with the American people about updated numbers.

In an open letter sent to U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) commander Navy Admiral Brad Cooper, Democrats wrote that the “publicly disclosed costs of the war have already been tragic,” citing the fact that as many as 23 servicemembers have been killed and 861 have been wounded since the start of the conflict.

“Despite a lack of clarity and candor from [the Department of Defense], press reports of attacks, video footage, satellite images, and photos leaked to the media by active U.S. service members have painted a dire picture of U.S. bases and facilities damaged and destroyed by Iran,” the letter stated, adding that the war has also caused “significant damage to the U.S.’s critical infrastructure in the region.”

“The administration’s ongoing efforts to hide the true cost of this war are outrageous and unacceptable,” the Democrats’ letter stated. “DoD has repeatedly tried to cover up the truth about the number of service members hurt and killed since the war began and has not disclosed these deaths and injuries to the public in a timely manner.”

The letter-writers are calling for more transparency from the administration, and a response from CENTCOM by November 2.

In a post on X, Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-Massachusetts), a member of the Armed Services Committee, reiterated her and her colleagues’ call for more information.

“Americans deserve to know how much of their money is being burned on Trump’s war with Iran,” Warren said.

Estimates vary, but one examination of household expenses by Moody’s Analytics suggests that the average family’s costs have increased by $2,000 as a result of the war. Energy prices in particular have seen monumental increases, with regular grade gasoline costs going up by 45 percent since late February.

In addition to economic costs for the U.S., the war is having a tremendously negative impact on the region’s environment, with emissions from military activities contributing to the climate crisis, bombings worsening the effects of drought and water scarcity/access in the region, and pollution threatening air quality for much of Western Asia, an analysis from the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace shows. In terms of loss of life in Iran, between 3,592 and 11,410 people have been killed, and an estimated 26,500 (or more) are injured, because of the war.

Truthout is one of only a few platforms for justice-oriented, grassroots journalism. Today, we face an existential threat.

Due to Google’s launch of AI search, we’ve seen a drastic plunge in our site traffic and, as a result, our revenue. We lost 15 percent of our readership overnight. This was a readership we painstakingly built over decades, and it vanished because Google chose corporate greed over a healthy democracy.

We are fundraising right now to meet our basic operating expenses. If you can support Truthout with a one-time or monthly donation, you will make a significant impact on our work. Anything you can do makes a difference — we appreciate your support.

author: webdev@democracynow.org (Democracy Now!)
title: A Wealth Tax on Billionaires? California Voters to Decide Prop 40
content:
As voters across the United States cast ballots on November 3, Californians are weighing whether to approve a one-time 5% tax on the wealth of billionaires in the state. The tax would apply to roughly 250 Californians who now hold an estimated $2.3 trillion in wealth. Supporters say the wealth tax could raise up to $100 billion, with about 90% going toward healthcare. The remaining funds would support education and food assistance programs.


If Proposition 40 passes, it will mark the first time a government in the U.S. successfully taxes the wealth — rather than just the income — of the ultra-rich.


“It’s past time that billionaires pay their fair share,” says Lorena Gonzalez, president of the California Federation of Labor Unions, which is backing the initiative.


We also speak with California Congressmember Ro Khanna, who criticizes fellow Democrats like Governor Gavin Newsom for opposing Proposition 40. “We can either be a Democratic Party that stands for the working class in the tradition of the New Deal, or we can continue to cater to the donor class,” says Khanna.

author: Lana Harb
title: Lebanon’s ‘pilot zone’ experiment: The case of Zawtar al-Gharbiyah
content:
Ihsan Yaghi’s house in Zawtar al-Gharbiyah is scorched from the inside. Piles of rubble fill the rooms she and her husband walk through to see what remains. What was not demolished by nearby Israeli strikes has been blackened by fire, with soot covering the interior walls. But Yaghi refuses to leave.


“Despite everything, this is still my land, and we have a very strong attachment to this land that we can’t let go of,” Yaghi tells Mada Masr.


Yaghi’s is one of roughly 100 families that have, since July, returned to Zawtar al-Gharbiyah, one of around 70 villages in southern Lebanon still under Israeli occupation, its residents displaced, its homes destroyed, its fields unreachable. The question of what should be done for the south, how to rebuild and how to return people to their land under continued occupation, has become one of the most pressing political questions in Lebanon. The answer currently on offer from the Lebanese government and its international partners is the “pilot zone.”


On July 21, the United States announced

the official commencement

 of pilot zone operations in three villages in southern Lebanon: Froun, Srifa and Zawtar al-Gharbiyah. The model emerged from the framework agreement — a US-mediated trilateral framework signed by Lebanon and Israel on June 26, under which the Lebanese military is to restore sovereign authority over all Lebanese territory pending Hezbollah’s disarmament. The implementation of pilot zones was to mark the agreement’s first practical step. The idea was that the Lebanese military would deploy to select villages in coordination with a limited Israeli withdrawal, allowing residents to return while reconstruction and services would be concentrated there. Those villages would serve as templates, proof that return and rebuilding are possible, and the model could then be replicated elsewhere in the south.


Mada Masr spoke to residents, municipal officials and others involved with the project to assess whether this is indeed a workable model for the south.


Two months in, it is falling short on nearly every measure residents say matters. People are returning to villages without water, electricity, schools or livelihoods, the prefabricated homes promised as a temporary fix have arrived at a fraction of the numbers requested, and there is no guarantee of safety so long as Israeli forces remain in position nearby and have not withdrawn.


Children walking by destroyed houses in Zawtar al-Gharbiyah, July 26. Photo by Ammar Ammar.


The model also treats villages as isolated units, when in reality they depend on one another for schools, shops, hospitals and work, activists say. While experts on the South’s history of war and reconstruction say the current process marks a fundamental shift from previous rounds of war, for those in the south adopting a more radical position on resistance, another pathway must be found.


***


The pilot zone is a new model for the south. Political historian Nassib Chams tells Mada Masr that it emerged from a major shift in Lebanese politics: direct talks with Israel.


Such talks were not the case during the 2000 Israeli withdrawal, after 20 years of occupation, or after the 2006 war. That shift, he says, is what allowed the pilot zone project to come into being, and it gives Israel agency and authority over the return of southern Lebanese.


“This is the first time in Lebanese history that we see many Lebanese expressing that they want peace with Israel. So, while Israel was always stronger militarily, it is the first time there is this much political support for Israel,” he notes.


He adds that the project remains loosely defined, with the government yet to give residents a clear account of what the pilot zones entail.


“We may not know what is in it. We don’t know the details of what is happening in the negotiations. So far, we have not seen an Israeli withdrawal or anything. Israeli military operations are still continuing,” he says. “Are the people supposed to test if their villages are still habitable? It is unclear what they are trying to achieve when it is not even contingent on a full Israeli withdrawal,” he says.


Israeli forces in Zawtar al-Sharqiyah, September 24. Photo by Ammar Ammar.


A resident of Zawtar al-Gharbiyah, speaking on condition of anonymity, tells Mada Masr that Froun and Srifa have no Israeli presence at all, while Zawtar al-Gharbiyah has a relatively limited presence of Israeli troops compared to its twin …

author: Unknown
title: Eşref Saral'a yönelik silahlı saldırıyla ilgili 2 kişi gözaltına alındı
content:
Trabzon'un Of ilçesinde Eşref Saral'ın silahla vurulmasına ilişkin soruşturma kapsamında aranan iki kişi, İstanbul'un Çatalca ilçesinde gözaltına alındı.

AA'da yer alan habere göre, İstanbul Emniyet Müdürlüğü Organize Suçlarla Mücadele ve İstihbarat şube müdürlükleri ekipleri, Trabzon'da meydana gelen silahlı saldırıyı yapanların yakalanması için çalışma yürüttü. Trabzon Emniyet Müdürlüğünce şüphelilerin İstanbul'a kaçtığının belirlenmesi üzerine yapılan çalışmalarda, Of Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığınca "kasten öldürmeye teşebbüs" ve "suç işlemek amacıyla örgüt kurma" suçlamasıyla yürütülen soruşturma kapsamında arananların İstanbul'da bulunduğu tespit edildi. Çatalca'da belirlenen adrese düzenlenen operasyonda Y.E.S. (30) ve B.İ. (34) gözaltına alındı. Gözaltına alınanların ikametlerinde arama çalışmalarının sürdüğü öğrenildi.

Trabzon’un Of ilçesi Cumhuriyet Mahallesi’ndeki balıkçı barınakları mevkisinde olan silahlı saldırıda Eşref Saral, vücuduna isabet eden 5 kurşunla ağır yaralanmış ve hastaneye kaldırılmıştı. Son dönemde Amedspor’a verdiği destek mesajlarıyla gündeme gelen Saral’a yönelik saldırıyı, hakkında kırmızı bülten bulunan firari Yakup Kerem Saral üstlenmişti. Sosyal medya hesabından açıklama yapan Yakup Kerem Saral, saldırıyı “Saral ailesinin itibarını korumak” gerekçesiyle gerçekleştirdiğini öne sürmüştü. Saral, açıklamasında saldırıyı bir uyarı olarak nitelendirerek ikincisinin daha ağır olacağı tehdidinde bulunmuştu.

Daha önce Sedat Şahin’e yönelik suikast planıyla da gündeme gelen Yakup Kerem Saral’ın üstlendiği saldırı, MHP Genel Başkanı Devlet Bahçeli’nin girişimiyle Sarallar ve Şahinler grupları arasında sağlandığı duyurulan "barış" sürecinin ardından yaşanmıştı.

title: KJK: Let us defend the revolution of humanity
content:
The Kurdistan Women's Communities (KJK) Coordination said: “First of all, we commemorate all the martyrs of the revolution, particularly the recently announced martyrs of Rojava, and extend our condolences to their precious families. As honourable children of humanity, they waged a great struggle to realise the ideal of a free life and became immortal. We call on all humanity, particularly the people of Rojava, their families and comrades, to uphold the values created by our fighters for a dignified life and freedom, and to participate in building a democratic and free society as a fulfilment of their commitment to the martyrs' memory.”


The statement continued: “The Kurdish people have waged a magnificent struggle and resistance, paying a heavy price against the policies of occupation and genocide in Kurdistan. This struggle, which we have carried out under women's leadership, has brought about social change and revolutions. The Rojava Women's Revolution emerged as the culmination and highest expression of the accumulated experience and legacy of our 53-year struggle and the entire history of women's struggle. In the fight against ISIS mercenaries, freedom fighters led by Kurdish women rewrote history in favour of the peoples in golden letters, proving that an alternative way of life is possible and becoming a source of hope for the world.”


The values of freedom and democracy are being targeted


The KJK statement also included the following: “The policies and threat of genocide against the people and women of Rojava, who embody the conscience, dreams and hopes of all honourable humanity, continue. The attacks that began in Aleppo (Heleb) and continued in Kobani (Kobanê) and Hasakah (Hesekê) target the values of freedom and democracy created under women's leadership. These attacks also target the process initiated by Abdullah Öcalan with his 27 February 2025 ‘Call for Peace and a Democratic Society’, as well as the alternative of coexistence among peoples embodied by Rojava.


The ancient peoples of Syria are not responsible for these ongoing attacks against the values, symbols and institutions created through the common struggle and immense sacrifices of the peoples of Rojava, or against our patriotic people. The responsibility lies with the Damascus government itself, its collaborators and its mercenaries. International powers and the Turkish state, which support or fail to prevent policies of aggression against the different communities, peoples, cultures and faiths that make up Syria, bear equal responsibility. These attacks cannot be considered independently of international policies. If they continue, all countries and peoples of the region, particularly the peoples of Syria, will suffer. The attacks being carried out against the Kurdish people and the oppressed in Rojava and Syria, the abduction of people and their killing when ransoms are not paid, the attacks on institutions established through the efforts of our great martyrs, and the targeting of our values all represent an insistence on war and the continuation of genocidal policies. They seek to occupy cities through provocations, conspiracies and methods of special and psychological warfare, creating the conditions to achieve what they could not accomplish through open military occupation. The disgraceful attacks carried out for days against the values of the Kurdish people, particularly in Hasakah, constitute a clear provocation and a policy aimed at removing Kurds from the region. It must be understood that those who seek to exploit the struggle of the people and women of Rojava, based on the perspective of coexistence and a Democratic Syria, and their approach of establishing democratic relations with the Syrian state for their own genocidal and liquidationist objectives will be defeated. 


No historical community or anyone seeking a dignified life can remain without a response to attacks against their existence, identity and values. As demonstrated previously by the resistance in Kobani and at the Tishrin Dam, resistance, the spirit of democratic unity among peoples and the struggle for a free life waged by women under the leadership of the Arins and Denizes, symbolised by their braids, will prevail. title: Smokescreen Saturday Exposed: Chris Packham Blasts The Quorn Hunt Over Sickening Fox Cruelty That Blows Apart Trail Hunting’s Biggest Lie
content:
When we showed wildlife campaigner Chris Packham the sickening footage of the Quorn Hunt, his response was damning:


“Another bloody year, another bloodied body, another animal tortured and torn to pieces to gratify the bloodlust of savages. Where is the damned consultation and where is the damned ban?”


Chris Packham condemns the Quorn Hunt footage.


The footage lays bare the brutal reality of cub hunting – the practice of using foxes to train young hounds to hunt and kill.


WARNING: DISTURBING FOOTAGE


Cub hunting is not some isolated activity. It is the preparation for the hunting season ahead. Throughout the autumn, young hounds are taught what to chase, what to kill and how to respond to the huntsman’s commands. What they learn – or fail to learn – during these crucial weeks sets the tone for the entire season.


This is what makes the Quorn Hunt footage so damning. It shows hounds being deliberately encouraged to seize and tear at a fox, with hunt staff repeatedly intervening to reinforce that behaviour.


On the eve of National Trail Hunting Day aka Smokescreen Saturday – as the British Hound Sports Association (BHSA) and the Countryside Alliance prepared to showcase so-called ‘trail hunting’, the Quorn Hunt provided a horrifying glimpse of the reality behind the myth of trail laying.


On Friday 16 October, 2026 Northants Hunt Saboteurs visited The Quorn Hunt’s kennel meet at Kirby Bellars, near Melton Mowbray, Leicestershire.


The Quorn has a long history of royal connections. King Charles regularly rode with the hunt when he was Prince of Wales. His association with the Quorn came to an end following the emergence of footage showing

hunt members pulling a fox cub from its den

 and throwing them to the hounds to be torn apart.


The footage begins with the saboteurs’ drone approaching a group of barns stacked with bales. Mounted riders are positioned around the outside of the covert – a classic cub hunting tactic designed to frighten fleeing foxes back into cover, where the hounds can kill them.


Riders surround the covert which forces the fox back towards the barns.


As the drone circles to the far side of the barns, a group of hounds comes into view. A quad bike can be seen approaching, alongside another rider. More hounds appear on the track, along with a riderless horse.


Two terriermen jump off the quad bike and run towards the hounds, which have gathered in a narrow passageway between two barns.


Trapped. The fox is between the two barns.


What the drone captures next is utterly horrific – and exposes the brutal reality behind the hunting industry’s claims about scent trails.


The huntsman is already on foot, surrounded by excited hounds. He is swinging something towards them, encouraging them to grab hold. As the footage unfolds, it becomes clear that he is swinging a fox.


First the huntsman is alone shaking the fox to excite the hounds.


The hounds are repeatedly encouraged to seize the fox. Eventually, several begin to grab hold, and the huntsman encourages them further, pulling and tugging against them as though playing a game.


The huntsman blows on his horn over the hounds reinforcing the sound of the horn call with the kill.


When the hounds finally take the fox from him, he bends over them as they tear at it and then blows his hunting horn – most likely sounding the traditional call for a kill, reinforcing the hounds’ association between the horn and their quarry.


He then gives one of the terriermen a thumbs-up.


Thumbs-up.


When the hounds begin to lose interest again, the terrierman picks up the fox’s body and repeatedly shakes it in front of them, encouraging them to take hold once more. He appears to push the fox towards the hounds jaws.


The terrierman also has a go with the fox – shaking the body into the hounds jaws.


When the dogs finally grip it, he pulls against them in a grotesque tug-of-war. Once the hounds take the fox from the terrierman, the huntsman again blows his horn over them.


As more hounds join in, the terrierman pats one of the dogs. But as he does so he appears to hear the drone and looks up.


The terrierman suddenly notices the drone. Too late.


Suddenly everything changes.


The fox’s body is hurriedly retrieved from the hounds, and the two terriermen scramble to stuff it beneath the hay bales.
