author: Benji
title: Töten im Takt – Die grausamste Maschine bei Tönnies
content:
Töten im Takt – Die grausamste Maschine bei Tönnies

Tiere leiden vor dem Schlachten Höllenqualen bei CO₂-Betäubung

ARIWA veröffentlicht jetzt erstmals umfangreiche Aufnahmen aus einem Schlachthof von Tönnies. Schlachthöfe gehören zu den schwierigsten Herausforderungen für Undercover-Aufnahmen, da sie extrem gut gesichert sind. Die Betreiber setzen alles daran, dass das, was dort geschieht, nicht an die Öffentlichkeit gelangt.


19.10.2026, Deutschland


 NDR berichtet mit Videomaterial von ARIWA.


Er ist Deutschlands größter Schlachtkonzern und gilt als eines der mächtigsten Unternehmen der europäischen Fleischindustrie: Tönnies. Als Marktführer produziert er 30 Prozent des gesamten deutschen Schweinefleischs. Allein 2023 meldete der Konzern einen Jahresumsatz von über 7 Milliarden Euro. Dafür tötet Tönnies jedes Jahr 16 Millionen


Schweine. 


Das uns vorliegende Material zeigt, wie Mitarbeiter*innen die Tiere beim Zutrieb schlagen und sie unter automatischen Toren eingeklemmt werden. Es zeigt den grausamen Erstickungskampf in der CO₂-Anlage mit Tieren, die in Gondeln vor Angst schreien und versuchen zu fliehen. Und es zeigt zahlreiche Verstöße gegen die gesetzlichen Vorschriften vor und während der Schlachtung.


Von der Ankunft bis zum Tod:

Erste Undercover-Aufnahmen aus Tönnies Schlachthof


Das vorliegende Material dokumentiert erstmals unabhängig den gesamten Ablauf der Schlachtung von der Ankunft der Tiere im Schlachthof bis zur Tötung. Die Aufnahmen zeigen, wie leidvoll die letzten Stunden im Leben der Tiere sind. Das liegt auch an einer Maschine im Schlachthof, die grausamer nicht sein könnte: Die sogenannte CO₂-Betäubungsanlage.


Die Betäubung vor dem Schlachten ist gesetzlich vorgeschrieben. Die Tiere sollen so vor Schmerzen und Stress geschützt werden. Auch zur Betäubung selbst gibt es eindeutige Vorgaben: Paragraf 12 der Tierschutz-Schlachtverordnung legt fest, dass Tiere “schnell und unter Vermeidung von Schmerzen oder Leiden in einen (…) Zustand der Wahrnehmungs- und Empfindungslosigkeit” versetzt werden müssen. Der Betäubungsvorgang darf also keine Schmerzen oder Leid auslösen und muss bis zum Tod des Tieres anhalten. Doch die Aufnahmen zeigen eindeutig, dass die Betäubung mit CO₂ gegen diese Vorschrift verstößt!


Ankunft im Schlachthof


Am frühen Morgen kommen die ersten LKWs auf dem Schlachthof an. An den aufgenommenen Tagen werden mindestens fünftausend Schweine pro Tag hier angeliefert und getötet. Tönnies verfügt über ein riesiges Netz von Zulieferbetrieben in ganz Deutschland.


Nach ihrer Ankunft werden die Tiere in enge Wartebuchten gebracht. Hier läuft sanfte Musik, sie soll die Tiere entspannen. Es wirkt makaber. Neunzig Minuten lang sollen sich die vom Transport und Ausladen gestressten Schweine hier beruhigen, dabei ist zu erkennen, wie ängstlich sie sind.


Doch das wahre Grauen kommt erst noch. Nach anderthalb Stunden öffnet sich ein Tor. Ein Mitarbeiter beginnt, die Tiere in einen Treibgang zu scheuchen. Dabei kommt Gewalt zum Einsatz: Wenn die Schweine panisch versuchen zu fliehen, schlägt der Mitarbeiter mit der Treibstange zu, auch ins Gesicht. Die Schweine werden nach und nach in Sechsergruppen aufgeteilt. Als nächstes geht es für sie in die Betäubungsanlage.


Per Gondel in den Erstickungskampf


Die Schweine sind jetzt in einem engen Abteil, aus dem es kein Zurück gibt. Ein Mitarbeiter treibt die Gruppen nacheinander in die Gondelkäfige, mit denen es in wenigen Augenblicken gut 9 Meter nach unten in eine mit CO₂ gefüllte Grube geht. Manche Tiere werden von den schweren hydraulischen Trenngittern eingeklemmt und können sich nicht alleine befreien. Sie schreien vor Schmerz.


Sobald die erste Gruppe von Schweinen in ihre Gondel getrieben wurde, schließt sich der Käfig aus dicken Metallstangen. Kurze Zeit später setzt sich die Gondel in Bewegung. Die versteckte Kamera fährt mit. Innerhalb weniger Sekunden reagieren viele Schweine mit Panik. Viele schreien, schnappen nach Luft, werfen sich gegen die Gitterstäbe und steigen aufeinander. Die Fluchtversuche können so heftig sein, dass manche Tiere sich verletzen und Blutspuren an der Anlage zurücklassen.


Je tiefer die Tiere in den Schacht fahren, desto heftiger werden ihre Fluchtversuche. Die CO₂-Konzentration beträgt nach wenigen Metern schon 80 Prozent. Zeitgleich wird oben die nächste Gruppe in die Gondeln getrieben. Sie können die Angstschreie ihrer Artgenossen aus den Gondeln unter ihnen hören.

author: Brian Hioe
title: Animal Rights Advocates Call for Referendum on Snare Traps
content:
ANIMAL RIGHTS ADVOCATES are currently campaigning for a referendum to be held on the use of wild boar snares.

In particular, animal rights advocates have long criticized wild boar snares as overly cruel. Such traps use spring-loaded mechanisms to tighten around animals’ limbs when triggered.

Nevertheless, such traps have also been criticized for ensnaring other species, as they do not distinguish. Endangered species such as Formosan black bears and leopard cats had also been killed by such traps, as have cats and dogs, sometimes resulting in their losing limbs if they survive.

Though claims had been made that Indigenous hunters used such traps as part of traditional hunting rights, animal rights groups have generally cited that this was rarely the case, in that Indigenous hunters generally do not use such traps. By contrast, such animal rights advocates state that Indigenous hunters more commonly use traps made from wood, bamboo and vines, and other natural materials. In the past, the Central Election Commission turned down calls for a referendum on the use of wild boar snares on the basis that the referendum was unclear as to whether it pertained to traps used by Indigenous hunters.

Otherwise, such traps are sometimes used by farmers as a means of preventing damage to their crops. Animal rights advocates have called on the government to provide electric fencing, protective netting, or other means for farmers to protect their livestock and crops.

The proposals called for by animal rights advocates are relevant to the use, display, and sale of wild boar snares, as well as their import and export. It is thought that China is a major source of some of the wild boar snares used in Taiwan.

It is unclear as to whether the Central Election Commission will approve the referendum currently called for by animal rights advocates. At the same time, without a major political party endorsing it as an issue, such a referendum is unlikely to gain traction. It is to be seen if either the DPP or KMT, or perhaps even both parties, throw their weight behind the proposal.

One notes that there have been cases of political bipartisanship between both major parties on the issue of animal rights in past years, as seen with politicians of both parties supporting enshrining animal rights in the constitution. Even so, such politicians ultimately did not prove serious about such promises outside of election campaigning, as a result of which neither the KMT nor DPP acted on claims in past election cycles that animal rights would see constitutional protection.

author: Sophie Lemcke
title: So ist es, als weibliches Rind in der Milchindustrie zu leben
content:
Die Milchindustrie ist ein grausamer Kreislauf des Leids und endet mit einem gewaltvollen Tod.


Wie fühlt es sich an, in dieses System hineingeboren zu werden, ohne die Möglichkeit, dem zu entkommen?


Der einzige Grund, weshalb die Industrie dich „produziert“ hat: Auch du sollst Kinder gebären, immer wieder, damit du Milch produzierst. Milch, die dann von Menschen, statt von deinem Kalb konsumiert werden kann.


Du wirst fixiert, während jemand das Besamungsgerät in deine Vagina sowie seinen Arm in deinen Anus einführt. Wenn die Zwangsbefruchtung nicht beim ersten Mal zur Trächtigkeit führt – was oft der Fall ist –, wird dieser Vorgang mehrfach wiederholt.


Neun Monate – wie bei uns Menschen – wächst dein Kalb in dir heran. Du spürst eine Verbindung, merkst, wie es sich bewegt und immer größer wird. Je schwerer du selbst wirst, umso stärker werden deine Gelenkprobleme. Die rutschigen und harten Spaltenböden, auf denen du fast dein ganzes Leben verbringst, führen oft zu Verletzungen.


Dann bringst du dein Kalb zur Welt. Um dich herum riecht es extrem nach Kot und Ammoniak, von den Ausscheidungen der Tiere.


Endlich ist es da, noch ganz nass und schwach. Du leckst ihm über das Fell, um es zu wärmen. Es sucht deine Nähe und will an deinem Euter die für ihn so wichtige Erstmilch trinken. Sie stärkt sein noch schwaches Immunsystem und gibt ihm Kraft. Doch dann kommen die Arbeiter*innen.


Sie zerren dein noch ganz wackelig stehendes Kalb weg von dir. Es ruft nach dir. Du versuchst, bei ihm zu bleiben, aber du hast keine Chance. Die Menschen haben es weggebracht – du wirst es wahrscheinlich nie wiedersehen und nach nur zwei Monaten direkt wieder gewaltvoll befruchtet.


Du wirst nach der Geburt monatelang mehrmals täglich in den Melkstand getrieben – und die meiste Zeit davon bist du bereits wieder schwanger. Dein Körper muss gleichzeitig ein neues Kalb versorgen, das in dir heranwächst, und täglich über 22 Liter Milch produzieren. Dein Euter und deine Zitzen schmerzen. Aufgrund der extremen Überzüchtung produzierst du viermal so viel Milch, wie du es natürlicherweise für dein Kind tun würdest.


Die Prozeduren und Haltungsbedingungen zehren stark an deinem Körper. Dein Euter ist entzündet und schmerzt bei jeder Berührung. Andere Tiere humpeln, weil ihnen jeder Schritt wehtut. Viele sind schwach und ausgelaugt.


Wenn du nicht schon vorher stirbst oder getötet wirst, weil dein Körper nicht mehr kann, dann wirst du voraussichtlich nach nur fünf Jahren getötet – obwohl du unter natürlichen Bedingungen 25 Jahre alt werden könntest.


Dann kommt der Tag, an dem du als nicht mehr profitabel giltst. Du wirst aus dem Stall getrieben – das erste Mal nach Jahren verlässt du ihn, aber das ist kein Grund zur Freude.


Zusammen mit anderen erschöpften „ausgedienten Milchkühen“ wirst du auf einen Transporter verladen. Du hast Mühe, über die Rampe zu gehen. Deine Gelenke schmerzen vom jahrelangen Stehen auf Spaltenböden. Im engen Transporter stehst du dicht an dicht mit den anderen Tieren, der Lkw wackelt. Manche fallen hin und werden versehentlich getreten. Eure Fahrt in den Schlachthof dauert mehrere Stunden, ohne Wasser, ohne Nahrung, ohne Pause.


Angekommen erwartet dich ein brutaler Tod. Überall riecht es nach Blut, du bekommst Panik, aber es gibt keinen Ausweg. Dann ein Bolzenschuss in deinen Kopf. Wenn die Betäubung korrekt durchgeführt wurde und wirkt, brichst du zusammen. Wenn nicht, kann es sein, dass du bei Bewusstsein und unter extremen Schmerzen erlebst, wie dir deine Kehle aufgeschnitten wird und du verblutest.


Es ist unvorstellbar, was Mutterrinder in der Milchindustrie erleiden müssen.


Der wahre Preis von Milch


Ein Ermittler von Animal Equality hat mehrere Monate undercover in einem deutschen Milchgewinnungsbetrieb gearbeitet und den Alltag der Tiere dokumentiert. Was unsere Undercover-Recherche zeigt, ist der wahre Preis von Milch: Ausbeutung, Gewalt, Schmerz, Leid und Tod.


Auf unserer Webseite erfährst du mehr und kannst die Stellungnahme des Betriebs nachlesen:


Zur Undercover-Recherche


Unterstütze dieses grausame System nicht!


Entscheide dich konsequent für pflanzliche Lebensmittel. Im Supermarkt findest du zahlreiche Alternativen zu Milch, wie:


Hafermilch – mild, cremig, perfekt für Kaffee und Müsli (oft die günstigste Option!)


Sojamilch – proteinreich, ideal zum Kochen und Backen


Mandelmilch – leicht nussig, besonders lecker in Smoothies


Reismilch – süßlich und gut verträglich …

title: Solidarität mit nichtmenschlichen Tieren im Klimakollaps
content:
Am 2. November ist Friederike Schmitz zu Gast in Leipzig. Ihr Vortrag beschäftigt sich mit der Frage von Solidarität mit nichtmenschlichen Tieren im Klimakollaps.

Plaque, Industriestraße 101, Leipzig

Orga: tierbefreier*innen Leipzig

Die Erderhitzung schreitet voran und wir müssen damit rechnen, dass Wetterextreme und Katastrophen unsere Gesellschaften massiv unter Druck setzen werden. Es ist daher realistisch, von Kollapsszenarien auszugehen – das bedeutet nicht zwingend ein einmaliges Ereignis, das plötzlich alles verändert. Es kann auch bedeuten, dass etablierte Systeme und Sicherheiten zunehmend instabil und unverlässlich werden.>

Die Kollapsbewegung fordert, dass wir uns gemeinsam darauf vorbereiten und solidarische Strukturen aufbauen, denn wer gegen Umweltzerstörung und Faschismus kämpft, kann sich auf den Staat nicht verlassen. Doch inwieweit sind nichtmenschliche Tiere dabei eingeschlossen? Und wie könnte es aussehen, wenn die Solidarität nicht an der Speziesgrenze haltmacht? Der Vortrag liefert einen Einstieg in diese Fragen und lädt zu Austausch und Diskussion ein.

Friederike Schmitz ist eine deutsche Philosophin und Publizistin mit dem Schwerpunkt Ethik und Politik der Mensch-Tier-Beziehung. Zu ihrem Schwerpunkt gehört die Klimagerechte Transformation von Landwirtschaft und Ernährung. In dem Podcast “Was zu retten ist?” thematisiert sie zusammen mit Annemarie Botzki (Campaignerin und Aktivistin) Klima, Kollaps und Ernährung.

author: L214
title: Végétalisation des menus des cantines scolaires : l’état des lieux de L214
content:
Au lendemain de la rentrée scolaire 2026, L214 dresse l’état des lieux de la végétalisation des menus des cantines scolaires dans 40 villes de France. Ce bilan, le premier depuis la prise de fonction des nouveaux élus à l’issue des élections municipales de mars 2026, révèle des situations contrastées : là où certaines villes se contentent du minimum imposé par la loi, d’autres font preuve de plus d’ambition, indépendamment de leur couleur politique.

La végétalisation des menus dans les cantines scolaires constitue un levier puissant et efficace à disposition des maires pour contribuer à réduire le nombre d’animaux tués pour l’alimentation en France. C’est pourquoi L214 propose trois mesures de végétalisation dans sa charte d’engagement du Sauvetage du siècle à destination des maires : instaurer une option végétarienne quotidienne, deux journées végétariennes hebdomadaires et un plat végétalien hebdomadaire.

Ce début d’année scolaire révèle de fortes disparités d’une ville à l’autre sur la mise en place de deux journées végétariennes par semaine. Sur les 40 villes de plus de 100 000 habitants étudiées par L214 :

14 villes proposent deux journées végétariennes par semaine ou plus,

12 villes proposent 5 à 7 journées végétariennes par mois,

14 villes se contentent d’une journée végétarienne par semaine, le minimum légal imposé par la loi EGalim.

Concernant la mise en place d’une option végétarienne quotidienne, le tableau est là aussi très contrasté : 11 villes proposent déjà cette option, alors que 24 villes proposent une option « sans viande » ou « sans porc » pouvant contenir du poisson, une alternative qui n’est donc pas végétarienne. Cinq villes ne proposent aucune alternative végétarienne quotidienne.

Certaines villes comme Bordeaux, Grenoble, Lyon, Montpellier et Paris font figure de bonnes élèves en cumulant d’ores et déjà une option végétarienne quotidienne et deux journées végétariennes hebdomadaires. D’autres villes vont même au-delà des mesures portées par L214, à l’image de Saint-Denis, qui propose 3 journées végétariennes chaque semaine dans ses cantines, ou de Montpellier, qui propose deux plats végétaliens chaque mois.

À l’inverse, Boulogne-Billancourt, Limoges et Le Mans notamment se limitent à une journée végétarienne par semaine, le minimum prévu par la loi.

→ Découvrir la charte d’engagement du Sauvetage du siècle

Cet état des lieux montre que la volonté de végétaliser les menus dans les cantines scolaires n’est pas portée par un seul parti politique. Parmi les cinq villes qui cumulent une option végétarienne quotidienne et deux journées végétariennes hebdomadaires, Bordeaux est dirigée par une majorité du centre, Grenoble et Lyon par des majorités écologistes, et Montpellier et Paris par des majorités de gauche.

Plusieurs villes affiliées à droite renforcent elles aussi la végétalisation de leurs cantines. Aix-en-Provence propose désormais deux journées végétariennes une semaine sur deux, et Metz en propose 5 à 7 par mois.

Pour Erwin Goeller, chargé d’affaires publiques de L214 : « La végétalisation des menus dans les cantines scolaires est un choix politique concret à la portée de chaque maire. L’enjeu a été pris au sérieux par plusieurs municipalités, mais les efforts restent très disparates selon les villes. Nous appelons les nouveaux élus à se saisir pleinement de ce sujet pour contribuer, à leur échelle, à réduire de moitié le nombre d’animaux tués pour l’alimentation en France ! »

author: Animal Rising Press
title: Guilty Verdict For King’s Sheep Rescuers In Theft Trial
content:
After a four-day trial at Norwich Crown Court, Rose Patterson, Sarah Foy, and Rosa Sharkey have all been found guilty of theft after the rescue of three lambs from King Charles III’s Sandringham Estate in May 2023. Sentencing to follow today.

Despite the verdict, Animal Rising claims that the rescue and subsequent trial have helped to put a spotlight on the reality behind animal farming in the UK, with over 10 million sheep being slaughtered yearly [1].

The controversial rescue made front-page news across the UK and headlines around the world [2]. It captured the attention of the British public, questioning how we relate to animals in the food system and if it’s a rescue or a theft to take them from farms.

Animal Rising director Rose Patterson, alongside Rosa Sharkey and Sarah Foy, rescued the lambs - Sammy, Sunny and Sooty - before informing police the following day. The women held signs outside Windsor Castle reading “I rescued the King’s sheep” before reporting what they had done to police. They each face up to 7 years' imprisonment.

Earlier this year, Patterson was found not guilty by a jury over another Animal Rising open rescue, after helping to rescue beagle puppies from MBR Acres, a facility breeding animals for testing [3].

Animal Rising director Rose Patterson, one of the three defendants found guilty today, said:

Sammy, Sunny and Sooty remain safe and are now fully grown.

The trial followed a series of open-rescue trials relating to Animal Rising’s rescue of beagles from MBR Acres. In January this year, Animal Rising made history by securing the UK’s first-ever not-guilty verdict in an open-rescue case [4]. The lambs were rescued from Appleton Farm, which forms part of the Sandringham estate.

Defendants Patterson and Foy are available for comment or broadcast interview upon request.

For further information, comment, or to arrange an interview, please email press@animalrising.org or call +44 1225 29 6691

High-Quality Pictures and Videos: https://show.pics.io/animal-rising-breaking-news

All images and videos in this file, on our social media, and website can be used with credit to Animal Rising under ‘fair use’ for the purposes of reporting.

[2] https://www.dailymail.com/news/article-12431619/Animal-Rising-protesters-charged-stealing-Kings-sheep-royal-Sandringham-Estate-driving-away-animals.html

https://www.dailymail.com/news/article-12126009/Will-stop-eco-clowns-Just-Stop-Oil-throw-orange-powder-Animal-Rising-kidnap-lambs.html

[3] https://www.cambsnews.co.uk/peterborough-court-acquittal-animal-rescue-beagles/

[4] https://www.animalrising.org/post/not-guilty-verdict-for-beagle-puppy-rescuers-in-landmark-legal-case

Rose Patterson, 37, is the Director of Animal Rising. An advocate for animals since 2012, she holds an MSc in Animal Welfare Science, Ethics, and Law and previously worked with World Animal Protection before joining Animal Rising in 2020.

Sarah Foy, 26, has been involved in a range of campaigns advocating for a just and sustainable food system that works for animals, farmers, and the planet. She brings a practical, hands-on approach to her advocacy, with real-world experience caring for rescued farm animals at sanctuaries and protesting alongside farmers.

Rosa Sharkey, 26, is a food charity worker. She is passionately committed to reducing the impact of our food system on the climate crisis, community action, and animal rights.

Animal Rising is a nonviolent campaign group working to fundamentally transform our relationship with animals and nature, and build a more sustainable future for animals, people and the planet. Animal Rising is calling on the Government to end factory farming by 2040 and support a transition to a sustainable plant-based food system.

The group has used a variety of civil disobedience and nonviolent direct action tactics, notably blockading McDonald's distribution centres in May 2021, blockading dairy industry sites in September 2022, disrupting the 2023 Grand National, rescuing lambs belonging to King Charles III in May 2023, and carrying out the UK’s largest undercover farm investigation in 2024.

author: unoffensiveadmin
title: ANONYMOUS GROUP LIBERATES 100 HENS FROM A BARN
content:
October, France.


received anonymously via email:


“We believe that the structures of speciesism are vulnerable and accessible.


Last week, we – an anonymous group – went to a factory farm in France and helped 100 hens escape from it. A few hours later, the liberated hens were already running on the grass and petting each other.


Rage consumed us when we arrived at the barn. The sky was dark, and everything was silent except for their screams and talks inside.


We entered and took them out, as fast as we could. After that, the night didn’t have the same color. We could hear them talk in their transport cages but we knew that they were free from harm, at last.


And, of course, we still deeply think of the ones who are still inside. We will continue to fight so that, one day, everyone could be free and safe.


If you can, please go inside those places of oppression, open the cages and take them out. You will experience more rage, fear and hope that what you are probably used to but every second of it will be so worth it. Because when you go on with your daily life later, you will know that the people you helped escape are now free and safe.


Thank you to everyone who fight alongside other animals and good luck with your actions.”

title: Max Oelschlaeger - The Wilderness Condition
content:
Author

: Max Oelschlaeger

Title

: The Wilderness Condition

Subtitle

: Essays on Environment and Civilization

Date

: Jun 1, 1992

Source

: <

press.princeton.edu

> & <

www.archive.org

>


 


 In this age of heightened sensitivity to environmental problems, the popular press inundates us with the issues of the moment. We hear of the immediate threats to our groundwater supply, to the rain forest, to the ozone. Yet nowhere do we find coverage of the fundamental issues of environmentalism, those elements such as philosophy and history that, though less dramatic, constitute the foundation from which we can reverse ecological breakdown.


 This vital collection of essays by some of the environmental movement’s preeminent thinkers addresses these deeper, neglected issues. Written from a broad range of perspectives, the authors explore the dynamic tension between wild nature and civilization, offering insights into why the relationship has become so conflicted and suggesting creative means for reconciliation.


 Introducing the concept of the wilderness condition, the essays probe the effects of history, psychology, culture, and philosophy on the environment. Included is commentary from Gary Snyder, award-winning author of

Turtle Island,

 who discusses how our prevailing assumptions about “nature” and “wilderness” impede conservation. Paul Shepard, author of

Man in the Landscape,

 presents his compelling, controversial theory that the seeds of our current ecological crisis were planted in the New Stone Age. And George Sessions explains how the two major schools of thought in the environmental movement differ on its most basic issues, again thwarting opportunities for change.


 Other essays discuss how Western philosophy has erroneously divorced humankind from nature; why Sierra Club founder John Muir’s early writings remain eminently relevant; and how elements of Eastern philosophy may hold the key to sucessful change.


 The contributors eloquently demonstrate why we can no longer take nature for granted, or assume that its existence is somehow second to humankind’s. They argue convincingly that no amount of technology will ever displace our primal connection to nature. But rather than simply deploring the prevailing attitudes toward our imperiled environment, the essayists offer fresh, realistic, and inspiring ideas for alleviating the crisis.


 Three themes unify the collection: the essayists, though they represent different traditions, share an evolutionary perspective that confirms why humankind and nature are by necessity interdependent; sensitive to language, the writers reveal how the words we choose when we consider environmental issues reflect our sometimes naive understanding of them; and most important, the essayists share the conviction that al! is not lost—and that we can initiate a worldwide trend toward recognizing the environment as a vital entity in its own right, thereby preserving its integrity.


 


 MAX OELSCHLAEGER teaches philosophy of ecology, environmental ethics, and wilderness studies at the University of North Texas. He is author of the influential and critically acclaimed The

Idea of Wilderness,

 which explores Western culture’s persistent attempts to separate humankind from the natural world.


 


 The Sierra Club, founded in 1892 by John Muir, has devoted itself to the study and protection of the earth’s scenic and ecological resources — mountains, wetlands, woodlands, wild shores and rivers, deserts and plains. The publishing program of the Sierra Club offers books to the public as a nonprofit educational service in the hope that they may enlarge the public’s understanding of the Club’s basic concerns. The point of view expressed in each book, however, does not necessarily represent that of the Club. The Sierra Club has some sixty chapters coast to coast, in Canada, Hawaii, and Alaska. For information about how you may participate in its programs to preserve wilderness and the quality of life, please address inquiries to Sierra Club, 730 Polk Street, San Francisco, CA 94109.


 


For A. E. Koenig, in memoriam


Introduction: The Wilderness Condition Today

author: Önder Algedik
title: The climate-changing policy behind Türkiye’s floods
content:
On October 14, a 14-year-old boy stepped into a puddle in a park in Balat, in Istanbul’s old city, and was electrocuted. A surveillance camera captured the moment. The governor’s office has opened an investigation.

The same storms flooded five other provinces, including Antalya, which will be host to COP31 in less than four weeks.

Istanbul alone recorded 1277 floods and 15 landslides; schools closed the next day.

None of this was a surprise. The day before the state meteorological service forecast about 21–50 millimetres of rain for Istanbul; parts of the city’s north received nearly 194mm. Cities are meant to be built for the worst case scenario, not the forecast.

Was this climate change? Without an attribution study, it is too early to say, but we do not need one to explain what happened.

Istanbul is a city of concrete and asphalt. Over five years, 98 square kilometres of new floor space was completed and 124 square kilometres started; more than a million new cars joined the traffic.

If you could park every vehicle in the city nose to tail, you would have a 12–lane car park from Istanbul to Paris.

The heaviest rain, up to 194mm, fell in the north, the city’s new construction frontier. Yet in the southern districts, where as little as 7mm fell, streets also flooded; they were paved long ago and “urban renewal” now even means concreting over the gardens between apartment blocks.

Is climate change responsible for the boy in Balat’s death?

In a similar case, in İzmir in 2024, the court-appointed expert blamed the municipal utility and the electricity distributor. Whoever is responsible must be named.

When “climate change” is continually discussed as a “natural” event, with no one behind it, it becomes the scapegoat. But it has a culprit, and that is the climate-changing policy.

Türkiye imports coal, oil and gas, and burns them; it forces everyone into cars and parcels the country out to cement companies.

Over 20 years, the number of vehicles rose from 8.5 million to more than 32 million and new floor area grew by 300%. Last year alone, Türkiye produced 98 million tonnes of cement.

It now emits two and a half times the greenhouse gases it did in 1990.

This is not just fossil fuels, but the fossil infrastructure which burns them — roads, concrete, cars and power plants.

In Demre, 22 people, including students and teachers who were trapped in a school, had to be rescued. The mayor said they had not seen such rain in 100 years.

That is a confession: a town with 25 centuries of history never planned for a once–in–a–century storm.

None of this will be on the table at COP31. Its Action Agenda does not even name coal, oil or gas, let alone fossil infrastructure.

The summit site is itself a concrete project. The company that won the US$160 million contract to build it is also a COP31 sponsor. The COP31 president, Murat Kurum, is the minister in charge of construction and zoning.

Türkiye has close to 2 million empty homes, not counting holiday houses. Ankara alone plans to spend US$480 million on asphalt in 2026. Put empty homes to use. Move asphalt budgets to public transport, pedestrian streets and bike lanes, and make public transport free.

But even that is not enough. Allowing existing fossil infrastructure to run to the end of its life would by itself push the world past 1.5°C. It has to be stopped, and public money moved from changing the climate to protecting cities from floods and heat.

That is what I call a climate revolution. It starts with naming the problem correctly.

The boy in Balat did not die because of the weather. He died of a policy. Name it.

[Önder Algedik is a climate researcher and activist with 350Ankara. His new book, Ya Fosil Düzen Ya Devrim (Fossil Order or Revolution), is published by İletişim.]

author: Mohamed Sheikh Nor
title: Somali Man Speaks Out on Mogadishu Streets About El Niño Threats.
content:
Osman Yusuf Oskar‚ wearing a T-shirt with the letters “SUPER EL NINO‚” walks the streets of Mogadishu carrying a megaphone and signs to alert other Somalis of the risks of heavy rains during the upcoming rainy season․


His voice can be heard above the sounds of traffic and crowds, urging others to heed warnings that El Niño-related floods will threaten millions of people in Somalia, primarily children, according to

Save the Children warns of El Niño floods in Somalia

).


Osman Yusuf Oskar warning a citizen in Mogadishu


Oskar is not a government employee or a meteorologist․ His campaign effort is a solo project to educate others about El Niño‚ a weather phenomenon with which most Somalis are unfamiliar․


“I am not an official or officer at the disaster management center․ I am stepping into their role of volunteering to spread the word to my people‚ who don’t know much about the Super El Niño‚” Oskar said․


Street by street‚ Oskar shares his warning in public settings․ Some people respond to his efforts; others ignore him and go about their business․ Oskar’s signs and megaphone are tools to help laypeople understand technical weather information․


His campaign follows Somalia’s recovery from one of the worst droughts in recent decades․


“While other governments of nearby countries were preparing for this disaster‚ we seem to have had no warning and no preparation for this‚” Oskar said․


“The time for warning has gone‚ and other countries bordering that nation now are preparing․” He said․


“Here in Somalia‚ our politicians and other government officials are more focused on their own activities and are not communicating to the general public about climate-related issues‚ including the Super El Niño weather event‚” he said․


The Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO)  has warned that strengthening El Niño conditions and forecasts of exceptionally heavy Deyr rains could raise the risk of severe flooding across Somalia, with up to a 90 percent probability of above-normal rainfall in parts of central and southern Somalia

FAO warning that El Niño raises the risk of severe Deyr flooding in Somalia


For the past four years‚ drought has caused massive hardship in much of the country‚ including loss of livestock and crops and migration of rural residents to urban areas and internally displaced persons’ settlements․


In addition to years of drought‚ people in these areas are now at risk of flooding and other impacts from heavy rains related to El Niño conditions․


The October-December Deyr rains are forecast to be above average in Somalia‚ increasing flood risks near major rivers and other locations across the country․


In vulnerable communities affected by drought‚ flooding may lead to additional population displacement and destruction of homes and crops‚ as well as greater health risks and service disruptions․


From drought to other climate-related risks.


The threat of flooding follows several years of drought that have disrupted the ability of many Somali families to earn a living․


Farmers and herders have lost livestock and crops due to lack of water and grazing land․ Many households have relocated to find food‚ water‚ health services‚ and other humanitarian aid․


Extended drought has reduced communities’ resilience to other shocks․


That vulnerability was evident during my recent reporting trip to Kismayo‚ which included a fact-finding trip to Jubaland with a UNICEF delegation and the Swedish ambassador to Somalia․


The delegation visited internally displaced persons’ settlements and a stabilization center treating severely malnourished children․


Children treated at the center suffered from long-term health problems caused by food insecurity and lack of other health services․


This scenario describes a larger

humanitarian crisis in Somalia, compounded by drought and aid funding cuts

, which are placing additional pressure on vulnerable households already struggling with lost income and other hardships.


Sandra Lattouf‚ UNICEF Somalia Representative‚ told African Arguments that a long dry spell and decreased aid had left many families in Somalia without their crops and other means of support․


“Now kids have begun to die because of malnutrition and diseases‚ and we need and urge donors to save lives․”


Sandra Lattouf

 said some children had died of malnutrition and other complications from diseases․


The warning is issued amid budget challenges for other humanitarian groups․

author: Kate Sharpley
title: An anarchist in the archive : Remembering Barry Pateman
content:
For over seven decades, Myanmar was consumed by the world’s longest civil war, but the Intha (Insaku), the "Children of the Lake/The People of The Lake," remained a peaceful exception. Nestled among high mountain peaks in Shan State, they lived peacefully with nature on the still waters of Inle Lake, famous worldwide for their stilt houses, floating gardens (ye-chan), and iconic leg-rowing fishermen, or at least that's what the state and tourism agency’s narrative for their brand image. The iconic leg-rowing fishermen have become a brand of Myanmar's tourism campaign since 1996, when the military was promising market reform and democracy.


Author


Al Wine


    Submitted by

heinhtetkyaw

 on October 17, 2026


Although recognized as one of Myanmar's 135 distinct indigenous groups, the Intha remain a "minority within a minority" in Southern Shan State, distinct in language and history from their Shan, Pa'O, Lisu, Taungtha, Kareni, and Danu neighbors, and their language is a branch of Widely accepted theories suggest their ancestors migrated from Lower Burma, Dawei, a long time ago, or a group of Tibeto-Burman who were still left behind. At the same time, the rest moved forward to the Irrawaddy Valley. Applying James C. Scott’s concept of “Zomia,” which describes upland societies that historically avoided centralized state control, the Intha experience can be understood as a form of aquatic adaptation. Rather than escaping into mountains, they survived on an economically marginal lake environment surrounded by hills. Their oral histories and religious traditions contain accounts of resistance against local feudal authorities. Even during British colonial rule, the region was viewed less as a profitable administrative center and more as a scenic recreational area.


This delicate socio-ecological balance began to shatter after the 2010 political reforms. Under President Thein Sein’s administration, military-tied tycoons and international investors targeted the lake's eastern shore for a massive "Hotel Zone" project. The infrastructure building has leveled hillsides, drained wetlands, and seized land with minimal compensation for the local population, leading to severe ecological damage, driving local fish populations toward extinction, and destroying traditional livelihoods.


Although Inle Lake was designated Myanmar's first UNESCO Biosphere Reserve in 2015, the surrounding Inlay Lake Wildlife Sanctuary had already been recognized as an ASEAN Heritage Park in 2003. It was later designated Myanmar's fifth Ramsar Wetland of International Importance in 2018. Despite these international conservation recognitions, environmental degradation driven by deforestation, unsustainable agriculture, tourism development, and weak conservation governance has continued. One of the most controversial cases involved Myanmar Naing Group Co., Ltd., owned by U Tun Naing Shwe, son of former military ruler Than Shwe, which proposed to construct a luxury hotel on land that had previously been part of the Inle Lake Wildlife Sanctuary. The proposal sparked widespread opposition from local communities, environmental organizations, and government agencies, becoming a prominent example of the conflict between tourism development and environmental conservation around Inle Lake.


Many farmers and fishermen lost their way of life; many were forced to migrate abroad for work. Those who stayed were pushed into minimum-wage work in construction and the hospital sector. Some local activists and scholars have criticized the commercialization of Inle Lake’s cultural practices, arguing that activities such as staged leg-row fishing and ethnic performances risk transforming living traditions into tourist spectacles rather than preserving their original social meaning.


The commercialization of agriculture and watershed degradation has intensified the ecological crisis at Inle Lake. Historically, the lake’s unique wetland ecosystem allowed the Intha to develop floating-garden agriculture, with tomatoes becoming one of the region’s most important economic crops. However, expanding domestic and regional markets encouraged increased use of chemical fertilizers, pesticides, and commercial seeds, contributing to nutrient pollution and ecological stress.


 At the same time, state land policies allowed customary lands in Shan State to be classified as vacant or wasteland and allocated to large-scale investors and military-linked companies. Many Environmental …

author: Anneke Demanuele
title: Westsiders campaign against AI hub
content:
I met Anthony and Samantha on Holden Road in Plumpton, 40 kilometres west of Melbourne’s CBD. We’ve parked our cars at the Melbourne Renewable Energy hub gate, behind which a huge expanse of land could become home to a hyperscale data centre owned and operated by Syncline Energy. 

The surrounding area is a green wedge, meaning that it should be protected from industrial and urban sprawl. There’s a free-range egg farm, rolling fields, some houses and a few horses. Samantha, who is campaigning against the development, lives five minutes away in Diggers Rest and learned to ride a horse right here. In fact, one we are looking at is called Betsy and is the very same horse. 

A 

petition

 against the AI hub raises concerns about environmental destruction, including “endangered ecological vegetation communities, biodiversity corridors, areas of Aboriginal cultural heritage sensitivity and conservation efforts”.

The Plumpton plan is still awaiting approval from the state government. If it gets it, the site will host a

 

350-hectare AI hub

, which the 

Age

 reports is the size of 175 MCG playing fields. The facility will have a maximum power draw of 2.5 gigawatts, more than the entire output of the Loy Yang A coal power plant. Loy Yang A provides around 

30 percent of Victoria’s power

. It would use more power than every other data centre currently operating combined. 

“It’s such a blatant display of profit over people”, says Anthony, who has also been campaigning against Syncline’s plans for months. 

Their campaign group started after a community meeting of 150 people in Sydenham. “Anthony and Ella produced these awesome pamphlets, so we’ve been doing lots of letterboxing”, Samantha says. “We also hosted an information night [and] we’ve got a day of action coming up. We also attended the Senate inquiry as witnesses.” 

The Senate inquiry held hearings in Yarraville last month. The inquiry has heard from residents, local politicians and data centre CEOs. Local testimonies include stories of monolithic structures bearing down on residents, diesel emissions and pollution, drone surveillance, and concerns about fire risk.

“The Plumpton site will have huge amounts of lithium-ion batteries, and we feel like this hasn’t been assessed or regulated enough”, Samantha says. Lithium-ion batteries can trigger thermal runaway, releasing toxic fumes and a self-sustaining fire. Because data centres need 24/7 power, they often rely on diesel or gas generators. This increases the risk of uncontrollable fires. “The combination of lithium batteries and diesel is a pretty nasty sort of fire”, a member of Fire Rescue Victoria 

told the ABC 

in June

. 

The Plumpton group is one of many across Melbourne, mostly in working-class areas. The wealthy areas of Melbourne are unlikely to be high on the list of potential sites for the centres. In fact, Belinda Dennett, CEO of the data centre lobby group, said she wouldn’t want to live near one. Samantha describes her as “AI in human form”. Anthony is frustrated that communities have no say in whether centres get built. “It’s so clear that the system is not set up for a democratic decision”, he says.

Samantha says those living near the site don’t have much idea what is coming to their doorstep: 

“Last time I checked, there’s about 80 residents around here. And none of these guys knows about it. It will be in full view of their backyards, and they almost don’t want to believe me; they think I’m almost a conspiracy theorist. But it’s going to be built here, and they haven’t been notified”. 

That’s why Samantha and her co-organisers have been hosting outreach meetings, and doing the letterboxing and door knocking. They want to inform their neighbours what is coming to their communities and fight it together. 

According to Samantha and Anthony, Syncline’s CEO is a “schmoozer”. At the Senate hearings, he said his company has done a “bad job” at community outreach. He’s trying to turn that around and convince locals the AI hub will benefit them. 

“He is very good at convincing people that this will benefit them, without explaining how”, Samantha says. Anthony and Samantha feel the campaign has put pressure on Syncline, which is now trying to win support for its plan by claiming it will create new jobs. But those in the campaign aren’t fooled.

They also aren’t fooled by the Labor government’s Sustainable Data Centre Action Plan. The government promises that data centres won’t be built near …

author: Dominic Gutoman
title: Displaced Marawi survivors still long for justice
content:
Marawi displaced survivor Baiminang Madale speaking in the opening of Alongan sa Marawi exhibit. Photo by Dominic Gutoman/Bulatlat.

More than nine years have passed since the Philippine government declared the “liberation” of Marawi City after the siege that displaced more than 300,000 families. Some of them are now living in different parts of the country, uncertain if they could return.

“We were already familiar with the term bakwit (evacuee/displacement). But the Marawi Siege was different. Before, our bakwit would only last for three days. This time, it feels as though we have been permanently driven out of Marawi,” Baiminang Madale, a displaced Maranao survivor living in Manila, said in the vernacular during the opening of Alongan sa Marawi (One Day in Marawi) exhibit.

The exhibit runs until November 15, 2026, at the Rift Gallery Edsa. It is organized by researchers, journalists, survivors, and advocates to commemorate the ninth year of the city’s so-called liberation. It seeks to provide a visual experience of Marawi from the survivors’ perspective.

“The Maranao, like other tribes and communities, have our own culture, dreams, and lives. Because of the Marawi Siege, we feel as though we have not simply been stripped naked, but forcibly stripped out of our homes that shape our identity,” Madale said. “Marawi is the very heart of the Maranao people. Imagine suddenly losing everything—it is far worse than a nightmare. We never thought something like this could happen to us.”

The Philippine government declared October 17 as Marawi Liberation Day starting in 2017 to mark what it called as a “military victory” against the Islamic State-linked Maute group after a five-month battle.

Madale, who is also part of the board of Ako Bakwit, a group working for the welfare and rights of internally displaced peoples (IDPs), said that there are many more families like hers forced to live in Manila since the siege.

Earlier this year, Bulatlat reported that the displaced families have yet to return to their homes in Marawi. Around 17,000 families or 80,000 individuals are still living in 15 temporary shelters in Marawi and Lanao del Sur, according to Marawi Advocacy Accompaniment.

Read: After 9 years, Marawi displaced families have yet to return to their homes

Under the Marawi Siege Victims Compensation Act of 2022, any owner of a residential, cultural, or commercial structure, and other properties in Marawi’s 24 MAA and eight barangays considered as other affected areas (OAA) is entitled to monetary compensation subject to verification.

Compensation claims, under the law, shall be filed within one year from the date of commencement of the filing (July 4, 2023) to the date of its termination (July 3, 2024).

Read: Group opposes Marawi Siege compensation planned changes

Data from the Marawi Compensation Board (MCB), the government body that awards monetary compensation to eligible claimants, showed that 3,699 claims were resolved from 2023 to June 30, 2026, amounting to P6.154 billion. This is 25.51 percent of the estimated 14,497 total claims to be resolved by the body by 2028.

Mindanao State University Prof. Sorhalia Latip-Yusoph said that the recovery and return process for the survivors are hurdled by a tedious bureaucratic process.

“The government’s requirements for returning are extremely difficult to meet. Sometimes, we do not understand why the process has to be so difficult. Perhaps they want to be strict,” Latip-Yusoph said. “Our fellow Maranaos (in bakwit) are truly the ones who, if we may put it this way, are the reason our hearts continue to ache. Many of them are still living elsewhere. I hope we will not reach the tenth year without being able to return home.”

Task Force Bangon Marawi was a government inter-agency task force group established by former President Rodrigo Duterte in June 2017 to facilitate rehabilitation, recovery, and reconstruction.

However, Madale said that the four stages of the task force’s process did not align with the needs of the IDPs and survivors of the Marawi siege. The process includes registration, mapping, submission of documents, and biometrics. However, most IDPs lack valid identification and their house/land ownership documents– most of the time– are not recognized by the government implementers.

“The process is inhumane. Even application to the Marawi Compensation Board (MCB) is difficult. They even prioritize illegal claimants,” Madale said. “I hope our government …

author: labor4pal
title: Dezionizing the University of California
content:
Sean Malloy and Ethnic Studies Council at UC

In September 2025, I wrote a guest post for Chris Newfield’s blog that highlighted the complicity of UC leadership and the Academic Senate in federal attacks on the university under the guise of combating antisemitism. In a follow-up guest post in May 2026, I identified Zionism as the driving force behind many of the external and internal threats to the UC and its faculty, staff, and students. Building on those earlier writings, I want to explore at some length what it would mean to “dezionize” the University of California. Anti-Zionism is not new and has existed since the creation of the Zionist political movement. Given the stakes of the current moment, however, it is not enough to be simply anti-Zionist in orientation. It is past time that we consider the real, material steps that we must take to both sever the UC’s connections to Zionism and address the current and past harms created by those connections.

Dezionization entails not only ending the UC’s complicity in the genocidal actions of the Israeli state (which would include divestment and the end of formal research and teaching collaborations with Israeli-linked entities), but also confronting the role of Zionist organizations, donors, Regents, and administrators in repression targeted at members of the university community. Since 2023, students, faculty, and staff have been the subject of individual discipline and surveillance while entire university policies have been written or re-written to institutionalize compulsory Zionism and stifle those who would speak out on behalf of Palestinian life. Confronting and redressing these individual and structural harms is a crucial element of any meaningful dezionization effort. And while addressing the issues of post-10/7 complicity and repression are important immediate goals, dezionization also requires an honest accounting of the historical role of Zionism at the UC. Building on the flawed but necessary efforts of universities to acknowledge their historical connections to slavery and indigenous genocide and disposession, dezionization must also involve acknowledging and at least attempting to redress past harms resulting from the UC’s long entanglement with Zionism.

Thanks for reading Ethnic Studies Council @ UC! Subscribe for free to receive new posts and support my work.Subscribe

Dezionization does not require that individual staff, faculty, or students renounce their own personal beliefs. It does insist that the UC as an institution should neither advance nor be beholden to a political project that has fueled genocide in historic Palestine and repression on our own campuses.

Dezionization is neither an easy task nor will it solve all of the problems currently confronting the UC. Ultimately, however, the current status quo is both immoral and untenable and those who care about the university’s future are going to need to commit to a series of radical changes which include, but are not limited to, confronting the corrosive effects of Zionism. If pursued correctly, the process of dezionization will itself contribute to making the university more democratic, anti-racist, and accountable to all. And while I have focused on the UC in this essay because it is where I have worked and organized for 21 years, my goal in writing this is to spark conversation about how we might move forward with dezionization in all the institutions in which we are entangled, wherever those might be.

Before considering what dezionization might look like in practice, it is important to directly confront the question of what Zionism is — and what it is not. Contemporary defenders of Israel have mounted an aggressive campaign asserting that Zionism is an integral part of Jewish religious andethnic identity. In a 2022 complaint filed against the UC Berkeley law school with the Department of Education targeting several student organizations who refused to platform Zionist speakers, attorneys Gabriel Groisman and Arsen Ostrovsky asserted that “A rejection of Zionism. . . is an act of antisemitism and direct assault upon the very core ethnic and racial identity of Jewish students.” Kenneth Marcus, a former George W. Bush and Donald Trump political appointee who directs the Zionist lawfare institution (the Louis D. author: Rizomatica
title: Comunidad María Colipi Viuda de Maril manifiesta su apoyo a los PPM David y Javier Mariñán Millahual
content:
Tirua 5 de Octubre de 2026


Carta de Apoyo David y Javier Mariñán


Sres.


A quien corresponda:


A través de esta carta, venimos a manifestar nuestro apoyo moral y respaldo a los miembros de nuestra comunidad, David Mariñán Millahual y Javier Mariñán Millahual, quienes han sido condenados por el Tribunal Oral en lo Penal de Cañete, a la pena de 84 años de prisión.


Los hemanos David y Javier Mariñán son miembros activos de nuestra Comunidad Indigena Maria Colipi Viuda de Maril, residen aquí desde su infancia y, hasta el momento de ser encarcelados, participaban cotidianamente de las actividades propias de nuestra cultura mapuche, destacando en su interés por las prácticas culturales tradicionales.


Es de destacar que, en el caso de David Mariñán, él llegó a presentarse al Tribunal de Cañete voluntariamente al enterarse que era requerido por una causa en la que salió unánimemente absuelto. Posteriomente, fueron notificados de esta nueva investigación en su contra, en el cual ambos fueron condenados de una forma poco transparente, pues su supuesta participación en los hechos se basa solamente en el testimonio de testigos protegidos.


La familia de los hermanos David y Javier Mariñán nos ha comunicado su decisión de acudir a tribunales internacionales si es que no obtienen justicia en Chile, lo cual como comunidad respaldamos, pues el año 2014 la Corte Interamericana ya condenó al Estado de Chile en un caso similar.


A través de esta carta saludamos a nuestros socios David y Javier Mariñăn Millahual, solidarizando con ellos y su familia en estos momentos difíciles que enfrentan.


COMUNIDAD INDIGENA MARIA COLIPI VIUDA DE MARIL

author: groundxero
title: এসআরএফটিআই-তে শিক্ষার্থী বরখাস্ত, উপাচার্যের ইস্তফার দাবিতে চলছে ধর্না মঞ্চ, পরিস্থিতি জটিল
content:
“… আমরা চেয়ারম্যান ও মন্ত্রকের হস্তক্ষেপ দাবি করেই যাব ও উপাচার্য ইস্তফা না দেওয়া পর্যন্ত আন্দোলন চলবে,” বললেন বরখাস্ত হওয়া এসআরএফটিআই-এর এক শিক্ষার্থী।


 


সুদর্শনা চক্রবর্তীর

 প্রতিবেদন


 


গত ২৭ সেপ্টেম্বর থেকে কলকাতার সত্যজিৎ রায় ফিল্ম অ্যান্ড টেলিভিশন ইনস্টিটিউট-এ পরপর দু’বার বিজেপি-আরএসএস আশ্রিত হিন্দুত্ববাদী দুষ্কৃতিদের আক্রমণ এবং শিক্ষা প্রতিষ্ঠানের উপাচার্যের কার্যৎ শিক্ষার্থী-বিরোধী মনোভাব ও পদক্ষেপের জন্য শিক্ষার্থীরা ক্লাস বয়কট ও শান্তিপূর্ণ অবস্থান-ধর্ণার পথ বেছে নেওয়ায় প্রতিষ্ঠানের পঠন-পাঠনে অচলাবস্থা তৈরি হয়েছে।


 


এরই মাঝে গত ১৫ অক্টোবর ছ’জন পড়ুয়াকে বরখাস্তের চিঠি পাঠানো হয়েছে। যে চিঠিতে বরখাস্তের কারণ ও সময়সীমা কিছুই সঠিকভাবে উল্লিখিত নয়। এই বরখাস্তের চিঠির বিষয়ে পড়ুয়ারা ইতিমধ্যেই আইনি ব্যবস্থা নেওয়ার দিকে এগিয়েছে। আচমকাই ১৫ অক্টোবর এই বরখাস্তের চিঠি পাওয়ার পর ১৬ অক্টোবর শিক্ষার্থীরা জরুরি ভিত্তিতে একটি সাংবাদিক সম্মেলনের ডাক দিন। তাঁরা প্রতিষ্ঠানের ভেতরে ধর্ণা মঞ্চের সামনে এই সাংবাদিক সম্মেলন করতে চাইলেও কর্তৃপক্ষের নির্দেশে দীর্ঘ সময় টালবাহানার পর সাংবাদিকদের প্রতিষ্ঠানের ভেতরে ঢোকার অনুমতি দেওয়া হয় না। শেষ পর্যন্ত বন্ধ মূল ফটকের ভেতর থেকেই বাইরে দাঁড়ানো সাংবাদিকদের সঙ্গে সাংবাদিক সম্মেলন করেন শিক্ষার্থীরা।


 


এই সাংবাদিক সম্মেলনে অংশ নেওয়া শিক্ষার্থীরা বারেবারেই যে বিষয়টির উপর জোর দিচ্ছিলেন তা হল – উপাচার্য নিজের বিবৃতি, কাজকর্ম, শিক্ষার্থীদের প্রতি নির্দেশের মধ্যে দিয়ে বারেবারেই যা প্রমাণ করার চেষ্টা করছেন তা হল, প্রতিষ্ঠানে সব কিছু স্বাভাবিক আছে এবং শান্তিপূর্ণ প্রতিবাদরত শিক্ষার্থীদের প্রতিবাদ তুলে নিয়ে ক্লাসে ফেরার জন্য চাপ দেওয়া হচ্ছে। এবং স্টুডেন্টস ইউনিয়ন-এর হাতে গোনা কয়েক জন শিক্ষার্থীই এই ক্লাস বয়কট ও অবস্থান বিক্ষোভে মদত দিচ্ছেন, বাকিরা সকলেই ক্লাস চালু করার পক্ষে। ১৫ অক্টোবর, সাংবাদিক সম্মেলনে অংশ নেওয়া পড়ুয়ারা এই বিষয়ে স্পষ্টতই জানান একেবারেই নতুন ও চলতি ব্যাচের সিনিয়র পড়ুয়ারা, এবং প্রতিষ্ঠানের সমস্ত ছাত্রছাত্রী একজোটভাবে এই প্রতিবাদে শামিল, তা আদপেই বরখাস্তের নোটিস পাঠানো পাঁচ-ছ’জন শিক্ষার্থী বা শুধুই স্টুডেন্টস ইউনিয়ন-এর বিষয় নয়।


 


বরখাস্তের বিষয়টির পাশে এদিন শিক্ষার্থীরা সরাসরি অভিযোগ আনেন সিকিওরিটি অফিসার পি কে, মুন্সি-র বিরূদ্ধে। উপাচার্যের পাশাপাশি মূলত তিনিই শিক্ষার্থীর বিরূদ্ধে নানাবিধ পদক্ষেপ নেওয়া, তাঁদের নানাভাবে হেনস্থা করছেন বলে অভিযোগ করেন তাঁরা। অন্যদিকে উপাচার্য বা অন্য কোনো কর্মীদের সঙ্গে কোনোরকম দুর্ব্যবহারের অভিযোগ সর্বৈব মিথ্যা বলেও জানান তাঁরা। এই পি কে মুন্সির বিরূদ্ধে প্রতিষ্ঠানের একজন অত্যন্ত বরিষ্ঠ মহিলা কর্মী, যিনি ১৯৯৫ থেকে কর্মরত ও শিক্ষার্থীদের প্রতি সমমনোভাবাপন্ন তিনি হেনস্থার অভিযোগ আনলেও কোনো রকম পদক্ষেপ নেওয়া হয়নি বলেও সেই অভিযোগপত্র সহ শিক্ষার্থীরা জানান।


 


তারেক, সুদীপ, অ্যারন, জয়দীপ, আকাঙ্খা, ব্লসম (স্টুডেন্টস ইউনিয়ন-এর সভাপতি) বক্তব্য রাখেন।


 


“আমরা সারা ভারতের বিভিন্ন প্রান্ত থেকে অনেক ফিল্ম স্কুলে পড়ার সুযোগ ছেড়ে এখানে পড়তে আসি। অথচ আমাদের হস্টেলের সুবিধা প্রথম থেকেই দেওয়া হয় না। আর আমরা গত কয়েক সপ্তাহ ধরে এখানে যা দেখছি তাতে আমাদের নিরাপত্তা নিয়ে আমরা চিন্তিত। একজন মুসলিম হিসাবেও এখানে উপাচার্য ও প্রতিষ্ঠানের আচরণে আমি প্রান্তিক বোধ করছি,”

 বলেন তারেক।


 


২৭ সেপ্টেম্বর ও ৪ অক্টোবরের আক্রমণের পরেও প্রতিষ্ঠানের প্রশাসনিক স্তর থেকে শিক্ষার্থীদের সঙ্গে কোনো রকম যোগাযোগ করা হয়নি। বাইরের যে ফ্যাসিবাদী শক্তির আক্রমণ সারা দেশ জুড়ে দেখা যাচ্ছে, তারই প্রতিফলন যেন প্রতিষ্ঠানের ভেতরেও দেখা যাচ্ছে বলে শিক্ষার্থীরা মন্তব্য করেন। এই আক্রমণের বিরূদ্ধে যাঁরাই উপাচার্যকে দায় স্বীকার করতে বলেছেন তাঁদেরই টার্গেট করা হচ্ছে। যাঁরা ৪ অক্টোবরের পর উপাচার্যকে সাময়িক ঘেরাও ও প্রতিবাদে অংশ নেন, তাঁরা বাদেও যাঁরা সেদিন ছিলেন না বা এমনকি কলকাতার বাইরে ছিলেন তাঁদেরও শো-কজ চিঠি পাঠানো হয়েছে। নিয়মশৃঙ্খলা ভঙ্গের অভিযোগ আনা হচ্ছে শিক্ষার্থীদের বিরূদ্ধে, যেখানে তাঁদের নিরাপত্তার দায় প্রতিষ্ঠান নিচ্ছে না। কেবলই তাঁদের নানা রকম ভয় দেখিয়ে ও তাঁদের উপর চাপ সৃষ্টি করে ক্লাস শুরু করতে বলা হচ্ছে – যার চরম উদাহরণ কোনো রকম আগাম ইঙ্গিত ছাড়াই শিক্ষার্থীদের বরখাস্তের নোটিস পাঠানো। উপস্থিত শিক্ষার্থীরা সকলেই জানান যে নব নিযুক্ত উপাচার্য এতদিন পর্যন্ত শিক্ষার্থীদের করা সমস্ত অভিযোগের প্রতিই কোনো রকম প্রতিক্রিয়া না জানানোয় এবং তাঁর পুরোপুরি ফ্যাসিবাদীসুলভ শিক্ষার্থী বিরোধী আচরণের জন্য শিক্ষার্থীরা একজোট ও একমত হয়ে তাঁর ইস্তফার দাবিতেই অনড় থাকছেন।


 


জয়দীপ যিনি দুষ্কৃতিদের আক্রমে আহত হয়েছিলেন ও এখনো যাঁর একটি অস্ত্রোপচার বাকি, তিনি জানান উপাচার্যের সঙ্গে দেখা করতে চেয়েও তিনি পারেননি। উপাচার্য কোনো অবস্থাতেই আন্দোলনরত ও দাবিপত্র জমা দেওয়া শিক্ষার্থী বা প্রতিনিধিদের সঙ্গে দেখা করতে রাজি হননি। এমতাবস্থায় পড়ুয়াদের দাবি – “

সব কিছু স্বাভাবিক এমনটা ভান করা অবিলম্বে বন্ধ করতে হবে এবং সংবাদমাধ্যম, সংশ্লিষ্ট মন্ত্রক সর্বত্র আসল ছবিটি, পড়ুয়াদের নিরাপত্তাহীনতার বিষয়টি তুলে ধরতে হবে।”


 


ধর্ম, বর্ণ, লিঙ্গ পরিচিতি নিয়ে সদ্য আসা উপাচার্য সন্তোষ আজমের চূড়ান্ত বৈষম্য করছেন বলেও …

author: Redazione_web
title: Quando il Messico incontra la Sicilia
content:
Domenica 27 settembre, nella Piazza del Villaggio di Locogrande, a Misiliscemi, c’è stato un evento che è stato un toccasana al cuore e alla testa. Un’iniziativa pubblica promossa da una rete di realtà del territorio ha trasformato una piccola piazza di provincia nel punto d’incontro tra la nostra terra e le lotte di tutto il mondo.


La mattinata si è aperta nel modo più semplice e vivo possibile: un laboratorio artistico e creativo collettivo, aperto a tutti e tutte. Già dalle dieci del mattino la piazza si è popolata di colori, pennarelli e grandi cartelli da riempire insieme. È stato uno spazio informale e leggero, ma allo stesso tempo profondamente radicato nei nostri problemi reali. Tra una scritta e una risata, lavoratori, residenti, attivisti e curiosi si sono ritrovati fianco a fianco. E parlando dei cartelli che stavamo preparando sull’acqua, sul diritto alla vita, contro la base militare e gli F-35 a Trapani-Birgi, sono nate riflessioni spontanee, genuine, fatte di sguardi e condivisione. In quel fare manuale e spensierato c’era già l’alternativa: riprendersi i propri spazi pubblici partendo dalla cura e dallo stare insieme senza deleghe.


Da quel clima di laboratorio, la mattinata è sfociata con naturalezza nel momento assembleare, iniziato verso l’una. Ed è lì che il respiro della giornata si è allargato in modo straordinario, ascoltando direttamente i rappresentanti della delegazione internazionale arrivata dal Messico. A prendere la parola per prima è stata la rappresentante del Centro per i Diritti Umani Frayba, portando con sé il peso e la lucidità di chi opera quotidianamente nel Chiapas, a fianco delle comunità oppresse. Ascoltarla è stato un pugno nello stomaco e insieme una spinta immensa: ci ha raccontato la violenza feroce e sistematica subita da chi difende i diritti umani, la terra e la vita contro i grandi interessi delle multinazionali e dei governi, ricordandoci cosa significhi fare i conti con i vicini di casa desaparecidos e con una militarizzazione che calpesta ogni forma di dignità umana.


Subito dopo, l’intervento dei delegati del Congresso Nazionale Indigeno (CNI) ha allargato ulteriormente lo sguardo, portando la voce viva dei popoli originari che resistono contro l’espropriazione dei territori e la devastazione ambientale. Hanno raccontato di come le comunità continuino a organizzarsi dal basso proponendo invece che imponendo, raccogliendo la forza radicale dello zapatismo per praticare l’autogoverno e difendere la propria terra rifiutando la logica cinica del profitto. Certo, chi vive lì affronta dinamiche e tragedie di una gravità per noi quasi inimmaginabile, eppure ascoltandoli parlare in quella piazza di Misiliscemi, la sensazione più nitida è stata un’altra, cioè che tutto il mondo è intrinsecamente legato.


Perché mentre ascoltavi le loro storie, capivi perfettamente che la mano che devasta i territori e calpesta i diritti laggiù è la stessa identica mano che in provincia di Trapani impone le basi militari, investe i nostri risparmi nel campo di addestramento per i piloti degli F-35 e condanna la nostra terra alla sete, all’abbandono e all’emigrazione giovanile. Il sistema economico, statale e militare che ci governa è totalizzante e globale, non fa sconti a nessuno e sfrutta le periferie del mondo per i propri profitti.


Ma la lezione più grande di quell’assemblea non è stata la constatazione amara di quanto questo sistema sia cinico: la vera forza è stata scoprire che la resistenza è altrettanto globale. In quella piazza si è toccato con mano cosa significhi l’internazionalismo: non una parola vuota da convegno, ma sguardi, parole condivise, mani che si stringono e la consapevolezza che i nostri problemi non sono affatto isolati. La nostra piccola vertenza locale contro la base di Birgi prende forza e respiro quando si collega alle lotte di chi, in ogni angolo del pianeta, rifiuta di essere merce o scarto.


La convergenza tra i popoli ci ha ricordato che la vera sicurezza non si costruisce con gli aerei d’attacco o con i confini armati, ma curando la terra, difendendo l’acqua e stringendo legami autentici di solidarietà. La strada per cambiare le cose è lunga, irta e difficile, come sappiamo bene qui in Sicilia, ma l’incontro a Locogrande ci ha lasciato una certezza luminosa: non siamo soli. E sapere di camminare insieme a chi, da lontano, lotta con la stessa nostra dignità, ti dà una spinta formidabile per continuare a fare la tua parte, qui, nel nostro piccolo …

author: Mag
title: Immer nur Behindertenwerkstätten: Warum verdienen Menschen mit Behinderung so wenig? Und wo bleibt die Inklusion?
content:
Dossier


„

In der Pandemie sind beinahe unbemerkt Löhne in Behindertenwerkstätten gekürzt worden. Schon vorher ließ sich von den Geld kaum leben. (…) Der Lohn der Beschäftigten in Behinderten-Werkstätten setzt sich in Deutschland aus mehreren Teilen zusammen: Ein sogenanntes Arbeitsförderungsgeld von 52 Euro wird aus Töpfen des Landes gezahlt. Dazu kommt ein Grundlohn von 89 Euro und ein individuell festgelegter Steigerungsbetrag. Diese beiden Posten müssen die Werkstätten selbst erwirtschaften. Als die Corona-Pandemie Deutschland erreichte, schlossen die Betreiber ihre Werkstätten für Menschen mit Behinderung. In der Folge konnten viele Aufträge nicht mehr erfüllt werden. Der Steigerungslohn entfiel. (…) 19 Prozent der Werkstätten, die an der Umfrage teil nahmen, gaben an, Löhne gekürzt zu haben. Weitere 18 Prozent gaben an, dass Kürzungen absehbar sind. Insgesamt hat sich in der Umfrage gezeigt, dass die Auswirkungen der Krise verzögert in den Werkstätten ankommen

…“

Artikel von Fabian Hillebrand vom 14.11.2020 im ND online

 

 und auch dazu:


Gerechtigkeit statt Almosen: Die GFF geht mit Jürgen Linnemann gegen das diskriminierende Entgeltsystem in „Werkstätten für behinderte Menschen“ (WfbM) vor Gericht


Mindestlohn in Werkstätten: Der sitzende Leistungsträger


„

Jürgen Linnemann hat 40 Jahre in Werkstätten für Menschen mit Behinderung gearbeitet. Jetzt zieht er für den Mindestlohn vor Gericht. (…) Sie klagen vor dem Arbeitsgericht Münster darauf, dass die Werkstatt ihm die Differenz zwischen seinem bisherigen Arbeitsentgelt und dem Mindestlohn zahlt. Linnemann sei Arbeitnehmer und habe dementsprechend Anrecht auf den Mindestlohn, so die Begründung. Der gesetzliche Mindestlohn müsse zudem auch in Werkstätten gelten. Anfang September soll das Arbeitsgericht eine Entscheidung treffen. Falls es beides verneint, will die GFF das derzeitige Entgeltsystem auf Vereinbarkeit mit Verfassungs-, Unions- und Völkerrecht überprüfen lassen. Bislang fehlen entsprechende Gerichtsentscheidungen. Das könnte sieben bis zehn Jahre dauern, wie Linnemanns Anwältin schätzt. Bis dahin ist er bereits in Rente. (…)


Das Sondersystem der Werkstätten hat der Bundesrepublik bereits zwei Rügen durch den UN-Fachausschuss für die Rechte von Menschen mit Behinderungen beschert. Reformpläne gibt es zahlreiche. Erst 2023 kam eine Studie im Auftrag der damaligen Ampel-Regierung zu dem Ergebnis, dass ein steuersubventioniertes Mindestlohnmodell besser funktionieren und zu mehr Gerechtigkeit führen würde. Andere fordern für einen inklusiven Arbeitsmarkt die Abschaffung der Werkstätten

…“

Artikel von Sarah Yolanda Koss vom 15.10.2026 in ND online

 


Nur 200 Euro Monatslohn. Jürgen Linnemann will per Musterprozess erreichen, dass in Werkstätten für behinderte Menschen Mindestlohn bezahlt wird. Er klagt gegen Lohndumping.


„

Der Mindestlohn von 13,90 Euro pro Stunde gilt fast überall – nicht aber in Werkstätten für behinderte Menschen. Jürgen Linnemann will das ändern. Er arbeitet in den Freckenhorster Werkstätten (NRW). Beim Arbeitsgericht Münster hat er auf Bezahlung von Mindestlohn geklagt. Es ist ein Musterprozess von bundesweiter Bedeutung.


Jürgen Linnemann arbeitet 24,3 Stunden pro Woche und erhält nur einen Stundenlohn von rund 2 Euro. Im Monat macht das knapp 200 Euro. Der 57-Jährige ist Teil eines Teams, das Dokumente digitalisiert. Bevor die Papiere gescannt werden, entfernt Linnemann die Tackerklammern. Für seine Tätigkeit im Werkstattrat – einer Art Betriebsrat – hat er bereits das Bundesverdienstkreuz erhalten.


Jetzt klagt Linnemann für eine bessere Bezahlung. Mit Unterstützung der Gesellschaft für Freiheitsrechte (GFF) und der NGO Sozialhelden hat Linnemann Klage beim Arbeitsgericht Münster erhoben. Er will 1.300 Euro zusätzlich pro Monat, den Mindestlohn eben. Die Klage hat große praktische Relevanz. Bundesweit arbeiten rund 300.000 Personen in rund 700 „Werkstätten für behinderte Menschen“ (WfbM), so der offizielle Titel. Voraussetzung ist, dass man zwar arbeitsfähig ist, aber auf dem normalen Arbeitsmarkt keine Chance hätte. Rund 75 der so Beschäftigten haben eine geistige Behinderung, 20 Prozent haben psychische Beeinträchtigungen, nur 5 Prozent haben eine körperliche Behinderung

…“

Artikel von Christian Rath vom 3.9.2026 in der taz online

title: Gök yarılırken cepheye sürülür gibi: İstanbul’un altında kalanlar
content:
Valilik “zorunlu olmadıkça dışarı çıkmayın” dedi. Fabrikada, tersanede, sokakta, hastanede çalışanlar için o zorunluluğu yine patronlar belirledi.

19 yaşındaki Mazlum Gürbüz, 29 Eylül'de Eyüpsultan Kemerburgaz'daki bir şantiyede yağmur hafifler hafiflemez tabela montajı için sahaya geri çağrıldı. Elindeki metal çıta yüksek gerilim hattına değdi, bir haftalık yaşam mücadelesinin ardından 5 Ekim'de hayatını kaybetti. Çocukluk arkadaşı Levent Çelik, o gün neden işi bırakamadıklarını şöyle anlatmıştı: “İşten çıkarılma korkusuyla mecbur kaldık, çalıştık.”

Aradan iki hafta geçmeden İstanbul ve çevresi çok daha büyük bir sağanakla boğuştu. Valilik okulları tatil etti, kamuda yalnızca belli gruplara idari izin verdi, motokuryeleri trafikten çekti ve halka “zorunlu olmadıkça dışarı çıkmayın” çağrısı yaptı. Özel sektörde çalışan milyonlar için ise tek bir düzenleme çıkmadı.

Kocaeli Başiskele'de Hayat Kimya ve Özka Lastik fabrikalarını su bastı, işçi servisleri tekerlek hizasına kadar suya gömüldü. Arslanbey OSB'de işçiler fabrikaya suların içinden geçerek ulaştı. Ford Otosan'da su basan bölümlerde işçiler sırılsıklam çalıştı. Tuzla ve Yalova tersanelerinde üretim bir an bile aksamadı, vinçlerin yalnızca “kontrollü” kullanılması istendi.

Bunlar ulaşabildiklerimiz. Ulaşamadığımız nice işyerinde de afet koşullarında bile kâr hesabı işçinin canının önüne kondu. Bu koşullarda çalıştırılan her işçi, kapıda bekleyen yeni bir Mazlum Gürbüz demek.

PTT'de taşeron olarak çalışan üç çocuk babası bir dağıtımcı, paketleri sokak sokak yürüyerek dağıtıyor. Çarşamba 165 paketle çıktı, ancak 135'ini teslim edebildi. Dün yine sokaktaydı: “Valilik 'zorunlu olmadıkça çıkmayın' demiş ama bize kimse 'bugün çalışmayın' demedi. Bu sabah da 130 paketle çıktım, bu en az 15 kilometre yol demek. Bizim gibi insanlar için zorunluluk bu.”

Dağıtımcıları yağmurda sokağa iten prim sistemi. 60 paketin üzerine çıkınca prim devreye giriyor: “Üstüne bir 60 daha koyarsam bir yevmiye daha almış gibi oluyorum. Böyle çalışmasam yetiremem. Böyle de yetmiyor gerçi.” Yetmediği için PTT'den sonra Maslak'ta servis şoförlüğü yapıyor, dün eve ancak 23.30'da girebildi: “İnsan işi değil ama başka yolu yok. PTT'den aldığım para ancak çocukların okuluna, beslenmesine gidiyor. Kirayı, faturayı kim ödeyecek?”

Uber Eats'te çalışan bir kurye, sabah birkaç paket teslim edip eve dönmüş ama çalışmayı sürdüren arkadaşlarına kızamıyor: “Hepimiz borçla yaşıyoruz. Ben çalışmadım çünkü bir dayanağım var. Dayanağı olmayan adam mecbur çalışacak, hem de bu havada daha çok çalışacak.” Sokakta kurye azalınca kişi başına düşen paket artıyor, sağanak birçok kurye için bir “fırsata” dönüşüyor. Boynuna kadar suya gömülmüş kurye görüntüsü için şunları söylüyor: “O insanı zincirle sürüsen suya sokamazsın. Ama bizi kendilerine köle ettiler, sıcak evimizden kendi ayağımızla çıkıp suyun içine giriyoruz.”

Motokurye yasağı ise sabit ücreti olmayan kurye için gelirsiz gün demek: “Millet ne yiyecek diye düşünmek yasağı koyanların görevi değil mi? Bunu ücretli izne dönüştürmek çok mu zor? Şirket paketini düşünüyor, devlet gelişigüzel yasak koyuyor, kurye ne yapacak? Beni düşünmediğin yasak önlem değil.”

Bakırköy Belediyesi'nin süpürge işçileri yağmurun bıraktıklarını temizlemek için sahaya sürüldü. Daha önce de haberlerimize konu olan soyunma kulübeleri artık kullanılamaz durumda: “Sivil kıyafetlerimizi koyacak yerimiz bile yok. Dün mesai bitiminde üstümü değiştirmeye girdiğimde kıyafetlerimi su içinde buldum. Herkes evine kaçmanın yolunu ararken kenti temizleyen işçilere reva gördükleri soyunma yeri bu mu?” İşçiler insani dinlenme alanı talebini yılın başında, sözleşme sürecinde dile getirmişti: “Kulak arkası ettiler. Şimdi damı akan, çamur içindeki kulübelerde üstümüzü değiştiriyoruz.”

Park bahçeler ve fen işleri müdürlüğündeki işçi sayısı ise eski başkan Kerimoğlu döneminde 95'ken işten çıkarmalar ve emekliliklerle 35'e düşmüş. Bir işçi anlatıyor: “Dün koca Bakırköy'ün felaketini 5 işçi 24 saat çalışarak toparlamaya çalıştı. 20'nin üzerinde ağaç devrilmiş, onlarca evi, dükkânı su basmış. Hepsine yetişmeye çalışıyoruz.”

Okmeydanı Perpa'da özel bir şirkette çalışan bir emekçi, dün 16.00'da izin alıp çıktı. 40 dakika otobüs bekledi, Sünnet Köprüsü'nde trafik kilitlenince yağmurun altında Alibeyköy metrosuna yürüdü: “Yanımızda kadın, erkek, genç, yaşlı vardı. Hasta bir teyzenin koluna girip oraya kadar getirdik.” Metrodan sonra Gazi'nin girişine kadar yine yürüdü, eve 19.50'de varabildi. Evi uzak iş …

title: Sağlık Bakanlığı: Eşitsizlikleri devam ettirmekte kararlıyız!
content:
Sağlık Bakanlığı İstatistik Yıllığı (SBİY) 2025 Haber Bülteni, 30 Eylül 2025, çarşamba günü, saat 17:00’de 

(!)

 yayımlandı. İlki 12 yıl önce, 2014 yılında yine eylül ayının son günü SBİY 2013 Haber Bülteni olarak yayımlanmıştı. Bülten, istatistik yıllığından yaklaşık üç, dört ay önce daha az sayıdaki veri grubunu kapsayacak şekilde yayımlanıyor. Bununla birlikte, ölümlülük, aşılama ve hizmet kullanımıyla ilgili bir önceki yılın verilerine 9-10 ay sonra da olsa ulaşabilmiş oluyoruz. Ve Türkiye’nin dokuz ilinin bulunduğu coğrafyada yaşayanların, AKP’li yılların bundan önceki 16 yılında olduğu gibi, 17nci yılında da değişmeyen bir biçimde sağlık ve sosyoekonomik eşitsizlere mahkûm edilmiş olduğunu görüyoruz. Bu haftaki yazıda söz konusu durumu ve AKP’li Sağlık Bakanlığı’nın verileri kendine saklamak gibi bir özelliğini kendilerinin sunduğu kaynaklar üzerinden ele alacağım.


ERİŞ BİLALOĞLU YAZDI


Yeni Bir Sıfırlama Çabası mı: Türkiye’de Bebek Ölüm Hızı


29 Ocak 2015


AKP’li bakanlık verileri kendine saklıyor


AKP tarafından 2002 yılında kurulan 58. Hükümet’e kadar sağlık ve sağlık hizmetleriyle ilgili veriler yıllardır istatistik yıllıklarıyla düzenli olarak kamuoyuyla paylaşılıyordu. Ancak

58. Hükümet ve o kabinenin Sağlık Bakanı Recep Akdağ ile birlikte, sağlık ve sağlık hizmetleriyle ilgili veriler kamuoyundan 2011 yılına kadar saklandı,

paylaşılmadı. Dünya Sağlık Örgütü başta olmak üzere, Türkiye’nin üyesi olduğu uluslararası kuruluşların talebi üzerine, bir AKP Hükümeti ve Sağlık Bakanı olarak ilk defa 2011 yılında, 2008 yılına ait veriler “Sağlık Bakanlığı Sağlık İstatistikleri Yıllığı 2008” başlığında Bakan Akdağ’ın önsözüyle yayımlandı. O nedenle Türkiye’nin 2003-2007 yıllarına ait sağlık ve sağlık hizmetleriyle ilgili verileri diğer yıllar gibi düzenli bir biçimde bugüne kadar paylaşılmadı.


Sağlık ve sağlık hizmetleriyle ilgili istatistikler, 2011 yılından sonra, Sağlık Bakanlığı ve Türkiye İstatistik Kurumu (TÜİK) tarafından düzenli olarak yayımlanıyor. TÜİK, özelikle doğurganlık ve ölümlülükle ilgili verileri Merkezi Nüfus İdaresi Sistemi (MERNİS) üzerinden iller düzeyinde, sağlık harcamalarıyla ilgili verileri Hazine ve Maliye Bakanlığı ile Sosyal Güvenlik Kurumu (SGK) ve yerel yönetimlerden ve “Hanehalkı Bütçe Anketi” çalışması üzerinden, hastalıklarla ilgili verileri de “Türkiye Sağlık Araştırması” üzerinden sağlıyor. Sağlık Bakanlığı da bu verileri kullanıp yaptığı hesaplamaları ve sağlık kurumları, sağlık emekçileri, ilaç, sağlık hizmetleri kullanımı vb. verileri Türkiye’nin makro düzeyde ekonomik ve sosyo-ekonomik yapıya göre gruplandığı 12 bölge, İstatistiki Bölge Bilgileri Sınıflaması-1 (İBBS-1), üzerinden paylaşıyor. Bununla birlikte, 

Sağlık Bakanlığı kaynakları üzerinden 81 ilden herhangi birinin sağlık ve sağlık hizmetleri verilerini, durumunu öğrenebilmek mümkün olamıyor.

Çünkü Sağlık Bakanlığı illerin verilerini yayımlamayı uzun zamandır tercih etmiyor.


Tabip Odası Bebek Ölümlerine Önlem Paketini Açıkladı


25 Eylül 2008


Bebek ölüm hızı önemli bir toplumsal sağlık düzeyi göstergesidir


Toplumların sağlık düzeyinin değerlendirilmesi ve izlenebilmesi amacıyla “bebek ölüm hızı”, “beş yaş altı ölüm hızı” ve “doğumda beklenen yaşam süresi” uluslararası alanda sıklıkla kullanılan, kabul görmüş üç değişkendir. Bunlar aynı zamanda, ülkelerin gelişmişlik düzeyi göstergeleri arasında da yer almaktadır. Çünkü, bu üç gösterge bir ülkede, bölgede, ilde vb. öncelikle beslenme, barınma, alt yapı ve eğitim başta olmak üzere, sosyoekonomik koşulların durumu ve sağlık hizmetlerinin ulaşılabilir olup olmamasıyla sağlık hizmetlerinin niteliğinden doğrudan etkilenmektedir.


Gebeliğin herhangi bir döneminde, canlı doğan bebeğin, birinci doğum gününü göremeden ölmesi, nüfus bilim (demografi) ve tıp alanında bebek ölümü olarak kabul edilmekte, tanımlanmaktadır. Bir ilde, bölgede ve/veya ülkede yıl içinde canlı doğan her bin bebekten kaçının birinci doğum gününü göremeden öldüğü de bebek ölüm hızı olarak tanımlanmaktadır. Bebek ölümlerinden doğumdan sonraki 

ilk ay içinde gerçekleşen

ölümler genellikle anne adayının sağlık, beslenme ve eğitim durumuyla doğum öncesi izlemlerin yapılıp yapılmaması ve doğum koşullarıyla ilişkilidir.
