author: dev
title: Crimes, casse, émeute et délinquance, polar et encoignures de portes
content:
Journaliste et écrivain marseillais

 [

1

]

, Cédric Fabre raconte ici les réactions au 17 octobre entendues à Cognac, l'un des derniers grands festivals du polar avec une ligne politique clairement engagée. Ou comment jusque dans la littérature historiquement

sociale

, on préfère parfois refuser le réel et choisir le déni.


(à l'arrache)


Pardon d'enfoncer à nouveau les portes ouvertes mais il y en a encore qui se cognent aux encoignures.


On était au formidable festival de polar de Cognac, la journée insurrectionnelle du samedi 17 octobre. Dans la salle de la Salamandre, avec des amis et amies chers et chères, auteurs, autrices, réals, acteurs, actrices, lecteurs, lectrices, et surtout avec Dany et Bernard (l'un des derniers grands directeurs et organisateur de festival de polar qui défend les « petits » éditeurs, et surtout qui ne cesse de réaffirmer une ligne politique, celle qui fait la réputation de ce genre littéraire dit « engagé »), à parler livres, films et séries ou docs projetés dans la salle au-dessus, causer romans de barricades et d'insurrection, pendant que c'était dehors que ça se passait…


On a vu, revu, vérifié beaucoup de vidéos, parfois mal légendées, on a recoupé ce que racontaient les camarades, des scènes dont ils ont été témoins. La violence inouïe des flics (on connaissait) sur des gamins, des provocations multiples, des flics-casseurs, des flics-pilleurs, des tabassages en règle, des gazages à dose jamais vue avec nassage, sur des points de départ de manifs, donc des citoyens conduits à un état de colère et de révolte ultime, des manifestants venus de partout, lycéens (mineurs et majeurs), parents, étudiants, travailleurs, ouvriers, commerçants, minots des quartiers, black blocs… Même combat et mêmes slogans bien souvent, méthodes « divergentes » -aucune condamnation de ma part des uns ou des autres émeutiers /car tout cela ne serait pas arrivé si…


(Bon, on a recoupé autant que possible, mais de nombreuses infos restent effectivement, par ailleurs, invérifiables)


Alors qu'on se retrouve entre auteurs et autrices qui choisissent la fiction pour tenter, souvent, de définir ce que sont les contours du réel, de manière la plus réaliste possible, on se heurte, dans le réel, lors de nombreux échanges, à des gens qui ignorent et récusent la réalité… Je raconte que mes deux filles, dans deux manifs différentes, à Angoulême et à Marseille, ont été gazées et nassées d'emblée, à peine arrivées au point de rencontre, dans une ambiance pacifique, et l'on m'assure que non, que ce n'est pas arrivé, que ce sont les « casseurs » -comme si, à ce stade et dans ces lieux, le pillage et la casse sortaient par ailleurs miraculeusement du champ politique. Je discute avec un ancien flic qui écrit des romans, qui est persuadé que la police n'a jamais gazé d'entrée de jeu… Il n'a pas l'info, pourtant relayée partout, on a les témoignages en direct d'une femme qui était devant la mairie de Bordeaux avant d'arriver à Cognac, c'est sourcé, c'est vérifié et recoupé, mais non, « ça n'est pas arrivé près de chez vous ». On a le doc sur le maintien de l'ordre sur Arte, on a le copain qui connait bien le truc de l'intérieur et qui raconte comment les formations des CRS aujourd'hui incluent ce « savoir-faire », l'usage de la violence préventive et incitative, les techniques des « appariteurs », les flics-casseurs. Tout ça est sourcé, documenté, mais non. L'écrivain dit : « Non, je pense que c'est faux, ça n'arrive pas ». Ne vérifiant pas pour autant que c'est le factuel.


La question « d'où vient la violence ? » est constamment éludée ; il n'y a aucune lisibilité des événements.


Alors ils cherchent le « bon » mot, celui qui va bien ; nous on dit les émeutiers, pas les « casseurs » - résultat de la novlangue et de l'inculture, soit la triste conséquence de la fin de l'instruction pour tous et des politiques d'éducation populaire, qui touchent ceux qui n'ont pas appris, qui transfèrent alors leur frustration et haine poisseuse précisément sur les jeunes qui veulent, eux, apprendre (tout est cohérent, ici) ; l'Histoire de France, l'Histoire des luttes sociales et politiques sont devenues un héritage peu à peu « refusé ». (Trop de « dettes » dans l'héritage ? Tout ce que les acquis/conquis sociaux doivent aux luttes, aux combats de rue, à la casse, à une certaine forme de violence ?) Bref, des tas de gens ne croient pas le/au réel, ils pensent et estiment que le réel se trompe, ils verrouillent tout pour que le …

author: dev
title: « Assommons les groupuscules d'extrême gauche ! »
content:
Détournement du célèbre « Assommons les pauvres ! » de Charles Baudelaire (Les idées s'améliorent. Le sens des mots y participe. Le plagiat est nécessaire. Le progrès l'implique.).


Pendant quinze jours je m'étais confiné dans ma chambre, et je m'étais entouré des journaux et des chaînes d'information à la mode dans ce temps-là ; je veux parler de ces émissions où il est traité de l'art de rendre les peuples libres, tranquilles et obéissants, en vingt-quatre heures. J'avais donc digéré, — avalé, veux-je dire, — toutes les élucubrations de tous ces entrepreneurs de sécurité publique, — de ceux qui conseillent aux Français de sacrifier leurs libertés individuelles sur l'autel de la sécurité collective, et de ceux qui leur persuadent qu'ils vivent dans un pays livré aux professionnels du chaos. — On ne trouvera pas surprenant que je fusse alors dans un état d'esprit avoisinant le vertige ou la stupidité.


Il m'avait semblé seulement que je sentais, confiné au fond de mon intellect, le germe obscur d'une idée supérieure à toutes les formules de maintien de l'ordre dont j'avais récemment parcouru le dictionnaire. Mais ce n'était que l'idée d'une idée, quelque chose d'infiniment vague.


Et je sortis avec une grande soif. Car le goût passionné des mauvaises informations engendre un besoin proportionnel du grand air et des rafraîchissants.


Comme j'allais entrer dans un café, je rencontrai une manifestation. Des étudiants défilaient en brandissant des pancartes sur lesquelles étaient inscrites quelques revendications que je n'eus pas le loisir de déchiffrer. L'un d'eux, un jeune homme d'apparence chétive, portait un sac à dos et tenait à la main une pancarte sur laquelle on pouvait lire : « Moins de flics, plus de frites ! » Il avait un de ces regards inoubliables qui renverseraient les gouvernements, si les regards renversaient les gouvernements, et si les slogans faisaient tomber les ministres.


En même temps, j'entendis une voix qui chuchotait à mon oreille, une voix que je reconnus bien ; c'était celle d'un bon Ange, ou d'un bon Démon, qui m'accompagne partout. Puisque Socrate avait son bon Démon, pourquoi n'aurais-je pas mon bon Ange, et pourquoi n'aurais-je pas l'honneur, comme Socrate, d'obtenir mon brevet de civisme, signé du subtil Retailleau et du bien-avisé Bardella ?


Il existe cette différence entre le Démon de Socrate et le mien, que celui de Socrate ne se manifestait à lui que pour défendre, avertir, empêcher, et que le mien daigne prévenir, neutraliser, réprimer. Ce pauvre Socrate n'avait qu'un Démon prohibiteur ; le mien est un grand sécurisateur, le mien est un Démon d'ordre, ou Démon de pacification.


Or, sa voix me chuchotait ceci : « Celui-là seul est libre, qui vit en sécurité, et celui-là seul mérite la sécurité, qui ne trouble jamais l'ordre public. »


Immédiatement, je sautai sur mon étudiant. D'un seul coup de poing, je lui bouchai un œil, qui devint, en une seconde, gros comme une balle. Je cassai un de mes ongles à lui briser deux dents, et comme je ne me sentais pas assez fort, étant né délicat et m'étant peu exercé aux opérations de maintien de l'ordre, pour neutraliser rapidement ce jeune homme, je le saisis d'une main par le collet de son blouson, de l'autre, je l'empoignai à la gorge, et je me mis à lui secouer vigoureusement la tête contre un mur. Je dois avouer que j'avais préalablement inspecté les environs d'un coup d'œil, et que j'avais vérifié que, dans cette rue momentanément déserte, je me trouvais, pour un assez long temps, protégé par les agents de police, qui, à quelques pas de là, observaient avec une bienveillance toute républicaine les progrès de mon intervention.


Ayant ensuite, par un coup de pied lancé dans le dos, assez énergique pour briser les omoplates, terrassé ce dangereux représentant de l'ultragauche, je me saisis de sa pancarte tombée à terre, et je le battis avec l'énergie obstinée des gouvernements qui veulent rétablir l'ordre public.


Tout à coup, — ô miracle ! ô jouissance du citoyen qui vérifie l'excellence de sa théorie ! — je vis ce jeune corps se retourner, se redresser avec une énergie que je n'aurais jamais soupçonnée dans un individu si manifestement hostile aux valeurs de la République, et, avec un regard de haine qui me parut de bon augure, le petit professionnel du chaos se jeta sur moi, me pocha les deux yeux, me cassa quatre dents, et avec la même pancarte me battit dru comme plâtre. — Par mon énergique intervention, je venais donc de …

title: Suite à la répression et à la mort d'un manifestant ivryen
content:
Communiqué de la Coalition antiraciste 2027, du Collectif Romain Rolland Ivry, de la Convergence Citoyenne Ivryenne, et de l'Assemblée des Quartiers


Le 19 octobre 2026


Depuis le début de l'année scolaire, les lycéen-nes mobilisé-es font entendre leurs revendications légitimes sur la dégradation du système scolaire : manque de moyens humains et matériels, d'enseignants et de personnels éducatifs, inégalités de traitement, d'orientation via ParcourSup, opacité, affectations aléatoires et impasses de ce système de sélection, discriminations négatives et territoriales des établissements avec un

IPS

 (indice de position sociale) faible situés dans les quartiers prioritaires de la politique de la ville, emplois du temps surchargés du fait de la réforme Blanquer, bâtiments vétustes et conditions d'enseignement indignes qui participent à la reproduction des inégalités scolaires et sociales...


Toutes ces revendications sont connues de longue date des autorités, et sont portées depuis des années par les élèves, leurs familles et les personnels de l'éducation nationale sans que les pouvoirs publics apportent de réponses à la hauteur des besoins.


Des collectifs militants dénoncent également ces injustices et soutiennent les mobilisations de la jeunesse.


Les lycéen-nes et étudiant-es tiennent depuis des semaines, malgré la répression policière et institutionnelle inédite qui s'est abattue sur les blocus. Violences policières, interpellations massives, tentatives d'interdire les rassemblements ou de fermer les lycées... les jeunes résistent face à cette violence visant à entraver leur liberté d'expression, de réunion et de manifestation.


Le 17 octobre, les mobilisations de la jeunesse ont convergé avec celle contre la vie chère et ont réuni des centaines de milliers de personnes. Cette mobilisation du 17 a été émaillée de graves violences policières, dans la continuité du mois précédent - les forces de l'ordre rouant de coups des manifestant-es de tous âges, faisant un usage massif de gaz lacrymogènes jusqu'à noyer des zones entières, y compris des espaces fermés, et à mettre en péril la santé, lasécurité et la vie des protestataires ou des passants.


De nombreuses et nombreux manifestant-es ont été blessé-es dans des circonstances qu'il reste à élucider et nous n'avons toujours pas de nouvelles d'uncertain nombre d'entre elles et d'entre eux.


Le 18 octobre, l'exécutif reconnaissait un mort, par arrêt cardiorespiratoire, près de la Place de la République, où la répression était particulièrement violente et l'air massivement saturé de lacrymogène.


La victime est ivryenne. Nous manquons d'informations sur sa place dans la manifestation, sur les circonstances de son décès et des soins qu'il a pu recevoir.


Les autorités doivent communiquer sans délai la réalité du bilande ces deux derniers jours de mobilisation et d'action, le nombre exact de mort-es et de blessé-es et les conditions dans lesquelles des manifestant-es sont tombé-es et ont été pris-es en charge.


La sécurité et l'intégrité physique des manifestant-es ont été mises en danger par les pratiques de «

 

maintien de l'ordre

 

». Savoir ce qui s'est passé pour ces manifestant-es, et en particulier pour cet ivryen décédé, devrait être la priorité absolue de ces prochaines heures.


Nos collectifs demandent aux élu-es et organisations politiques, notamment locales, de presser l'exécutif par tous les moyens de déliver les informations que nous attendons toutes et tous. Des proches des victimes, leurs soutiens, leur entourage, veulent plus de transparence sur le bilan du week-end et sur les responsabilités en jeu.


Nous demandons donc en premier lieur à Monsieur le Maire d'Ivry, Philippe Bouyssou, à Madame la députée d'Ivry, Mathilde Panot et à Monsieur le Sénateur, Pascal Savoldelli, de tout faire pour obtenir les informations exactes sur les conditions de décès du manifestant ivryen.


Nos collectifs se tiennent à la disposition de la famille et des proches du manifestant décédé samedi pour les épauler dans la recherche de la vérité et les accompagner dans leur deuil.


Soutien au mouvement, solidarité avec les victimes

 

!


Coalition antiraciste 2027, Collectif Romain Rolland Ivry, Convergence Citoyenne Ivryenne, Assemblée des Quartiers

title: Après le 17, approfondir la rupture
content:
La société de l'abondance trouve sa réponse naturelle dans le pillage, mais elle n'était aucunement abondance naturelle et humaine, elle était abondance de marchandises - Guy Debord


Une inversion systématique de la réalité


"Chaos insoutenable", "horreur", "guerre civile", "République assassinée", politiciens et éditorialistes s'apitoient en chœur sur les dégâts matériels du 17 octobre.


A droite comme à gauche, tout l'échiquier politique condamne et stigmatise. Danger pour l'ordre institutionnel pour les uns, défaut de respectabilité sociale pour les autres. Et dans ce marasme d'indignations morales, pas un mot pour les mutilé⸱es, ni pour l'incroyable courage de celles et ceux qui sont descendu⸱es dans la rue.


Faut-il rappeler à ces donneurs de leçon que les principaux acquis sociaux ont été le résultat de moments insurrectionnels

 

?

Que l'ébranlement d'un pouvoir verrouillé dans sa tour d'ivoire n'est pas un dîner de gala

 

?

 Qu'il n'y a pas de Révolution française sans incendie des hôtels aristocratiques, sans attaques des barrières d'octrois chargées de percevoir les taxes, sans mise à sac du couvent Saint-Lazare et sans pillage des arsenaux

 

?


En définissant la violence par la seule destruction de biens matériels ,

le pouvoir revendique le monopole du langage et l'inversion systématique de la réalité.

 Les mains arrachées deviennent alors de simples accidents et le pillage d'un magasin de luxe - pourtant couvert par des assurances privées - se transforme en un crime odieux. En réalité, dès la matinée, Laurent Nunez n'a cessé d'agiter les épouvantails de l'ultragauche et de

LFI

 pour justifier une répression sanglante.


À nous de remettre les mots à l'endroit.

La première violence, c'est la violence sociale qui prive une majorité de la population de toute perspective d'avenir et les maintient dans la misère

. C'est celle qui nous contraint de trimer tous les jours et de perdre notre vie à la gagner. C'est celle qui multiplie les lois racistes, accordent des permis de tuer aux flics, expulsent les pauvres de leurs logements, et laissent crever les gens aux urgences dans les hôpitaux publics.


La vraie violence, c'est aussi la violence policière. Ce sont les

 8 000 arrestations de lycéennes en deux semaines

, c'est un mort place de la République dans des circonstances troubles, ce sont les mains arrachées à Lens la semaine dernière, et celle d'un adolescent de 17 ans à Saint-Étienne samedi. La vraie violence, c'est un homme de 27 ans qui a perdu un œil un Strasbourg, c'est une adolescente qui a été éborgnée à Mulhouse, c'est des tirs de

LBD

 dans la tête à Clermont et Saint-Nazaire, c'est encore les 2 300 arrestations pour la seule journée du 17 octobre dont on sait qu'une grosse partie risque de finir en prison.


La vraie violence, c'est auss

i le mépris de ce gouvernement face à l'ampleur de la révolte

, c'est la droite de Retailleau qui appelle à l'état d'urgence, ou celle d'Édouard Philippe qui appelle à un retour des «

 

peines planchers

 

».


"On récupère ce qu'on paye toute l'année"


Quand ça fait plus de 30 ans que l'État fait la sourde oreille aux revendications sociales, il ne faut pas s'étonner que ça pète.

 Il ne faut s'étonner que les gens se saisissent d'une situation où l'autorité est provisoirement contestée pour s'affranchir des règles qui disciplinent notre quotidien (travail, boulot, dodo). Il ne faut pas s'étonner que les gens se libèrent pour un temps des règles de la marchandise qui nous obligent à avoir des taff de merde pour payer notre bouffe et notre logement, sans jamais avoir assez pour s'offrir les fringues étalées dans les vitrines de luxe. Alors oui, samedi, pendant quelques heures, Hugo Boss, Louis Vuitton,

HM

, MacDo ou Apple ont fait les frais de leur obscénité.


Dans les médias, tous les politiciennes et éditorialistes de plateaux rejouent l'opposition classique entre les bons et les mauvais⸱es manifestant⸱es, les bons et les mauvais pauvres, les lycéen⸱es respectables et les voyous sans scrupules, la "belle jeunesse" pacifiste et les "jeunes de banlieue" descendus en bandes. Cette opposition, minée par un racisme latent, montre également une ignorance crasse de ce qui se joue en ce moment.


Dans tous les cas, ce n'est pas à nous de dire ce qu'il "faut faire" ou "ne pas faire"

. Ce qu'on a vu samedi, c'est

un large mouvement de révolte avec plusieurs composantes

title: Wahono Karyadi & Matsutake - Anarchist Archives: Critique & Self-Critique #1.1
content:
Author

: Wahono Karyadi & Matsutake

Title

: Anarchist Archives: Critique & Self-Critique #1.1

Date

: 2026

Notes

: Anarchist Archives: Critique & Self-Critique—will be written and published periodically—is a space for those running the Archipelago Anarchist Archive to engage in critical reflection.

Source

: Retrieved on October 14, 2026 from https://archive.org/details/@archipelago-anti-authoritarian-archive


 Printed and published (or even unpublished) works—such as books, pamphlets, leaflets, and zines—hold a significant place among anarchists. This is because such media have proven capable of preserving the diverse experiences and thoughts of many individuals; in certain cases, even if there is an intervention targeting these printed materials, their existence will endure—if not be eternal—longer than the lifespans of the individuals who lived through those experiences and produced those ideas. And the individuals who have fully preserved these printed and published words will subsequently receive a benefit, such as having access to revisit past “practices for reaching emancipation” (movements and struggles).


 That is why, according to Baker (2023) in his study of Spanish anarchist counterculture—or the process of evolutionary change—many anarchist libraries were established to provide access to a comprehensive collection of printed works that had long gone out of print. Unfortunately, the history of the growth of this counterculture—or the process of anarchist evolutionary change—did not proceed smoothly in Indonesia; in fact, it came to a standstill. This was because Indonesia endured a prolonged period of authoritarianism—in its harshest form. The anarchists of the 1920s were exiled to Digul following the 1926 uprising; meanwhile, individuals with (anarcho-)syndicalist leanings who emerged in the 1940s were forcibly removed by Sukarno’s Old Order regime from the factories they had self-managed and were gradually pushed out of the intellectual sphere by the PKI; their very existence became completely untraceable following the 1965 genocide and the rise of Suharto’s New Order regime to power (Bima, 2018).


 However, this prolonged period of authoritarianism was not unique to anarchists in Indonesia. The prolonged period of harsh authoritarianism—namely, the Communist regimes of Gheorghe Gheorghiu-Dej (1948–1965; 17 years) and Nicolae Ceaușescu, meant that anarchists in Romania and Indonesia shared—without denying the differences in the impacts of the post-communist era in Romania versus the post-colonial and post-military-authoritarian eras in Indonesia, which created complex distinctions—a commonality in the historical development of their anarchist cultures. This is because when the communist regime came to power, anarchists were marginalized—ranging from having their movements suppressed to being killed—and those who survived had to go into exile abroad or, if they remained in Romania, chose to go completely underground (Anarhiva, 2021). This situation ultimately meant that the anarchists who emerged in Romania during the collapse of the communist regime in 1989 or afterward—the majority of whom were active in the anarcho-punk scene— had only a fragmentary understanding—or none at all—of the anarchists who existed before them, meaning they automatically lacked a collective experience to draw upon when practicing anarchist or anti-authoritarian principles (Tataran, 2026).


 In line with Adrian Tataran, Ucok (2026) also made a nearly identical point during a discussion of the book Unfinished Nation held at the Bunga di Tembok Library. According to him, before Bima Satria Putra’s book Perang yang Tidak Akan Kita Menangkan was published—long after the Reformation—in 2018, the anarchists who emerged—and just like in Romania, many of whom were also active in the anarcho-punk scene—during the fall of Suharto and his New Order regime and the period that followed had no knowledge of earlier anarchist movements, so it briefly crossed their minds that they were the first generation of anarchists in Indonesia. Consequently, lacking the experience and collective memory passed down from earlier anarchists, these later-emerging anarchists had to start from scratch; in stark contrast, the authoritarian regime—though said to have collapsed—already possessed a bureaucracy, structures, and a military that had been built up over decades, were well-established, and ready to be handed down, making it no difficult task …

title: Sea // Fish - Prison Futures
content:
Author

: Sea // Fish

Title

: Prison Futures

Date

: 10/20/2026


Introduction


 Across Turtle Island the network of U.S. prisons stretch from edge to edge in a vast network. The proliferation of prisons across the occupied land gestures towards the racial ordering of the settler society’s long project of of colonialism and coloniality. With the advent of European settlers on Abya Yala and Turtle Island two significant constituent elements emerged. That being the confluence of multiple modes of productions in unison around the accumulation of capital by European settlers, these modes took the form slavery, serfdom, and salaried labor. With this was the sociogenic imposition, codification, and reification of race as both a biological and hierarchical ordering (Quijano 2000: 216). This historical process of human ordering—in the productive and ideological forces—is the coloniality of power. Colonialism begets a global, and specifically trans-Atlantic consideration. With the transferring of capital to the European metropoles colonial projects and the coloniality of power cross germinate into local formulations of race, hence the local construals of race require global considerations (Pierre 2013: 1). I argue that people in prison utilize communication with the outside world to challenge their position as colonial subjects under global white supremacy, and in doing so exercise their agency as counter-normative spatial politics. To do so, I trace the writings of Kuwasi Balagoon and Malik Muhammad as they exercises agency under incarceration and counter the stability of inside/outside through action and communications.


 Understanding and parsing the U.S. prison system requires attending to the colonial context they emerged in. The ethnic cleansing, genocide, and forced serfdom of Indigenous people of Turtle Island/Abya Yala by Europeans transformed the land into the Americas and in doing so capitalism emerged for the first time. Through the violent force of European settlers, the labor of all Others was aligned in the accumulation of capital (Quijano 2000: 219). The forced migration of Afrikan communities to the newly transfigured Americas as enslaved laborers produced, not only the commodities that made the European and settled metropoles wealthy but also, the bottom of stratified racial taxonomy to which Europeans became white, Indigenous peoples Indian, and Afrikan peoples Black (McKittrick 2013: 3; Quijano 2000: 219; Wynter 2003: 309). Intimately bound to the transformation of Afrikan peoples into a racialized as Black population on occupied Turtle Island is the colonial experience of Afrikan peoples in Afrika. Specifically, in the modes of production and the social formulations under European plantocracies. The economic production of “native labor” being that of agrarian serfdom for Afrikan peoples in Afrika racialized as native, African, and Black (Pierre 2013: 24, 40, 50), specifically recalls the modes of production of Afrikan people on Turtle Island post-emancipation as sharecroppers.


 In Sylvia Wynter’s “Black Metamorphosis”, the transition out of plantation production to sharecropping is marked by this racial and geographic transformation. Wynter identifies that under capitalism, invented by European colonization of Turtle Island/Abya Yala, three zones of labor control existed that of the peripheral plantation economy, the semi-peripheral serfdom economy, and the wage labor economy exclusive to the core (151). It is thus that from the transition of enslavement to post-emancipation labor configurations to which the labor of Afrikan peoples on Turtle Island became native laborers in the colonial configuration shifting from peripheral to semi-peripheral (Ibid.). With this was Jim Crow, the indirect rule built on bifurcated legal constructions of apartheid, was the continuity of slave laws which reified the Black subject position as human Other (153–154). With the transition of Black labor as enslaved chattel labor to native labor the transition from human animal to human Other implicated the Black subject as a contradictory human, one who was now minimally human, but whose labor must be devalued to maintain the coloniality of power (162–163).


 This important historical transition of productive forces in the U.S. underscores the transition from Plantation Archipelago to the Archipelago of Human Others, in this is the Prison Archipelago (Wynter 2003: 321,329; Wynter 1970s: 372). Through the coloniality of …

title: Mistral - Iolaus’ Lament
content:
Author

: Mistral

Title

: Iolaus’ Lament

Subtitle

: or Why You Should Move to the Country

Date

: 2020

Source

: PDF provided by librarian


 


Iolaus provided essential help to Heracles in his battle against the Hydra, his second labor. Seeing that Heracles was being overwhelmed by the multi-headed monster (the Lernaean Hydra), who grew two heads in place of each one cut off, Iolaus helped by cauterizing each neck as Heracles beheaded it.


Beginning


 We deny our bodies. We deny each other. We deny ourselves to this world.


 Cross the river from New Orleans and drive the highway southwest to the edge of the city, to the receding boundary between empire and the wild. The air thickens as the swamp enfolds you in its warm breath. The chemical lawns of poisoned people and cheap geometric boredom, which just a few miles back dominated the landscape, are now intrusions upon it. The swelling symphony of insects crescendos as a blue heron perched at the edge of a property line cranes her head to dark water. Spanish moss sways in a light breeze, almost dripping, over a trio of turtles on a log. Sufficiently warmed by the sun, they plop one by one into the cool bayou.


 You drive, the car belching exhaust, the engine increasingly alone as its stertorous roars become faint metallic whines, as its mechanized brethren are left behind. A family in a blue SUV is the last to pass. The screaming children in the back are the eternal return of our condition.


 You accelerate, the scene out your window transitioning like a flipbook: new-finished homes becoming the naked frames of future ones, then Lot For Sale signs, then the fresh stumps of clear cuts, then finally unscathed groves of bald cypress and tupelo and the homes of a kaleidoscope of creatures, from the mycelia in the wet soil to the birds nesting in snags. Fog lifts into stratus clouds, leaving dewdrop whispers on elephant ears and cattails.


 Now you and the road are what do not belong—the last remaining markers of the living death; you are in a hermetic capsule looking out, a reluctant emissary of this culture. The faster you go, the harder you try to flee, the more strenuous and stubborn your resistance, the more impossible it seems to defy.


 When you trace this moment, this progressive frontier, back to where you came from in the city somewhere, you realize that today’s boundary is essentially the same one that delimited the crude settlement on the bank of the Mississippi River in 1718—which in the beginning only extended from the river to Rampart Street, the wilderness a great mystery beckoning beyond the wall. There are no words to describe the voracious inertia of our appetite. You realize that this is the same partition as the ramparts that were taken down after the Natchez were subdued and the marais was drained—when the fledgling settlement became a city; it is the same line as it was when the Americans came, and their development flowed upriver of Canal Street before expanding radially in unimpeded degradation—ramifying, eroding. And it is the same boundary, the same corrupted ovule, that sprouted in the Greater Antilles in 1492, Jamestown in 1607, Plymouth in 1620, Hawaii in 1778, and a thousand times elsewhere long before, when the mother countries had been wild: as when France was Gaul and tribes there fought against Caesar’s incursions. The natural world splintered where profitable, and in-waiting where there is not yet a dollar to be made or power to be accrued.


 And constantly surrounding, impinging, from the maws of billboards to the mouths of intimates, are the cacophonous signs and symbols declaring

Never Better!

 or

A Work in Progress!

 or

We Have Arrived!

 and all the other deceptions, proclamations of supremacy, and self-celebrations that reverberate over the increasingly silenced wild.


 It is more tangible than any ideology when your throat tightens in the humidity, more profound than any philosophy when the wipers cannot cut through the misting blur. It is so much deeper than politics when the car pulls over, when the head lowers into the hands, when you concede it is tears that fall and run in rivulets.


 You sit there on the gravel shoulder, pathetic and choking on what we have done and soon will do—the limitless depth of it all. The car takes you here or there, it does not matter. This newly built home is the desert of the Fertile Crescent; this Wolmanized wooden frame is the paved forests of Europe; this real estate …

title: Maureen Wright - Book Review: A Brave and Beautiful Spirit
content:
Author

: Maureen Wright

Title

: Book Review: A Brave and Beautiful Spirit

Date

: 2020

Source

: Women’s History Review. <

https://doi.org/10.1080/09612025.2020.1844413

>


A Brave and Beautiful Spirit: Dora Marsden 1882–1960

, Les Garner, Portland, OR, Union of Egoists, 2019 (first published 1990), 1–486 pp., £19.95 (pb), ISBN 978-1944651-14-5


 The lives of women who refused to conform to the ‘Vicwardian’ stereotypes of femininity took many forms, but perhaps one of the most individual was that of Dora Marsden (1882–1960), scholar, Freethinker, Egoist and militant suffragette of the Women’s Social and Political Union (WSPU). Les Garner informs us that Emmeline Pethick-Lawrence, long-time Treasurer of the WSPU, wrote of Marsden in 1909 that her ‘brave and beautiful spirit’ exemplified the disposition most valued by the leaders and strategists of the organisation. Yet before too much time had passed, Marsden had left the WSPU behind, writing in a torrent of ‘hurt anger and not a little arrogance’ (122) that its leaders, the infamous Pankhurst women, were insensible to her independent style of regional organisation, and that she obstinately refused to comply with what she saw as their ‘autocratic’ demands. It was an opinion she held for the rest of her life, which came to its close in 1960 in the withdrawn isolation of a mental asylum in Dumfries. It was a tragic end to what, in many ways, was a tragic life.


 The re-issue of Garner’s 1990 biography of Marsden by the Egoist Press is simply that, a re-issue. Garner writes in a new preface to the book that although it would have been ‘tempting … to … re-write’ (11) he chose not to, on the grounds that his current political activism would have suffered as a result of having to become ‘seldom seen’ (11) as he worked on the manuscript. The pun on the name ‘Seldom Seen’, the name of the Lake District residence Marsden occupied with her mother Hannah in the 1920s, was deliberate, but I feel the work involved would have been worthwhile, particularly in light of the excellent recent scholarship undertaken by Lucy Delap, Tanya Cheadle, Sheila Rowbotham and others on Freethinkers, Socialists and the feminist

avant-garde

. Dora Marsden is a key figure among such pioneers and a re-write, penned in the midst of new discoveries of the twenty-first century, would have been both appropriate and timely.


 Marsden was not alone among early twentieth-century feminist pioneers in finding Emmeline and Christabel Pankhurst’s WSPU guilty of moving away from its Radicalliberal and Socialist roots. She was also not alone in pursuing a life that, increasingly, questioned the relationship between the ‘personal and sexual life and social change’ (161). In common with her close friend, the bright and effervescent Mary Gawthorpe (regional Organiser of the WSPU in Leeds), Marsden rose from a poverty-blighted childhood, via the route of probationer and pupil-teacher to the role of an independent woman, earning her own living through teaching. At Owen’s College where she took her degree, she was in the orbit of likeminded women, including scientist Rona Robinson, Eva Gore-Booth and Theresa Billington. It was this ‘network of friends and sympathisers’ which proved ‘vital’ (63) to Marsden, both in the period of her suffragette activism and, latterly, while working on the

Freewoman

 group of publications from 1912. Following graduation in 1903, Marsden gained her first teaching post in Leeds, later moving to Colchester and Manchester before becoming Headmistress at Altrincham Pupil-Teacher Centre in 1908. Garner informs his readers that Dora’s work had made her ‘well aware of the vast gulf between idealized concepts of women’s lives and reality’ (70), and it was for these reasons she became attracted to the suffrage movement. She was courageous, exceptionally determined and held ‘a strong belief in her own abilities’ (70), but these qualities led her away from the WSPU after only a few years. Ultimately, she also shied away from the designation ‘feminist’, her evolving philosophy leading her to embrace humanism, individualism (especially that form exemplified by the German postHeliganist Max Stirner) and a ‘keenly developed’ (209) egoism.


 Marsden became the poster-girl of the WSPU; this was after one day in 1909 in which she endured such ‘rough treatment’ at police hands it was like being ‘in the thick of [a] battle’ (102–3). But even though she and Rona Robinson had been awarded the …

title: Aldo Santiago - The Political Persecution Against an Absolved Mazatec Indian, Miguel Peralta, Continues After 11 Years of Legal Battles
content:
Author

: Aldo Santiago

Title

: The Political Persecution Against an Absolved Mazatec Indian, Miguel Peralta, Continues After 11 Years of Legal Battles

Date

: July 13, 2026

Notes

:

Translated from Santiago, Aldo, "Continúa persecución política contra Miguel Peralta, mazateco absuelto tras 11 años de lucha legal",

 Avispa Midia

, 13 July

,

2026

.

https://avispa.org/continua-persecucion-politica-contra-miguel-peralta-mazateco-absuelto-tras-11-anos-de-lucha-legal/

 Part of a series of translations in solidarity with Miguel Peralta from a little corner in Chicago known as Blood Fruit Library

Source

: Retrieved 10/19/2026 from https://www.patreon.com/bloodfruit/posts/new-transl-after-165960159


 Four days after the Oaxaca Third Criminal Division of High Court Justice absolved ex-political prisoner Miguel Peralta Betanzos, accused of homicide and attempted homicide, on March 6, deputy Elisa Zepeda Lagunas presented a new legal appeal to review the sentence of said Mazatec defendants in a legal process that totals more than 11 years.


 According to a communiqué sent out by family members, collectives, and organizations following Peralta's defense, the constestation against his absolution was presented on March 10, and submitted before the Nation's Supreme Court of Justice (SCJN) as "Amparo Directo in Review 2705/2026."


 Said appeal was evaluated by the president of the Court, a position filled by minister Hugo Aguilar Ortiz, who approved its admission this past April 17. By June 12, the SCJN gave notice that the case would be reviewed by minister Loretta Ortíz and solicited the previous records in order to form the legal analysis.


 "Today, once again, we are about to return to the Supreme Court at the whims of deputy Elisa Zepeda and her closeness with the president of said institute. This has nothing to do with justice, but rather with the use of these institutions to persecute and wear down anyone who resists," shared Peralta upon learning of the new contestation. The legal cause stems from the events of December 2014 and, since then it has passed through state trials, Collegiate Tribunals and even the SCJN itself.


 Miguel Peralta, born in the community of Eloxochitlán de Flores Magón in the Mazatec Mountains, was detained on April 2015 in Mexico City and transferred to Oaxaca, where he remained incarcerated for four and a half years, charged with the killing a person and of supposed attempted homicide against Elisa Zepeda, within a context of aggression of petty warlord groups that belong to Zepeda against the Community Assembly.


 On October 2019, the Huautla Joint Lower First Instance Courts had absolved him upon considering that the evidence presented in the trial did not prove his responsibility of the crimes, and so Peralta left prison despite the fact that the prosecution appealed the resolution. By March 2022, the Oaxaca Third Criminal Chamber revoked the absolving sentence and emitted one of 50 years behind bars. He remained under political persecution while he continued his legal defense, since, upon issuing an arrest warrant, the possibility for his arrest at any time was kept open.


 On August 2023, a Collegiate Court granted a direct writ of amparo to Peralta. Without resolving the background case, the sentence was limited to ordering the resumption of part of the legal process, such that the Mazatec defense appealed to the SCJN. On November 2024, The First Chamber revoked the resolution and concluded that the Oaxacan tribunal had infringed Peralta's right to obtain justice by not considering the fact that he belonged to a First Peoples and in failing to analyze the case from an intercultural perspective.


 The Court returned the file to the Oaxaca First Collegiate Tribunal of Penal Matters so that it may issue a new sentence which took into consideration of the social, cultural, and political context of Eloxochitlán. At this stage, expert anthropological opinions became involved who documented the existence of petty warlords in said community, for which there have been human rights violation against the townspeople and a power imbalance that has placed the townspeople under more than a decade of political persecution.


Justice Delayed


 On February 20, 2026, the Collegiate Tribunal cataloged just how lacking the evidence against Peralta was. It also pointed out contradictions in the testimonies made against him, making it clear that the charges against him were fabricated, thus …

author: CNT Sierra Norte
title: 21 de octubre. Charla informativa: hacia la huelga general del 11 de noviembre
content:
Este miércoles 21 de octubre, a las 19:00 horas, nos encontramos en La Cabrera para hablar de la huelga general del próximo 11 de noviembre, resolver dudas y organizarnos colectivamente.


La huelga es una de las herramientas más importantes que tenemos como clase trabajadora para defender nuestros derechos y conquistar mejores condiciones de vida. Frente a la precariedad laboral, la pérdida de poder adquisitivo, la especulación con la vivienda y el deterioro de los servicios públicos, necesitamos organizarnos y unir nuestras luchas.


A la hora de secundar una huelga surgen muchas preguntas:

¿Puedo hacer huelga en mi trabajo? ¿Tengo que avisar a la empresa? ¿Pueden sancionarme? ¿Qué ocurre con mi salario? ¿Qué reivindicamos?


Para responder a estas cuestiones y debatir sobre la próxima convocatoria de huelga general del 11 de noviembre, organizamos una

charla informativa abierta a todas las personas interesadas

, junto a la Sección Sindical de Educación de la Comunidad de Madrid de CNT y el nodo Sierra Norte del Sindicato de Inquilinas de Madrid.


¿De qué hablaremos?


El derecho a huelga y cómo ejercerlo.


Quién puede secundar la convocatoria y qué protección legal tiene.


Las obligaciones de las empresas y los derechos de las personas trabajadoras.


Las reivindicaciones de la huelga general del 11 de noviembre.


La importancia de organizarse en los centros de trabajo y en nuestros barrios y pueblos.


No es necesario estar afiliada a ningún sindicato ni tener experiencia previa en movilizaciones.

La charla está abierta a todas las personas que quieran informarse, compartir inquietudes y participar.


Guía práctica: conoce tu derecho a huelga


Para facilitar el acceso a la información, compartimos también la guía de CNT

«Derecho a la huelga: te resolvemos 8 dudas frecuentes»

, un material que aborda cuestiones habituales sobre el ejercicio de este derecho fundamental.


En ella encontrarás información sobre la participación en huelgas sin afiliación sindical, los periodos de prueba, las situaciones de becarios y falsos autónomos, los servicios mínimos, la obligación de avisar a la empresa, los descuentos salariales y la protección frente a represalias.


Conocer nuestros derechos es el primer paso para poder defenderlos colectivamente.


La organización, el apoyo mutuo y la solidaridad son nuestras mejores herramientas.


Te esperamos este miércoles. ¡Acude, participa y difunde la convocatoria!


 ¡Unamos las luchas de la clase trabajadora!


 CNT Sierra Norte

author: The Canadian Press
title: Mother of First Nation woman who couldn’t get medical transport and died seeks reform
content:
If only. It’s a phrase that plays over and over again in Eva Mamakwa’s mind.


If only her daughter, Miranda Mamakwa, had made it to at least one follow-up appointment after open-heart surgery, she may be alive.


If only Indigenous Services Canada’s

non-insured health benefits program

 had arranged travel for just one of her four missed appointments, Miranda may be alive.


The 31-year-old mother of three from Fort Severn First Nation died on Sept. 8, weeks after asking people on social media to seek action in case of her death.


“I don’t want this to happen to anyone else,” Eva Mamakwa said in an interview with The Canadian Press from her home before falling quiet, overcome with emotion. She is speaking out about her daughter’s death for the first time.


Since Miranda Mamakwa’s death, more than a dozen First Nations and tribal councils have filed a human rights complaint that alleges widespread neglect of their communities’ health needs, while chiefs have demanded reform from the federal agency in charge of arranging medical travel for remote First Nation people.


Indigenous Services Canada said it’s working to improve delivery of the service, while the minister in charge has said she requested a fact-finding mission on the circumstances that led to Miranda Mamakwa’s death.


Months ago, Mamakwa’s family was filled with hope as she underwent surgery at the University of Ottawa Heart Institute in April to replace a valve in her heart. She recovered over two weeks at the hospital in Ottawa, then two more weeks at the Thunder Bay Regional Health Sciences Centre.


On May 24, she arrived home in Fort Severn First Nation, the most northerly community in Ontario that sits near the mouth of the Severn River on Hudson Bay.


Her doctors wanted to see her for several followups. She had blood clots and had been put on blood thinners, which required testing on an ongoing basis, Eva Mamakwa said. Doctors booked her daughter for an echocardiogram and an appointment with a vascular surgeon in Thunder Bay.


Miranda Mamakwa was thrilled to be back home; her children were excited and her mother was caring for her.


That excitement would soon abate.


Eva Mamakwa said she went to the First Nation’s nursing station to begin the administrative process to arrange travel back to Thunder Bay for her daughter’s first followup appointment. Nurses soon faxed Miranda’s documentation to the non-insured health benefits program — faxes are protocol — and the family waited to hear back on travel plans.


She said the agency never responded and her daughter missed her first appointment on May 28. Eva Mamakwa then called NIHB’s office in Sioux Lookout, Ont., and got someone on the line.


“I told her that it was extremely important that Miranda go to her followup appointments,” she said. “I talked to her and she listened to me and she said they would send her travel, but travel never came.”


She said the NIHB told her the request never arrived despite more than one tranche of faxes being sent.


The same thing occurred for followup appointments on June 11, July 2 and Aug. 6, Eva Mamakwa said, despite multiple faxes and phone calls.


“They didn’t care at all,” she said.


As the summer progressed, Miranda Mamakwa became more tired, slept more and started losing feeling in her fingers.


On Aug. 19, she wrote a Facebook post about the problems with NIHB and the missed appointments.


“If I die, pls go after (them),” she wrote.


On Sept. 6, she started to feel sick. Her stomach hurt and she began vomiting. “We just thought she might have caught the flu from her kids,” her mother said.


But Eva Mamakwa soon realized that “something was terribly wrong.”


Her daughter needed immediate help. Later that day, Skycare, which operates on behalf of provincial air and land ambulance Ornge, arrived, and airlifted her to the intensive care unit of the Thunder Bay Regional Health Sciences Centre, some 850 kilometres away.


The next day, Eva Mamakwa and Mike Bluecoat, Miranda’s father, got a call from the ICU doctor.


“He told me that Miranda had a lot of bleeding in her brain, she was hemorrhaging,” she said. “Even if they send her down south (to Toronto), to try and help her, that she wouldn’t have survived it.”


The doctor told them to fly to Thunder Bay so they did, with Miranda’s children in tow. Eva Mamakwa’s oldest daughter was already at the hospital to support her sister.


They arrived to crushing news.

author: Sara Connors
title: Nearly all people who recently died from toxic drugs in Whitehorse were Indigenous: coroner
content:
At least seven Indigenous people have died in Whitehorse in recent months as a result of toxic substances, according to

Yukon’s chief coroner.


Chief coroner Heather Jones, who said in an update on Monday that a surge of recent deaths since early July were linked to toxic substances, confirmed in an email to APTN News that seven of the eight people who died identified as Indigenous.


She said she could not yet comment on two additional deaths suspected to be linked to toxic substances.


“While substance-related deaths have remained a significant concern in the Yukon, the recent concentration of deaths within a short period of time is alarming and highlights the ongoing dangers associated with the unregulated drug supply,” she said in Monday’s release.


The release states that prior to July, the last confirmed toxic substance death investigated by the Yukon coroner’s service was in October 2025.


Preliminary findings show cocaine was present in all eight confirmed deaths.


Fluorofentanyl, a highly potent synthetic opioid related to fentanyl, was also detected in five of the deaths.


Carolina Koutras, health researcher and chief operating officer with public health non-profit One Yukon Coalition, said in an email that it tests for fluorofentanyl through its wastewater monitoring program.


She said the program can detect the three distinct forms of the substance: para-fluorofentanyl (p-FF), meta-fluorofentanyl (m-FF), and ortho-fluorofentanyl (o-FF).


She noted that para-fluorofentanyl, which is known to be highly potent, is the most consistently detected form of the substance and has been identified in every wastewater sample since monitoring for it began. Meta-fluorofentanyl, she said, has been detected intermittently, most recently appearing on Sept. 18. She said ortho-fluorofentanyl has not yet been detected.


Koutras said that Health Canada’s surveillance data shows fluorofentanyls were implicated in 32 per cent of apparent opioid toxicity deaths in Canada in 2024, a noticeable increase from 26 per cent in 2023.


Read More:


Advocates suspect rise in overdoses in Whitehorse linked to new synthetic opioid 


Jones, meanwhile, said in the release that the recent uptick in deaths is “deeply concerning.”


“These deaths underscore the continued presence of a dangerous and unpredictable drug supply in our community and the devastating impact it has on individuals, families, and friends,” she said.


According to the release, the service has investigated 157 confirmed substance-related deaths since April 2016, 133 of which involved opioids. It states that 117 of those opioid deaths involved fentanyl.


The number of substance-related deaths in the Yukon was the highest in 2021 with 25 reported deaths. Last year the service reported 18 deaths.


The post

Nearly all people who recently died from toxic drugs in Whitehorse were Indigenous: coroner

 appeared first on

APTN News

.

author: Thiago Domenici
title: Hospitais do Rio de Janeiro, Flávio Bolsonaro e a acusação de Lula na Band
content:
“Eu queria fazer a pergunta: se ele [Flávio Bolsonaro] tem noção da destruição que ele fez nos seis hospitais federais do Rio de Janeiro, que nós agora estamos recuperando”. Essa foi a fala do presidente e candidato à reeleição Lula (PT), no último debate realizado pela TV Bandeirantes no domingo, 18 de outubro.


O presidente acusou o concorrente Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) de mandar nos hospitais federais do Rio durante o governo do pai, Jair Bolsonaro. Lula falou de UTIs fechadas, de unidades sucateadas e de um “pedágio” cobrado de funcionários para estacionar no que Flávio respondeu que Lula estava “vomitando um monte de mentiras”.


A informação usada por Lula foi revelada pela

Agência Pública

 em 1º de outubro, na

reportagem

 de Caio Briso, que trouxe documentos oficiais e entrevistas que indicam como o senador Flávio Bolsonaro, sem cargo no Executivo à época, exerceu forte influência sobre a rede de saúde entre 2019 e 2022, em plena pandemia de Covid-19.


O Rio é a única cidade do país com hospitais administrados pelo governo federal, herança dos tempos em que era a capital do país. São seis unidades: Bonsucesso, Andaraí, Cardoso Fontes, Ipanema, Lagoa e Servidores do Estado. Com orçamento alto e muitos contratos terceirizados, a rede virou um “feudo” de políticos fluminenses, segundo fontes consultadas sob reserva pela reportagem que traz detalhes de como Flávio Bolsonaro influenciou a saúde do Rio no governo de Jair Bolsonaro.


No debate, Flávio chegou a assumir uma mea culpa sobre o mal resultado da gestão do pai na saúde. “De fato, a saúde não foi uma área que a gente teve o melhor resultado. Eu faço aqui esse mea culpa”,

afirmou

 o senador. Apesar disso, ele argumentou que Jair comprou as vacinas, sem informar que o presidente deu várias declarações contrárias à compra de vacinas, além de desinformar sobre o efeito delas.


Leia a fala de Lula na íntegra


“Eu queria fazer a pergunta: se ele [Flávio Bolsonaro] tem noção da destruição que ele fez nos seis hospitais federais do Rio de Janeiro, que nós agora estamos recuperando. Fizemos parceria com a iniciativa privada, com a prefeitura, para que a gente dê conta daqueles hospitais. Aquele hospital tem que ser hospital de qualidade, aquele hospital tem que ser referência.


Mas sabe o que ele fazia quando ele tomava conta desses hospitais? Ele cobrava até pedágio dos funcionários, os caras pagavam estacionamento. Então, quem está assistindo pode ir lá perguntar, pode ir lá perguntar, pode ir nos hospitais perguntar para a enfermeira, para médico. Tinha um hospital lá do Rio de Janeiro, federal, que ele tomava conta, que não tinha cozinha (…) Então é o seguinte, rapaz: pelo amor de Deus, quando a gente trata de saúde, você tem que tratar de saúde com respeito, com muito respeito (…)”

author: Unknown
title: Nijerya'da ilk Ebola virüsü vakası tespit edildi
content:
Nijerya hükümeti, başkent Abuja'nın bulunduğu Federal Başkent Bölgesi'nde (FCT) ilk Ebola virüsü vakasının tespit edildiğini bildirdi.

Nijerya Sağlık ve Sosyal Refah Koordinasyon Bakanı Muhammad Pate, başkent Abuja'da düzenlenen basın toplantısında, laboratuvar testleri sonucunda ülkede Ebola virüsü vakasının doğrulandığını belirtti. Pate, Doğu Afrika'ya, özellikle Uganda'ya seyahat geçmişi bulunan kadın hastanın, 7 Ekim'de belirtilerle Nijerya'ya döndüğünü, belirtilerin 4 gün sonra ilerlediğini ve yapılan testlerin ardından kadında Ebola virüsü enfeksiyonunun doğrulandığını ifade etti.

Hastanın şu anda izolasyonda tutulduğunu ve tedavi gördüğünü kaydeden Pate, temaslı takibi çalışmalarının başlatıldığını ve şu ana kadar 44 temaslının belirlendiğini söyledi.

Sağlık Bakanlığı, FCT Sağlık Sekreterliği, Afrika Hastalık Kontrol ve Önleme Merkezleri (Africa CDC) ve diğer ortakların virüsün yayılmasını önlemek için koordineli şekilde çalıştığını bildiren Pate, ülkenin giriş noktalarındaki gözetim ve denetimlerin de artırıldığını vurguladı.

Pate, sağlık kuruluşlarına olası vakalara karşı yüksek düzeyde teyakkuzda olmaları çağrısında bulunurken, Nijeryalılardan da sakin ve dikkatli olmalarını istedi.

Halka hijyen kurallarına uymaları, ateş, halsizlik, baş ağrısı ve ishal gibi belirtilere karşı dikkatli olmaları ve halk sağlığı yetkilileriyle işbirliği yapmaları tavsiyesinde bulunan Pate, hükümetin 2014'teki Ebola salgınıyla mücadele deneyiminden ve yıllar içinde geliştirilen halk sağlığı mekanizmalarından yararlandığını kaydetti.

Pate, temaslıların takip ve gözetim altında tutulduğunu, hükümetin salgını kontrol altına alma çalışmalarına ilişkin kamuoyunu düzenli ve şeffaf biçimde bilgilendireceğini ifade etti.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Unknown
title: Borç, haciz, güvencesizlik, ağır çalışma: Metal işçisi mengenede
content:
Erdal Kılıç [email protected] Muzaffer Özkurt

Bursa’da hava ağır. Sadece bulutlu, yağmurlu olduğu için değil. Geçim sıkıntısı, borçlar, geleceği görememe, siyasi baskılar, ağırlaşan çalışma koşulları, işten atılma korkusu… Metal işçileri, her yandan mengeneye alınmış gibi. Hangi işçi ağzını açsa bu sıkışmışlık hissediliyor.

Bursa’nın üç ana fabrikası olan Renault, TOFAŞ ve Bosch’tan işçilerle görüşüyoruz. İşçilerin büyük kısmının kıdemi 10 yılın altında. Sayıları hızla artan, kıdemi 5 yıla kadar olan işçilerin ücretleri 35 bin lira ile 45 bin lira arasında. Herkesin gözünün üzerinde olduğu 10 yıl civarı işçilerin ücreti 70-90 bin lira. 1990’lardan bu yana çalışan az sayıda EYT’li işçinin emekli maaşıyla birlikte 200 bin liraya yakın geliri var. Önceki dönemin mücadelelerine şahit olmuş, deneyim sahibi ama elindekini kaybetmekten korkan en eski işçilerle; ücretleri düşük, geçmiş mücadelelerden bihaber ama öfkeli genç işçiler arasındaki bölünme her geçen gün derinleşiyor. Genç işçilere dair değerlendirmeler ise çoğunlukla “Telefon için işe girmişler, ne yapacakları belli değil” şeklinde oluyor. Bu sözlerin sonuna bir ama geliyor: “Ama bu fabrikalarda bir şey olacaksa onlar yapacak.”

Borçsuz işçi yok. Fabrika bünyesindeki kooperatiften markette ne satılıyorsa içinde olan kooperatiflerden veresiye mal alınabiliyor. Ücret alınır alınmaz da kaynaktan kesiliyor. Aylar geçtikçe, enflasyonla birlikte kesilen miktar artıyor. Kredi borçları nedeniyle hacizlik olan işçi sayısı da... Bekarlar evlenmekten korkuyor çünkü sürekli boşanma haberleri dillerde.

Genç işçiler arasında daha yaygın olmak üzere ekonomik sıkışmışlıktan çıkmak için kolay yol tercih ediliyor: Kumar! Fona para yatırmak, borsa oynamak da kumarın içinde sayılıyor. Zira son vurgunla birlikte eşinin bilezikleri dahil neyi var neyi yoksa kaybeden işçi sayısı az değil. İntiharların artma olasılığı sıklıkla dile getiriliyor. Açıktan, herkesin içinde para kaptırdığını söylemek işçiler için hiç kolay değil. Muğlak konuşulsa da temel gündem bu.

Fabrikalarda örgütlü Türk Metal’in ise bu kadar dikkate alınmadığı hiçbir dönem yaşanmadığını söylüyor işçiler. Sendikacıların sadece sosyal medyada paylaşmak için fotoğraf çektirmeye geldiğini, hiçbir soruya cevap vermediğini söyleyen genç Renault işçileri, Influencer diyor sendikacılara, “Şipşak” lakabı takıyor. 2015’te düşük ücrete karşı başlayan Metal Fırtına’nın ilk hedefi sendikacılardı. Şimdi ise sendikacılar için “insan kaynakları departmanı” tarifi kullanılıyor. Dolayısıyla gözler sendikacılardan çok patronda.

Patronlar işte bu bölünmüşlüğü, işçiler arası güvensizliği istedikleri çalışma düzenini hayata geçirmek için kullanıyor. İşsizlik ortamının da etkisiyle “Benim istediğim gibi olacaksın, yoksa güle güle” çok rahat söyleniyor. 57 saniyede bir arabanın üretildiği fabrikada, çay molasına 10 saniye erken çıkılamıyor. Çıkılması halinde üretim şefi bandın dibinde bitiyor. Üretimin 1 dakikanın üzerine çıkması ise kırmızı alarm demek. Ücretlerin avro karşısında eridiği dönemlerde TL dışında hesap yapmayan patron temsilcileri, kur baskısı nedeniyle şimdi ağızlarını dolar ve avroyla açıyor: “Ücret maliyetleri 2 bin 300 avro civarında, Fas’ta/Hindistan’da bu 450 avro.”

Ülke genelinde artan baskı nedeniyle “Şikayet etsek Silivri’de alırız soluğu” diyorlar. İşçilerin karamsar olmasının temel sebebi ülkenin içerisinde bulunduğu durum. 25-30 yaş arasında olup AKP’den ve Erdoğan’dan umudu olan işçi sayısı çok az. 25 yaş altı gençlerde durum daha da sert; “Zaten emekli olamayacağız. Çalışarak bir yere varmanın imkanı yok” diyorlar. Herkese öfkeliler. İktidara, muhalefete, yüksek ücretli işçilere hatta “tembellik edip” üzerlerindeki çalışma yükünü artıran yaşıtlarına… Aileleri de bu öfkeden nasibini alıyor. “Bu iktidarı getirdiler, gençliğimizi yaşayamadık” diyorlar: “Kaos çıksın”, “Yer yerinden oynasın”, “Benzin döksünler ilk ben kibrit çakarım.”

Kemalpaşalı, köyle ve tarımla bağları süren, hâlâ ekip biçmeye devam eden pek çok işçi, ürünleri para etmediği için köylü eylemlerinde de yer almış. Bir işçi, “Zarar ettiğim için 200 bin lira cebimden para verdim. Sadece toprağıma tutunmak istiyorum” diyor. Toprağını ekmeyi bırakan çok sayıda işçi var. Kemik AKP’li sayılan bu işçiler arasında da çözülme başlamış. Zarar arttıkça, iktidardan da uzaklaşıyor Kemalpaşalı işçiler. “Mahalle baskısı” diye tarif ettikleri genel hava nedeniyle alternatifi yine sağ partilerde arıyorlar.

author: Leanne Sanders
title: First Nations leaders in Alberta say referendum vote decisive, but Canada has work to do
content:
After months of uncertainty, the Alberta referendum has, for now, settled the debate around the province separating. But for chiefs who worked hard to get their members to vote in order to protect the treaties, there’s more work ahead.


The grand chief of

Treaty 8 Sovereign Nations

 in Alberta said while leaders believed the referendum would turn out the way it did, “there is a sigh of relief.”


“The numbers were never in the separatists favour, and for the referendum to be brought forward was, in our opinion, a big waste of time,” said Trevor Mercredi in an interview Tuesday with

APTN News

. “And, the time and funding could have been better spent. But I will say that our nations are optimistic.”


Treaty 8 is made up of 39 First Nations across three provinces and the Northwest Territories. Twenty-four of them are in northern Alberta. Treaty 8 supported legal challenges and welcomed rulings from the Court of King’s Bench in finding errors in how separation referendum processes were handled without proper consultation or respect for constitutional obligations.


While the referendum battle was won, Mercredi points out “separatism here in Alberta is not going to go away.”


“We just have to push it aside and do the work that we need to do. And there’s a lot of work that needs to happen here in Alberta to gain back the working relationship between the provincial government and the nations,” Mercredi said.


Mercredi acknowledged the political momentum created by the referendum and that while First Nations have not traditionally participated in federal, provincial, and municipal elections, he said that has to change.


“We need to understand that elections and voting are important, and we will be motivating our people to vote at the next provincial election as well. So, this is just the start,” Mercredi said.


As for what comes next, Mercredi said Premier Danielle Smith and the United Conservative Party have to look inward.


“I think the UCP have to reevaluate their conditions and figure out exactly who they’re here for when it comes to Albertans. There was a faction of people that would like to see Alberta separate, and it’s about time that the UCP look at the majority of Albertans and start working for them,” Mercredi said.


NDP MLA Jodi Calahoo Stonehouse credits the hard work of several women including Cara Currie Hall in getting voters to come out.


“Those women really mobilized the movement and the chiefs also contributed a tremendous amount of resources, of energy and commitment to upholding treaty and trying to defeat separatism while battling the racism that was coming out from the separatist side,” said Calahoo Stonehouse, who’s Cree and Mohawk from Michel First Nation northwest of Edmonton. “But, there’s a gift in that and now we have to do something about it. It’s time to repair that.”


A former national chief of the Assembly of First Nations (AFN) also had a message for Canada the day after the referendum.


“Alberta’s decisive vote to remain in Canada is a historic moment, but it also raises important questions about the future of our country,” said Matthew Coon Come in a statement.


Coon Come was a key figure in turning back the separatist tide when Quebec tried to secede from Canada in the 1995 referendum under Jacques Parizeau and the Parti Quebecois. Quebec’s first referendum in 1980 was won by the federalist side by 20 points. But in 1995, a narrow majority of voters opposed secession – 50.6 per cent to 49.4 per cent.


Coon Come maintains “Canada’s future must be built on more than keeping provinces together. It must also be built on honouring the Treaties, respecting constitutional obligations and ensuring that all parties have a meaningful place in shaping the future.”


“The next chapter must be about listening,” Coon Come said, “addressing legitimate grievances and strengthening the relationships that hold this country together—including the Crown’s Treaty relationships with First Nations.”


Ahead of Monday night’s vote, the current national chief of the AFN, Cindy Woodhouse Nepinak reminded Alberta that Treaty Nations “are in sovereign relationships with the Crown. The truth is that no province has the right to alter these constitutional realities.”


“Regardless of Monday’s result, we will be re-inviting Premier Smith to participate in next week’s First Nations-First Ministers’ Meeting in Ottawa, and the National Day of Ceremony with the Prime Minister and other First Ministers …

author: Clayton Aldern
title: Segundo turno das eleições será referendo sobre futuro da Amazônia
content:
Depois dos resultados do primeiro turno, observadores ambientais acreditam que o dia 25 de outubro não será apenas a disputa final entre Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva e Flávio Bolsonaro: a votação será também um referendo sobre o futuro da Floresta Amazônica.


“Estamos muito preocupados com os riscos para a Amazônia caso Flávio vença a eleição, porque ele nega as mudanças climáticas”, afirmou

Carlos Nobre

, uma das maiores autoridades na área e um dos cientistas brasileiros mais conhecidos do mundo.

“Se ele for eleito, certamente o desmatamento na Amazônia vai aumentar. Estamos em uma situação muito grave.”


Flávio Bolsonaro faz campanha com uma

agenda

 favorável ao agronegócio e à desregulamentação. O candidato do PL, que terminou o primeiro turno à frente de Lula por 2,2 milhões de votos, promete zerar o desmatamento ilegal até 2029. Mas o

programa de governo

 do filho de Jair Bolsonaro também defende um processo de licenciamento ambiental “ágil e moderno”, que “não servirá mais como instrumento para bloquear quem deseja investir e gerar empregos”.


Monica de Bolle, economista do Peterson Institute for International Economics, nos Estados Unidos, avalia que uma vitória de Flávio repetiria o mandato de seu pai, marcado pelo

aumento

 do desmatamento, pela queda acentuada no número de autos de infração ambiental e pela quase

duplicação

 das emissões de carbono na Amazônia em 2019 e 2020, na comparação com a média registrada entre 2010 e 2018.


“Jair Bolsonaro basicamente desmantelou a estrutura de fiscalização. E acho que isso provavelmente aconteceria de novo”, afirmou de Bolle.


Onipresente, mas sem direito a voto na próxima eleição, a própria Amazônia está em jogo.

 A floresta enfrenta uma série de ameaças, da seca às queimadas, passando pela extração de madeira e pelo desmatamento. Embora o Código Florestal permita que proprietários rurais desmatem até 20% de suas terras na Amazônia, a rede de monitoramento MapBiomas

estimou recentemente

 que 97% da supressão da vegetação nativa na Amazônia em 2025 apresentava indícios de ilegalidade.


Durante o atual mandato de Lula, as taxas de desmatamento na Amazônia caíram a cada ano. Se o Brasil voltasse ao ritmo registrado durante o governo de Jair Bolsonaro, a floresta perderia cerca de 45.600 quilômetros quadrados nos próximos quatro anos, em comparação com aproximadamente 23.000 quilômetros quadrados caso o ritmo observado em 2025 fosse mantido. A diferença equivale a uma área aproximadamente do tamanho do estado de Sergipe.


Os resultados do primeiro turno sugerem que os interesses do setor agropecuário provavelmente contribuíram para o bom desempenho de Flávio Bolsonaro.

 Lula perdeu votos em quase todos os municípios do país na comparação com seu desempenho em 2022. Mas, como a

Agência Pública


mostrou

, nos municípios onde o agronegócio representa mais da metade da economia local, sua votação caiu quase oito pontos percentuais, três vezes a perda registrada nas áreas onde a atividade não predomina.


Se o próximo governo acelerar o desmatamento, as consequências podem ser devastadoras para a Floresta Amazônica, para seus moradores e para as atividades econômicas que dependem de sua preservação.

Há décadas, cientistas que estudam florestas e clima alertam para um possível

ponto de não retorno

:

 se uma área grande demais da floresta for derrubada, o ciclo da água deixará de ser forte o suficiente para sustentar um ecossistema de floresta tropical.


Em seu lugar, a região se transformaria em uma floresta degradada e em um ambiente seco, como o cerrado, provocando a liberação líquida de carbono que intensifica o aquecimento global e reduzindo as chuvas que abastecem as plantações de soja nas áreas próximas.


O ponto de não retorno em questão depende de vários fatores e é difícil de estimar. No entanto, o limite de desmatamento mais citado é de 20% a 25% da cobertura florestal da Amazônia, intervalo

proposto pela primeira vez em 2018

, por Nobre e pelo biólogo conservacionista norte-americano Thomas Lovejoy.


Os dois argumentaram que “as sinergias negativas entre desmatamento, mudanças climáticas e uso generalizado do fogo” colocariam a floresta em um ciclo de retroalimentação quando esse limite fosse ultrapassado. Um

estudo publicado na revista

Nature

, em maio deste ano, estimou que a faixa do ponto de não retorno estaria mais próxima de 22% a 28% de desmatamento, considerando o aquecimento global de 1,5 a 1,9 grau Celsius que o mundo …

author: Julia Conley
title: Trump Admin Backed Alberta’s Separatists. Canadian Voters Rejected Secession.
content:
Separatist leaders sought advice on their “Let Alberta Decide” campaign from Republican operatives.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

The leader of the movement that opposed separatists’ efforts to achieve independence for the Canadian province of Alberta said Monday night that voters’ resounding rejection of the secession push would “send a very strong message to the rest of the world,” after Trump administration officials backed the effort.

“Don’t mess with Canada,” said Thomas Lukaszuk, a former deputy premier of Alberta who led the Forever Canadian campaign.

With more than 1.8 million votes counted Tuesday morning, 75.7% of Alberta voters had supported remaining in Canada with no further referendum. Just over 24% voted in favor of holding a second referendum on separating from the country, which would have been binding.

Around 76% of voters in the Canadian province of Alberta have rejected a proposal to hold a referendum on independence, according to unofficial results. It's a victory for PM Mark Carney but more than 300,000 backed the proposal, and separatists say their grievances remain. pic.twitter.com/vZ5gUA7Cwr

Separatist leaders, many of whom came to prominence after leading protests against public health precautions during the coronavirus pandemic, were welcomed to meetings at the US State Department in recent months, where they sought advice on their “Let Alberta Decide” campaign from Republican operatives. The meetings, said British Columbia premier David Eby, amounted to “treason.”

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent expressed support for the separatist movement, which does not have a central leader but is backed by groups in Alberta including the Alberta Prosperity Project and Stay Free Alberta.

Bessent said in January that the province, which holds the world’s fourth-largest proven oil reserves, could be “a natural partner for the US.”

“I think we should let them come down into the US,” Bessent told right-wing podcaster Jack Posobiec. “They have great resources. The Albertans are very independent people… Alberta has a wealth of natural resources, but they won’t let them build a pipeline to the Pacific.”

Former Trump administration adviser and Republican megadonor Elon Musk also said on social media this month that Alberta “should separate” from Canada.

The referendum came as President Donald Trump has threatened to take over Canada and make it “the 51st state,” accusing the Canadian government of treating the US “very badly.” He has imposed 50% tariffs on a range of Canadian imports, setting off a trade war.

Separatists in Alberta, whose views have long been in the minority, have complained that the province “sends $20 billion more to Ottawa every year than it gets back,” and fumed over any environmental policies that threaten Alberta’s oil industry, one of the most polluting in the world.

Canceled oil pipelines, a bill banning oil tankers from stopping and unloading at ports on British Columbia’s coast, and an emissions cap have been decried as evidence that the federal government has treated Alberta as “a colony,” as one separatist told The Associated Press Monday — despite the fact that the emissions cap was dropped for the province’s oil and gas sector last year.

“They want to take and take and take from us, and not return anything,” Dustin Degenhardt said while voting.

Danielle Smith, the leader of the United Conservative Party and the premier of Alberta, said she supported the province remaining in the country and applauded the vote results.

But at a recent online forum, Smith outlined the concerns of separatists, saying families face growing affordability struggles and asserting the province has been forced to provide hundreds of thousands of immigrants whom the federal government has resettled there.

A report released in June by the Calgary Chamber of Commerce found that seceding from Canada would shrink Alberta’s economy by $62 billion per year.

Prime Minister Mark Carney said after the vote Monday night that the decision by a large majority of voters was “a great result for Canada.”

“Albertans have chosen unity,” said Carney. “They’ve chosen to build together. They’ve chosen to continue to take care of each other, to move forward together.”

Podcast host Laura Babcock said Tuesday that “the separatists and Trump lost. Canada won.”

author: Chris Walker
title: Mahmoud Khalil Files Appeal to SCOTUS to Block Trump Admin From Detaining Him
content:
The pro-Palestine activist says the Trump administration is infringing upon his free speech rights.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

Former Columbia University graduate student and pro-Palestine activist Mahmoud Khalil has filed a request to the Supreme Court, asking it to overturn an appellate court’s ruling that could lead to his being detained and deported by the Trump administration in the near future.

Khalil is a legal U.S. resident, and his spouse has citizenship status, making the administration’s attempt to deport him last year an extraordinary move. In March 2025, shortly after he graduated, he was detained by immigration officials, with Secretary of State Marco Rubio utilizing scarcely used powers of his office to do so despite Khalil’s legal residency, citing unfounded claims that the activist was involved in “antisemitic protests and disruptive activities” while studying at Columbia.

Khalil was kept in a Louisiana immigration jail, but was released in June 2025 after a federal judge found Rubio’s actions were likely unconstitutional. The administration appealed, and in January 2026, a 2-1 decision from the Third Circuit Court of Appeals overturned the lower court’s decision, stating that Khalil’s claims couldn’t be addressed at that level of the judicial system, and had to be moved to an immigration court, which is managed by the executive branch.

On Monday, Khalil and his lawyers announced that he was appealing that decision to the Supreme Court, hoping that they will overturn it, allowing him to remain protected from being detained again for the time being. He called the continued efforts by the administration an assault on his free speech rights.

“If the Trump administration can punish someone for their pro-Palestine speech, this or any future administration can punish anyone for any speech, whether it’s pro-Palestine, pro-Israel, or anything,” he said in a statement announcing his appeal.

Khalil will still have legal avenues available to him to challenge the Trump administration’s attempts to deport him, but his options to thwart the White House’s actions would be much narrower if the Supreme Court doesn’t take his case. For a case to be heard, at least four of the nine sitting justices must agree to the writ of certiorari that Khalil submitted to them. Afterward, it would likely be a few months before oral arguments begin, and then it would likely take until the end of the current term — around May or June 2027 — for a decision to be rendered.

Khalil’s case has been rife with irregularities, including being pushed by the Trump administration to proceed at a faster tempo than other similar cases. Khalil also detailed last spring the horrors he faced while he was detained in Louisiana, decrying how his rights were being infringed upon.

“I think about the breakneck speed with which my case was heard and decided, running roughshod over due process,” he wrote in his piece for The Washington Post. “On the flip side, I think about those I am locked up with, many of whom have been languishing for months or years waiting for their ‘due process.'”

“Why should protesting Israel’s indiscriminate killing of thousands of innocent Palestinians result in the erosion of my constitutional rights?” Khalil stated, adding that, “A democracy for some — a democracy of convenience — is no democracy at all.”
