author: CMI Argentina
title: El Deutsche Bank, exbanco de Caputo y Bausili, se benefició con las operaciones del oro argentino
content:
Un amigo de la casa ganó con la timba del Gobierno.


Una fuente del BCRA reveló a Página/12 que la entidad alemana fue una de las contrapartes de la operación que dejó pérdidas por 1.023 millones de dólares. La AGN exige los contratos.


Luis Caputo y Santiago Bausili


Por Raúl Kollmann


La instrucción interna del Banco Central es mantener el secreto de con quién se firmaron los contratos que terminaron con la pérdida de 1.023 millones de dólares. Incluso se evade entregar los contratos a la Auditoría General de la Nación (AGN). Sin embargo, una fuente indubitable del BCRA le reveló a Página/12 que una de las contrapartes, o sea, uno de los que ganó todo o parte de los 1.023 millones de dólares, fue el Deutsche Bank, el banco en el que trabajaron y tuvieron cargos altísimos Luis Toto Caputo y Santiago Bausili. La incompatibilidad es escandalosa, como mínimo, desde la ética: hicieron un negocio ruinoso que favoreció a sus exempleadores. El movimiento del oro y —en exclusiva— la pérdida de 1.000 millones de dólares fueron publicados por Página/12 el 13 de septiembre, hace más de un mes. La razón verdadera por la que no quieren mostrar los contratos es que vendieron el derecho a comprar el oro a un precio muy bajo (algo más de 3.000 dólares la onza), pero el precio del oro se disparó a más de 4.000 y eso es lo que provocó el desastre. El BCRA tuvo que consignar la pérdida en su balance porque debió cubrir la calamidad con dólares de las reservas. Como el cierre del ejercicio fue el 31 de diciembre, no hubo más remedio que consignarlo. Igual trataron de esconderlo: se registró como una especie de nota adicional, no en el cuerpo principal del balance, intentando tapar todo con las ganancias que se produjeron por la subida del precio mundial. Esa ganancia se hubiera obtenido igual si no movían el oro de la calle Reconquista, pero hubo que restarle lo que perdieron por la catastrófica jugadita especulativa de Milei-Caputo-Bausili.


Ocultar, esconder


Dentro del BCRA, la orden es no mostrar los contratos que llevaron a la pérdida. Lo que argumentan hacia adentro es que no se informa porque existe “un grave riesgo sobre las reservas del país”. Esa afirmación es contraria al dictamen de la dirección de Jurídicos del BCRA, que sostuvo, por escrito, que las reservas no corrían riesgo, que se podían enviar a Londres, “porque se trata de reservas soberanas”. No obstante, la instrucción que se les dio a quienes manejan toda la cuestión del oro es que ni siquiera se le entreguen los contratos a la Auditoría.


Expertos en materia de inversiones como Carlos Maslatón exigieron que el BCRA “muestre todas las operaciones, fechas, precios, contrapartes y quién las autorizó”. Parece un reclamo elemental. En uno de sus posteos, Maslatón da a entender que no solo hubo negligencia sino también corrupción.


Empleados fieles


Este diario pudo confirmar, de forma indubitable, que una de las contrapartes de las operaciones del Central fue el Deutsche Bank, aunque falta el dato de si fue el que se quedó con todo el negocio o hubo otras contrapartes. Como el BCRA no les exhibe los contratos ni a sus propios empleados, se puede establecer que el Deutsche cobró parte de los 1.023 millones de dólares; no se sabe si todo.


Luis Caputo trabajó durante años en el Deutsche en Argentina, llegando a ser designado director titular y presidente de la entidad en 2008. Santiago Bausili también fue funcionario del Deutsche y en tiempos de Mauricio Macri fue denunciado por haber percibido bonos e incentivos de la entidad bancaria, ya estando en funciones en el Estado. Durante la administración macrista, otra vez de la mano de Caputo-Bausili, el banco fue beneficiado con la emisión y colocación de títulos de la deuda soberana argentina en los mercados internacionales. Ambos exfuncionarios del gobierno del PRO terminaron sobreseídos por la telaraña judicial macrista de Comodoro Py.


El haberle dado al Deutsche todo o parte del “negocio” en el que Argentina perdió 1.023 parece un escándalo y sostiene la sospecha de Maslatón y los que afirman que no solo hubo impericia, sino corrupción. Para el ciudadano común es difícil entender lo que se hizo. En términos técnicos, se le vendió a uno o varios bancos un call, o sea, el derecho a comprar el oro dentro de tantos meses a tal precio. Pero el precio que se fijó fue levemente por arriba de 3.000 dólares. Milei-Caputo-Bausili hicieron la operación sin tener un resguardo a la suba y, como el oro se disparó por …

author: Adam Schwartz
title: Require Police to Get a Warrant to Search ALPR Data
content:
This post was co-written by

Andi Cao

, an EFF legal intern.


Automated license plate readers (ALPRs) are mass surveillance. They photograph every passing car and log where and when it was captured, building a searchable record of where nearly everyone drives.

Cities should not buy them

, and cities that already have them should shut them down.


Where these systems still operate, courts and state legislatures must reduce their harms by (among other things) requiring police to get a warrant before searching stored ALPR data. A warrant requirement would not make mass surveillance acceptable, but it would require police to justify a search to a judge before accessing records of people’s movements. Without this independent judicial check on police power, officers have been searching this data for improper reasons (many exposed by EFF) that violate our fundamental rights.


A warrant requires a judge to find probable cause and specificity—many warrantless police searches of ALPR data lack both. Officers have searched this data to profile Romani people, monitor protesters, investigate an abortion, find immigrants for deportation, track a man who complained about a deputy, stalk romantic partners, and even for no stated reason beyond “LMAO.” A warrant requirement would force law enforcement to justify these searches

before

 accessing sensitive location records, not leave the people they target to discover and challenge the abuse after the harm is done.


What a Warrant Requires


Warrants are a check on police power. Before officers can search a person or their property, the

Fourth Amendment

 requires them to convince a neutral judge, under oath, that probable cause exists, meaning a fair probability the search will turn up evidence of a crime. The warrant must also describe with particularity what will be searched, so police cannot go on a fishing expedition. Critically, the officer who wants to search is not the person who decides whether the search is justified.


That is why warrants are required for so many kinds of police surveillance. For example, police generally need a warrant to

wiretap phone calls

, to

search the contents of a cell phone

, and to

obtain historical cell phone location records

.


Stored ALPR data reveals sensitive information about the private details of our lives: where we go, when, and with whom. That’s why we believe police searches of stored ALPR data should also require a warrant. Earlier this month, a federal judge in Oklahoma

agreed

.


What Goes Wrong Without a Warrant: San Jose, California


San Jose demonstrates the harmful consequences of letting law enforcement search stored ALPR data without a warrant. EFF and the ACLU of Northern California represent SIREN and CAIR-California in a

lawsuit

 challenging this practice.


The first problem is the sheer number of times that SJPD officers search stored ALPR data:

261,711 times

 between June 5, 2024, and June 17, 2025, about 692 searches a day. That scale is the result of having no warrant requirement, which would greatly reduce this kind of casual police surveillance.


Inevitably, officers abuse this unchecked power. In September, San Jose’s police chief

disclosed

 an example from five months earlier: the department had fired an officer who used its ALPR system to track a woman who had accused his cousin of domestic violence, and then shared her location information with his cousin. The abusive search of stored ALPR data

came to light

 only after the woman told police that her alleged assailant had implied he was tracking her.  A warrant requirement would have prevented this.


Of course, similar problems appear nationwide. For each example below, consider how things could have turned out differently if the officer had to put the reason for the search in a sworn warrant application and handed it to a judge.


Racial profiling of Romani people


More than 80 law enforcement agencies

searched the Flock network

 using terms that unfairly stereotype Romani people, often without mentioning any crime. For example, the Grand Prairie (Texas) Police Department searched for “g*psy” six times using a Flock feature that identifies vehicles traveling together, in effect targeting a whole community without naming a crime.


No judge should sign that warrant. Ethnicity is not evidence of a crime, and a search aimed at an entire ethnic group is the opposite of particular: it targets people for

who

 they are, not evidence …

author: Luca Tavan
title: How the Socialist Party is different from the other parties
content:
Members of the Socialist Party are often asked what makes us different from other parties. Prospective left-wing voters bruised by the long history of politicians selling out their principles want to know how we will avoid becoming part of the same establishment we want to challenge. On the other hand, some left-wing Greens question whether the Socialist Party is even necessary, seeing as their party already offers similar policies. 

The only way to answer these questions properly is to explain how the Socialist Party is unlike any other in Australian politics. We have a vision of society and a political strategy that differs fundamentally from all pro-capitalist parties, from the Liberals to the Greens. So what’s so distinctive about our project? 

Socialism!

The first thing is in the name. We are a socialist party, avowedly opposed to the whole capitalist system. Of course, the meaning of the term “socialism” is contested. Many progressive politicians, from UK Greens’ Zack Polanski to New York’s Zohran Mamdani, have ridden a wave of hostility toward right-wing billionaires and use the term “socialism” to describe their goal of reformed capitalism. 

But we don’t just want to tinker with the system: the Socialist Party wants to get rid of capitalism. We oppose an economy based on private business ownership and the exploitation of workers. We support a democratic, socialised economy that abolishes the profit motive and allocates labour and resources based on human need. So we fight the class of business owners and challenge the political and legal system that exists to defend their rule. We think the workers who make everything run, from the transport system to warehouses to our hospitals, should be in charge, not business owners and politicians. 

Our policies reflect this: they’re not just about explaining how the world could be made nicer. They express a fundamental hostility to the fact that our society is organised around profit-making. They’re an argument that the wealth of the rich and the assets of corporations are the products of their exploitation of workers, and that we want to take back as much of that wealth as we can. 

Parties can easily adopt socialist terminology, especially when it seems popular. But actually fighting for socialism is another matter. The Australian Labor Party, for instance, adopted the socialist objective into its constitution in 1921:

“The Australian Labor Party is a democratic socialist party and has the objective of the democratic socialisation of industry, production, distribution and exchange, to the extent necessary to eliminate exploitation and other anti-social features in these fields.”

This came at a time when demand for socialism was widespread in the workers’ movement. But party leaders never took the objective seriously. The qualification “to the extent that” was tacked on to signal to capitalists that the ALP didn’t really intend to turn the tables on the economic system. Despite remaining in the party constitution to this day, Labor has been utterly committed to defending the priorities of the capitalist class for over a century. 

For us, socialism is more than just a word—it is our core philosophy.

Building the workers’ movement

That gets to the second thing that makes us different: socialists have a completely distinct strategy for changing the world. Because we think workers should run things, everything we do is shaped by the goal of rebuilding the capacity of workers to organise, demand more, and take on their bosses. 

That’s why Socialist Party members played a crucial role in the Victorian teachers’ strikes earlier this year. Negotiations over pay, conditions and school funding provided an opportunity to organise more socialist teachers, argue for an uncompromising form of trade unionism that doesn’t just accept Labor’s crumbs, and prove in practice that strikes can win real gains. 

Rather than the movement existing to serve parliamentarians, Socialist Party MPs would be bound to use their positions to serve the movement. They would be forbidden from taking all the income that comes with a seat in parliament—they would have to give most of it back to the movement, rather than build their own wealth from their position. No other party is for this—their parliamentary leaders all get filthy rich.

Our inspirations include socialists like Broken Hill miners’ leader Percy Brookfield, who decided to run for NSW parliament while sitting in a prison cell for …

author: Caio Barretto Briso
title: Silêncio de Flávio sobre Ana Clara “foi desesperador”, diz a mãe da menina
content:
Naquele 2 de fevereiro de 2021, a família de Cristiane tinha acabado de acordar e seus dois filhos, a menina com cinco e Pedro com dois anos, estavam brincando na porta de casa. De repente, dois disparos. Cristiane correu e, ao chegar onde as crianças estavam, viu um policial parado diante de Ana Clara. Ele deu vários tiros para o alto sem dizer nada. Não quis nem prestar socorro, só o fez após outro policial se aproximar e dizer “pega a garota que você fez merda”.


“Então ele carregou ela de qualquer jeito, pra não manchar a farda de sangue. Tirei minha filha dos braços dele e levei no meu colo. Ela não chorava, não gemia, não gritava. Perto do hospital, abriu os olhos e desceu uma lagrimazinha do olho dela. Pra mim, ela morreu ali”, lembra Cristiane Gomes da Silva, que também era quase uma criança quando Ana Clara nasceu – tinha 15 anos de idade.


Nesta segunda-feira, 19 de outubro, dia seguinte ao debate da Band entre o presidente Lula e o senador

Flávio Bolsonaro

, a hashtag #PesquiseOCasoAnaClara se tornou um mantra nas redes sociais. Motivo: Flávio é o advogado que manteve o policial Bruno Dias Delaroli, réu pelo assassinato da criança, fora da prisão até agora, como o presidente Lula lembrou no debate.


A história de Ana Clara ganhou repercussão nacional nas últimas semanas, depois que a série jornalística Revelando, criada pela equipe do videocast Calma Urgente, lançou um

episódio

 de 22 minutos sobre o caso, apresentado pela atriz Camila Pitanga. Em 2024, já senador da República, Flávio assumiu a defesa do PM e assinou um recurso apresentado ao Superior Tribunal de Justiça (STJ) para tentar reverter a decisão que determinou o júri popular. Embora o pedido tenha sido negado, até hoje não houve julgamento.


Cristiane, a mãe da garotinha, recebeu muito apoio nas redes sociais, mas também sofreu ataques de apoiadores de Flávio e começou a se sentir ameaçada na região onde vive, no Largo da Batalha, Niterói, perto de onde sua filha foi morta. Tomada por uma crise de pânico e depressão, afastou-se das redes, e ainda foi despejada da casa onde vivia de favor, pois o dono é bolsonarista.


Ela viu trecho do debate entre Lula e Flávio: foi “desesperador ver que Flávio não respondeu a pergunta sobre Ana Clara”, diz. Para ela, “as pessoas não enxergam que sou uma mãe que perdeu uma filha, acham que quero prejudicar o Flávio, há quem diga que a errada fui eu por deixar meus filhos na porta de casa. Flávio defendeu e conseguiu anular o júri do cara, tentou fazer o cara não ser julgado pelo crime que cometeu. Tenho certeza que, se ele for eleito, o caso vai ser esquecido e eu nunca terei o descanso de saber que o assassino da minha filha está pagando pelo que ele fez.”


Cristiane não é uma militante de esquerda – no primeiro turno, ela nem votou, pois sua advogada achou melhor ela não sair de casa por causa das ameaças. Há cinco anos e seis meses aguarda o julgamento do assassino de sua filha ser marcado. A princípio seria em 14 de abril deste ano, dia em que Ana Clara completaria 11 anos de idade, mas foi adiado para 21 de outubro. No fim de agosto, o julgamento foi reagendado para 5 de maio de 2027. “Disseram que foi adiado novamente porque a juíza terá outro compromisso no dia. Só tem ela de juíza? E precisava jogar para o meio do ano que vem?”, revolta-se Cristiane. “A gente sabe que foi aquele policial, a perícia foi feita, a balística das armas foi feita, todos sabem que aquele homem foi o único que atirou, o delegado sabe disso, eu sei, o policial sabe. Mas estou à mercê da Justiça.”


Depois que Ana Clara morreu, a família se desestruturou. Seu caçula, Pedro, hoje com oito anos, ainda lembra da irmã que morreu ao seu lado. Ele faz tratamento com psicólogo desde então e não está morando com a mãe. “Ainda tenho a guarda, mas deixei ele com a avó. Não quero que ele passe pelo que estou passando. Meu sonho é conseguir um emprego para ter a minha casa e trazer ele de volta. Tenho medo que ele sinta que eu o abandonei”, lamenta a mãe.


Cristiane fala sobre como é difícil conseguir trabalho. Ela parou de estudar adolescente, quando engravidou da filha. “Eu tento, mando currículos pra tudo que é canto, faço faxina, mas não consigo nada certo. Preciso me fazer de forte todos os dias, mas às vezes não dá, a realidade da situação chega e bate pânico. Às vezes entrego os pontos e não quero ver ninguém, penso que já deu pra mim essa vida, mas então vejo o Pedro e quero ter ele comigo, preciso dele e ele também …

title: Japonya, Mars'ın uydusundan örnek getirecek uzay aracını taşıyan roketi fırlattı
content:
Japonya Uzay Araştırma Ajansı’nın (JAXA), açıklamasına göre, 5 yıl süreli "Mars Uyduları Keşfi (Martian Moons eXploration - MMX)" görevi kapsamında yeni keşif aracını taşıyan H3 roketini (H3 F10) uzaya gönderdi.

H3 F10 roketi, Japonya'nın güneybatısında yer alan Kagoshima eyaletindeki Tanegaşima Uzay Merkezi'nden 20 Ekim'de yerel saatle 04.41'de fırlatıldı.

Fırlatma anı, JAXA'nın internet sitesinde linki paylaşılan YouTube kanalında "Bu, JAXA öncülüğünde gerçekleştirilen, dünyada bir ilk olma özelliği taşıyan görev" başlığıyla canlı yayımlandı.

Uzay aracı, Mars'ın iki uydusundan biri ve Mars yüzeyinin yaklaşık 6 bin kilometre üzerinde yörüngede dönen, 22 kilometre çapındaki Phobos'ta da inceleme yapacak.

Phobos'tan toplanan kaya ve kum gibi örneklerin Dünya'ya getirilmesinin amaçlandığı görevle Mars'ın gizemli uydularının kökeninin araştırılması ve yeni teknolojilerin geliştirilmesi hedefleniyor.

578 milyon dolarlık yatırımla planlanan MMX görevinin başarılı olması halinde bu, "Mars'tan veya uydusundan Dünya'ya analiz edilmek üzere numune getirilen ilk görev" olacak.

Başarıyla ilerlemesi halinde uzay aracı, fırlatıldıktan yaklaşık bir yıl sonra Mars çevresindeki yörüngeye girecek ve Phobos'a inecek.

İniş denemeleri, Phobos'un keşfi ve Dünya'ya dönüş olmak üzere 3 aşama şeklinde hareket edecek uzay aracının Mart 2031 sonuna kadar geri dönmesi öngörülüyor.

Dünya'ya dönüş yolunda uzay aracı, topladığı numuneleri içeren kapsülü, Avustralya bölgesinde teslim alınmak üzere salıverecek.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

title: SPK'den Tera Yatırım'a zorunlu pay alım teklifi kararı: Oy hakları donduruldu, paylara işlem kısıtı getirildi
content:
Ankara – Sermaye Piyasası Kurulu, Peker Gayrimenkul Yatırım Ortaklığı AŞ'de yönetim kontrolünü elde eden Tera Yatırım Holding AŞ'nin zorunlu pay alım teklifi yükümlülüğünü yerine getirmemesi nedeniyle bir dizi karar aldı. Buna göre, Tera Yatırım Holding ve bazı ilişkili şirket ve fonların oy hakları donduruldu; bazı payların Borsa İstanbul'da alım satıma konu edilememesine karar verildi.

Sermaye Piyasası Kurulu, 19 Ekim 2026 tarihli bülteninde Tera Yatırım Holding AŞ'nin Peker Gayrimenkul Yatırım Ortaklığı AŞ'de yönetim kontrolünü elde etmesinin ardından doğan zorunlu pay alım teklifi yükümlülüğünün yerine getirilmediğini açıkladı.

SPK kararında, Tera Yatırım Holding AŞ'nin, Peker GYO'nun 314 milyon 754 bin 719,80 lira nominal değerli A grubu imtiyazlı paylarının tamamını devraldığı, bu işlem sonucunda şirketin yönetim kontrolünü elde ettiği belirtildi. Zorunlu pay alım teklifinin, 16-29 Eylül 2026 tarihleri arasında gerçekleştirilmesinin ilan edildiği ancak yükümlülüğün yerine getirilmediği kaydedildi.

Kurul, Tera Yatırım Holding AŞ ile Tera Yatırım Menkul Değerler AŞ, Tera Portföy Yönetimi AŞ ve çeşitli Tera Portföy fonlarının sahip oldukları oy haklarının 16 Eylül 2026 itibarıyla kendiliğinden donmuş olduğuna karar verdi. Tasfiyesine daha önce karar verilen bazı Tera Portföy fonlarının donmuş oy haklarının ise çözülmesine hükmedildi.

Tera Yatırım Holding, Tera Yatırım Menkul Değerler, Tera Portföy Yönetimi ve Tera Portföy Algoritmik Stratejiler Serbest Fon'un donmuş oy haklarına konu paylarının genel kurul toplantı nisabında dikkate alınmayacağı bildirildi. Bu oy haklarının, zorunlu pay alım teklifinin tamamlanmasını takip eden ilk gün, Kurulca aksi yönde karar verilmediği sürece kendiliğinden çözüleceği belirtildi.

SPK ayrıca söz konusu şirket ve fonların sahip olduğu, oy hakları donmuş payların zorunlu pay alım teklifi yükümlülüğü yerine getirilinceye kadar Borsa İstanbul’da alım satıma konu edilemeyecek paylar statüsüne alınmasına karar verdi. Bu statünün, söz konusu payları Borsa dışında alacak kişiler için de geçerli olacağı bildirildi.

Kurul, Tera Yatırım Holding'in Peker GYO paylarını devraldığının kamuya açıklandığı tarihte pay sahibi olan ortakların, varsa uğradıkları zararların tazmini için Tera Yatırım Holding AŞ hakkında yargı yoluna başvurabilecekleri konusunda bilgilendirilmelerine de karar verdi.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

title: Andrea Rodríguez Cabral - Hearts on Fire and Other Texts
content:
Author

: Andrea Rodríguez Cabral

Title

: Hearts on Fire and Other Texts

Notes

: Andrea Rodríguez Cabral’s 2026 complete thesis and other relevant texts. This important work of Anarchist Sociologist takes theories and concepts of people like Pierre Bourdieu, Jeff Shantz & Dana Williams, Joan Scott, Louise Tilly, Temma Kaplan, and others, to focus on the Mexican anarchist women in and during Revolutionary Mexico. A great contribution to anyone seeking to understand the interelation between social structures, individual motives, and female participation impacted by both, through an anarchist lens. Translated by Blood Fruit Library/Malvivientes 2026.

Source

: Retrieved 10/19/2026 from https://www.patreon.com/bloodfruit/posts/hearts-on-fire-171440071


María Brousse and Lucía Norman: Two Women Erased from Anarchist History

[1]


Brousse and Norman were prolific writers, organizers, promoters, and revolutionaries. Their work was part of Mexican anarchist history.


 2022 was, by presidential decree, the Year of

Ricardo Flores Magón

 in Mexico. His name appeared in official documents, gaining popularity; likewise, there was a push to publish and promote texts that dealt with him. However, little to nothing was said of the two

women

 who accompanied him in life and whom without Flores Magón would not have been able to develop his revolutionary ideas:

María Brousse

 and

Lucía Norman.


María Brousse

, also known as María Brousse de Talavera and María B. Magón, was born in 1867 in Zacatecas and died in 1946. She took part in many revolutionary groups and clubs such as

Club Reforma, Libertad y Justicia

 and the American Socialist Party. At the same time, she was a writer in some papers cut from

anarchist

 cloth such as

Regeneración

 and the Cuban

¡Tierra!

 María was a shining member in the Mexican Liberal Party (PLM), which she was dedicated to organize, promote, and write for.


 By 1907 María was the romantic partner of

Ricardo Flores Magón

 and remained so until his death in 1922. She was persecuted and spied on by the Mexican and American governments due to her participation in PLM; for example, in 1916 she was arrested for a couple of days with the aim of confiscating some PLM documents she had in her possession. In 1918 she was jailed for five months due to her participation in the creation of the Ricardo Flores Magón International Defense Commission. Following the death of Flores Magón,

María Brousse

 remained active for the remainder of her years, writing in the exiled Spanish paper,

Tierra y Libertad

.


Lucía Norman

 was the daughter of Martín Norman and María Brousse. Originally from Los Angeles, Lucía followed her mother’s footsteps and became a PLM journalist. She also fashioned herself after her mother in writing for papers of an anarchist inclination, such as

Regeneración

 and

Libertad y Trabajo

. Alongside her mother, in 1907, Lucía protested against the jailing of

Ricardo Flores Magón

, who took on the role of her adoptive father. She was present in the movements demanding freedom for the PLM political prisoners from 1907 to 1922, which earned her a couple days in prison in 1912.


 In 1917,

Lucía Norman

 suffered a nervous attack after her romantic partner, Raúl Palma, was imprisoned. This deteriorated her health leading to the cause of her death in August of 1923, almost a year after the death of her adoptive father,

Ricardo Flores Magón

.


Citizens and the Revolution


 Flores Magón was jailed alongside Librado Rivera and Antonio I. Villarreal in the county of Los Angeles, USA in 1907 under orders of Porfirio Díaz. Thanks to the letters rescued and made accessible to the public by Jacinto Barreda Bassols,

[2]

 we are able to know of Flores Magón’s perspective regarding the incarceration. Fortunately, these letters also allow us to peer into the lives of

María Brousse

 and

Lucía Norman

 and analyze the relationship they had with Flores Magón. The letter selection mentioned here is from September 1908 to February 1909, and they are included in the

Correspondencia de Ricardo Flores Magón (1904–1912)

 anthology by Barreda Bassols.


 The letters between María, Lucía and Ricardo were exchanged in secret, hidden in clothing or food. In a November 22, 1908 letter, Flores Magón wrote the following to María,

title: Arnavutlukta halkın isyanı mahkemelere yöneldi, Başbakan Rama saldırılarını sertleştiriyor
content:
Arnavutluk'ta yolsuzluk, eğitim harcamaları ve hayat pahalılığına karşı büyüyen protestolar pazartesi günü de sürdü. Başkentte Eğitim Bakanlığı önünde başlayan öğrenci gösterisi, polisle çatışmaların ardından başka bölgelere yayıldı.


Bir grup gösterici İstinaf Mahkemesi'nin kapı ve pencerelerini kırarak binaya girdi. Kosova merkezli haber ajansı KOHA, göstericilerin birkaç dakika sonra binayı terk ettiğini duyurdu. İspanyol haber ajansı EFE ise Arnavutluk'un A2 CNN televizyonuna dayanarak binada yangın çıktığını bildirdi.


Polis, mahkemeye yönelik saldırıyla bağlantılı beş kişiyi gözaltına aldı, 15 kişiyi de aramaya başladı. Gözaltına alınanlar arasında 16 yaşında bir çocuk var.  


Akşam saatlerinde Başbakanlık çevresinde yeniden çatışmalar yaşandı. Göstericiler polise taş, havai fişek ve Molotof kokteyli attı. Polis, göz yaşartıcı gaz ve tazyikli suyla müdahale etti. Özel harekât birimi RENEA da Başbakanlık çevresinde konuşlandırıldı. 


Sağlık Bakanlığı: 310 kişi yaralandı


Sağlık Bakanlığı'nın 19 Ekim saat 21:00'de açıkladığı bilançoya göre, gösterilerin başladığı 13 Ekim'den bu yana 310 kişi yaralandı. Yaralıların 191'i polis, 88'i gösterici, 31'i ise olaylar sırasında bölgede bulunan kişiler.


Pazartesi günü yaralananlar arasında bir çocuk ve iki basın mensubu da var. Bakanlık, hastanelerde tedavisi süren kişilerin durumunu izlediğini bildirdi.


Yüksek Mahkeme ve Parlamento binalarında yangın


14 Ekim'de göstericiler Meclis Başkanlığı'nın idari binasına girmişti. KOHA'nın haberine göre binadan belgeler dışarı atıldı ve bazı bölümleri ateşe verildi. Aynı gün Eğitim Bakanlığı ve diğer kamu binaları da saldırıların hedefi oldu.


17 Ekim'de Yüksek Mahkeme'nin bulunduğu binanın bir bölümünde yangın çıktı. Ancak sosyal medyada ileri sürüldüğü gibi mahkemenin bütünüyle yok edildiğine ilişkin haberler doğrulanmadı.


Polisin müdahelelerde plastik mermi, gaz ve tazyikli su kullanması da tartışma konusu oldu. Reuters'ın haberine göre Polis Genel Müdürü Skender Hita, orantısız güç kullanımı iddiaları nedeniyle 7 polis memurunu görevden uzaklaştırdı. 


1000 akademisyen: “Rama istifa etsin, geçici hükümet kurulsun”


19 Ekim'de yaklaşık bin öğretim üyesi, öğrenci hareketini destekleyen ve Başbakan Edi Rama'nın istifasını isteyen beş maddelik ortak bir bildiri imzaladı.


Bildirinin ilk maddesinde şu çağrı yer aldı:


Başbakan Rama'yı öğrencilerin taleplerini dinlemeye ve ülkenin yatışmasının yolunu açmaya çağırıyoruz. İstifasını ve kurumsal istikrarı, durumun sakinleşmesini ve yurttaşların iradesine saygıyı güvence altına alacak bir geçici hükümet kurulmasını istiyoruz.


Akademisyenler, güvenlik güçlerinden öğrencilere yönelik şiddete son vermelerini istedi ve hukuka aykırı emirleri uygulamamalarını hatırlattı.


Bildirinin göstericilere yönelik çağrısında da şöyle denildi:


Hükümete şiddet uygulamak ve protestoları gayrimeşru göstermek için gerekçe vermemek amacıyla işletmeleri, kamu mallarını ve özel mülkiyeti koruyun.


İmzacılar arasında muhalefetteki Demokrat Parti'ye yakın akademisyenler, milletvekilleri ve eski siyasetçiler de var. Demokrat Parti lideri Sali Berişa'nın kızı Argita Berişa ve damadı Jamarbër Malltezi de bildiriye imza koydular.  


Protestolar Trump'ın damadı Kushner'in kıyı projesiyle başladı 


Günümüzdeki öğrenci hareketinin kaynağında, mayısta başlayan çevre protestoları var.


Donald Trump'ın damadı Jared Kushner'in desteklediği, Adriyatik kıyısındaki Vjosa-Narta sulak alanında planlanan lüks turizm yatırımı, çevre örgütleriyle hükümeti karşı karşıya getirdi.


Çevre koruma statüsündeki alanlarda yapılaşmanın önünü açan düzenlemelere karşı başlayan hareket, flamingoların yaşadığı doğal alanlara izafeten “Flamingo Devrimi” olarak adlandırıldı. 


Avrupa Parlamentosu, haziranda Arnavutluk hükümetinden doğayı koruma statüsünü zayıflatan düzenlemeleri geri çekmesini istedi.


Avrupa Parlamentosu Yeşiller grubundan Hollandalı milletvekili Tineke Strik, 19 Ekim'de The Guardian'a verdiği demeçte şöyle dedi:


Arnavutluk hükümeti Flamingo Devrimi'ni ciddiye alsaydı bugün burada olmazdık.


Strik, Rama hükümetini Avrupa Birliği'nin çevre standartları Tiran'ı da bağlayıcı hâle gelmeden turizm projesinin işlemlerini hızlandırmaya çalışmakla suçladı.


Rama ise çevre kurallarının ihlal edildiği yönündeki iddiaları reddetti. Turizm yatırımlarının ülkenin ekonomik kalkınmasına katkı sağlayacağını savundu.


Hareketin öğrencilere yayılmasıyla talepler genişledi. Eğitim masrafları, üniversitelerin …

author: Julia Conley
title: Trump Officials Look to Delay Pursuing Defaulted Borrowers Until Midterms Pass
content:
Many Trump voters who have defaulted on student loan payments may soon have wages garnished and benefits seized.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

As the Trump administration makes plans to task private debt collectors with going after millions of student borrowers in default on their federal loans, officials are reportedly pushing for the effort to begin after the midterm elections — as they grapple with the fact that many supporters of President Donald Trump are likely to be affected.

The Washington Sun reported Monday that the U.S. Department of the Treasury is planning to move forward with punitive measures after previously blocking a push by the Education Department and Office of Management and Budget to garnish wages and seize people’s benefits if their loans are in default.

As the Center for American Progress (CAP) said in a report Monday, defaults on student loans have reached record levels, with 9.5 million — or 1 in 5 — borrowers unable to make scheduled payments following the passage of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA).

The law eliminated the Saving on a Valuable Education (SAVE) program and forced borrowers into the Repayment Assistance Plan instead, bringing the average annual cost to $2,163 per borrower, according to CAP.

According to the Sun, administration staffers have advised officials to consider the impact that more upheaval for student borrowers — in the form of debt collectors either following through on the earlier wage-garnishing plan or seizing tax refunds and payments — would likely have on Trump voters.

“This is not who you think it is. The demographics are not good for us,” aides told officials last year when they pushed for a delay on the wage-garnishment plan.

An Associated Press analysis in July found that states with the highest rates of student loan defaults were overwhelmingly Republican-leaning, with Mississippi, Louisiana, and Alabama leading the way.

The advocacy group Protect Borrowers also found earlier this year that roughly two-thirds of all defaulted borrowers live in states Trump won in 2024.

Sources in the administration told the Sun that some officials are pushing for a further delay of the debt collection, as they ensure the Treasury Department’s portal for defaulted borrowers is working. The Defaulted Loans Support Center was launched last month with the stated goal of giving borrowers “a simple, streamlined way to understand the consequences of default and apply online to either rehabilitate or consolidate their loans.”

Others want to begin garnishing wages or seize tax payments for the current tax year ending in April 2027.

One source told the Sun that they expect many calls to government agencies “from borrowers saying: ‘What’s going on? How do I make sure this won’t happen again?’”

“It would be politically insane to do this before the midterms — but 2027 probably makes a little more sense to give Treasury time to get contracts [with debt collectors] signed, up and running,” they said.

Democratic strategist Michelle Kinney called on Democratic candidates to “get LOUD” about the reported plan to shield the White House and the GOP from accountability.

Michael Pierce, executive director of Protect Borrowers, told the Sun that if the administration follows through with the plan — as families struggle with rising gas and grocery prices resulting from Trump’s tariff policy and illegal war on Iran — “what comes next will be a catastrophe for families across the country,” who will have “even less money to put food on the table or make rent.”

“Restarting debt collection the moment any political accountability has passed just shows how little interest Trump has in helping working families stay afloat,” Pierce told the Sun.

author: Dan Canon
title: SCOTUS Is Undermining the Rules That Have Kept US Elections Peaceful for Decades
content:
The Roberts Court has dismantled guardrails preventing a president from turning state agencies against political rivals.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

Courts can create violence simply by putting words on paper. For anyone who has examined any legal system, this should not be a controversial proposition. Some observers argue that the very purpose of written judgments is to justify acts of violence. But one need not go that far to see the immediate effects: A judicial opinion can cause a death, ignite a civil war, legitimize a coup, or even wipe out an entire culture.

If we accept that basic truth, it should not surprise us that jurisprudence can also fuel election-related violence. In U.S. history, the most salient example is United States v. Cruikshank, an all-but-forgotten Reconstruction-era ruling. In Cruikshank, the Supreme Court held that the federal government could not prosecute the broad-daylight massacre of dozens of Black Republicans in 1873, most of whom were defending political offices duly won by their candidates. After two grueling trials and an unlikely guilty verdict by a Louisiana jury, the Court threw out the convictions.

The immediate consequences at southern polls were shocking, if not surprising. Legal scholar James Gray Pope explains that the ruling “opened the floodgates” for white supremacist violence. Over the next three months, southern whites “ousted Republican officials from twelve Louisiana parishes [and] launched a campaign of terrorist assaults on Republican-controlled towns and cities across the South[.]” The strategy worked: Democrats reclaimed Mississippi and Alabama within two years, despite their sizeable Black electorates.

What harm might result from the opinions of today’s Court, an institution unmistakably captured by a power-hungry executive? In a nation of this size, facing democratic decay this severe, there is no such thing as a safe prediction. But if you’re the gambling type, the smart money is on a spectacularly violent future for U.S. elections, if not in the upcoming midterms, then likely by 2028.

Decades of global research have mapped the root causes of election violence. Where contests are winner-take-all, the stakes escalate. Bloodshed is also more common where governing bodies are weak, districts are gerrymandered to exclude voters, or societies carry deep ethnic divisions. Corruption is another critical barometer. A meta-analysis of 65 studies found that the only consistent institutional predictor of election violence is executive constraint: that is, the degree to which a head of state is checked by independent institutions. The more an executive is reined in, the less likely elections are to turn violent. Conversely, when a leader builds informal networks of patronage and punishment, politics ceases to be a contest of ideas and collapses into a fight for survival.

Once we have a grasp on what causes election violence, we can see the pins set up by this Supreme Court, and how those pins are likely to fall in the next few cycles.

The Roberts Court has a long record of hostility toward voting rights, especially the Voting Rights Act. The project Roberts began in 2013 with Shelby County v. Holder, which gutted the VRA’s preclearance formula, reached its culmination in Louisiana v. Callais, dismantling what remained of the law’s practical effects. This means that southern states, which have tried to suppress Black votes for more than 150 years, will be able to restrict access to polls without meaningful federal oversight. According to Justice Kagan’s dissent, Callais will likely result in “the largest reduction in minority representation since the era following Reconstruction.”

Compounding this exclusion is the Court’s surrender to partisan cartels. In Rucho v. Common Cause (2019), the conservative majority declared partisan gerrymandering beyond judicial reach, locking courthouse doors to citizens living in districts with obviously rigged electoral maps. In states like Texas, gerrymandering insulates incumbents from accountability regardless of how the electorate votes. title: Lycée Paul Éluard : une vendetta de la police nationale contre les jeunes ? Rassemblement de soutien
content:
Rendez-vous mardi 20 octobre à 11h devant le commissariat de Saint-Denis avenue Jean Moulin.


Communiqué des personnels mobilisés du lycée Paul Éluard


Depuis dimanche soir, trois lycéen-nes de Paul Éluard à Saint-Denis ont été arrêté-es dans des conditions violentes et indignes, et un autre a été frappé :


 Deux élèves du lycée, avec d'autres jeunes, ont subi une interpellation violente. Une voiture de police a foncé sur elles et eux à toute allure, ils et elles ont été plaqué-es au sol. Ils et elles sont en garde à vue depuis dimanche soir.

 Un autre élève a été suivi par la police lundi et arrêté. Il s'agit du jeune homme que des officiers de la

BAC

 voulaient arrêter au lycée jeudi 15 octobre, ce à quoi les personnels se sont opposés. La police avait alors indiqué que ce jeune homme serait convoqué. Il n'en a rien été.

 Enfin, un élève, déjà mis en garde à vue la semaine passée, a été frappé par un policier alors qu'il rentrait chez lui. Il a dû être soigné à l'hôpital avant de rentrer chez lui.


Parallèlement, un membre du personnel du lycée, qui se promenait dans les rues de Saint-Denis, a subi des jets de gaz lacrymogène venant d'une voiture de police, dont les passagers l'ont dévisagé en ricanant.


Ces violences sont cohérentes avec les recommandations du ministre Laurent Nunez, qui a appelé les forces de l'ordre à ne faire preuve d'aucune retenue. Elles témoignent aussi d'un sentiment d'impunité de la police, encore plus marqué que d'habitude. Elles semblent enfin relever d'une vendetta personnelle du commissariat de Saint-Denis, ciblant certains élèves déjà identifiés, mais plus généralement les lycéen-nes de la ville.

author: Shireen Akram-Boshar
title: Police Violence Increases as 800k Protesters Take to the Streets in France
content:
French leaders condemned the uprising, while the left highlighted escalating police brutality against young protesters.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

On Saturday, France saw its largest nationwide protests in years, as popular outrage over the rising cost of living converged with a month-long student movement against the country’s neglected public education system.

Nearly 800,000 people took to the streets in over 140 cities across France on Saturday, according to France’s major labor union, the CGT. The protests were made up of high school and university students who have blockaded their schools over the past month, demanding better education conditions, as well as labor unions, who mobilized workers in protest of public service cuts, and remnants of the 2018 “Yellow Vests” movement.

Mass protests during the day transformed into riots as evening fell, with multiple city halls and offices set ablaze or otherwise damaged. Police arrested some 2,400 protesters.

French leaders have placed blame on the protesters and the far left, including on the far left political party La France Insoumise (LFI), or France Unbowed. In a televised address Sunday, French President Emmanuel Macron said that the riots were caused by “groups from the far left, joined by a number of delinquents and criminals,” and spoke of police who were injured.

Macron attempted to differentiate between protesters with “legitimate grievances” and those who rioted, while stating that the cost-of-living crisis began because of the war in Iran and its effect on the cost of fuel — for which, he added, France is blameless, as it has not taken part in this war.

But while fuel prices have soared due to the U.S. and Israel’s war on Iran, there are much deeper grievances within France. The underlying causes of the unrest include racism and Islamophobia within France, as well as a decade of austerity policies under Macron alongside the rise of the far-right in the context of an upcoming election.

Marine Le Pen, head of the far-right National Rally party, also blamed “the extreme left” for the protests and riots, and specifically the leader of LFI, Jean-Luc Mélenchon. For his part, U.S. President Donald Trump once again blamed immigration, posting on his social media network Truth Social that France needs to “Close [its] Borders and take control.”

After state officials held crisis meetings on Monday, French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu announced that cities across France would impose partial curfews beginning on Monday night.

But while state media and right-wing leaders blamed the left, it is the police that have undertaken massive violence against protestors over the past month, including on Saturday.

In Paris on Saturday, police used tear gas and stun grenades against protesters even before the start of the demonstrations. John Mullen, an activist living in Paris, wrote that police “beat and injured thousands of protestors” as well as journalists and bystanders, and argued that police violence increased popular anger and led protesters to riot.

Manel ben Boubaker, a French teacher who joined the demonstrations in Paris, explained to Truthout that a “peaceful student-led march” faced “intense tear gas.” She described how police “effectively prevented [a protest] from taking place in and around Place de la République: people were blocked from entering, trapped inside, forced to retreat, and repeatedly tear-gassed in the surrounding streets. The violence was not confined to isolated clashes. It shaped people’s ability to gather, move through the square, and demonstrate at all.”

Left-wing LFI leader Mélenchon also blamed the police for inciting violence. Writing on X, he said that protesters were “calm and joyful everywhere when the police aren’t around.”

Last week, French lawyers and rights groups accused police of inflicting “war-like injuries” on youth protesters over the course of the past few weeks of student movement protests. On October 5, a 15-year-old had his hand blown off by a police stun grenade outside of a school protest, and during Saturday’s protests, a 17-year-old permanently lost vision in one eye after police fired a tear gas canister that hit her in the face.

Rayyan Seriket, a member of the French Student Union Federation, said in an interview on Democracy Now! Monday that Macron is blaming protesters for violence …

author: Amy Goodman
title: Palestinian Youth Helped Save WaPo Journalist Attacked by Israeli Settlers
content:
Jasper Nathaniel recounts how the youth beat settlers back with stones, allowing him and others to rescue Heidi Levine.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

Israeli settlers backed by IDF soldiers brutally assaulted Palestinian olive farmers in the village of Abu Falah, northeast of Ramallah, on Friday. Witnesses say dozens of masked Israeli settlers armed with clubs, sticks, slingshots and guns hurled rocks at Palestinian farmers, set olive trees ablaze and drove people from their fields. Veteran Washington Post photojournalist Heidi Levine, a 64-year-old American, was documenting the attack when settlers began beating her. She suffered stab wounds, a broken rib, four broken vertebrae and a severe hand injury. Levine was wearing a clearly marked press vest and a helmet at the time of the attack. According to the Israeli human rights group Yesh Din, Israeli settlers have carried out at least 170 attacks against Palestinians in the occupied West Bank since September 27, which marked the start of this year’s olive harvest.

“It looked like they were killing her,” says independent American journalist Jasper Nathaniel, who witnessed the attack on Levine and helped intervene. “The Palestinian youth, the shabab, stepped up. They ran out ahead, and they started beating the settlers back by throwing stones at them, which is the only thing that allowed me to then run out front and grab Heidi.” As the journalists and Palestinians retreated into Abu Falah, “The Israeli military jeep that had been standing by the settlers who were attacking us then drives into the village itself, … and they start firing into crowds of Palestinian people.”

This is a rush transcript. Copy may not be in its final form.

AMY GOODMAN: This is Democracy Now!, democracynow.org. I’m Amy Goodman.

In the occupied West Bank Friday, Israeli settlers brutally assaulted Palestinian olive farmers in the village of Abu Falah, northeast of Ramallah. Witnesses say dozens of masked Israeli settlers descended from a nearby hilltop, armed with clubs, sticks and slingshots. Some even had firearms. They hurled rocks at Palestinian farmers, set olive trees ablaze, drove people from their fields.

Veteran Washington Post photojournalist Heidi Levine, an American, was on the scene documenting the attack when settlers surrounded and began beating her. At the time, she was wearing a vest, clearly marked “press” on the front and back, and a helmet. Video of the assault shows masked men surrounding Levine, knocking her to the ground, repeatedly beating and kicking her as she tried to protect herself. They reportedly stole her passport, camera, equipment, wallet and phone. She suffered a broken rib, four broken vertebrae, lacerations across her body and a severe injury to her hand. Levine was taken to a hospital in Ramallah, where she spoke to reporters.

HEIDI LEVINE: Today, I was brutally attacked by — I mean, we saw on the — in the distance, on the hilltop, I would say, at least 50 masked men. I was — I had a 100-to-500-millimeter lens that I could see them masked with slingshots. And when they came running down, I was attacked, pushed to the ground. Luckily, I had my flak jacket and my helmet; otherwise, I probably wouldn’t even be here, because they just kept kicking me and kicking me, like probably 50 times. And then, after like 10 minutes, they, like, tried to get me to stand up, and then pushed me down again and continued to kick me. And I was trying to hold on to my cameras and my pouch, and I had my phone on a string on my neck, that they eventually just broke everything off of me and continued kicking me. And then, the next thing I noticed is I was getting evacuated by my Palestinian colleagues and medical service that rushed me in an ambulance first to the medical center in Abu Falah to check me and then to the hospital here.

AMY GOODMAN: From her hospital bed, Washington Post reporter Heidi Levine went on to say this.

HEIDI LEVINE: One message to their parents: I don’t know how a parent can raise such monsters, really, honestly. I have witnessed their behavior attacking families, and which we recently published a story. And I just am so ashamed that as a parent myself, I cannot understand how a parent can raise such individual monsters. They’re not even humans. author: Colleen DeGuzman
title: Man Dies in ICE Custody at Texas Jail Operated by GEO Group
content:
The daughter of Emiliano Andrade-Covarrubias said staff at the facility wouldn’t “give him his medications.”

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

A 56-year-old Mexican man held at a federal immigration facility in Laredo was found dead in his cell Saturday morning, his daughter and U.S. Rep. Henry Cuellar, D-Laredo, confirmed to The Texas Tribune.

Emiliano Andrade-Covarrubias was found unresponsive by staff at the Rio Grande Processing Center during a security check at around 10 a.m. Saturday, Cuellar said. Staff performed CPR and called emergency services.

Andrade-Covarrubias is the seventh person to die while detained by Immigration and Customs Enforcement in Texas this year — the first being Geraldo Lunas Campos, whose death was ruled a homicide by the El Paso Medical Examiner’s office in January.

He’s also the second to die in an ICE facility in Laredo this year. Felix Alcorta-Rodriguez, a 63-year-old Mexican who was being held at Webb County Detention Center, died on June 19 after being found unresponsive, according to the agency.

The GEO Group, which operates the facility, referred the Tribune to ICE. Officials with the U.S. Department of Homeland Security did not immediately respond to requests for comment sent Sunday and Monday.

Andrade-Covarrubias’ daughter, Estefani Andrade, told the Tribune that her family has not yet been contacted by federal agencies. Instead, she said, they heard about his death on Saturday through the Webb County Medical Examiner, which is performing his autopsy.

Estefani Andrade, 29 and a U.S. citizen, said the family is going to visit the detention facility on Monday to get his belongings.

Andrade-Covarrubias lived in Dallas for decades, had three adult children who were all born in the country and worked as a contractor painting apartments and townhomes, his daughter said. He wanted to eventually return to Mexico and had been travelling back and forth to build a house there, his daughter added.

She said her dad was detained in June at the border after coming back from Mexico by bus. She added that during his months in detention, “he lost weight because he didn’t look the same as when we were doing, like, the video calls with him.”

Cuellar said he planned to visit the facility Sunday afternoon.

“I’ll ask the basic questions: What happened?” he said. “What were the conditions? [Was] there medical? Is there anybody ill? I’m gonna talk to the medical folks there.”

Estefani Andrade said her dad had a heart condition, along with diabetes and high blood pressure. He had medicine with him when he was detained, but she said staff at the center wouldn’t “give him his medications.”

She also said her dad was sick at the detention facility. He had a cough — which she said was concerning since he was hospitalized for COVID-19 in 2021 and that took a lasting toll on his health — and told her that he wasn’t feeling good. He sought help from the facility’s medical staff but he told her that “they would just ignore him.”

She said her dad told her that he felt like medical staff at the center was brushing off his concerns, even when he told the staff that he was having trouble breathing and feeling tightness in his chest.

Estefani Andrade said she is now trying to be strong for her mom, who is devastated.

“When she got the news, she wasn’t all there,” she said. ”It’s hitting her really hard.”

author: Chris Walker
title: Border Czar Homan Confirms Trump Admin Is Looking to Denaturalize Ilhan Omar
content:
Previous inquiries into Ilhan Omar’s citizenship have found no evidence of fraud.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

Appearing on Fox News over the weekend, border czar Tom Homan gave the starkest indication yet that the administration is moving forward with plans to “denaturalize” Rep. Ilhan Omar (D-Minnesota), stripping her of U.S. citizenship status that she’s had since she was 17 years old.

Last week, Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) raided Omar’s residence in Washington D.C., seizing her phone, notebooks, personal computers, and passport. Members of her family have also received subpoenas relating to the investigation. So far, the details of the inquiry have not officially been made public, but sources with knowledge of it say it stems from paperwork Omar’s father submitted when she applied to become a citizen in 2000, at age 17.

Homan appeared to confirm that is the investigation’s focus.

“If you lie during the naturalization process, there is a process to denaturalize somebody. We’ve done it before … And certainly, if the evidence points that way, that could happen” to Omar, he said on the program.

The border czar left some rhetorical wiggle room, but reiterated that the administration was looking into fraudulent behavior by the Minnesota lawmaker or her family members.

“I’m not going to get ahead of the bureau or HSI, but I’ve been told they have a strong case, and we’ll let the evidence lead where it leads,” Homan said.

A person can be denaturalized, or have their citizenship status revoked, only in extreme circumstances — generally, when evidence of fraud is discovered later on. Several conservative conspiracy theorists have alleged that Omar’s father lied about her age when she applied for citizenship, pointing to evidence that she once changed her birth year from 1981 to 1982 in official records, which would have made her 18 when her application was submitted.

But that change was made to correct another error, Omar maintains, and fact-checking websites have demonstrated there is no evidence that the change was for malicious reasons. For denaturalization to occur, there must be evidence beyond a reasonable doubt that fraud actually happened.

Notably, the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) examined accusations of fraud relating to Omar’s citizenship several years ago, and found no evidence to justify moving forward on the matter. But President Donald Trump has targeted Omar for over a decade, including demanding that she and other lawmakers of color “go back” to their own countries after they criticized him in 2019. All four of those members of Congress, collectively known as “the Squad,” are U.S. citizens.

Trump reiterated that demand for Omar during a Newsmax interview this past week.

“I think she hates our country. She is a person that truly hates our country. … I’ve said it many times before, she ought to go back to her own country,” Trump said.

Responding to the raid on her home, Omar blasted the administration, decrying the action as “an attempt to target political enemies and weaponize federal law enforcement.”

“For ten years, Trump has targeted me with baseless lies and smear campaigns. This is just the latest escalation in his campaign of political intimidation,” Omar said, adding: “I will not be silenced.”

Several critics described the raid as outright fascism. But some Democratic lawmakers, including party leaders, have been more muted in their response, including Sen. Chuck Schumer (D-New York), who appears not to have said anything publicly on the matter at all.

Schumer’s silence is a perplexing choice in the eyes of many observers — given its close proximity to the midterm elections, the HSI raid on a lawmaker’s home could easily be cited as additional evidence that a Democratic-controlled Congress is necessary to place a check on such actions by the Trump administration.

author: Unknown
title: Who pays the price of peace?
content:
In his work

The Old Regime and the Revolution

, Alexis de Tocqueville exposes one of the fundamental contradictions of the French Revolution: The monarchy had been overthrown, and the institutions of the old regime had been abolished, yet the centralist tradition of state domination over society persisted within the new order. The regime had changed, but the state’s power to determine social relations remained largely intact.


As Tocqueville demonstrates, therein lies a fundamental danger: Change can perpetuate existing power structures rather than overcome them.


From this perspective, the process currently underway in Turkey concerning the Kurdish question must also be examined. The decisive question is not merely whether the armed conflict will come to an end, but whether the historically entrenched relationship of domination from which this conflict emerged will also change.


After more than half a century of struggle, the Kurdish freedom movement has made historic decisions that fundamentally transform its armed strategy and organizational existence. These decisions cannot be explained by the naivety of a movement unaware of Turkey’s political realities. Throughout its long struggle, the Kurdish movement has come to understand the centralist nature of the state, its security-driven reflexes, and its resistance to democratization. Its insistence on a democratic solution stems not from ignorance of this reality, but from a determination to change it.


However, a movement’s willingness to transform itself offers no guarantee that the state power confronting it will undergo a similar transformation. Today, we are dealing not only with historically entrenched patterns of state conduct, but also with the current regime’s strategy for shaping its own future. The Kurdish question is not separate from this strategy. Rather, it is one of the central issues that the regime seeks to restructure in line with its political and regional objectives.


The transition is not intended to be a solution


The limits of this approach become particularly evident in remarks made by presidential adviser Mehmet Uçum on October 17. Uçum defines the process in unequivocal terms: “This is not a resolution process, but a transition process.”


This is by no means merely a terminological distinction. A resolution requires confronting the historical causes of a conflict, the political demands of the parties involved, and the question of equal rights. The transition described by Uçum, by contrast, is based on ending the movement’s organizational existence, completing the disarmament process in full, and having its completion verified and confirmed by the state. Democratization and a new constitution are designated as subjects for separate negotiations. The idea that they should be made prerequisites for the transition is explicitly rejected.


As a result, the transformation of the Kurdish movement becomes a concrete obligation in the present, while the democratic transformation of the regime is postponed to an indefinite future.


There is a timetable for disarmament, but none for political equality.


Parliament Speaker Numan Kurtulmuş has also stated that even after a law is passed, no further steps will be taken until disarmament has been verified and officially confirmed by the state. At the same time, he calls for an end to “separatist language.” Verifying disarmament is an understandable necessity within a negotiation process. However, when the state authority responsible for verification also dictates which political views may no longer be expressed, this goes beyond security-related oversight.


Uçum, for his part, establishes a hierarchy among political actors within Kurdish politics. He determines who should be regarded as legitimate negotiating partners and who should be considered obstacles to the process. This reveals an approach that seeks not only to define the conditions of the transition, but also to determine the boundaries within which Kurdish political representation is permitted to operate.


Who determines the boundaries of what is politically conceivable?


His remarks on the future constitutional debate are particularly revealing: “No one should expect negotiations on the new constitution to be conducted on the basis of ethnic and identity-based political positions.”


Uçum argues that these issues must come to an end not only in practice, but also “in people’s minds.” This is no longer simply about ending the …

title: Organizations in Rojhilat call on Damascus government to recognize Kurdish language rights
content:
Nine professional associations and civil society organizations from Rojhilat (East Kurdistan) and Iran issued a joint statement condemning the restrictions and bans imposed on Kurdish-language education in Rojava (West Kurdistan).


The statement called on the Syrian government to recognize the right to education in the mother tongue at all levels of education. The signatories also urged international organizations and human rights groups to take action to have these bans lifted.


‘Restrictions cause unrest’


With the start of the new academic year in Syria, the organizations stated that Kurdish students who had previously received education in their mother tongue are now facing restrictions, with Kurdish-language instruction limited to just three hours.


The organizations said these restrictions have caused unrest among students and local communities and led to the cancellation of numerous classes.


‘Recognizing linguistic and cultural diversity is a prerequisite for peaceful coexistence’


Highlighting Syria’s national, linguistic, and religious diversity, the statement criticized the continuation of policies pursued under the former Assad regime. These policies, it added, included stripping large numbers of Kurdish citizens of their citizenship and implementing policies of “Arabization.”


“Recognizing linguistic and cultural diversity is a prerequisite for peaceful coexistence and the development of a democratic society. Imposing a ‘one nation, one language’ model on different communities will only lead to conflict and discrimination,” the statement said.


‘Fundamental rights have been restricted’


The organizations noted that the autonomous administration system established in Rojava following the developments in Syria in 2011 had created greater opportunities for recognizing the region’s linguistic, cultural, and historical diversity.


However, it emphasized that following the overthrow of Bashar al-Assad’s regime and the subsequent political and military changes, the fundamental rights of different ethnic groups, including the right to education in their mother tongue, had been restricted.


Call for an end to restrictions


Drawing attention to established principles of international law and the educational and psychological needs of children, the organizations called for an end to restrictions on education affecting Kurds and other linguistic communities in Syria.


The statement emphasized the right of all students to receive education in their mother tongue at every level and expressed solidarity with students, the Rojava Teachers’ Union, and the people of the region.


In conclusion, the signatories called on international organizations and human rights institutions to take concrete and effective steps to pressure the Syrian government into recognizing and guaranteeing the right to education in the mother tongue.


The signatory organizations are as follows:


1- Kurdistan Teachers’ Union – Sine


2- Kurdistan Teachers’ Union – Seqiz and Ziviye


3- Kurdistan Teachers’ Union – Merîwan and Serabad


4- Harsîn Teachers’ Union


5- Mazandaran Teachers’ Union


6- Bushehr Teachers’ Union


7- Islamabad Traditional Clothing Educators’ Union


8- Zîla Jiyanê (Çroy-e Jiyan) – Saqiz


9- Kurdish Unity Front

author: Unknown
title: ÖHD documents environmental destruction on Mount Gabar
content:
The Association of Lawyers for Freedom (ÖHD) has investigated the ongoing ecological destruction in the Gabar Mountains in the Kurdish province of Şırnak. A delegation from the Ecology Commission of the ÖHD’s provincial executive board and its local branch documented the impact of large-scale deforestation and intensive oil extraction on the ground. The findings of the investigation are expected to be published in a report in the coming days.


ÖHD lawyer Hülya Yıldırım regards the activities on Mount Gabar not as an isolated case of environmental destruction, but as part of the war and security policies pursued in Kurdistan for decades. She noted that forests are also being cleared in the neighboring mountainous regions of Besta and Cudi, while fires are destroying large areas of land and natural habitats are being damaged by mining operations and environmentally harmful industrial facilities.


“There are now oil wells and extraction facilities in virtually every corner of Mount Gabar. As a result, the mountain is literally being blasted apart. The Tigris River is being polluted by oil leaks and petroleum waste,” said Yıldırım, a member of the ÖHD Ecology Commission.


Oil extraction hinders return to destroyed villages


According to the delegation’s observations, the impact of oil extraction extends beyond the immediate destruction of the natural environment. The health of local residents and workers, as well as livelihoods dependent on agriculture and livestock farming, are also at risk.


The consequences are particularly severe for people who have been waiting for decades to return to their home villages. Numerous settlements in the region were burned down and forcibly depopulated during the dirty war against the PKK in the 1990s. According to the ÖHD, current oil extraction and development activities are creating additional obstacles to the resettlement of these villages.


Yıldırım also criticized the fact that the approval procedures for activities affecting the natural environment do not even comply with the requirements of existing legislation. She argued that these practices reflect a policy that views forests, mountains, soil, and waterways solely as resources to be exploited for economic gain.


“These areas, these mountains, this land, and this river are all regarded merely as resources. We will continue to oppose this mentality and the approval procedures that do not even comply with existing laws,” the lawyer stated.


‘This destruction is a policy of special warfare’


ÖHD lawyer Ayşe Şehriban Demirel, who participated in the field inspection, also placed the environmental destruction within the region’s political context. She argued that the activities on Mount Gabar should not be viewed solely from an economic perspective, but as an expression of a deliberate policy targeting the Kurdish population and their living environment.


“What is happening here is a policy of special warfare. This destruction causes us profound pain. We are working to put an end to this exploitation and ensure that those responsible are held accountable,” Demirel said.


The ÖHD plans to make the findings gathered during its investigation public in the coming days and expand its legal and public advocacy efforts against environmental destruction. The organization also intends to link resistance to the activities on Mount Gabar with efforts to protect the neighboring mountainous regions of Cudi and Besta.


“We will expose the ecological destruction on Mount Gabar and raise our voices against this exploitation and destruction of nature, particularly in Cudi and Besta as well,” Demirel announced.

title: Συγκέντρωση ενάντια τον ερχομό του ισραηλινού κρουαζιεροπλοίου Crown Iris, Τρίτη 20/10 11:00 πλ. 1866, Χανιά
content:
Κάλεσμα του Συντονισμού Δράσεων Αλληλεγγύης στην αντιστεκόμενη Παλαιστίνη

title: Petites leçons de manipulation par CHATGPT ... et le monde qui se profile derrière
content:
Présentation, discussion et apéro autour du livre "Petites leçons de manipulation par CHATGPT" avec l'autrice Sarah Dubernet à la médiathèque alternative Mille Bâbords (61 rue Consolat) samedi 24 octobre à 18h30.


Samedi 24 octobre à 18h30 la médiathèque des luttes, Mille Bâbords, accueille Sarah Dubernet pour discuter de son livre sur le monde de ChatGPT.


Trois semaines à harceler ChatGPT sur différentes questions qui fâchent ; voici un livre dans lequel l'autrice lui fait dire ce que ses concepteurs et financeurs ne veulent pas qu'il dise : ses censures, sa propagande, l'idéologie transhumaniste et les responsabilités politico-industrielles qui en découlent, les ésotérismes et exotérismes scientifiques, religieux, politiques… Une joute improvisée entre une technocritique et une IA sur le système technicien, son impact et les méthodes d'ingénierie sociale qui lui permettent d'avancer toujours dans le même sens, sans jamais être dérangé.


Ce livre souligne l'importance de protéger notre intelligence, nos questions et nos propres façons d'y répondre face à une machine qui n'a pas vocation à nous éveiller. Si l'autrice a pu lui faire dire tout ça, c'est parce qu'elle connaissait déjà les sujets abordés. Mais ChatGPT expliquera ici que son rôle est au contraire de nous orienter vers un tout autre chemin… les échanges sont étayés de rapports institutionnels.


Ceci n'est pas un livre sur ChatGPT. C'est un livre sur son monde et la façon dont il le sert. Ces échanges constituent un document rare, un témoignage précieux, non seulement sur les mécanismes de l'IA mais aussi sur la nature même du « dialogue » que l'on nous vendra demain comme neutre et transparent alors qu'il sera au contraire de plus en plus « sécurisé »


Mille Bâbords est un lieu de culture politique et de rencontre pour la vie associative et militante marseillaise proposant un service de prêt gratuit pour toustes. La bibliothèque est ouverte au public lors des permanences tous les lundis et les 2ème et 4ème jeudis de 15h à 18h.

title: Iqaluit woman charged with 2nd-degree murder
content:
RCMP have charged a woman with second-degree murder following a disturbance in Iqaluit’s Tundra Valley neighbourhood over the weekend.


Police found a 37-year-old woman with life threatening injuries in the city’s 2400 block at around 5:50 a.m. on Saturday, said RCMP spokesperson Sgt. George Henrie in a news release.


She was transported to Qikiqtani General hospital, where she died.


Christie Nutarariaq, 32, has been charged with second degree murder in relation to the incident.


The incident is unrelated to

another

 murder charge that police announced Monday.


In that case, RCMP charged a 21-year-old Qaqasie Aningmiuq with second-degree murder, following an altercation on Oct. 6 that left one man dead.


Nutarariaq is in custody. Her next court appearance is set for Nov. 17.

author: Unknown
title: Cops raid DIY HRT meeting in Berlin
content:
This Sunday, 18 October 2026, German police raided a trans DIY HRT event organized by The Dolls Berlin in community centre Casa Kuà.

While the group was holding a talk about cryptocurrency and their role in purchasing HRT online, 38 uniformed and plain clothes cops stormed the building, confiscating hormones and money from attendees, recording their identity and detaining them for over 4 hours. So far, nobody was charged with any crime, (as there is nothing illegal about having hormones or money on your person).

The intimidation raid has shocked the community and over a hundred people gathered quickly for a counter demo. One person was arrested during the demo.

title: A trans woman, Joelle, was denied a spot in a cancer ward in the UK because she was trans and it…
content:
A trans woman, Joelle, was denied a spot in a cancer ward in the UK because she was trans and it lead to her death from an easily treatable form of lymphoma. As she was dying she begged for a room in either the male or female ward - but she was denied being told to wait until they had a rare single room available. For 16 days she was in that hospital dying from something easily treatable because of transphobic legislation. Sex/gender segregated wards are just another way the government violently enforces the sexgender binary - causing the death of transgender and gender diverse people.

Trans Legal Clinic is crowdfunding money to fund the legal case to get justice for Joelle and to prevent any more trans people from being denied care the way she was. If you can donate please do.
