author: Natalia Viana
title: A eleição das Big Techs
content:
Quer receber os textos desta coluna em primeira mão no seu e-mail? Assine a newsletter Xeque na Democracia, enviada toda segunda-feira, 12h. Para receber as próximas edições,

inscreva-se aqui.


“Wow”, tuitou Elon Musk, dono do X, depois que as apostas no site Polymarket passaram a favorecer Flávio Bolsonaro na disputa contra Lula, demonstrando quem é seu favorito nas eleições brasileiras. O advogado Martin de Lucca, tuitou: “Primeiro eles cancelaram o X. Depois cancelaram o Rumble. Recentemente, até cancelaram o Polymarket. O tiro saiu espetacularmente pela culatra”, escreveu Lucca, que advoga para a Truth Social, rede de Donald Trump, e para a Rumble, rede social de direita que teve investimento milionário de JD Vance e de Peter Thiel, depois da vantagem de Flávio no primeiro turno. “Que bela manhã, né Brasil?”. 


JD Vance reuniu-se com Flávio Bolsonaro em maio deste ano, e com André Marinho, filho do coordenador de campanha bolsonarista, em abril. Seu aliado e fiador, Peter Thiel, esteve em São Paulo apenas duas semanas depois, em 30 de abril, com uma comitiva de pelo menos 15 executivos, segundo

revelou

 o jornalista Paulo Motoryn. De acordo com o

site Amado Mundo

, a rede Rockbridge Network, fundada por JD Vance, mantém um representante integrante dentro da sede de campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro em São Paulo, e enviou um plano de trabalho que incluía a criação de um Conselho de Tecnologia para assessorar sua campanha,

segundo

 o Intercept. 


Mark Zuckerberg, em janeiro do ano passado, nomeou o Brasil – sem nomear – ao afirmar que “os países latino-americanos têm tribunais secretos que podem ordenar empresas para silenciosamente derrubar [posts]” e que se uniria ao governo de Donald Trump para lutar contra essas ordens secretas – a referência eram ordens do STF depois da tentativa de Golpe de Estado em 2023. 


Os donos das Big Techs estão acompanhando de perto as eleições brasileiras. Afinal, sabem que elas serão cruciais para definir como será o futuro dos seus negócios. 


O caso mais notório de interferência, até agora, tem sido a Meta – empresa que mais faturou com impulsionamento de campanhas, R$282 milhões. Mesmo assim, funcionários da empresa

reclamaram

 em canais internos da inação dos desenvolvedores lotados nos EUA em reverter o banimento da conta de anúncios da campanha de Lula no Instagram, em 9 de outubro. Os americanos fizeram corpo mole em vez de permitir condições iguais às do adversário, que seguia impulsionando seus conteúdos. 


Mas esse foi apenas um dos eventos. Na semana passada, a IA da Meta permitia que qualquer pessoa criasse imagens pró-Flávio e contra o Lula – acusando o PT de corrupto, por exemplo. Se o mesmo pedido era feito sobre o candidato do PL, a IA respondia que não podia gerar a imagem. A Meta reconheceu que sua IA permitiu a criação de imagens favorecendo Flávio e que “a conta de anúncios da campanha de Lula foi desativada por engano por pouco mais de 1 hora, e não por razões políticas”.


Antes disso, a Meta suspendeu por algumas horas a conta do canal Revelando Brasil no Instagram, que tem publicado vídeos documentais sobre casos envolvendo Flávio Bolsonaro, quando este se tornava o principal assunto das redes, uma semana antes do primeiro turno. Até agora não houve explicação do porquê.    


A tendência para o lado da campanha do filho de Jair incomodou até mesmo o TSE, que na semana passada decidiu que a Big Tech tem que agir com isonomia sobre conteúdos das duas campanhas – e que

prove

 que está fazendo isso. Em caso de descumprimento, a Meta terá que pagar R$ 500 mil por dia.


O Ministério da Justiça acionou a Agência Nacional de Proteção de Dados (ANPD) e o Ministério Público Federal para abrir uma investigação contra a Meta, e a Procuradoria Federal dos Direitos do Cidadão do MPF já

abriu um procedimento para investigar a empresa

. Além disso, a deputada Érika Hilton (PSOL-SP) está coletando assinaturas para uma CPI na Câmara dos Deputados para investigar se está havendo interferência das Big Techs nas eleições. 


A mobilização chamou a atenção da imprensa internacional – o que forçou a Meta a publicar um comunicado negando tentar interferir nas eleições. A empresa ainda saiu com essa: “Há muito tempo, a Meta alerta que as regras rígidas do Brasil para conteúdo digital aumentam o risco de aplicação excessiva e ameaçam a liberdade de expressão. Desde 2025, essas regras ampliaram a possível responsabilidade das plataformas por conteúdo e anúncios …

author: Alexei Miagkov
title: Announcing Privacy Badger for Safari on macOS
content:
Exciting news for Safari users: Privacy Badger is now available on Safari for macOS! You’ll need Safari version 26.5 or higher to use it.


Whether you want to protect yourself from data brokers or just don’t want Big Tech profiting off your browsing data, Privacy Badger is here to help. More than 4 million people already use EFF’s free tracker-blocking extension to take a stand against online surveillance. Safari users can now join them and EFF in the fight for a better web. 

 


Install Privacy Badger


Support the Fight Against Online Tracking


Safari support has been one of Privacy Badger’s most

requested

 features for years. Thanks to recent improvements in Safari's extension support, we’ve finally made it happen for Safari version 26.5 and higher. Privacy Badger is now available on all major desktop browsers. And before you ask, yes, we will look into supporting

Safari for iOS

 once we've ironed out any issues on macOS.


Why Install Privacy Badger on Safari?

 


Most websites

 contain invisible tracking code that lets companies collect, share, and profit from your personal data. Some of those companies are data brokers that sell your information to anyone willing to pay. Creepy ads are just the tip of the iceberg when it comes to the harms of online tracking: Once your information enters the data broker ecosystem, it’s nearly impossible to know

who buys it

 or what they’re doing with it. Privacy Badger blocks online trackers to prevent your browsing data from being used against you. 

 


Privacy Badger goes beyond Safari’s 

built-in privacy features

 to provide additional protection against online tracking. In its default browsing mode, Safari limits the information that trackers can access but still allows them to load. Privacy Badger blocks trackers from loading in the first place, preventing them from tracking you using

techniques

 that bypass Safari’s protections.

 


Privacy Badger works well by itself, and will continue to enhance your privacy when installed along side an ad blocker or with 

Safari’s Advanced settings

 to

block trackers in all windows

. Since Privacy Badger

automatically learns

 to block trackers, Privacy Badger will block trackers that other tools don’t know about or

choose not to block

.

 


For example, Privacy Badger blocks

tracking from widgets

 like embedded tweets, comments sections, and video players. These widgets can share your data even if you never click on them. Privacy Badger prevents these trackers from loading and replaces them with

click-to-activate placeholders

.

 


Beyond tracker blocking, Privacy Badger automatically sends the

Global Privacy Control (GPC) signal

 to tell websites not to sell or share your personal information. The GPC signal is already legally binding in 

a growing number of states

, including California, Colorado, New Jersey, and Connecticut. 

 


All these features (

and more

) work together to help keep your browsing activity private on Safari.

 


Try It Out and Spread the Word

 


If you use Safari on macOS, give Privacy Badger a try. You’ll install Privacy Badger through the App Store on your macOS device. Installing extensions is a little more complicated on Safari than other browsers, so follow Apple’s

directions here

 if you’re having trouble. 

 


This is our first release of Privacy Badger for Safari, and we will keep improving it based on your feedback. If you run into any problems, let us know by emailing

extension-devs@eff.org

, or by opening an issue on

GitHub

. And if blocking harmful trackers causes issues on a website you visit, you can

disable Privacy Badger for that specific site

 while keeping it enabled and protecting you everywhere else. You can also let us know about broken sites by using the “Report broken site” button found next to the “Disable for this site” button in Privacy Badger’s popup window.

 


When you use Privacy Badger, you join EFF and millions of other users in the fight for a better web. Help spread the word by telling your friends and family who use Safari that they can use Privacy Badger too! 

 


Install Privacy Badger

 


Support the Fight Against Online Tracking

author: Chris Walker
title: Abdul El-Sayed Schools Heckler Who Questioned His Loyalty to the US
content:
The heckler asked El-Sayed if he disavowed the Muslim Brotherhood, which the candidate has done in past remarks.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

Michigan Democratic candidate for U.S. Senate Abdul El-Sayed responded to a heckler at a recent campaign event who appeared to question his loyalty to the country based solely on his religious beliefs.

El-Sayed, who is Muslim, spoke on Saturday at a campaign event in Caro, Michigan, a Republican-leaning area of the state. A heckler who identified himself as “Tommy” shouted toward the candidate, interrupting the forum by asking El-Sayed if he would “disavow the Muslim Brotherhood.”

El-Sayed has already repeatedly disavowed the Muslim Brotherhood, and has fended off myriad attacks against him that have emanated from anti-Muslim voices. He responded to the outburst by questioning why Tommy would ask the question in the first place.

“Sure, yeah, absolutely,” El-Sayed said, according to a video that has now been shared by his campaign. “But I want to ask the question — why are you asking the question? … What are you implying? Do you assume that I wouldn’t?”

“Yes,” Tommy responded, rationalizing his action by saying he had not heard El-Sayed distance himself from the group before.

El-Sayed turned the question around on Tommy. “Have you disavowed them? I haven’t heard you disavow them yet,” the candidate pointed out.

“You’re asking the question because, implicitly, you assume that I’ll have dual loyalties, right? You assume that somehow I wouldn’t disavow, or that I’ll have some higher order of allegiance other than the Constitution,” El-Sayed continued. “Tommy, is that what you imply?”

The heckler responded, “Yes,” to which El-Sayed added: “Why would you think that about me?”

This is Tommy. Tommy had a question about my allegiances. Listen to the end to hear about his.

Tommy continued to claim it was because he hadn’t heard El-Sayed expressly disavow the organization. When El-Sayed said that he just did, and continued to press Tommy to actually answer the question, the heckler wouldn’t do so.

“Have you asked everybody in your life if they disavow them?” he said to Tommy, who responded that he hadn’t. El-Sayed asked once more why the question was really asked. Tommy again said it was because he hadn’t personally heard El-Sayed say he disavowed the Muslim Brotherhood.

“Everybody knows the answer, Tommy, answer the question,” El-Sayed pressed.

After it became clear that Tommy wouldn’t recognize his bias against Muslims as the basis of the question, El-Sayed redirected the conversation once again, pointing out that he would have to affirm an oath to the Constitution if he is sworn into office.

“I’m going to swear to the Constitution of the United States and that Constitution guarantees us all the right to practice whatever faith we want to or no faith at all,” El-Sayed said.

The Senate candidate also cited the example of President John F. Kennedy, who was attacked for his Catholic faith in the election of 1960. Kennedy famously said he was “not running to be a Catholic president but was running to be president and happened to be Catholic,” El-Sayed reminded Tommy. “I’m not running to be a Muslim senator. I’m running for the U.S. Senate and happen to be Muslim.”

I’m never going to tell you what faith you can or cannot practice. I want to protect your right to practice your faith as you choose as a Christian man. The only question though is that it seems like you don’t want to protect my right to practice as I choose.

He then asked Tommy whether he would disavow any violations of the separation between church and state. Tommy said he wouldn’t.

“I think it’s you who needs to understand the Constitution, not me,” El-Sayed countered.

Independent journalist Marisa Kabas has identified “Tommy” as Thomas Teepell, a former aide to Missouri GOP Sen. Josh Hawley, reporting that his presence at the event may be part of a larger operation of young Republicans in Michigan working to disrupt events in support of El-Sayed.

The polite but assertive back-and-forth between the candidate and heckler went viral on social media over the weekend, with many analysts praising El-Sayed for his nuanced arguments defending religious freedom and rejecting baseless attacks on his own faith that wrongly insinuate he isn’t qualified to run or has dual loyalties.

Despite El-Sayed’s citations of Kennedy’s arguments …

author: Lin Taylor
title: Israeli Firm Used Online Ads to Infect Millions With ‘Zero-Click’ Spyware
content:
Israeli adtech firm Discover-Tech used online ads to operate a global spy network targeting millions of people, including Al Jazeera journalists, a new report has revealed. 


Presenting as a legitimate company, Discover-Tech purchased malicious online ads to infect devices with spyware from

Candiru, an Israeli firm blacklisted by the US government. 


Discover-Tech ran a platform called Controlium to “automatically infect devices the moment an advertisement is rendered – a form of zero-click attack,”

 according to a

report by Citizen Lab

, a research group at the University of Toronto, and

cybersecurity firm Confiant

. 


The ads were displayed in over 70,000 mobile apps and more than 120,000 websites between March and June 2026, impacting millions of users globally, the report found.


“This is the first-ever public confirmation of zero-click mercenary spyware delivered via targeted ads,” it said.


“Discover-Tech’s ads also covertly directed millions of devices to contact Candiru’s servers, likely for large-scale tracking and reconnaissance.” 


Broadcaster Al Jazeera said it reached out to Citizen Lab when it was targeted in 2024 and 2025.


“Al Jazeera worked voluntarily with Citizen Lab’s researchers, and… that cooperation helped verify and publicly document these attacks,” the network

said in a statement

. 


“The targeting of journalists is an attack on press freedom and on the public’s right to know. Those responsible must be held accountable.”


Israel raided the offices of the Qatari news network in the occupied West Bank city of Ramallah in 2024, ordering it to shut down its operations. At least 12 of the network’s journalists and media workers have been killed in Gaza since the start of Israel’s genocide in October 2023. In June this year, Al Jazeera condemned Israel’s “deliberate killing” of its cameraman, Ahmed Wishah.  


The report said Discover-Tech ads reached national security agencies, various ministries of defence, Nato and several international media networks, but did not find evidence linking the attacks to the Israeli government.


Novara Media approached Discover-Tech for comment.


The

Committee to Protect Journalists (CPJ) has urged

 governments and authorities to investigate the attacks, particularly those targeting journalists. 


“The mass surveillance architecture supporting online advertising is being harnessed for other purposes and puts journalists at risk,” said Jonathan Rozen, CPJ’s deputy director of research. 


“Citizen Lab’s findings that Al Jazeera devices were infected with spyware delivered via targeted ads make these surveillance dangers even clearer.”


Since 2023, Israel has killed

 more than 240 journalists and media workers

, more than any other government, the press freedom group has said.

author: AbdouMaliq Simone
title: The radical openness of the popular economy
content:
Urban Africa is constantly finding ways to thicken urban life with new resourcefulness: from makeshift maker labs to the vast associations of traders with their own home-grown, expansive financial systems — where remittances circulate alongside locally generated credit and savings — to self-generated webs of electricity and water provisioning under the radar, to neighborhood investments in shared containers of imported goods, to local circuits of production and distribution of foodstuffs, intermingled with diverse labor arrangements across regions and borders. These are what we call popular economies.

Residents inhabit environments replete with different land statuses, regulatory frameworks, histories of economic specialization, repositories of cultural memory, behavioral styles, and social arrangements. Urban popular economies entail how these various components of an archive are pieced together and interrelated to produce specific mobilities and access to resources and opportunities. It is a move toward an expanded diversification of how accumulation, social reproduction, and livelihood get built. African cities are renowned for their informal sectors, self-built neighborhoods, as well as histories of piracy, brigandage, circumvention, smuggling, and subversion. The popular economy intersects with these elements in a continuous unfolding and elaboration of more overarching efforts to create distinctive processes of urbanization within and outside the hegemonic structures of capital accumulation and political domination.

In April 2026, researchers and activists from various African cities gathered in Nairobi to reflect on the popular economy. They explored questions related to orientations, practices, political engagements, and spatial arrangements that might offer ways to inhabit contemporary urban conditions differently. If the future, as a horizon of multiple disjunctions and possibilities, is captured by the reign of probabilities and adversarial networks, then what is the terrain of the improbable? Given the multiple temporalities that characterize territorial operations underpinning popular economies, can we think of a way of life not indebted to calculation, redemption, or culmination?

Popular economies and their various forms of organization seek different ways of inhabiting the present and thus recuperating the insurgencies of both pasts and futures. Euro-American notions of the human have long emphasized a progressive, developmentalist trajectory of improvement and enhanced capacity: a life moving toward a straight timeline, toward the fulfillment of unbounded human potential. This has intensified global turbulence, unsettled ways of living among the majority, and withheld the time needed for society to be a living force in itself — generating vulnerabilities and fragmentation on a planetary scale.

As Timothy Mitchell argues in his book

The Alibi of Capital: How We Broke the Earth to Steal the Future on the Promise of a Better Tomorrow

, this temporal movement acts to constitute a future from which a wide range of payments can be extracted; a future already encumbered by debts continuously owed to those who acquired, at a discount, the rights to those payments. This is a violence done to time itself, one that limits future dispositions to a mere surplus of the present. The future is foreclosed, not primarily through the threat of extinction, but rather through an investment in what can be extracted from that future and monetized now.

This same logic operates at the level of knowledge. Dominant knowledge functions as information: in

Achille Mbembe’s

 terms, a juxtaposition of words stripped of ambiguity, which reduces the capacities of all localities when circulated and imposed. Pattern recognition becomes geared toward preemption; time is reoriented to the number of steps a program needs to reach completion, and space to the memory required to scale a specific function to execute a program — all of this coupled with increasingly enormous expenditures of energy, as

Wolfgang Ernst

 and

Rob Kitchin

 have shown. Localized knowledge has been generalized to the scale of what

Bernard Stiegler

 called a biospheric locality, an upscaling made possible by reducing knowledge to data amenable to computation and by eliminating whatever resists that reduction. Localities become points along the same line, subject to measures of comparability and proportion — the more or less — with the subsequent fight …

author: CMI Argentina
title: Plan Cóndor II: Trump prepara otra cumbre para coordinar la persecución de la izquierda
content:
Milei estuvo en diálogo con Marco Rubio, quien está organizando la conferencia junto con el gobierno alemán. El Presidente volvió a hablar esta semana de una “alianza” entre la izquierda radical y el terrorismo islámico.


Por Luciana Bertoia


El Departamento de Estado prepara una nueva cumbre para discutir cómo perseguir a los movimientos de izquierda a los que califican como “terroristas”. El encuentro se prevé para el mes próximo en Alemania, confirmaron voceros de la cartera que conduce Marco Rubio, ante una consulta formulada por Página/12. En su

 primera edición en Washington

, Javier Milei había enviado a dos funcionarios de alto rango: su canciller, Pablo Quirno, y el número dos de la Secretaría de Inteligencia de Estado (SIDE), José Lago Rodríguez.


El 16 de julio pasado, Marco Rubio encabezó la conferencia sobre el resurgimiento del terrorismo político en la que participaron enviados de más de 60 países.

El Departamento de Estado describió el encuentro como la conformación de una “coalición” contra la izquierda.

En la apertura del evento, el titular del Departamento de Estado comparó su cruzada con la coordinación que funcionó en los años 70 y puso como ejemplo de organizaciones a Montoneros y Tupamaros. La base del éxito de esta nueva empresa, sostuvo Rubio, sería una vieja receta: el trabajo mancomunado de las fuerzas de seguridad y el intercambio de inteligencia. O sea, lo que ya existió en el Plan Cóndor.


Argentina, a través de los emisarios de Milei, tuvo un rol importante en el encuentro de julio. Según trascendió, Quirno fue uno de los oradores. Sin embargo,

el canciller no dio a publicidad su discurso, a pesar del pedido expreso que hizo el diputado nacional Agustín Rossi, bajo el argumento de que estaba amparado por el secreto.

 Rossi encontró que no todos los países siguen esta lógica. La

canciller de Georgia, Maka Botchorishvili, publicó su intervención en la que le agradece a Marco Rubio por poner el asunto del terrorismo en la cima de la agenda.


La SIDE le respondió al Frente de Izquierda y sus Trabajadores (FIT), que tiene como referente a Myriam Bregman, que toda la información relativa a la cumbre estaba alcanzada por la clasificación de seguridad y que si se difundía esa información podría comprometerse el Sistema de Inteligencia Nacional (SIN). Según Cristian Auguadra, la única información pública era la que distribuía el propio Departamento de Estado.


La semana pasada, se conoció que el gobierno alemán había respondido a un pedido de informes que hizo Die Linke (La Izquierda) sobre la coordinación antiterrorista con Estados Unidos. Allí, las autoridades decían que estaban trabajando en un encuentro que se haría en otoño –o sea, antes del 21 de diciembre– en Alemania.


Página/12 remitió una consulta al Departamento de Estado. Voceros de ese organismo explicaron que la cumbre se hará en noviembre y que será coorganizada por Estados Unidos y Alemania. No precisaron cuál será la fecha, aunque es probable que sea después del 3 de noviembre, cuando en Estados Unidos se celebrarán las elecciones de medio término que serán una prueba de fuego para Donald Trump.


Milei pasó los últimos días en Estados Unidos. El jueves, mientras las fuerzas de seguridad reprimían la marcha en la que se pedía que el Gobierno cumpla con la Ley de Financiamiento de la Educación Universitaria (LFEU), Milei encabezó un acto en la embajada argentina en Washington en el que habló de una “alianza entre la izquierda radical y el terrorismo islamita”.


Al día siguiente, en los tribunales de Comodoro Py, aparecieron unas quince denuncias del Departamento de Investigaciones Antiterroristas de la Policía Federal Argentina (PFA). En un juzgado explicaron que se trataba de presentaciones que suelen hacerse en base a relevamientos que hace el Buró Federal de Investigaciones (FBI) en redes sociales. Según las fuentes judiciales, no estarían vinculadas a actividades de ciberpatrullaje por la marcha.


El FBI tiene un vínculo estrecho con el Gobierno. La versión oficial es que el Centro Nacional Antiterrorismo (CNA) se creó en coordinación con esa agencia estadounidense y es el primero de su tipo en la región. El 7 de octubre, el FBI compartió en sus redes sociales que había una delegación argentina para llevar adelante un intercambio estratégico sobre contraterrorismo. author: Charlotte Reck
title: Amazon ‘Uses AI in Warehouses to Predict Whether Workers Will Join Unions’
content:
Amazon has been accused of using AI to track employees and rank how likely they are to form unions.


The online retail giant uses a tool called Atlas in an apparent bid to predict acts of dissent by workers in the UK, the US and Canada, a

document

 released as part of court proceedings between Amazon and Canadian union Unifor show. 


The document, which appears to be a training manual for company leaders, has led the

GMB Union to accuse Amazon

 of using “Orwellian” AI tools to spy on workers. 


“Workers deserve to be able to work free of the fear of excessive surveillance,” said GMB organiser Rachel Fagan.“If Amazon bosses are using Atlas or similar AI-fuelled systems in the UK, the British public deserve to know”.


The document also contains pointers for managers on listening to workers’ concerns without “over-sympathising”. 


Atlas gives warehouses a risk score of between 100 and 900 for union activity, with a lower score meaning it believes workers are more likely to unionise. A higher score is “better” for leaders at the company, the document says.


This “makes it clear that they think the union is bad”, Michael Newman, a partner at London-based law firm Leigh Day, told openDemocracy. 


Atlas is described in the document as a “labour risk framework to clarify how Amazon evaluates emerging workforce issues, labour union targets and internal or external labour threats.”


It outlines a five-tier scale – where tier one denotes workplace disruption and “imminent” worker action, while tier five merits “no immediate perceived risk”. 


The scale can be used to determine staffing decisions, resource planning and action to “mitigate risks” while avoiding reduced productivity or profits, the document says.


In the UK, two Amazon warehouses have been listed in tier one, while 14 others in the US and Canada were named in this high-risk tier.


At a warehouse near Coventry named BHX4, there has been an “active organising campaign” while previous strike action has been recorded at another at EMA4 Sutton Coldfield. 


Newman said that the findings relay “a very different story” to Amazon’s claim that it has no desire to deter workers from joining a union.  


An Amazon spokesperson denied that Atlas is used to counter union activity and refuted the characterisation of the technology as surveillance of individual employees. 


“This is site/building level activity only,” they told openDemocracy, adding that the company does not “track individual employees’ opinions, affiliations or union membership”.


Atlas is used to “help us understand where associates need more support and to ensure we’re addressing issues that they raise”, they added.

author: Sergey Eledinov
title: Sudan: Nobody Hands Over a Gun for Nothing
content:
On 6 October, Sudan’s army chief Abdel Fattah al-Burhan

said again

 that there would be no negotiations with the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) of Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo, known as Hemedti,

or ‘any other party’

, and that the war would go on until victory. A day earlier, Donald Trump’s envoy Massad Boulos

had disclosed a meeting with him in Egypt

. Washington is pushing a 90-day humanitarian truce and, according to

sources cited by Reuters

, made Burhan’s visa for the UN General Assembly conditional on it.


In 1996, General Alexander Lebed

told the journalist Yevgeny Kiselyov

 on Russia’s NTV that ‘all wars, even hundred-year wars, end in negotiations and peace all the same’. He then asked whether it was worth piling up mountains of corpses only to sit down and negotiate anyway. In August that year, at Khasavyurt, he signed

a truce

 himself; the

peace treaty

 followed in May 1997. The troops left, the other side kept its weapons, and the question of Chechnya’s status was put off until the end of 2001. Three years later the war was back.


Khasavyurt is remembered as a breather that the enemy exploited. But a breather works for everyone. The second war was triggered by the

raid into Dagestan

 in August 1999. It came from the side that considered itself the winner, and it was led by the field commanders Shamil Basayev and Khattab, not by Maskhadov, whose signature was on the peace. We cannot say which pushes harder back to war: revanchism born of the bitterness of defeat, or the euphoria of victory.


Burhan sees the breather from one side. In his view, the calls for a truce

coincided with attempts

 to let the RSF expand its territory. He is right about one thing: what he is being offered is not a peace plan. The truce proposed by the Quad (the US, Saudi Arabia, the UAE and Egypt) is designed for two and has still not been agreed. But Burhan has no peace plan either. His condition is that the RSF first

leave the cities and gather in designated areas of Darfur

, and only then comes a truce. That is a plan for victory written up as a precondition.


The principle and its price


The mediators have a principle. The Quad

set it down in September 2025

: the transition must not be ‘controlled by any warring party’. This autumn Washington went further. On 15 September Boulos

said

 that ‘there is no future for any of the two leaders in the country’, and on 22 September the State Department

declared

 that neither the army nor the RSF, nor their leaders, represent legitimate constitutional governance: ‘they rule through force of arms alone.’ As a principle, this is easy to support. It is harder to picture what it looks like in practice.


Yet it is the army and the RSF that Washington is asking to sign the truce, and in early October Boulos met Burhan. This is not ambivalence. Legitimacy is a question for national reconciliation, and a truce cannot settle it. The Americans want to hand power back to civilians. But those who hold the weapons are not going to give them up for nothing.


That is rational, though rational is not the same as right. Barbara Walter

described this logic

 in 1997: for an armed group, its weapons are the only guarantee that a deal will be honoured, and disarming leaves it defenceless. Civil wars therefore almost never end in a settlement unless a third party guarantees it.


The alternative is to take the guns by force. The Sahel is trying, and it is not going well. In November 2023 Mali’s army, with Wagner,

took Kidal

; in

January 2024

 Bamako tore up the 2015 Algiers peace accord; in April 2026 it lost Kidal. On 6 October the army went back in after the Azawad Liberation Front announced a ‘strategic and controlled withdrawal’; the armed groups say there was no fight. Force takes towns. It does not take the guns.


Who holds the guns


In Sudan the guns are not held by only two sides. Fighting alongside the army are the

Joint Force

 of former Darfuri rebels, the movements of Minni Minawi and Gibril Ibrahim, together with the

Sudan Shield Forces

 of Abu Aqla Kikl, who defected from the RSF in 2024, and a host of militias. Fighting alongside the RSF is Abdelaziz al-Hilu’s SPLM-North, with its own command and its own territory. Abdel Wahid al-Nur’s SLM, in the Jebel Marra mountains, has joined neither side. A signature by two generals does not bind them, just as Maskhadov’s signature did not bind Basayev. In July, Ezzat Khairi

showed convincingly

 in these pages that a …

author: Hudson Hongo
title: EFF Launches Privacy Badger for Safari on macOS
content:
Free Tracker Blocker Used by Millions Will Protect Even More Users' Privacy

SAN FRANCISCO—Privacy Badger, the

award-winning

 tracker blocker made by the member-supported digital rights nonprofit

Electronic Frontier Foundation

 (EFF), is now available for Safari on macOS.  


Safari users can

download the free browser extension

 today and join the more than 4 million people using Privacy Badger to take a stand against data brokers and online surveillance. Users will need Safari version 26.5 or higher to use it.


Ranked as one of the best ad tracker blockers by

The Wirecutter

,

Consumer Reports

,

PC Mag

 and more, Privacy Badger is different from other blocking extensions. Created by EFF to stop companies from spying on you online, Privacy Badger

automatically learns

 to block hidden trackers on the web, along with additional privacy-protecting features. 


"Most websites contain invisible tracking code that lets companies collect, share, and profit from your personal data," said Lena Cohen, Staff Technologist at EFF. "Creepy ads are just the tip of the iceberg when it comes to the harms of online tracking: Once your information

enters the data broker ecosystem

, it’s nearly impossible to know who buys it or what they’re doing with it. Safari support has long been one of Privacy Badger’s most requested features and EFF is excited to be able to make this important tool available to Safari users to fight back for a better web." 


On Safari, Privacy Badger goes beyond the browser’s

built-in privacy features

 to provide additional protection against online tracking. In its default browsing mode, Safari limits the information that trackers can access, but it still allows them to load. Privacy Badger blocks online trackers from loading in the first place, preventing them from tracking you using

techniques

 that bypass Safari’s protections. 


With today's launch, Privacy Badger

is now available

 on all major desktop browsers. 


As the leading nonprofit defending online civil liberties, EFF is committed to fighting mass surveillance in the courts, through activism, and by making free, privacy-protecting tools like Privacy Badger. Now, even more people can join the movement against online tracking, by installing Privacy Badger themselves, telling their friends and family who use Safari about it, or

by supporting Privacy Badger today

. 


For more on Privacy Badger for Safari on macOS:


https://www.eff.org/deeplinks/2026/10/announcing-privacy-badger-safari-macos


For more on the dangers of online tracking:


https://www.eff.org/deeplinks/2025/03/online-tracking-out-control-privacy-badger-can-help-you-fight-back

 


For more on how Privacy Badger works:


https://privacybadger.org/

press@eff.org

title: Stratégies de récupération : Comprendre ses émotions lors d'évènements très stressants
content:
En tant que militant.es, activistes, manifestant.es, nous sommes souvent exposé.es à des stress et de la violence. Au gré des expériences et de leur répétition, cette exposition génère des impacts individuels et collectifs, parfois traumatiques. Pour s'ancrer dans la durée, nos luttes et nous mêmes avons besoin d'anticiper, de comprendre, et de résorber ces impacts.

 A contre-pied de la pensée selon laquelle chacun.e doit se soigner soi-même, on pense qu'il est essentiel d'envisager le soin collectivement, d'en faire une priorité dans nos luttes mais aussi plus largement dans espaces d'organisation et de confiance.


 Comment gérer nos réactions psychologiques et émotionnelles après la violence (policière), la répression ou d'autres expériences très stressantes

 

? Comment apporter du soutien dans ces contextes

 

?


 Cette brochure, éditée par le collectif Soutien et Rétablissement, apporte quelques conseils et outils pour soi et celleux qui nous entourent

author: Miriam Lafontaine
title: Man charged with murder following Oct. 6 altercation that left another man dead
content:
RCMP have charged a man with second-degree murder in connection with an altercation that happened Oct. 6 in Iqaluit.


Qaqasie Aningmiuq, 21, was arrested on Oct. 16, Nunavut RCMP said Monday in a news release issued by Sgt. George Henrie.


Police previously

identified

 the man who died as 38-year-old Robert Kipanik.


He was among two people transported to Qikiqtani General Hospital with life-threatening injuries on Oct. 6, after police responded to calls about an altercation at around 9:55 p.m. in the 300 block of the city.


The other person survived after being medevaced to Ottawa. Police have not identified them.


The RCMP’s Major Crime Unit is handling the investigation.


Aningmiuq remains in custody until his next court appearance, which is scheduled for Nov. 17.

author: Mag
title: Rechte Gewalt, leere Kassen: Ostdeutsche Zivilgesellschaft unter Druck
content:
Dossier


„In der Bundespolitik ist das Entsetzen über den Erfolg der AfD bei der Bundestagswahl noch immer groß. (…) „Zwickau, Chemnitz, Zittau – da würde ich von extrem rechten Dominanzbestrebungen sprechen“, zählt die Expertin [Heike Radvan, Professorin für Rechtsextremismusforschung] für Sachsen auf. Die soziale Dynamik ziele darauf ab, den öffentlichen Raum für alle Personen einzuschränken, die nicht in ein rechtes Weltbild passen, beispielsweise durch dominantes Auftreten von AfD-Abgeordneten im Kommunalparlament – und durch Bedrohungen und Gewalt. (…) Exemplarisch für [die] AfD-Strategie stehen die Attacken auf das Bundesprogramm „Demokratie leben“ des Bundesministeriums für Familie, Senioren, Frauen und Jugend, das zivilgesellschaftliche Initiativen und Vereine fördert, die sich für Demokratie und gegen Extremismus engagieren…“  

Artikel von Elisa Pfleger in den »Blättern« 4/2025


 und mehr daraus/dazu:


Demokratieprojekte in Sachsen-Anhalt: Was kostet die Demokratie?


„

Eine mögliche AfD-Landesregierung in Sachsen-Anhalt könnte vor allem ein Ziel haben: Demokratieprojekte beenden. Die sollen nun eilig gerettet werden.


Es ist ein „Appell“, mit dem sich Sebastian Koch vergangene Woche an den kleinen Verein Ipse Exitare in der Altmark in Sachsen-Anhalt wandte. Es liege ihm fern, Kritik zu äußern, schrieb der AfD-Politiker in einer direkten Nachricht. Aber er müsse anmerken, dass sich der Verein zuletzt kritisch über die AfD geäußert habe – und das sei verboten. Solche „Verstöße können und müssen zum Entzug der Förderung führen“, schreibt der AfD-Mann weiter. Und dass seine Partei künftig alle Vereine hinsichtlich ihrer „Neutralitätspflicht“ überprüfen wolle.


Der Heimat- und Kulturverein, der Konzerte und Veranstaltungen organisiert, die Dorfkirche sanierte oder das jährliche „Lichtblütenfestival“ veranstaltet, wollte sich auf taz-Anfrage dazu nicht äußern. Gegenüber der Volksstimme zeigte er sich aber irritiert. „Das ist doch völlig abstrus“, sagte Vereinschef Tilo Mottschall. „Was soll das denn bedeuten? Förderung gibt es dann nur noch für das, was der AfD passt?“ AfD-Mann Koch, der gerade erstmals in den Landtag einzog, relativierte seine Aktion auf taz-Anfrage. Man müsse schon sehr viel Fantasie besitzen, um darin eine Drohung zu sehen, schrieb er. (…)


Dabei ist Ipse Excitare gar kein explizit politischer Verein, nicht einmal ein dezidiertes Demokratieprojekt. Gerade deshalb erschüttert die Nachricht von Koch viele in Sachsen-Anhalt. Selbst die CDU-Landtagsabgeordnete Sandra Hietl-Heuer verurteilte Kochs Nachricht als „Einschüchterung“. Kochs Nachricht unterstreicht, was die AfD seit Langem plant: den linken „NGO-Sumpf austrocknen“, wie es die rechtsextreme Partei nennt. (…)


Panik vor einer AfD-Landesregierung


Bei vielen Initiativen in Sachsen-Anhalt herrscht Panik. Noch ist der Landeshaushalt für das kommende Jahr nicht beschlossen. Die Verhandlungen dürften starten, sobald die neue Regierung steht – und sich über Monate hinziehen. Dass eine AfD-geführte Landesregierung darin Gelder für die kritische Zivilgesellschaft einplanen wird, bezweifeln viele. Das hat schon jetzt konkrete Folgen. So berichtet Antje Arndt von der Mobilen Opferberatung, die mit ihrem Team Betroffene rechter Gewalt unterstützt, dass bereits alle Angestellten gekündigt seien, weil die Zukunftsaussichten völlig unklar seien. (…)


AfD könnte Bundesfördermittel blockieren


Zum Sozialministerium gehört auch das Landesdemokratiezentrum, das zusammen mit dem Bund auswählt, welche Projekte mit Bundesmitteln gefördert werden. Auch dieses Zentrum könnte die AfD abschaffen oder ihm auferlegen, die vom Bund bewilligten Fördergelder nicht weiterzugeben. Eine konkrete Überlegung deshalb: Das Landesdemokratiezentrum an einen freien Träger anzudocken – womit dieses künftig unabhängig von der Landesregierung wäre

…“

Artikel von Anne Fromm und Konrad Litschko vom 18.10.2026 in der taz online

 


AfD nimmt mit parlamentarischen Anfragen Einfluss auf Soziale Arbeit in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern und Thüringen


„Die AfD in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern und in Thüringen nutzt parlamentarische Instrumente ihrer Landtagsfraktionen, insbesondere zahlreiche Kleine Anfragen, um Einfluss auf das Sozialwesen und die Soziale Arbeit in den beiden Bundesländern zu nehmen. author: Soraya Kishtwari
title: This Politician Posted a Quote About Palestinian Resistance. Now France Is Dragging Her Through the Courts
content:
For the last three years, Rima Hassan has watched in horror as thousands of people have been killed in her family’s homeland. The French jurist and La France Insoumise (LFI) MEP, who was born stateless in a Palestinian refugee camp in Syria, is one of France’s most outspoken critics of both Israel’s genocide in Gaza and the complicity of Europe’s governments.


Now, she could be sent to prison over a post on social media.


In March, Hassan posted a quotation on X/Twitter attributed to Kōzō Okamoto, a member of the Japanese Red Army who took part in a 1972 attack on an Israeli airport in which 26 people were killed.


“I gave my youth to the Palestinian cause,” Okamoto’s quotation read. “As long as there is oppression, resistance will not only be a right, but a duty.”


Far-right National Rally politician

Matthias Renault

, interior minister

Laurent Nuñez

 and two French pro-Israel lobby groups reported Hassan to prosecutors for

apologie du terrorisme

(the glorification of terrorism) – a criminal offence.

Hassan denied the charges

 and said her main goal had been to share a quotation about the “philosophy of resistance”, and that she couldn’t be accused of glorifying terrorism for doing so.


Hassan’s trial began on 19 October. If found guilty, she could be sentenced to up to seven years in prison and fined €100,000 under French law. Her situation, she said, is the latest in a series

 of legal and political battles in France over solidarity with Palestine

.


“

People who stand in solidarity with Palestine are labelled as terrorists because it [this label] is the only instrument that allows them to silence concrete opposition and activism,” Hassan told Novara Media ahead of her trial.


This isn’t the first time the French state has brought the full force of its institutional machinery against Hassan.

22 legal proceedings

 have been initiated against her in the last two years in connection with her political views (six have been closed by prosecutors without questioning, 13 after questioning and three remain open). In September, a separate trial in relation to

two social media posts from 2025

 was adjourned.


Prior to the opening of the investigation

 into the post in March, police had

reportedly already been surveilling Hassan

, tracking her movements and monitoring her phone activity. In April, she was taken into custody for questioning in what she describes as a “deliberate attempt” to circumvent her parliamentary immunity. Details of her arrest, including the claim she was carrying drugs, were then

leaked to the press

 (the drug probe was subsequently dropped).


Hassan’s lawyer, Vincent Brengarth, has

long maintained his client’s innocence

, alleging the prosecutions are part of a “campaign of judicial harassment aimed at silencing her”. Five UN special rapporteurs have

raised similar concerns

, warning the French government that Hassan appeared to be facing “political and judicial harassment”.


Hassan told Novara Media she believed that the accusations against her were a “misuse of anti-terrorism laws”.


“The shift is very interesting,” she said, noting how she believes that we’re moving towards a situation in which the accusation of terrorism is directed at “all political opposition”.


Hassan’s case is perhaps the most high-profile of hundreds of cases of alleged

apologie du terrorisme

 offences in France.

In October 2023, police arrested trade union leader Jean-Paul Delescaut over a leaflet published following the 7 October attacks (Delescaut was convicted and sentenced, before being

acquitted on appeal

). In another case, the suspended sentence of a former deputy mayor, Mohamed Makni, for sharing a quotation which described the attacks as “resistance” was upheld by France’s highest court (Makni is now

challenging the ruling

 at the European Court of Human Rights). B

etween October 2023 and October 2025,

more than 350 people

 were convicted of the offence in total. While it’s unclear how many were in relation to Palestine, rulings surged after 7 October.


None of this may surprise anyone living in the UK. Since it was banned as a terrorist group in July 2025, those in the UK expressing support for Palestine Action, an organisation which targeted companies

 involved in supplying military equipment to Israel,

risk up to 14 years in prison. What’s followed, due to huge public opposition to the ban, has been

a 1,553% uptick in terrorism arrests

 – 94% of them in the …

author: Jolene Banning
title: My ancestors showed me how to grieve
content:
Jolene Banning’s daughter Amber-baa, depicted through the eye of an eagle. Illustration by Jessie Boulard


Content warning: This story deals with child loss and grief. Please look after your spirit and read with care


Three years ago I was hit with a pain so deep that it seared through every fiber of my body. 


Two police officers pulled up in my driveway, driving a dark SUV, wearing dark suits and ties. They came to inform me that my child, my baby, my daughter Amber had died. 


The blow of information left me numb, stunned, separated from myself like I was watching this happen instead of partaking. 


Instantly, I became a member of a club I never wanted to belong to: of parents who have lost their children. Because I know I’m not alone in this rapidly growing group of people. It doesn’t feel natural to bury our children, so young, so beautiful. 


Amber-baa had long, shiny dark brown hair, round brown eyes, thick eyebrows and a million dollar smile — which she should, considering how much I paid the orthodontist. She was warm, caring, and fun to be around. She lit up a room and made sure everyone felt seen. And in the blink of an eye, without warning, I had lost all of that. The silence was deafening. The pain was inescapable. 


Experiencing this kind of loss and grief is not uncommon for Indigenous people. In “Canada,” our communities experience significantly higher mortality rates. Our women and girls are at a 12 times higher risk than the average citizen to go missing or be murdered.


Violence against us is fuelled by systemic racism, sexism, and colonialism — as outlined in

Reclaiming Power and Place, the Final Report of the National Inquiry into Missing and Murdered Indigenous Women and Girls

.


We hear about these losses. Sometimes it makes the news, stats are shared, but then we don’t hear from anyone again. The news has passed, new topics are making headlines. 


Losing my daughter, and losing other important people in my life too soon, led me to want to acknowledge this and share my reality, and I grapple with how we can begin to heal. 


My first loss came when I was only 13. My baby brother was only six months old and died of meningitis after spending a week in the Toronto Hospital for Sick Children. After that, I would go on to lose many of my aunties, uncles and cousins, and grandparents. 


Many lives shut down before they even reached their prime.


“For these four days, my pain was spread out amongst everyone at the fire.”


When I lost my girl, on April 28th, 2023, there was no way I was sending her on her next journey in a way that was not ours — in a church made of brick and mortar while someone delivered a sermon about finding God and peace. 


So I turned to my Anishinaabek community and found knowledge holders and learners willing to share with me. 


I was told I need to send my girl off with a four-day sacred fire ceremony, something I had never done or even participated in until this loss. 


I called the Elders that I knew, and many people worked behind the scenes to ensure I had enough fire wood, food, and company. Firekeepers attended to the fire and explained which direction to enter, drum groups stopped by and offered songs. 


Every morning, as the sun rose, my dad was there, sharing family stories. Relatives from the north made the trek to offer medicine, condolences and stories of their own.


Another community member, who lost a child, offered to make my daughter a headstone. It’s a simple cross, with her information, and features a painted medicine wheel. 


For these four days, my pain was spread out amongst everyone at the fire.


I also learned during this ceremony that my daughter needed to start her journey and there were ways I could assist her. 


She needed her own bundle with exactly four matchsticks, a copper cup, an outfit made in her colours so our ancestors can recognize her and moccasins — basic and unembellished ones, since our offerings grow in size when they reach the other dimension, realm, Spirit World, and we don’t want her weighed down, unable to walk. 


I was told she will come to a crossing, where she will have to share everything about herself and her journey so far. Then our ancestors will travel across the divide to accept her. Her bundle was packed just right.


Every day and every night over four days we feasted for her by offering a spirit plate to the land, another to the fire. 


In Anishinaabek culture, we add the prefix -baa onto a name …

author: Chris Walker
title: More Than $137 Million Has Been Spent on AI-Generated Midterm Ads
content:
The vast majority of ads emanate from GOP campaigns, depicting their Democratic opponents in fictionalized scenarios.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

Millions of dollars have been spent on AI during this year’s midterm election campaign, oftentimes through candidates using the technology to depict their opponents in fictional situations, portraying them in negative ways to unsuspecting voters.

According to research from Wesleyan University, over 200 ads have used AI in this election cycle. The ads have totaled more than $137 million in campaign spending.

More than 80 percent of the ads have been produced by Republican candidates or political action committees (PACs) aligned with the GOP. One such ad, featuring Democratic Gov. Kathy Hochul (who is running for re-election in New York), features her walking alongside New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani. The governor reminds Mamdani, “don’t say affordable” while the two refer to how they plan to govern the state moving forward.

No such statement from Hochul exists, and the video of them walking next to each other in such a way is entirely fictional. The ad doesn’t contain any disclaimer informing viewers that it’s generated by AI.

“It’s the year of the AI election,” Fred N. Davis III, founder of Strategic Perception, an advertising firm based in Hollywood, said to The New York Times. “It’s top of mind for everybody in my business and pretty much everybody in the political business.”

Some candidates who have become the victims of AI advertising are pushing back. Rebecca Cooke, a Democrat seeking to unseat Rep. Derrick Van Orden (R) in a contentious election in Western Wisconsin, sent a “cease and desist” order to him for posting a series of online AI ads he made against her. One of those ads featured fictionalized versions of Cooke and former President Joe Biden, with the former stating that she plans to “take advantage of as much corruption as possible” if Democrats win the elections.

“These defamatory, misleading videos undermine our democratic process and are the exact kind of mudslinging voters are tired of,” the letter said to Van Orden.

Wisconsin law forbids the use of deepfake videos in political messaging, but there is a loophole for federal candidates. The letter takes note of that state statute, telling the Republican lawmaker that he is “violating the spirit of the law.”

Van Orden has continued to produce AI videos. And though he has used Cooke’s image less often, he has now resorted to using an animated duck to refer to her, whose voice sounds eerily similar to the Democratic candidate’s.

For his own part, President Donald Trump has rejected calls for the government to regulate AI, instead touting a non-binding “self-policing” accord that he and several AI companies have signed onto. He has also sought to rebrand AI as “super intelligence,” and has made the extraordinary claim that any criticism of the technology is akin to an act of treason.

American voters, meanwhile, would like to see more regulation of AI.

According to a Johns Hopkins University poll published this summer, most Americans back a “right to human” law, which would allow them to opt out of AI interactions if they so desire, including 79 percent who support that concept in health care settings, 76 percent who back it in legal proceedings, and 73 percent who say such a law should apply when AI is aiding in government services.

A recent CNN poll also found that most Americans believe the U.S. government is not doing enough to regulate AI, with 71 percent of respondents expressing that view. Support for regulation is also bipartisan — 85 percent of Democratic-leaning respondents support regulation, while 63 percent of Republican-leaning respondents do as well, the survey found.

Truthout is one of only a few platforms for justice-oriented, grassroots journalism. Today, we face an existential threat.

Due to Google’s launch of AI search, we’ve seen a drastic plunge in our site traffic and, as a result, our revenue. We lost 15 percent of our readership overnight. This was a readership we painstakingly built over decades, and it vanished because Google chose corporate greed over a healthy democracy.

We are fundraising right now to meet our basic operating expenses. If you can support Truthout with a one-time or monthly donation, you will make a significant impact on our …

author: Andrea
title: ᐃᓄᑐᖃᓄᑦ ᓄᓇᓯᐅᑎᖓ ᐊᖅᑯᑎᒧᐊᕈᓐᓇᖅᐳᖅ 2027−ᒥ, ᓯᕗᓕᖅᑎ ᐅᖃᖅᐳᖅ
content:
For the English version of this story, please see

Elder van project could hit the streets in 2027, premier says

.


ᑕᓪᓕᒪᓂ ᐊᑐᐃᓐᓇᐅᔪᓂ ᓄᓇᓯᐅᑎᓂ ᐃᓄᑐᖃᑦ ᓄᓇᓯᐅᑎᓂ ᓂᐅᕕᖅᑕᐅᓚᐅᖅᑐᓂ $1 ᒥᓕᐊᓐᓂ ᐃᓄᓕᒫᓄᑦ ᑮᓇᐅᔭᖏᓐᓂ ᓱᓕ ᐅᖅᑯᑎᒦᙱᓚᑦ ᐊᕐᕌᒍ ᐊᑕᐅᓯᕐᒥ ᐊᖅᑯᑎᒦᓐᓇᑎᒃ ᓯᕗᓪᓕᖅᐹᒥ ᐱᓕᕆᐊᕆᔭᐅᔪᒥ ᓇᓗᓇᐃᖅᓯᓚᐅᖅᑎᓪᓗᒍ ᑕᐃᒪᐃᑦᑐᒥ ᐱᔨᖅᑎᕋᕐᓂᐅᔪᒥ.


ᑐᓂᓯᔪᓐᓇᙱᑎᓪᓗᒍ ᓇᓗᓇᐃᖅᑕᐅᓯᒪᓂᖓᓂ ᖃᖓ ᐱᔭᕇᖅᓯᒪᔭᕆᐊᖃᕐᓂᖓᓂ ᓄᓇᓯᐅᑎᓄᑦ ᐱᒋᐊᖅᑎᑕᐅᓪᓚᕆᖕᓂᖓᓂ, ᓯᕗᓕᖅᑎ ᔮᓐ ᒪᐃᓐ ᐅᖃᓚᐅᖅᐳᖅ “ᐱᔪᒪᓂᕆᕙᖓ” ᑕᑯᓂᕐᒥ ᓄᓇᓯᐅᑎᓂ ᐊᐅᓚᑕᐅᒃᑲᓐᓂᕐᓂᖏᓐᓂ 2027−ᒥ — ᐊᕐᕌᒍᑦ ᐱᖓᓱᓂ ᖄᖏᖅᓯᒪᔪᓂ ᓂᐅᕕᖅᑕᐅᓚᐅᖅᑎᓪᓗᒋᑦ.


“ᓄᑖᙳᕆᐊᖅᑎᑕᐅᓂᖓ, ᒫᓐᓇᐅᔪᒥ, ᓱᓕ ᐊᐅᓚᑕᐅᙱᑦᑐᖅ,” ᐅᖃᓚᐅᖅᐳᖅ ᐅᖃᓘᑎᒃᑯᑦ ᐊᐱᖅᓱᖅᑕᐅᓂᐅᔪᒥ ᐅᒃᑐᐱᕆ 9−ᒥ. “ᑭᓯᐊᓂ, ᒐᕙᒪᕗᑦ ᒪᓕᒍᒪᐅᑎᖃᙱᓚᑦ ᐆᒧᖓ.”


ᐱᓕᕆᐊᒃᓴᖅ ᓄᖅᑲᓚᐅᖅᐳᖅ 2025−ᒥ, ᐃᓱᐊᓂ ᓯᕗᓂᐊᓂ ᒐᕙᒪᒃᑯᑦ ᑲᑎᒪᔨᐅᓂᖏᓐᓂ, ᐱᔾᔪᑎᖃᖅᑐᒥ ᐱᑕᖃᙱᓗᐊᕐᓂᖓᓂ ᐊᐅᓚᑕᐅᓂᖓᓄᑦ ᑮᓇᐅᔭᓂ ᐊᑐᖅᑕᐅᔪᒃᓴᐅᑕᐅᔪᓂ.


ᑕᒪᓐᓇ ᐊᓯᔾᔨᓚᐅᖅᐳᖅ ᐅᐱᕐᙶᖅ 2026−ᒥ ᒪᓕᒐᓕᐅᖅᑏᑦ ᒫᓐᓇᐅᔪᒥ ᒪᓕᒐᓕᐅᕐᕕᖕᒥ ᐊᖏᓚᐅᖅᑎᓪᓗᒋ $1.25 ᒥᓕᐊᓐᓂ ᖄᒃᑲᓐᓂᐊᒍᑦ ᑮᓇᐅᔭᖃᖅᑎᑦᑎᓂᕐᒥ, ᒪᐃᓐ ᐅᖃᓚᐅᖅᐳᖅ.


ᐸᓯᒥ ᐱᔨᑦᑎᕋᕐᓂᖅ ᓯᕗᓪᓕᖅᐹᒥ ᐅᖃᐅᓯᐅᓚᐅᖅᑎᓪᓗᒍ, ᐱᓕᕆᖃᑎᖃᕐᓂᐅᓚᐅᖅᐳᖅ ᐅᑭᐅᖅᑕᖅᑐᒥ ᓯᕗᓂᒃᓴᒧᑦ ᐊᔪᙱᓐᓂᐅᔪᓂ ᐱᕙᓪᓕᐊᑎᑕᐅᓂᖓᓂ, ᐅᑭᐅᖅᑕᖅᑐᒥ ᐱᓕᒻᒪᒃᓴᓂᕐᒥ ᓕᒥᑎᒃᑯᓐᓂᑦ, ᐊᒻᒪ ᑐᒃᑐ ᑖᒃᓯᓂᑦ.


ᐊᑕᐅᓯᕐᒥ ᓄᓇᓯᐅᑎᖃᖅᐳᑦ ᐊᑐᓂ ᑕᓪᓕᒪᓂ ᓄᓇᓕᐅᔪᓂ: ᐃᖃᓗᐃᑦ, ᐃᖃᓗᒃᑑᑦᑎᐊᖅ, ᑲᖏᖅᖠᓂᖅ, ᓴᓪᓕᑦ ᐊᒻᒪ ᐸᖕᓂᖅᑑᒥ. ᐅᑭᐅᖅᑕᖅᑐᒥ ᓯᕗᓂᒃᓴᒧᑦ ᐊᔪᙱᓐᓂᐅᔪᓂ ᐱᕙᓪᓕᐊᑎᑕᐅᓂᖓᓂ, ᓇᖕᒥᓂᕆᔭᐅᔪᒥ ᑲᒻᐸᓂᐅᔪᒥ, ᓂᐅᕕᓚᐅᖅᐳᑦ ᑮᓇᐅᔭᖃᖅᑎᑕᐅᓪᓗᑎᒃ ᓄᓇᕗᒻᒥ ᒐᕙᒪᒃᑯᓐᓂ.


ᖁᑉᐸ ᒪᐃᒃ ᓇᖏᖅᐳᖅ ᓴᓂᓕᐊᓂ ᐃᓄᑐᖃᑦ ᐸᓯᖓᓂ ᐊᐅᓚᑕᐅᔪᒥ ᐸᐃᕆᓃᑦ ᑲᑐᔾᔨᖃᑎᒌᖏᑦ ᐃᖃᓗᖕᓂ ᐃᓄᑐᖃᑦ’ ᖃᒻᒪᖓᓂ ᐅᒃᑐᐱᕆ 9−ᒥ. (ᑎᐊᕆᓐ ᓕᐊᑦᔅ ᐊᔾᔨᖁᑎᖓ)


ᑭᒡᒐᖅᑐᐃᔨᐅᔪᓂ ᐅᑭᐅᖅᑕᖅᑐᒥ ᐱᓕᒻᒪᒃᓴᓂᕐᒥ ᓕᒥᑎᑯᓐᓂᑦ ᐊᒻᒪ ᑐᒃᑐ ᑖᒃᓯᓕᕆᔨᒃᑯᓐᓂ ᐊᑐᐃᓪᓐᓇᐅᓚᐅᙱᓚᑦ ᐅᖃᐅᓯᒃᓴᓕᐅᕐᓂᕐᒥ ᐆᒧᖓ ᐅᓂᒃᑳᓕᐊᖑᔪᒧᑦ.


ᐊᑐᐊᒐᒥ ᐱᕙᓪᓕᐊᑎᑕᐅᕙᓪᓕᐊᕗᖅ ᐱᓕᕆᓂᐅᑉ ᑐᓄᐊᓂ ᐊᒻᒪ, ᐱᔭᕇᖅᑕᐅᒍᓂ, ᒐᕙᒪᒃᑯᑦ ᐸᕐᓇᒃᐳᑦ ᑐᓂᓯᓂᕐᒥ ᖃᐃᖁᔨᓂᐅᔪᒥ ᑐᒃᓯᕋᐅᑎᓂ ᓯᕗᓂᐊᓂ ᐃᓱᐊᓂ 2026−ᒥ, ᒪᐃᓐ ᐅᖃᓚᐅᖅᐳᖅ.


ᓱᓕ ᐃᓱᒪᒃᓴᖅᓯᐅᕈᑕᐅᓂᐊᖅᐳᖅ ᖃᐃᖁᔨᓂᐅᔪᖅ ᐃᓄᓕᒫᓅᖓᓂᐊᕈᓂ ᐅᕝᕙᓘᓐᓃᑦ “ᖃᐃᖁᔨᓂᐅᔪᑎᒍᑦ,” ᐃᓚᒋᐊᖅᓯᓚᐅᖅᐳᖅ.


ᐅᑭᐅᖅᑕᖅᑐᒥ ᐱᓕᒻᒪᒃᓴᓂᕐᒥ ᓕᒥᑎᑦ ᐊᐅᓚᑦᑎᓚᐅᖅᐳᑦ ᓇᖕᒥᓂᖅ-ᑮᓇᐅᔭᖃᖅᑎᑦᑎᓂᐅᔪᒥ, ᕿᓚᒻᒥᐅᔪᒥ ᐊᕿᑦᑐᒥ ᐱᒋᐊᖅᑕᐅᓂᖓᓂ ᐱᔨᑦᑎᕋᕐᓂᐅᔪᒥ ᐃᖃᓗᖕᓂ ᐊᕐᕌᓂᐅᓚᐅᖅᑐᒥ ᐅᒃᑐᐱᕆ 2025−ᒥ. ᑲᒻᐸᓂᐅᔪᖅ ᑭᐅᓚᐅᖅᐳᑦ 200−ᐸᓗᖕᓄᑦ ᐱᔨᑦᑎᕋᕐᓂᕐᒧᑦ ᖃᐃᖁᔨᓂᐅᔪᓂ ᐱᓇᓱᐊᕈᓯᐅᑉ ᓄᙳᐊᓂᑕᒫᒥ.


ᖁᑉᐸ ᒪᐃᒃ, ᑲᑎᒪᔨᐅᖃᑕᐅᔪᖅ ᐸᐃᕆᔩᑦ ᑎᒍᒥᐊᖅᑎᒃᑯᑦ ᐃᖃᓗᖕᓂ ᐃᓄᑐᖃᓄᑦ ᑲᑐᔾᔨᖃᑎᒌᖏᓐᓂ, ᐊᑐᓚᐅᖅᐳᖅ ᓄᓇᓯᐅᒻᒥ ᐱᖓᓱᐃᖅᓱᖅᖢᓂ ᐃᖏᕐᕋᓂᕐᒧᑦ ᐃᓄᑐᖃᒃᑯᑦ ᖃᒻᒪᖓᓄᑦ, ᓂᕿᑖᕐᕕᖕᒥ ᐊᔪᖅᓴᖅᑐᓄᑦ, ᐊᒻᒪ ᓂᕿᓄᑦ ᓂᐅᕕᕐᕕᓄᑦ, ᐅᖃᓚᐅᖅᐳᖅ.


ᓄᑖᖅ ᓄᓇᓯᐅᑎᒧᑦ ᐊᔭᐅᕐᕕᖓ ᐊᒃᓱᕈᕐᓇᒐᓚᓚᐅᖅᐳᖅ ᓂᐅᕐᓗᖁᑎᖓᓄᑦ, ᐅᖃᓚᐅᖅᐳᖅ, ᑭᓯᐊᓂ ᐃᑲᔪᖅᑎᐅᔪᒥ ᐸᓯᒥ ᐊᔪᕐᓇᙱᑎᑦᑎᓚᐅᖅᐳᖅ ᒪᔪᕋᕐᓂᕐᒥ ᑭᓯᐊᓂ ᑎᑭᐅᑎᔪᓐᓇᓕᕋᒥ ᐊᒡᒐᒧᑦ ᑎᒍᒥᐊᕐᕕᓄᑦ ᐃᓄᐊᓂ ᐸᓯᒥ ᐃᑭᓇᓱᐊᖅᑎᓪᓗᒍ, ᐅᖃᓚᐅᖅᐳᖅ.


“ᐱᐅᕐᔪᐊᓚᐅᖅᐳᖅ ᐃᑲᔪᖅᑕᐅᓂᖃᖅᖢᓂ,” ᐅᖃᓚᐅᖅᐳᖅ.


ᐃᓄᑐᖃᑦ ᑲᑐᔾᔨᖃᑎᒌᖑᔪᖅ ᐃᒻᒥᓂᒃ ᐊᐅᓚᑦᑎᕗᑦ ᐱᖓᓱᓂ ᓄᓇᓯᐅᑎᓂ, ᐃᓚᖃᖅᑐᒥ ᐃᓄᑐᖃᓄᑦ ᐸᓯᖓᓂ. ᑭᓯᐊᓂ ᐸᓯᐅᑉ ᐊᑐᐃᓐᓇᖃᖅᑎᑦᑎᓂᕐᒥ ᐊᔭᐅᕐᕕᖓ ᓱᕋᒃᓯᒪᖕᒪᑦ ᐊᑯᓂᐊᓗᒃ, ᐅᖃᓚᐅᖅᐳᖅ ᑲᑎᒪᔨᐅᖃᑕᐅᔪᒥ ᐊᐃᓂᐊᖅ ᖁᐊᒐᖅ.


”ᐅᑕᖅᑭᙳᓚᐅᖅᐳᒍᑦ ᓄᑖᒥ ᐸᓯᒥ ᑕᐃᒫᒃ ᐃᓱᒪᒋᔪᓐᓃᓚᐅᖅᐸᕗᑦ” ᒪᐃᒃ ᐃᓚᒋᐊᖅᓯᓚᐅᖅᐳᖅ.


“ᐅᔾᔨᕈᓱᒃᐳᖓ ᐊᑯᓂᐸᓘᓂᖓᓂ ᐅᑯᐊ ᓄᓇᓯᐅᑎᑦ ᓯᕗᓪᓕᕐᒥ ᓂᐅᕕᖅᑕᐅᓚᐅᖅᑎᓪᓗᒋᑦ, ᐊᒻᒪᓂᕆᐅᖕᓂᖃᒐᓚᒃᐳᖅ ᐊᒻᒪ ᐊᑲᖅᓴᙱᓐᓂᐅᔪᒥ ᓱᓕᓂᐅᔪᒥ ᓱᓕ ᐊᐅᓚᑕᐅᙱᓐᓂᖏᓐᓂ,” ᒪᐃᓐ ᐅᖃᓚᐅᖅᐳᖅ. “ᒪᓕᒃᑐᒥ ᐱᓕᕆᓂᐅᔪᒥ ᑕᑯᓂᕐᒥ ᐊᑐᐊᒐᕐᒥ ᓴᖅᑭᑎᑕᐅᓂᖓᓂ, ᐊᐅᓚᑦᑎᓇᔭᖅᑐᒥ ᑕᐃᔅᓱᒥᖓ ᑮᓇᐅᔭᖃᖅᑎᑕᐅᓂᐅᔪᒥ ᐊᒻᒪ ᑕᑯᓂᕐᒥ ᐃᖏᕐᕋᓂᖓᓂ ᓄᓇᕗᓕᒫᒥ ᐃᓄᖕᓄᑦ ᐊᐅᓚᑦᑎᓂᐊᖅᑐᓄᑦ ᑕᐃᒪᐃᑦᑐᒥ ᖃᓄᐃᑦᑑᓂᖓᓂ ᐱᔨᑦᑎᕋᕐᓂᐅᔪᒥ.”

title: Gewerkschaften, Sozialabbau und Widerstand: Fast 25 Jahre Theorie und Praxis
content:
Dossier


„…

Als die größte Klippe für wirksame einheitliche Proteste und den Widerstand gegen die Hartz-Gesetze hat sich die breite Akzeptanz des Leistungsprinzips und der Lohnabhängigkeit als einziger Quelle der Existenzsicherung erwiesen. Dies gilt für die Gewerkschaftsbürokratie gleichermaßen wie für die meisten der (noch?) beschäftigten wie erwerbslosen Lohnabhängigen selbst. (…) Durch diese Propaganda wurden auch die Gewerkschaftsspitzen ins Boot geholt, die ihre oberste Aufgabe schon immer darin gesehen haben, „Menschen in Arbeit zu bringen“. (…) Die Mischung aus der angeblichen Alternativlosigkeit der Lohnabhängigkeit und der Angst vor Hartz IV lässt die Belegschaften weitere Verzichte bei Lohn wie Arbeitsbedingungen hinnehmen, anstatt die erkämpften Standards zugunsten aller Lohnabhängigen hochzuhalten

…“  Bittere Bilanz im

Wie auf dem zweiten digitalen Ratschlag am 8. September beschlossen, will der Gewerkschaftsratschlag im Nachgang der bundesweiten Proteste am 21. und 26. Im Zentrum stehen dabei die Fragen: Wie können wir (noch) mehr Menschen in Bewegung bringen? Und wie können wir wirkungsvoll den Druck auf die schwarz-rote Bundesregierung erhöhen? Gemeinsam sollen hierfür die konkreten nächsten Schritte verabredet werden. author: Unknown
title: Koçyiğit: We want to see peace in the budget, in language, and in practice
content:
The Turkish government plans to increase spending on defense and the arms industry by more than 60 percent in 2027. Gülistan Kılıç Koçyiğit, deputy parliamentary group chair of the DEM Party, criticized these budget priorities in light of the ongoing Peace and Democratic Society Process. While billions are being allocated to the military and security apparatus, funding remains insufficient for social welfare, healthcare, and education, she underlined.


At a press conference in the Turkish Parliament in Ankara, Koçyiğit put the planned defense expenditure for 2027 at 3.454 trillion Turkish lira (nearly 62.1 billion euros). This represents an increase of 60.28 percent compared to the 2026 budget. The planned increase, she argued, contradicts political statements about a peaceful resolution of the Kurdish question.


“We would have liked to see a substantial portion of the budget actually allocated to improving the well-being of the population and covering healthcare and education costs,” the DEM Party politician stated.


‘We want to see peace in the budget, in language, and in practice’


Koçyiğit called for the peace process not to be limited to political statements and negotiations. She stated that a departure from decades of conflict-driven policies must also be reflected in the state’s economic priorities.


“The peace process must also be reflected in economic policy. If there is genuine sincerity here, we want to see all the effects of peace. We want to see peace in the budget, in language, and in practice. We want to feel it in every aspect of life,” Koçyiğit said.


According to the DEM Party, the planned military expenditure is part of a fundamentally misguided budget policy. Koçyiğit argued that the draft 2027 central government budget primarily serves the interests of capital, while the social needs of the population are pushed into the background.


According to the figures presented by Koçyiğit, government expenditure is expected to increase by 44.09 percent and revenue by 44.35 percent. At the same time, the budget deficit is projected to rise by 42.57 percent. She was particularly critical of the growing burden of interest payments.


Koçyiğit pointed out that the public funds earmarked for these payments could instead be used to support farmers, improve healthcare for low-income people, and safeguard the living conditions of pensioners and minimum-wage workers.


Floods hit low-income communities particularly hard


In addition to the budget debate, Koçyiğit addressed the recent devastating floods in Istanbul, which claimed six lives and caused significant economic damage. Low-income neighborhoods were particularly hard hit.


She emphasized that the consequences of such disasters cannot be attributed solely to extreme rainfall, but are also the result of inadequate preventive measures and poor urban planning. These shortcomings, she added, further exacerbate existing social inequalities, particularly in poorer neighborhoods.


Koçyiğit criticized the lack of adequate attention to public infrastructure and the protection of the population, saying: “The floods once again demonstrate how closely social inequality, political priorities, and the population’s vulnerability to natural disasters are interconnected.”

author: Mada Masr
title: State security prosecution summons Mada Masr editor-in-chief for investigation
content:
Lina Attalah, Mada Masr’s editor-in-chief, received a summons today from the Supreme State Security Prosecution to attend a questioning session on Wednesday, October 21. The summons did not say why she is being questioned.


The new investigation, Case 9072/2026, is the sixth case brought against Mada Masr, its journalists and its editor-in-chief in the past six years. The most recent was in August 2025, when the security prosecution released Attalah on LE30,000 bail. She was questioned at the time on charges of “broadcasting false news” and “using a website without a license,” based on a National Security Agency investigation report, in relation to a Mada Masr story on prisoners’ complaints of abuse in detention facilities.

When

asked

why she trusted the sources cited in the story, Attalah said she had abided by professional journalistic standards and had acted in the public interest.

 She also pointed to the legally protected right to inform authorities of events through publication, noting that the outlet presents a full range of viewpoints.

author: Unknown
title: Амеде Дюнуа - Доклад "Анархизм и Организация"
content:
Автор

: Амеде Дюнуа

Название

: Доклад "Анархизм и Организация"

Дата

: 27 августа 1907

Источник

: Anarchisme & Syndicalisme: Le Congrès Anarchiste International d'Amsterdam (1907), с. 155-161


 Четвертое заседание, Вторник, 27 августа. – Утреннее заседание.


 Около девяти часов заседание открывается.


 РУДОЛЬФ ЛАНГЕ избирается председателем конгресса, а КРИСТИАН КОРНЕЛИССЕН и Р. ДЕ МАРМАНД – его заместителями.


 Повестка дня предусматривает обсуждение вопроса: «

Синдикализм и анархизм

»

[1]

. Но поскольку один из докладчиков, товарищ Джон Тёрнер, ещё не прибыл

[2]

, конгресс решает сначала обсудить вопрос: «

Анархизм и организация

». Слово предоставляется докладчику Амеде Дюнуа.


АМЕДЕ ДЮНУА.

 – Не так далеко то время, когда большая часть анархистов была против всякой мысли об организации. Тогда затеянный нами проект вызвал бы среди них бесчисленные протесты, а его авторов заподозрили бы в скрытых реакционных намерениях и в авторитарных замыслах.


 Это было время, когда анархисты, изолированные друг от друга, ещё более изолированные от рабочего класса, казалось, утратили всякое социальное чувство; когда анархизм с его непрестанными призывами к преобразованию индивида представал перед многими как высший расцвет старого буржуазного индивидуализма.


 Считалось, что индивидуальное действие, «индивидуальная инициатива» способна заменить всё. Изучение экономики, явлений производства и обмена обычно считалось чем-то незначительным, и даже некоторые из наших, отрицая всякую реальность классовой борьбы, соглашались видеть в современном обществе лишь антагонизмы мнений, к которым «пропаганда» как раз и должна была подготовить индивида.


 Как абстрактный протест против оппортунистических и авторитарных тенденций социал-демократии, анархизм за последние двадцать пять лет сыграл немалую роль. Почему же вместо того, чтобы на этом остановиться, он попытался построить – в противовес парламентскому социализму – идеологию, которая была бы ему всецело присуща? В своих смелых порывах эта идеология слишком часто теряла из виду твёрдую почву реальности и практического действия и слишком часто также в конце концов приземлялась, хотела она того или нет, на пустынные берега индивидуализма. Так и пришли мы к тому, что перестали мыслить организацию иначе как в формах, неизбежно угнетающих «индивида», и стали систематически отвергать всякое коллективное действие. Однако именно в этом вопросе об организации, который нас как раз занимает, совершается знаменательная эволюция. Несомненно, эта частная эволюция должна быть связана с общей эволюцией, которую анархизм претерпел во Франции за последние годы.


 Смешавшись активнее, чем прежде, с рабочим движением, мы преодолели расстояние, отделяющее чистую идею, которая так легко превращается в неприкосновенную догму, от живой реальности. Мы всё меньше интересовались нашими прежними абстракциями и всё больше – практическим движением, действием: синдикализм [то есть профсоюзное движение], антимилитаризм заняли у нас первое место. Анархизм предстаёт нам гораздо меньше в облике философской и моральной доктрины, чем в качестве революционной теории, в качестве конкретной программы общественных преобразований. Нам достаточно видеть в нём наиболее совершенное теоретическое выражение стремлений пролетарского движения.


 Анархистская организация всё ещё вызывает возражения. Но эти возражения весьма различны в зависимости от того, исходят ли они от индивидуалистов или от синдикалистов.


 Против первых достаточно сослаться на историю анархизма. Он вышел путём развития из «коллективизма» Интернационала, то есть, в конечном счёте, из рабочего движения. Следовательно, он не есть недавняя, наиболее совершенная форма индивидуализма, но одна из разновидностей революционного социализма. То, что он отрицает, – это не организация; напротив, это правительство, с которым, как сказал нам Прудон, организация несовместима. Анархизм не индивидуалистичен; он федералистичен, «ассоциационистичен» в первую очередь. Можно было бы определить его так: всесторонний федерализм.


 Впрочем, непонятно, каким образом анархистская организация могла бы вредить индивидуальному развитию своих членов. Ведь никто не был бы обязан в неё вступать и, вступив, не был бы обязан из неё не выходить.


 Возражения, выдвигаемые с индивидуалистической точки зрения против наших проектов анархистской организации, не выдерживают проверки: они с тем же успехом обратились бы против любой структуры общества. Возражения синдикалистов …

author: Cecília Melo
title: Sem educação, clima ou fome: O dito e não dito na propaganda eleitoral de Flávio Bolsonaro
content:
“A boca fala do que o coração está cheio”, diz o versículo 31 do capítulo 12 do livro bíblico de Mateus. E apesar de a fé ter entrado em cheio na campanha presidencial, a lição não parece ter sido colocada em prática pela propaganda eleitoral do candidato de extrema direita Flávio Bolsonaro (PL). Educação, fome, moradia, mobilidade e clima foram termos que nenhum dos guias de exibição gratuita na TV mencionaram ao longo de sua corrida presidencial. A palavra “constituição”, inclusive, não foi sequer mencionada pelo candidato em 14 inserções gratuitas até o momento.  


Segundo especialistas ouvidos pela

Agência Pública

, até então, o foco do discurso de Flávio Bolsonaro esteve em provocar comoção nos eleitores, através do medo e projetar força pessoal, através da autopromoção. 


A palavra “Brasil”, por exemplo, é a mais usada pela campanha do ultradireitista, numa frequência mais de 18 vezes superior a termos como “proposta(s)”.

 Embora faça parte do seu slogan “O Brasil vai Vencer”, “Brasil” também é usado conjuntamente a “Brasileiro(s)” e “Soberania” para criar sentido de pertencimento nacional, unidade, identidade coletiva e à defesa da nação. É o que diz a professora e pesquisadora em semiótica da Universidade Federal do Rio Grande do Norte (UFRN) Lilian Muneiro.


A responsabilidade pela elaboração do conteúdo dos guias – roteiro, cenário e edição, por exemplo – é integralmente do partido político.

 A legislação garante o espaço na programação de rádios e televisões, comerciais e públicas, para veiculação do guia ou propaganda eleitoral de candidatos a cargos estaduais, federais e presidência durante 70 minutos por dia, distribuídos entre os comerciais da emissora. 


O levantamento da

Pública

 identificou as palavras mais repetidas por Flávio Bolsonaro nos 14 vídeos de seu guia eleitoral até agora. As peças estão disponíveis no perfil do candidato no YouTube e foram exibidas em rede nacional de 28 de agosto a 14 de outubro. O levantamento também identificou palavras que o candidato não citou, mesmo sendo assuntos de preocupação mundial. 


Para a professora do Departamento de Letras da UFRN e pesquisadora em análise do discurso, Cellina Muniz, a escolha de palavras de Flávio Bolsonaro não deve ser interpretada como coincidência, pois para seu campo de estudos, as palavras que usamos não são só nossas, e carregam uma história.

A construção narrativa visa projetar uma imagem de si “historicamente associada a regimes tipicamente autoritários. Governos totalitários, de diferentes posicionamentos ideológicos, sempre se pautaram na idolatria da figura mítica de um ‘chefe’ que tenta se afirmar simultaneamente como combatente e como guardião”, avalia.


O dito…


O termo “medo” aparece duas vezes mais que “esperança” nos guias eleitorais de Flávio Bolsonaro. “Esse discurso tenta comover seu público e construir sua adesão por meio do apelo emocional com a criação de um ‘inimigo’ a ser combatido (as milícias, o petismo etc.)”, avalia a professora Cellina Muniz.


“O Brasil nunca teve tanto medo”, disse o candidato no programa exibido no dia 1º de setembro, se referindo a grupos de facções espalhados pelo Brasil.

 “Comando Vermelho”, “facções”, “PCC” “organizações narcoterroristas” e “milícias” não são termos dos mais recorrentes no guia eleitoral, mas aparecem duas vezes mais que as palavras “democracia” e “paz” na mensagem passada aos eleitores.


Apesar do apelo ao medo, alguns fatos conectam o candidato ao universo que critica. Ainda em setembro, a revista

piauí

 expôs que em 2023, o senador Flávio enviou emenda parlamentar para o Instituto de Formação Profissional José Carlos Procópio (Ifop), uma ONG sediada na Taquara, reduto miliciano na Zona Oeste do Rio. O pedido partiu de Robson Calixto Fonseca, o “Peixe”, preso e condenado por agir como braço operacional da organização criminosa dos irmãos Brazão, os mandantes do assassinato de Marielle Franco. Peixe é apontado como o elo entre os Brazão e os milicianos da região de Jacarepaguá.


Em sua análise, a pesquisadora de semiótica Lilian Muneiro comentou que os vocábulos sobre segurança produzem juntos um “eixo de sentido associado à vulnerabilidade, ao risco, à necessidade de proteção e ao restabelecimento da ordem.

 Nesse conjunto, também é possível observar a dimensão passional do discurso”, afirma.


As escolhas do que compõe o discurso repetido de Flávio Bolsonaro também ajuda a indicar suas prioridades narrativas. O candidato do PL falou mais em …
